questions.explanation:

power so that the machine cannot be operated without all guards in place. The interlocking 
guard prevents operation of the control that sets the machine in motion until the guard is 
moved into position, so that the operator cannot reach the point of operation or the point of 
danger.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of protective footwear?
questions.explanation:
Fitted orthotics is not a type of safety protective footwear. 

Safety shoes have impact-resistant toes and heat-resistant soles that protect the feet against 
hot work surfaces common in roofing, paving and hot metal industries. The metal insoles of 
some safety shoes protect against puncture wounds. Safety shoes may also be designed to be 
electrically conductive to prevent the buildup of static electricity in areas with the potential 
for explosive atmospheres or nonconductive to protect workers from workplace electrical 
hazards. 

Electrically conductive shoes provide protection against the buildup of static electricity. 
Employees working in explosive and hazardous locations such as explosives manufacturing 
facilities or grain elevators must wear conductive shoes to reduce the risk of static electricity 
buildup on the body that could produce a spark and cause an explosion or fire. Foot powder 
should not be used in conjunction with protective conductive footwear because it provides 
insulation, reducing the conductive ability of the shoes. Silk, wool and nylon socks can 
produce static electricity and should not be worn with conductive footwear. Conductive shoes 
must be removed when the task requiring their use is completed. Note: Employees exposed to 
electrical hazards must never wear conductive shoes. 

Electrical hazard, safety-toe shoes are nonconductive and will prevent the wearers' feet from 
completing an electrical circuit to the ground. These shoes can protect against open circuits of 
up to 600 volts in dry conditions and should be used in conjunction with other insulating 

equipment and additional precautions to reduce the risk of a worker becoming a path for 
hazardous electrical energy. The insulating protection of electrical hazard, safety-toe shoes 
may be compromised if the shoes become wet, the soles are worn through, metal particles 
become embedded in the sole or heel, or workers touch conductive, grounded items. Note: 
Nonconductive footwear must not be used in explosive or hazardous locations. 

Foundry Shoes, in addition to insulating the feet from the extreme heat of molten metal, 
foundry shoes keep hot metal from lodging in shoe eyelets, tongues or other shoe parts. These 
snug-fitting leather or leather-substitute shoes have leather or rubber soles and rubber heels. 
All foundry shoes must have built-in safety toes.

questions.question: Compared to local exhaust ventilation, dilution ventilation:
options: Is more suitable for highly toxic substances
Is not adequate for ventilating hazardous point source emissions
Must be used as make-up air
Uses less air than local exhaust ventilation
questions.explanation:

with highly toxic materials. In these situations local exhaust ventilation should be used. 
Because of these limitations, short circuiting of exhaust is less critical than in local exhaust 
ventilation. The air from general ventilation may or may not be used for local exhaust 
ventilation make-up air, depending upon the type of local exhaust ventilation device.

questions.question: You are a safety professional in a large corporation with a high-rise corporate office building. The building is occupied totally by employees of your company except for a few service contractors and first floor space leased by store tenants. Life safety is one of your principle concerns. Strategies for evacuation that you may consider include all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Relocation means to move people away from the fire floor, generally two floors up or 
down from the fire. A horizontal exit on the same floor is possible when fire walls, ceilings, 
and floors exist that allow people to evacuate through a fully protected enclosure before 
arriving at a stairwell. Staged evacuation can take several forms but essentially means to 
evacuate people in stages and to perhaps use a series of safe areas in the staging. There is no 
such term as a vertical exit.

questions.question: In conducting a safety and health audit at a plant owned by your company, you discover that an extremely hazardous solvent is being used which has a high probability of injury. What is your first course of action?
options: Recommend that the solvent be substituted
Initiate actions to construct engineering controls
questions.explanation:
The first course of action is to take air samples for analysis. Then, you can determine 
whether further action is warranted. 
With no indication of negative impacts occurring, the most appropriate action is to conduct 
further assessment of the solvent use to verify that no imminent hazard exists. If an imminent 
hazard is determined to exist, immediate action is required, such as stopping the operations 
and requiring appropriate PPE. If no imminent hazard exits, then a longer term action can be 
considered, such as material substitution or engineering controls.

questions.question: A worker's muscles act on an angle of 45º with respect to the direction of motion. The horizontal force necessary to start moving the item is 256 N and is measured standing in front of the item to be moved. What is the actual muscle force needed to start moving the item?
questions.explanation:
Using the cosine trigonometric identity and vector mechanics: 
Cosine of Angle = Adjacent Component / Hypotenuse Resultant 
cos 45º = 256 N / Hypotenuse Resultant 
Hypotenuse Resultant = 256 N / cos 45º 
= 256 N / 0.7071 = 362 N

questions.question: Some of the following six statements VIOLATE hoisting equipment and crane regulations. Indicate which statements violate these regulations. I. Loads may be only traversed over the heads of the actual materials handling crew performing the lift. IV. Holding and self-setting brakes are optional for loads under 10,000 lbs. V. Hoist rope or chain must be free from kinks or twists. VI. Hoisting or traveling is permissible only when a qualified person is on the load or hook.

CFR 1910.179. Spelled out are that loads must not be carried over the heads of people; hoists

holding brakes must be applied automatically when the power is off for powered hoists; and

questions.question: Occupational fatalities due to workplace violence (homicide) is the ______________ leading cause of occupational fatalities in the United States.
questions.explanation:
Workplace violence has emerged as an important safety and health issue in today's 
workplace. Its most extreme form, homicide, is the second leading cause of fatal occupational 
injuries in the United States. Nearly 1,000 workers are murdered, and 1.5 million are 
assaulted in the workplace each year. According to the BLS Census of Fatal Occupational 
Injuries (CFOI), there were 709 workplace homicides in 1998, accounting for 12% of the 
total 6,026 fatal work injuries in the United States. Environmental conditions associated with 
workplace assaults have been identified and control strategies implemented in a number of 
work settings. OSHA has developed guidelines and recommendations to reduce worker 
exposures to this hazard but is not initiating rulemaking at this time.

sin 60º = 250 lb / hypotenuse leg length 
0.8660 = 250 lb / hypotenuse leg length

= 288.68 lb

questions.question: If the mean and median diastolic blood pressure screened on a large population of men are both 83 mm Hg, and the standard deviation of the screening is 12 mm Hg, which is TRUE?
options: About 95% of the men have a diastolic blood pressure between 59 and 107 mm Hg
About 80% of the men have a diastolic blood pressure between 71 and 95 mm Hg
About 50% of the men have a diastolic blood pressure between 71 and 94 mm Hg
questions.explanation:
When the mean and median numbers of a set are the same, one may assume that the 
population is normally distributed. In a normal distribution, approximately 95% of the results 
are within the mean plus or minus 2 standard deviations. This means that the diastolic blood 
pressure of 95% of the population of men falls between the mean minus 24 mm Hg and the 
mean plus 24 mm Hg (1 standard deviation is 12 mm Hg, 2 is 24 mm Hg).

questions.question: A pallet of material in a freight elevator which goes up with constant upward acceleration exerts a push on the floor of the elevator whose value is:
options: Equal to the weight of the pallet and its load
Greater than the weight of the pallet and its load
Less than the weight of the pallet and its load
Less than the weight of the pallet but greater than its load
questions.explanation:
Applying Newton's third law of motion, "Every action (force) is accompanied by an 
equal and opposite reaction (force)", the push of the floor of the elevator must be enough to 
support the weight of the pallet and its load and in addition, must accelerate the combined 
weights upward. Hence, the push of the elevator is greater than the weight of the pallet and 
load by an amount needed to give it acceleration [F = W + W (a/g)].

questions.question: The worker/working surface coupling has been cited as a causative factor in a large percentage of slips and falls accidents. The major mediating variable in this type of accident is the:

specific gravity. The specific gravity (SG) of a substance may be found from the relation:

1 ft3 of water weighs 62.4 lbs and SG of cast iron is 7 
Then:

7 = (Weight of 1 ft3 of iron)/(62.4 lbs) 
(7)(62.4 lbs) = (weight of 1 ft3 of iron) 
436.8 lbs = (Weight of 1 ft3 of iron)

For a parallel circuit, the total current is the sum of the branch currents (opposite from 
calculating resistances). 
IT = 12.3 A + 8.5 A + 4.2 A 
IT = 25 A 
P = E * I 
P = 110 V * 25 A = 2,750 W

questions.question: A wheelbarrow contains a load of 216 lb at an average distance of 1.50 ft from the axle. If the shaft of the wheelbarrow is 4 ft long, what is the force exerted upward by the fulcrum?
questions.explanation:
Since the wheelbarrow is in equilibrium, the forces pulling it upward are equal to the 
sum of the forces pulling it downward. 
The downward force = load = 216 lb 
The upward force = (216 lb * l.50 ft) / 4 ft= 81 lb 
Therefore the fulcrum must exert an upward force of: 216 lb - 81 lb = 135 lb

questions.question: Vapors of flammable and combustible liquids are:
options: Normally liquid at room temperature and have molecular weights lower than those which are gases
questions.explanation:
The vapors of flammable liquids are generally heavier than air. Examples are alcohol, 
naptha, gasoline, kerosene, and carbon disulfide. This is logical because gas or vapor density 
is proportional to molecular weight, and the compounds which are normally liquids at room 
temperature have higher molecular weights than those which are gases. Note that because 
vapors of flammable and combustible liquids are heavier than air, they tend to settle in lower 
areas and the trail of vapors can spread far from the liquid itself. If this vapor trail contacts a 
source of ignition, the resulting fire can FLASHBACK to the source of the vapors.

questions.question: Increasing the temperature or pressure will have the following effect on the LEL and UEL:
options: Raise the LEL and lower the UEL
Lower the LEL and raise the UEL
Raise the LEL and raise the UEL
Lower the LEL and lower the UEL
questions.explanation:
Flammable or explosive limits are concentrations of a vapor or gas in air below or 
above which propagation of a flame does not occur on contact with a source of ignition. The 
lower explosive limit (LEL) is the minimum vapor concentration below which the vapor-air 
mixture is too lean to burn or explode. The upper explosive limit (UEL) is the maximum 
vapor concentration above which the mixture is too rich to burn or explode. Increasing the 
temperature or pressure lowers the LEL and raises the UEL.

questions.question: In a work area the noise levels are 95 dBA for 2 hr, 90 dBA for 4 hr and 85 dBA for 2 hr. Does this exceed the OSHA limits?
questions.explanation:
Using OSHA Allowable 90 dBA for an 8 hour period: 
Allowable exposure time, T = 8/2 (L-90)/5 
Therefore: 
For 95 dBA, T = 4 
For 90 dBA, T = 8 
For 85 dBA, T = 16 

Noise dose (%), D = 100 [sum C1/T1] 

D = 100 [2/4 + 4/8 + 2/16] = 100 [1.125] = 112.5% 
This exceeds the allowable daily exposure by more than 12%.

questions.question: Which type of ionizing radiation, sometimes used in manufacturing operations, is the least penetrating?
questions.explanation:
Of the five kinds of radioactivity that are of general concern (e.g., alpha, beta, gamma, 
x-ray, and neutrons), alpha particles are the least penetrating. They will not penetrate thin 
barriers. For example, paper, cellophane, and even skin, will shield alpha particles.

questions.question: Which kind of radioactivity is considered to be a critical internal hazard?
questions.explanation:
Alpha particles may be inadvertently ingested, inhaled, or absorbed into the body as a 
result of improper handling. Internally, alpha particles are acutely hazardous because of their 
ionizing ability through very short distances in soft tissue. Depending on the chemical and 
physical form of the radioactive material, alpha particles may deposit in specific organs and 
produce acute radiation doses in those organs.

preferred choice for beta sources is low density plastic materials such as plexiglass or lucite. 
High density materials, like lead, are less effective because of the production of secondary X-
rays when the beta particles strike lead atoms.

questions.question: Acute poisoning refers to:

Exposure to highly toxic materials over a month or less
Low dose exposures over a short period
questions.explanation:
Acute exposures are the result of a single rapid exposure to a high dose of a material 
over a very short time period. Low or high doses to a toxic material over a period of days or 
weeks is not an acute exposure, it is a chronic exposure. Low doses over a short period do not

questions.question: Fatalities among workers performing quenching operations on metal drosses have been caused by:
questions.explanation:
Most cases of arsine poisoning occur after the accidental generation of the gas in the 
workplace. During recent years many incidents have involved a reaction between arsenic and 
aluminum, with the subsequent release of hydrogen in the presence of water to permit the 

formation of arsine gas. Arsine usually evolves when nascent hydrogen is generated in the 
presence of arsenical compounds or by the hydrolysis of a metallic arsenide in contact with 
water. Invariably, there is an acid medium where metal is present (e.g., dross residues, 
galvanized implements, aluminum tanks or implements) thereby creating the key ingredients 
necessary for arsine formation. Arsine generation is a concern of metal pickling operations.

questions.question: If a wire is 200 ft long and has a resistance of 1.5 and a diameter of 2 mm, what will the resistance be if the length is 140 ft and the diameter is 2.5 mm?
questions.explanation:
Use the formula: R2 = R1(L2 / L1) (D12 / D22) 

R2 = R1 (140 ft/200 ft) [(2 mm)2/(2.5 mm)2] 
R2 = 1.5 * 0.7 * 0.64 
R2 = 0.672 
Remember that the cross-sectional area of a round conductor changes with the square of the 
diameter.

questions.question: Assume a fan operates at 81% of maximum efficiency and delivers 6,000 cfm of air against a total pressure of 2 in. H2O. What horsepower is delivered?

questions.question: How much horsepower is expended by a gasoline engine driving a winch used to raise a 2,200 lb fixture a distance of 20 ft in 10 sec?
questions.explanation:
Horsepower is obtained from the formula: 
Work = Force * Distance 
W = 2,200 lb * 20 ft = 44,000 ft-lb 
Power = Work/time 
P = 44,000 ft-lb / 10 sec 
P = 4,400 ft-lb/sec 
Converting ft-lb/sec to hp: 
P(hp) = (4,400 ft-lb/sec) / [550(ft-lb/sec)/hp]

questions.question: What effort must be exerted by a material handler who is required to push a 200 lb barrel up a 10 ft long inclined plank on to a dock that is 2 ft above the ground? (Neglect friction.)
questions.explanation:
The work done in pushing a barrel up an inclined plane is equal to the resistive load 
multiplied by the height of the plane: 
Length of Incline * Effort = Resistive Load * Height of Incline 
10 ft * Effort = 200 lb * 2 ft 
Effort = (200 lb * 2 ft) / 10 ft = 40 lb

questions.question: A box weighing 500 lb is to be pushed up a ramp with a 5% grade. If the coefficient of friction is 0.15, what is the force required to push the box up the ramp?

5% grade = tan-1 0.05 = 2.86 º 
cos 2.86º = resultant force / 500 lb 
r = (0.9988) 500 lb 
r = 499.4 lb 
Calculate the friction force component: 
friction force = f r 
= (0.15)(499.4 lb) 
= 75 lb 
Calculate the dynamic force component: 
sin 2.86º = d / 500 lb 
d = 0.0499 * 500 lb 
d = 25 lb 
total force = dynamic force + friction force 
total force = 25 lb + 75 lb 
= 100 lb

questions.question: Which of the following engineering controls would be the most appropriate for a worker exposed in a steel mill to air temperatures exceeding 105ºF?
questions.explanation:
Although increasing general ventilation, using cooling fans, or providing spot cooling 
would result in some improvement, the application of radiant heat shielding is more 
appropriate. A steel mill (or forge shop, foundry, glass manufacturing plant) is a hot-dry 
industry, where the thermal load on the worker is increased by the sensible heat given off by 
the process equipment. The major heat source is radiant heat from molten metals and cherry 
red ingots, while that of the surrounding hot air is secondary. Radiant heat has no appreciable 
heating effect on the air it passes through, but its energy is absorbed by any object it 
strikes. Therefore, the application of a shield to either absorb or reflect the radiation from the 
heat source would be appropriate.

questions.question: When designing an ergonomically desirable work place, which of the following is a good design practice?
options: Allow room for employees to lean forward or to the side to reach objects
Design the work so that employees can move about and use different muscle groups
Place objects within close reach to discourage excessive movement
Design work which requires the arms to be held up or out
questions.explanation:

helps prevent overuse of any one muscle group. Leaning, restricted movement, and extension 
of arms all can cause injury over the long-term.

questions.question: Work surface height for standing work places should be designed as follows for precision work:
options: Below wrist height with padded rests for elbows
Shoulder height with a back rest
Above elbow height with padded forearm rests
Standing work places should be discouraged
questions.explanation:
The work should be placed above elbow height for best posture and provide padded 
forearm rests to allow resting of arms on surface. Work surfaces below elbow height may 
cause arm fatigue, and shoulder height work will cause back and shoulder fatigue. Standing 
work places can be well-designed to allow for low stress work with low fatigue. Adjustability 
will allow the employees to determine the best height for their needs.

questions.question: Manipulative tasks are highly repetitive and can cause an overload of muscles and joints. All of the following are good design guidelines for manipulative arm and hand work EXCEPT:

Prevent body joints from exercising the extremes of their ranges of motion
Keep elbows at an angle of 60º at or above mid-torso height

least strain on the muscles and tendons. Keeping body joints within the range of motion and 
away from extremes reduces potential for strains and sprains. Straight wrists will prevent 
repetitive motion injuries.

questions.question: Canopy hoods can best be used when:
options: Thermal currents can be taken advantage of
Canopy hoods should never be used
questions.explanation:
Canopy hoods are best used where heated materials give off contaminants that tend to 
rise which the canopy hood can capture and remove. The toxicity of the material is less of an 
issue if the canopy hood is able to keep the concentration below hazardous levels. Canopy 
hoods do tend to draw a high volume or air, which can lead to higher makeup air and energy 
costs.

questions.question: In determining the volume of dilution air needed in a room, you need to know:
options: Rate of generation of the contaminant
questions.explanation:
All that is needed for determining the volume of dilution air needed is the specific 
gravity and molecular weight of the contaminant, the TLV, and generation rate. A "K" value 

needs to be determined, based on the safety factor and mixing characteristics of the room. 
The size of the room is not a factor in this calculation.

questions.question: As a rule of thumb, what percentage of the exhaust face velocity of an unflanged open duct is present at 1 duct diameter from the duct?
questions.explanation:
At one duct diameter from an unflanged open duct exhaust, there is only 10% of the 
initial face velocity available for capture of contaminants. Conversely, at 30 duct diameters 
from the source of a blowing airstream, there is still 10% of the velocity measured at the 
source.

questions.question: Which of the following is most vulnerable to damage/injury precipitated by exposure to electromagnetic radiation:
questions.explanation:
Of the above choices, the eye is the most vulnerable part of the body to 
electromagnetic radiation. The skin is also vulnerable - particularly to ultraviolet radiation 
exposure (sunburn). The susceptibility of the eye is partially due to its receiving radiations 
not entirely limited to the visible portion of the electromagnetic spectrum. The function of 
certain portions of the ocular apparatus may be most easily impaired by minimal or threshold 
damage because of the delicate functional balance of component parts.

questions.question: A Class II laser:
options: Does not have enough power to injure a person accidentally when viewed for less than 1/4 sec
Does not have enough power to injure person accidentally when viewed for less than 1/2 sec
Cannot produce accidental injury if viewed directly for more than 1/2 sec
Produces a hazardous direct or specularly reflected beam
questions.explanation:
To provide guidance on the evolution and control of laser radiation hazards, a 
classification scheme was established (ANSI Z-136.l, Standard for the Safe Use of Lasers). 
This scheme is based only on the ability of the laser to produce injury, which in five classes, 
range from safe to very hazardous. Class II, or "low-power" devices, are those visible lasers 
which do not have enough power to injure a person accidentally, but which may produce 
retinal injury when viewed directly for more than 1/4 sec.
questions.source: Domain 1 - Advanced Application of Safety Principles - Question Bank.pdf

questions.question: A Class IIIb laser:
options: Does not have enough power to injure a person accidentally
Cannot induce injury when viewed within the beam with the unaided eye
Can produce accidental injury if viewed directly
Produces a hazardous direct or specularly reflected beam
questions.explanation:
To provide guidance on the evaluation and control of laser radiation hazards, a 
classification scheme was established (ANSI Z-136.1, Standard for the Safe Use of Lasers). 
This scheme is based only on the ability of the laser to produce injury, which in five classes, 
range from safe to very hazardous. A Class IIIb consists of lasers which can produce 
accidental injury if viewed directly. Intrabeam viewing of either the direct beam or a mirror-
like (specular) reflection of the beam should also be considered hazardous.

questions.question: One problem associated with flux-cored arc welding of stainless steel is the production of aerosols containing:
questions.explanation:
Welding fumes can contain constituents of the material being welded and the 
consumable materials (e.g. flux). Stainless steel welding results in fumes containing nickel 
and chromium. Often flux is used which contain fluorides. These fluorides are also released 
into the air during the welding process. 

Blunt, J., and Balchin, N.C., Health and Safety in Welding and Allied Processes, 5th ed. 
Finch, R., Welder's Handbook: A Complete Guide to MIG, TIG, ARC and Oxyacetylene 
Welding

Sources of ultraviolet light include electric arcs such as those produced during arc welding, 
photocopy machines, laser printers, and ultraviolet lamps. VDT monitors do not produce 
ozone.

questions.question: What is a "photon"?
questions.explanation:
A photon is any item on the electromagnetic (EM) spectrum. An ionizing photon can 
be an x-ray, gamma, or cosmic ray. Do not confuse "phonon", a sound wave, with "photon." 
A nucleon is a particle in the nucleus, either a proton or a neutron. Non-ionizing 
electromagnetic (EM) radiation types would include infrared and visible light.

options: Radiation reduced in energy from ionizing
The visible portion of the electromagnetic spectrum
questions.explanation:

ionizing portion of the spectrum begins at 10 keV and below. This roughly corresponds to the 
area of soft x-rays and high energy ultraviolet light.

questions.question: Which is the LEAST likely definition of a neutron?
options: An effective neutral component of the nucleus
questions.explanation:
Neutrons are not fundamental particles like electrons and protons. They will decay 
when separated from the nuclear force into a positive and negative component and, therefore, 

are considered to have an effective charge of zero. Neutrons, like protons, have an amu about 
equal to 1 and are considered to be a nucleon.

questions.question: What is the mathematical relationship of the wavelength of a photon to its frequency?
questions.explanation:
The wave equation: speed of light = frequency * wavelength. The speed of light is a 
constant; therefore, the relationship is inverse. In other words, as the wavelength decreases 
the frequency will increase. Conversely, if the wavelength increases the frequency will 
decrease.

questions.question: What is the "half-life" of a radionuclide?
options: Amount of time to eliminate ½ the dosage
Average time that the average radionuclide exists
Time required for a radionuclide to decay to ½ activity
Amount of time for the body to eliminate ½ the dose
questions.explanation:
The "half-life" is also known as the physical half-life. One half-life is the time it takes 
for a given amount of a radioactive material to decrease in activity by 50%.

questions.question: Hot dry skin, dizziness, nausea, rapid weak pulse, and rapid shallow breathing are symptoms of:
questions.explanation:
Heat stroke is a serious medical emergency caused by a failure of the central nervous 
system sweat control, thus leading to loss of evaporative cooling. This process leads to 
confusion, collapse, delirium, and coma. Cooling of the body must be started immediately if 
vital organ damage or death is to be averted.

questions.question: Evidence suggests that short term occupational exposure to vibration causes:
options: Severe physiological effects on the body
Moderate physiological effects on the body
Increased risk to the spine and the peripheral nervous system, the digestive system, and the reproductive system
Only small physiological effects which are reversible
questions.explanation:
In most occupational settings, the damage from vibration is thought to occur from the 
micro-trauma induced by vibration exposure over a long period of time, usually years. In the 
initial stages, vibration injury is reversible if the worker is removed from the exposure or the 
exposure is eliminated from the job.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true?

questions.question: An 8.0 ft steel ladder is placed against a building. The top of the ladder is 7.6 ft up the building wall then slips 1.0 ft down. How far did the bottom of the ladder move?

Theorem for right triangles (i.e., a2 + b2 = c2 where a and b are sides of a right triangle, and c 
is the hypotenuse.) 
Solving for the new base: (8.0 ft)2 - (6.6 ft)2 = (new base)2 
64 ft2 - 43.6 ft2 = (new base)2 
20.4 ft2 = (new base)2 
ft2 = new base 
New base = 4.5 ft 

Solving for the original base: (8.0 ft)2 - (7.6 ft)2 = (original base)2 
Original base = 2.5 ft. Therefore the base changed from 2.5 ft to 4.5 ft, a change of 2.0 ft.

questions.question: A three-leg sling is supported from a single point and attaches to a 1,000 lb steel cylindrical object at three equidistant points along the cylinder's circumference (i.e., the attachment points on the steel cylinder are 120º apart). The center of gravity of the cylinder runs through its center. When attached to this steel cylinder, each leg of the sling creates a 30º angle with respect to the load. What is the tension in each leg of the sling?
questions.explanation:
Since the center of gravity of the load is through its center, and since each leg of the 
sling attaches to the load equidistant from its adjacent legs, each leg will carry exactly 1/3 of 
the load. The angle each leg of the sling makes with the load is measured as 30º. Therefore, 
the tension in each leg of the sling is equal to 1/3 of the total load (1,000 lb) divided the sine 
of 30º. 
Tension (in one leg) = 1/3 of total load / sin 30º 
Tension (one leg) = 1/3 of 1,000 lbs/sin 30º 
Tension (one leg) = 333.3/0.5 
Tension (one leg) = 667 lbs 
When you have the angle of each leg of the sling with respect to the load (or with respect to 
the horizontal), divide the load by the sine of the angle.

questions.question: A vehicle is traveling at a constant speed of 45 mph. On average, the vehicle accelerates at a rate of 1 ft/sec2 four times per hour for 30 seconds to pass other vehicles. How far does the vehicle travel in one hour?
questions.explanation:
In 58 minutes the vehicle goes 45 mph * (58 min / 60 min/hr) = 43.5 miles To 
determine the distance traveled in the remaining two minutes of acceleration, use s = vot + 
at2/2 
Convert 45 mph to 66 ft/sec 
t = 120 seconds (2 minutes) 
s = (66 ft/sec)(120 sec) + (1 ft/sec2)(120 sec)2) / 2 
= 7,920 ft + 7200 ft 
= 15,120 ft = 2.9 miles 
43.5 miles + 2.9 miles = 46.4 miles

questions.question: A man pushes a 30 lb object for 8 ft on a 15º inclined plane. If the dynamic coefficient of friction is 0.40, how much work did he perform?

direction of the plane, forming a vector triangle. The force from the weight in the direction of 
the plane can be determined by: 
cos 75 = Fp / 30 lb 
Fp = 7.8 lb 
The force perpendicular to the plane. 
Fn = sin 75 * 30 lb = 28.9 lb 
Dynamic friction force to be overcome is: Ff = 0.4 * 28.9 lb = 11.6 lb 
The man has to overcome both forces. 
Ft = 11.6 lb + 7.8 lb = 19.4 lb 
Work performed = 19.4 lb * 8 ft = 155.2 ft-lb

questions.question: The factor which is primarily responsible for dust gaining entrance to the alveolar regions of the lung is:
questions.explanation:
Particle size is the most important factor in determining respirability. It is the ability of 
the smaller particles to negotiate the turns and twists of the respiratory tract that allows them 
to gain access to the lower portions of the respiratory system. The composition and 
concentration are important once the deposition of the particle has occurred; that may cause 
the biological response to the substance. The condition of the mucociliary system affects the 
clearance of particles from the lung, once deposited.

questions.question: The size particle which has the greatest retention in the lung is:
questions.explanation:

area where they have less of a chance of being cleared from the lung. Particles less than 1.0 
micron tend to stay in the airstream and are breathed back out, while particles greater than 5.0 
microns are captured in the upper respiratory tract and do not get to the lower portions of the 
lungs.

questions.question: An electrician assures you that the a standard duplex wall receptacle is wired correctly. questions.question: Carbon monoxide is particularly dangerous because:
options: It inhibits blood cells from carrying oxygen
It is not easily transferred in cellular respiration
It is a systemic poison that inhibits enzyme generation
It paralyzes the respiratory center of the brain

blood and interrupting the normal oxygen supply to the body tissues.

questions.question: A room 50 ft x 20 ft x 10 ft contains 100 ppm of CCl4. How much time is required to lower the concentration to 25 ppm if a blower generating 300 cfm is used to clear the room?
questions.explanation:
t = log10(C/Co) (-2.303) (P/Q) 
Where: 
C = end concentration 
Co = beginning concentration 
P = room volume 
Q = flow of air 
Substituting we get: 
t = log10(25/100) (-2.303) (10,000 ft3/300 cfm) = 46 min

questions.question: A 50 ft x 190 ft x 20 ft building is supplied with 8,000 cfm. What is the number of air changes per hour in the building?
questions.explanation:
Determine total building volume: 
50 ft * 190 ft * 20 ft = 190,000 ft3 
Convert cfm to ft3/hr: 
8,000 cfm * 60 min/hr = 480,000 ft3/hr 
480,000 ft3/hr / 190,000 ft3 = 2.5 air changes/hr

questions.question: An exhaust system operating at 25,000 cfm is increased to 30,000 cfm. What is the required increase in the fan horsepower to handle the increased volume?
questions.explanation:
Fan horsepower varies as the cube of the fan speed and cube of the fan volume. 
Therefore, the required ratio of increase in the fan speed is: 
(30,000 CFM/25,000 CFM)3 = 1.73 
The required increase in the fan horsepower is 73%. You must ensure that the fan motor 
horsepower rating is ample.

questions.question: Calculate the density of standard air at 200ºC and at 0.7 atm:
questions.explanation:
Remember to convert degrees C to Kelvin 
Density is defined as mass per unit volume (m/V) 
PV = nRT 
PV = mRT/M 
Remember that n = m/M where "m" is the mass and "M" is the molecular weight 
We want to find the density; therefore, we need to rearrange the equation to solve for density 
(m/V) 
PV = mRT/M 
PVM = mRT 
PVM/RT = m 
PM/RT = m/V = 
 = (0.7 atm * 28.96 g/mol) / (0.08205 l-atm/mol-K * 473° K) 
= 0.522 g/l

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding a critical orifice?
options: Used ahead of the sampling device
Constant flow occurs when downstream pressure is more than 53% of upstream pressure
Each can only be used for a specific flow rate

A critical orifice achieves a specific constant flow rate when downstream pressure is 
less than 53% of upstream pressure. It is used in the field when constant flow at a specific 
flow rate is important and a strong enough pump to achieve high static pressure is available. 
The orifice must be used downstream of the sampling device.

options: Velocity varies directly as the square of the RPM
Power varies directly as the cube of the RPM
Flow rate varies directly with the RPM
Static pressure varies directly as the square of the RPM
questions.explanation:

the correlation between velocity and RPM would be a direct relationship if the diameter of

questions.question: Velocity pressure is:
options: The velocity of air divided by 4005 times the square root of the Sp
The difference between total pressure and static pressure
Proportional to the square root of velocity
questions.explanation:
The total pressure in a ventilation system is equal to the static pressure plus the 
velocity pressure. The velocity pressure, therefore, is the difference between the total 
pressure and the static pressure. The CFM is equal to the area of the duct multiplied by 4005 
times the square root of the velocity pressure. The velocity pressure is directly related to the 
square of velocity of air in the duct.

questions.question: Which type of hood would you recommend be designed for operations which release sudden surges of hot gases and vapors?
questions.explanation:
Canopy hoods are effective for the control of hot processes and for those operations 
which release sudden surges of hot gases and vapors such as those where the thermal currents 
caused by rising hot air funnel the contaminant into the exhaust system.

questions.question: In general, which of the following operations would require the greatest capture velocity to achieve effective exposure control?
questions.explanation:
Grinding operations release contaminants at high initial velocities. The other 
operations release contaminants with low velocities. Higher capture velocities would be 
required to entrain the releases from the grinding operations.

questions.explanation:

halogented hydrocarbons.

Sharpening tools at a stand grinder
questions.explanation: Ammonia (NH3) is a gas; spectacles would not provide protection.

questions.question: Which respirator has an assigned protection factor of 10,000?
options: SCBA operating in pressure demand mode
SAR in pressure demand mode with auxiliary SCBA in positive mode
questions.explanation:
The protection factors were determined by conducting quantitative fit testing on 
human volunteers. The higher the factor, the more protection. Therefore, a SAR with an 
escape SCBA offers the same protection as an SCBA. Both must be in the supply mode. The 
demand mode may introduce contaminants into the face during strenuous circumstances.

questions.question: The static magnetic field TLV for an 8-hour TWA whole body dose should not exceed:
questions.explanation:
The TLV for static magnetic fields is 600 Gauss or 60 milliTeslas (mT) for a whole 
body dose. Extremity doses can be 6,000 Gauss (600 mT). Static magnetic field can pose a 
severe danger to workers with pacemakers, and their exposure should not exceed 5 Gauss 
(0.5 mT). 

ACGIH TLVs and BEIs

Cppm = (Pvapor / Ptotal) x 106 ppm 
= (7 x 10-3 mm Hg / 760 mm Hg) x 106 ppm 
= 9.2 ppm

questions.question: Biological exposure indices data is important because they include type(s) of exposure in addition to inhalation. Which of the following exposures are least likely to be assessed by a BEI?
questions.explanation:
BEI's measure certain biological functions to determine the "total" exposure from all 
routes. BEI's do not measure transplacental exposures. They may provide some useful 
information however on exposure of the fetus to workplace chemicals.

questions.question: A device that protects equipment from an overload by opening the circuit automatically is commonly called a:
questions.explanation:
Circuit breakers and fuses are overcurrent devices that open a circuit automatically 
when there is excessive current flow from an accidental ground, short circuit, or overload. 
The circuit breaker trips open when its mechanical mechanism is activated; it can be reset. 
The fuse contains a strip of wire or fusible metal link which melts when overloaded. GFCI 
devices do not protect equipment, per se. They are designed to protect people by opening a 
circuit rapidly upon detecting a fault.

questions.question: In choosing a noise control barrier, which represents the best choice of design?
questions.explanation:
Air tight enclosures yield the best noise protection. Small leaks can cause significant 
noise leakage. It is best to design enclosures to keep leaks to an absolute minimum.

questions.question: In the design of a noise reducing enclosure, all of the following characteristics are desired EXCEPT:
options: Enclosure made of solid non-porous material
questions.explanation:
Acoustical-absorbing material on the outside of an enclosure is much less effective 
than having the sound-absorbing material on the inside.

questions.question: When a respirator has a HEPA filter, the filter is 99.97 % effective at capturing monodisperse particle _____ microns or larger in diameter.

HEPA filters are 99.97% efficient at collecting monodisperse particles 0.3 microns or 
larger.

questions.question: When a respirator is worn by more than one person it must go through an additional step of cleaning. This step is called:
questions.explanation:
Any time a respirator is worn by more than one person it must be disinfected. If 
possible, it is preferable to have each person have their own respirator. This is difficult, 
however, in the case of emergency response respirators such as SCBA's. The employer's 
Respiratory Protection Program must stipulate in writing how the disinfection process will 
occur.

questions.question: Which of the following items does not affect the fit of a respirator?
questions.explanation:
Dentures, sideburns, and the adjustment straps all effect how well a respirator fits. The 
exhalation valve, although very important to respirator function, does not effect the fit.

other listed devices all have lower protection factors.

questions.question: The two most common techniques employed for the control of bioagents are:
questions.explanation:
Disinfection and sterilization are the two most common techniques used to control 
bioagents. It is important to note disinfection and sterilization are not synonymous operations. 
To disinfect means to get rid of some pathogenic microorganisms that cause infection, but 
does not imply complete destruction of all that are harmful, whereas, sterilization means the 
absolute destruction of all living organisms.

questions.question: Early hearing loss caused by noise:

Is not generally noticeable to the subject
questions.explanation:
Most people do not notice the hearing loss until there is significant detriment to their 
hearing.

questions.question: What type of guarding should be installed at the approach zone to a fixed robotized workstation?
questions.explanation:
A robotized work station is divided into a robot movement zone (work envelope) and 
the zone of approach to it. The boundaries of the zone can be defined so that the limits within 
which protection is provided are known. Fixed barriers with interlocked gates permit 
workzone entry into an area, free from robot movement, which are monitored by the 
interlock. More detail on safety requirements for industrial robots can be found in ANSI/RIA 
R 15.06 - 1986 and NIOSH publication No. 88-108.

The NFPA has a color code for sprinkler heads to indicate temperature rating. 

Uncolored: 135ºF - 170ºF 
White: 175ºF - 225ºF 

Blue: 250ºF - 300ºF

Orange: 500ºF - 650ºF

questions.question: When walking through a chemical mixing area, you noticed that the automatic sprinkler heads faced the roof and were color-coded blue. What should this tell you?
options: It was an intermediate temperature pendent sprinkler head with an operating temperature of 175ºF- 225ºF
It was a high temperature upright sprinkler head with an operating temperature of 250ºF - 300ºF
It was an extra high temperature upright sprinkler head with an operating temperature of 325ºF - 375ºF
It was a high temperature pendent sprinkler head with an operating temperature of 250ºF - 300ºF
questions.explanation:
Sprinkler heads facing up are called "upright". When color coded blue, it signifies a 
high temperature rating with a 250ºF - 300ºF operating temperature. NFPA 13 2-2.3.2 - 
Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems

questions.question: Placing a shield between an ionizing radiation source and an employee is an example of:
questions.explanation:
Hazard control is accomplished by either engineering or administrative 
(management) control. Generally, any type of control that requires design, construction, or design modifications is 
categorized as engineering control. 
The best way to eliminate hazards is by means of engineering controls. However, if engineering controls cannot be 
implemented, then hazards must be controlled by means of administrative controls. Examples of administrative 
controls include training and reducing the time a worker is exposed to hazards.

questions.question: A stock insurance company is best defined by which of the following statements?
options: Insurance company which is profit motivated
Insurance company with at least 100,000 shares of stock
Insurance company that is not allowed to sell Workers' Compensation insurance
questions.explanation:
Stock insurance companies are profit oriented, and are generally publicly 
traded firms. The company issues shares that can be purchased by the public in order to raise capital. Stock 
insurance companies pay their shareholders in capital appreciation, dividends, or both.

questions.question: The BEST method to reduce employee exposure to airborne chemicals to an acceptable level is by means of:
options: Reducing the number of exposure hours
questions.explanation:
In control of any workplace hazard, engineering control must be 
considered first. Administrative controls such as job rotation and use of appropriate PPE must only be considered 
when engineering controls are either not feasible or cannot solve the problem.

questions.question: Point source airborne contaminants are best controlled by:
options: General ventilation with a compression ratio of 10 or more
questions.explanation:
Local exhaust ventilation is the most effective method of controlling point 
source airborne contaminants. 
Dilution ventilation involves bringing in clean air to dilute the contaminated air, and then exhausting the diluted air. 
Dilution ventilation does not eliminate exposure, but should be designed in such a way as to bring the concentration 
down to a safe level.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of engineering noise control?
options: Reducing the number of hours of exposure
questions.explanation:
Engineering controls are used to permanently eliminate or lessen the 
severity of a hazardous condition. In this case, use of sound absorbing materials for control of over-exposure to 
noise is a good example of engineering control.

questions.question: Which of the following insurance coverage is used to provide liability coverage for a company engaged in the cleanup of a hazardous waste site?
questions.explanation:
This type of insurance coverage is for work that is performed away from 
the company, such as that done by consultants, contractors, and remediation companies.

questions.question: The preferred angle range for fixed industrial stairs is:
questions.explanation:
The preferred angle range for fixed industrial stairs is 30 to 35 degrees. 
The preferred angle for a ramp is no more than 15 degrees. The preferred angle range for fixed ladders is 75 to 90 
degrees.

questions.question: In ventilation design, the number of room air changes per unit time can be obtained by:
options: Multiplying the room volume by the volumetric flow rate of air in the ventilation system.
Dividing the room volume by the volumetric flow rate of air in the ventilation system.
Dividing volumetric flow rate of air in the ventilation system by the room volume.
Subtracting the volumetric flow rate of air in the ventilation system from the room volume.
questions.explanation:
The number of air changes can be obtained by dividing the volumetric 
flow rate by the room volume. For example, a ventilation rate of 600 cubic feet per minute in a room of 300 cubic 
feet will provide 2 air changes per minute.

questions.question: Which of the following organizations mandates lockout/tagout programs for service or maintenance of certain types of equipment?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is OSHA.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true in regard to chemical labels?
options: Labels are used on drums of hazardous chemicals.
Labels are used on transportation vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Labels are used on gas cylinders.
Labels are used on bottles of hazardous chemicals.
questions.explanation:
Placards are used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. The 
Department of Transportation has standards and regulations (49CFR) for placards and labels.

questions.question: In liability insurance coverage, the term "OCP" is an acronym for:
questions.explanation:
"OCP" is an acronym for Owners and Contractors Protection. This type of 
insurance protects a business owner, property owner, or general contractor against liability due to the negligent act 
of an independent contractor or subcontractor who performs work on their behalf. The independent contractor or 
subcontractor purchases the policy. This type of policy covers a specific project at a specific location.

questions.question: Insurance coverage falls into four broad categories. Which of the following is NOT one of these categories?
questions.explanation:
Fire insurance is covered under property insurance. Health insurance is 
the fourth category.

questions.question: Business Income Coverage (BIC) insurance addresses the loss exposures relating to loss of income and/or extra expense to operate. Which of the following is NOT one of the three elements of the loss exposure covered by the basic BIC form?
questions.explanation:
"Property" covers damage to or destruction of real property. "Perils" are 
covered causes of loss. "Consequences" covers loss of business income as a result of interruption or partial 
suspension of business.

questions.question: Ground Fault Circuit Interrupters (GFCI) work on the principal of sensing a difference in the amount of electric current entering and leaving a circuit. The difference is considered to be electric current that is leaking to the ground. Once a difference has been detected, a GFCI opens the circuit in:
questions.explanation:
GFCIs are fast-acting devices that, once a current leakage has been 
detected, open the circuit in 0.02 to 0.03 seconds. 
A ground fault is an unintentional electrical path between a power source and a grounded surface. Ground faults 
most often occur when equipment is damaged or defective, such that live electrical parts are no longer adequately 
protected from unintended contact. If your body provides a path to the ground for this current, you could be burned, 
severely shocked, or electrocuted.

questions.question: Which of the following fall protection systems absorb the energy of an actual fall?
questions.explanation:
Fall arrest systems are usually comprised of a lanyard that is connected 
to a beam through a choker. The lanyard is connected to an energy absorber that in turn is connected to a full body 
harness.

questions.question: Ozone (O3) is a powerful oxidizing agent and is considered to be a hazardous gas. Which of the following operations is most likely to produce ozone?
questions.explanation: Ozone is produced during electric arc welding operations.

questions.question: Hexavalent chromium, which is toxic, can most likely be produced as a result of which of the following operations?
questions.explanation:
Stainless steel contains chromium. Stainless steel can produce trivalent 
and hexavalent chromium. Hexavalent chromium is much more toxic than trivalent chromium. Toxic hexavalent 
chromium can be converted to trivalent chromium by a reduction chemical reaction.

questions.question: The total pressure in a/an _________ ventilation system is equal to the sum of velocity pressure and static pressure.
questions.explanation:
In closed ventilation systems, total pressure is equal to the sum of static 
and velocity pressure: TP = SP + VP.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: Which of the following markings is used on many products manufactured in Europe, indicating that the product meets the health and safety standards?
questions.explanation:
The CE marking on European products is similar to the UL marking used 
on many US products. 
The CE marking is mandatory for products sold in the European Economic Area (EEA). By putting the CE marking 
on their products, manufacturers declare that their products meet the requirements set for by the European 
Commission (EC).

questions.question: Per DOT regulations, _________ drivers are not allowed to consume alcohol within four hours before starting their driving shift.
questions.explanation:
Per DOT regulations found in 49 CFR, commercial drivers are not 
allowed to consume alcohol within four hours prior to starting their driving shift.

questions.question: The type of liability insurance that helps protect individuals and companies that provide professional advice and services from bearing the full cost of defending against a negligence claim made by a client is called:
questions.explanation:
This type of coverage focuses on the policyholder's alleged failure to 
perform, cause financial loss, and errors and omissions in the service or product sold.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true in regard to course of construction insurance?
options: It covers a building under construction.
It covers perils such as fire, wind, and theft.
The policy will pay for damages up to the coverage limit.
The coverage limit must accurately reflect the total value of the structure, including labor costs and land value.
questions.explanation:
Course of construction insurance, also known as builders risk insurance, 
does not cover land value.

questions.question: Per DOT regulations, the post-accident drug and alcohol test applies to all drivers who are involved in fatal crashes. The test must also be conducted on all CDL drivers who are cited for moving violations arising in a crash that requires a vehicle being towed or an injury requiring medical attention away from the scene. The alcohol test must be conducted within _________ hours and the controlled substances test must be conducted within _________ hours of the crash.
questions.explanation:
CDL drivers are also subject to unannounced random testing for alcohol 
and drugs.

questions.question: All of the following are components of an insurance contract EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Privity refers to a one-on-one direct relationship and is not a component 
of an insurance contract. 

Other components of an insurance contract include the following: • The declaration page lists the name of the 
insurance company, the name of the insured, what is covered under the policy, the amount of coverage, the time 
that the policy is in effect, and how much premium the insured must pay for the coverage. • The definitions section 
explains the terminology that is used in the policy. • The insurance agreement section states what the insurance 
company promises to do. • The exclusions section states what risks are not covered under the policy. • The 
conditions section specifies those provisions of the policy that are required to be met before the insurance company 
pays the claim. • The endorsements section contains amendments to the original policy.

questions.question: Incorporation of safety at the design stage of a potentially hazardous industrial process, rather than after it is operating, is important because:
options: OSHA regulations requires a place of employment free of all hazards.
It has an economic advantage to the company.
It decreases management liability before plant operation.
It educates design engineers in safety standards.
questions.explanation:
Incorporation of safety at the design stage has a clear economic 
advantage. It is much less expensive to make changes at this stage compared to changes made after construction 
of a facility.

questions.question: In facility design, the responsibility for identifying and controlling hazards associated with equipment lies with:
questions.explanation:
The design team is responsible for understanding the hazards associated 
with equipment and control of those hazards.

questions.question: A pump is sending cooling water to a reactor. Loss of cooling water to this reactor would cause the reactor to explode. A fail-safe design for the system is BEST portrayed by:
options: Activation of a spare pump on failure of the cooling water pump.
Automatic shut down of process on failure of the cooling water pump.
questions.explanation:
The best fail-safe design is depicted in statement (a). This would allow 
the plant to operate safely and efficiently when the cooling water pump fails. The (b) statement would result in loss 
of production and additional cost for startup.

questions.question: The concept of Energy Theory in safe design of processing facilities states that the severity of an accident is related to:
questions.explanation:
The energy theory relates the kind and severity of injuries to statements 
(a), (b), and (c). 
The energy theory states that the cause of accidents is energy transfer with enough force to cause bodily or 
property damage. Therefore, preventing and controlling energy buildup and creating an environment that is not 
capable of energy conduction can greatly reduce the potential for accidents.

questions.question: Floor slipperiness is measured by:
questions.explanation:
A slip meter is a device that measures floor slipperiness. Slip meters 
measure the static coefficient of friction. The smaller the coefficient of friction, the more chance for people to slip on 
the floor.

questions.question: One of the more commonly encountered hazards for ground supported scaffolds is:
questions.explanation:
Tipping is one of the more commonly encountered hazards for ground 
supported scaffolds. This can be prevented by attaching the scaffold to a firm structure such as a building.

questions.question: Drums containing Polychlorinated Biphenyls (PCB) must be made of:
questions.explanation:
PCB drums must be made of metal and must meet DOT specifications 
(49CFR).

questions.question: The severity of electric shock primarily depends on:
options: The electric current flowing through the body
The body capacitance to absorb electrical energy
The body transmittance for electrical conductivity
questions.explanation:
The amount of electric current flowing through a victim's body determines 
the severity of an electric shock. Since current is dependent on the voltage and resistance of the body, these factors 
are also important considerations. For example, a circuit providing a potential difference of 220 volts sends more 
current through the body as compared to a circuit of 110 volts.

questions.question: Ventricular fibrillation caused as a result of electric shock refers to:
options: Fibers of the heart contract separately
Fibers of the heart contract simultaneously
Fibers of the heart expand beyond limit of elasticity
questions.explanation:
In order for the heart to perform its function as a pump, fibers of the heart 
must contract together in a coordinated manner. Ventricular fibrillation refers to the situation where these fibers 
contract separately resulting in cease of blood circulation in the body.

questions.question: Interlocks used in electrical equipment must meet which of the following criteria?
questions.explanation:
Interlocks used in electrical equipment must be of the fail-safe type. This 
means that the device must be designed in such a way to compensate for its failure without creating a safety 
problem.

questions.question: An electrical circuit protective device such as a fuse or circuit breaker protects the circuit from overload by:
questions.explanation:
Fuses and other circuit protective devices automatically open the circuit 
in the event of overflow of current. This action stops the flow of current.

questions.question: "Arcing" refers to:
questions.explanation:
"Arcing" is the flow of electrons through air between two conductors that 
are not in direct contact with each other. This electron flow generates a visible light.

questions.question: Electrical bonding:
options: Eliminates the electrical charges between two conductors
Eliminates the potential difference between two conductors
Sends electrical charges to the ground
questions.explanation:
Bonding does not remove the charges; however, it makes the potential 
difference between the two objects equal so there is no driving force for current flow between the two objects.

questions.question: The electrolytic fluid in lead-acid batteries during charging can produce:
questions.explanation:
Hydrogen gas can be produced during charging of lead-acid batteries. If 
hydrogen reaches its flammable limits, there is a potential for explosion or fire.

questions.question: An electrical system is considered to be de-energized (no potential difference in any component of the system):
options: When the power to the circuit has been shut off
After the system has been shut off and tested
After the power has been shut off and proper lockout/tagout has been performed
questions.explanation:
An electrical system can be considered de-energized only after 
appropriate tests have been conducted. For example, many electrical circuits having capacitors can store electrical 
energy for a long time after the system has been shut off. Also, systems that are grounded can have charged 
capacitors that might cause an electrical shock.

questions.question: For control of electrostatic hazards which one of the following types of clothing is preferable?
options: Type of clothing has no effect
questions.explanation:
Conductive clothing and shoes cause the electrostatic charges to safely 
flow to the ground.

questions.question: The surface conductivity of an electrostatically charged surface:
options: Will increase with an increase in humidity
Will decrease with an increase in humidity
Humidity has no effect on surface conductivity
Will increase with an increase in temperature
questions.explanation:
Humidity will increase surface conductivity. Humidity is the ratio of partial 
pressure of water vapor in air to equilibrium vapor pressure of water at a given temperature. An increase in 
temperature results in an increase in equilibrium vapor pressure and a decrease in relative humidity resulting in a 
decrease in surface conductivity.

questions.question: Which of the following is associated with equipment failure for facility design and operation?
questions.explanation: Statements (a), (b), and (c) are all associated with equipment failure.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT associated with plant layout for facility design and operation?
options: Number of people required to operate the plant
questions.explanation: Plant layout does not take into account the cost of instrumentation.

questions.question: In new chemical plant layout where most processing equipment is located outdoors, which of the items listed below should be considered first?
options: To group similar equipment in one location
To determine the direction of the prevailing wind
To minimize piping and pumping costs
questions.explanation:
The direction of prevailing wind will determine the location of many 
pieces of equipment.

questions.question: In designing outdoor plant layout, all equipment that may spill flammable materials should be located:
options: In an isolated area on the upwind side
Near fire stations and on the upwind side
questions.explanation:
Flammables should be placed on the downwind side otherwise, it is 
possible that the wind would carry the vapors from a spill over the plant where they could be ignited.

questions.question: The areas for containment of relatively large spills of liquefied petroleum gases must always be constructed below grade because:
options: These gases have a vapor density that is greater than one.
A person on the grade level or above will not be asphyxiated.
Spilled material can flow to these areas by gravity.
questions.explanation:
Gravity flow is not a reason, because liquefied petroleum gases (LPG's) 
turn into gaseous form once the pressure is reduced to atmospheric. Construction of containment areas below 
grade allows movement of emergency vehicles to and from the spill without creating additional hazards such as fire 
or explosion.

questions.question: Which of the following is the leading cause of work related injuries and deaths?
questions.explanation:
Motor vehicle accidents are the leading cause of work related injuries and 
deaths in the United States.

questions.question: When a source emits light that reaches a given surface, the surface can:
questions.explanation:
Light is a wave phenomenon and like other waves it can be absorbed, 
transmitted, or reflected by a surface.

questions.question: The quantity of illumination is measured by which of the following instruments?
questions.explanation:
The instrument used for measurement of the quantity of light is called a 
light meter.

questions.question: Which of the following organizations set forth standards for eye and face protection?
questions.explanation:
The American National Standard Institute ANSI sets forth standards for 
eye and face protection (ANSI Z87.1). These standards have been adopted by OSHA.

questions.question: Most personal devices used in fall protection:
options: Minimize the impact of a fall
Shield an individual from falling objects
questions.explanation:
Although statements in (a) and (b) are true, most personal fall protection 
devices are designed to interrupt a fall after its occurrence.

questions.question: All of the following are effective measures for fall protection EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Hard hats are personal protective equipment used exclusively for head 
protection.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT an administrative control of hazards?
options: Discipline an employee for unsafe work practices
Provide work rotation to reduce fatigue
questions.explanation:
Personal protective equipment is part of the "engineering control" of 
hazards.

questions.question: Before an employer can assign an employee to jobs requiring the use of a respirator, the employer:
options: Must consult with employee and obtain his/her consent to use a respirator.
Must test employee's reactions and performance while using a respirator in a non-hazardous atmosphere.
Must obtain written permission from a physician on employee's ability to use a respirator.
Document employee's performance while using a respirator for a period of no less than 10 days.
questions.explanation:
OSHA requires that only able persons be assigned to jobs which require 
the use of a respirator. This determination must be made by a qualified physician who informs the employer of the 
results of examination in writing.

questions.question: The stress generated in an object as a result of application of a force is equal to the:
options: Value of the compression stress minus the tensile stress
Value of the compression stress minus the shear stress
Value of the compression stress divided by the shear stress
Value of the force divided by the area upon which it acts
questions.explanation: Stress is defined as the value of force divided by the area.

questions.question: The term "creep" is referred to as:
options: The ability of a given material to resist tensile stress
Slow but permanent deformation of a material under a given load
The ability of a material to withstand shear stresses
An individual with uncivilized, and at times, unusual behavior
questions.explanation:
Creep is referred to as very slow but permanent deformation of a material 
that is under a given load.

questions.question: Shoring is required for all the trenches more than 4 feet deep unless:
options: They are sloped to an angle of repose
The trench is in a stable rock
questions.explanation: No shoring is required for situations stated in (a) and (b).

questions.question: A trench is:
questions.explanation:
Situations presented in statements a, b, and c are correct about trenches. 
Some OSHA recommended safety tips for trenches are listed below: • Do not enter an unprotected trench! • Trench 
collapses cause dozens of fatalities and hundreds of injuries each year. • Trenches 5 feet deep or greater require a 
protective system. • Trenches 20 feet deep or greater require that the protective system be designed by a registered 
professional engineer. 
Protective systems for trenches are the following: • Sloping protects workers by cutting back the trench wall at an 
angle inclined away from the excavation. • Shoring protects workers by installing aluminum hydraulic or other types 
of supports to prevent soil movement. • Shielding protects workers by using trench boxes or other types of supports 
to prevent soil cave-ins.

questions.question: The guard on a grinding wheel must:
options: Cover the wheel as completely as the nature of the work permits
questions.explanation:
It is impossible to fully enclose the grinding wheel as some portion of the 
wheels must be exposed to perform grinding on the part. Guards on grinding wheels must be adjustable to provide 
adequate protection when the diameter of the wheel decreases.

questions.question: Which of the following organizations has the most number of standards for unfired pressure vessels?
questions.explanation:
Unfired pressure vessels such as compressed air tanks, steam-jacketed 
kettles, etc. must follow the ASME code, section VIII, division 1 and 2.

questions.question: The recommended maximum allowable slope for a ramp is:
questions.explanation:
Ramps should be constructed using the minimum possible slope. The 
recommended maximum value for the slope of a ramp is 15 degrees. However, the slope should never exceed 20 
degrees.

questions.question: An indoor warehousing operations, the preferred type of powered truck is:
questions.explanation:
Electric trucks do not generate carbon monoxide and are preferred over 
other types for indoor operations. LPG powered trucks generate considerably less carbon monoxide compared to 
gasoline trucks.

questions.question: The most common occupational injuries resulting from manual materials handling are injuries to the:
questions.explanation:
Injuries to the back are the most common type of injuries resulting from 
manual materials handling. Many studies indicate that about 25 percent of all worker's compensation claims account 
for injuries to the lower back.

questions.question: Many powered materials handling vehicles have a high center of gravity. This means that:
options: The maximum load rating of the vehicle is increased compared to an identical low center of gravity vehicle.
The pressure exerted on tires is less than an identical vehicle with a low center of gravity.
The gravitational force exerted on the center of the vehicle is less than that of an identical vehicle with a low center of gravity.
When the vehicle operated in a turn, it has a greater potential for rollover compared to an identical vehicle with a low center of gravity.
questions.explanation:
The higher the center of gravity, the greater the potential for a rollover 
during a turn.

questions.question: One of the problems associated with safety inspections is:
options: Control methods may not be economical
Hazards are allowed to accumulate between inspections
Lost time cases cannot be detected
questions.explanation:
A safety inspection usually causes a surge in safety and health activities. 
However, after a period of time hazards are allowed to accumulate until the next inspection.

questions.question: One of the disadvantages to an external safety inspection is:
questions.explanation:
An external safety audit is normally conducted by outside consultants 
hired by the organization. The major advantage of an external audit is its "objectivity." The disadvantages include 
lack of familiarity of the auditor with the facility and the personnel, high cost, and the possibility of no or minimum 
follow-up.

questions.question: During a safety inspection of your facility, you have discovered an unsafe act being committed by an employee. Your best course of action is:
options: To stop the unsafe act and instruct how the job can be done safely.
To report an unsafe act to employee's supervisor.
questions.explanation:
A sound safety management program sets forth provisions to stop unsafe 
acts as soon as they are discovered and to provide adequate training.

questions.question: Accident causes can be classified into basic, indirect, and direct causes. An unsafe act by an employee which results in an accident is an example of which one of the following accident causes?
questions.explanation:
Poor management is an example of basic causes of accidents. Unsafe 
acts or unsafe conditions are indirect causes of accidents. These can lead to direct causes of an accident such as 
unplanned release of energy which can result in fatality, injury, or property damage.

questions.question: There are four different types of machine guarding: fixed, adjustable, interlocked, and self-adjusting. Which of the following is NOT an advantage of fixed guards?
options: Can be constructed to suit many applications
Can provide a high level of protection
Adjustment and repair may require removal
questions.explanation:
Statement (d) is one of the limitations of fixed guards. Another limitation 
is the possibility of interference with visibility. 
Adjustable guards provide an adjustable barrier. One of the advantages of this type of machine guarding is that it 
can be constructed to suit many specific applications and stock sizes. Adjustable guards can have the disadvantage 
of allowing employees' hands to enter the danger zone, may require high maintenance, and they may be made 
ineffective by the operator. 
Interlocked guards turn off the power to the machine if they are removed or pushed out of position. The openings of 
a self-adjusting guard are determined by the movement of the stock. As the operator moves the stock into the 
danger area, the guard is pushed away, providing an opening which is only large enough to admit the stock. After 
the stock is removed, the guard returns to the rest position.

questions.question: _________ machine guards shut off or disengage power and prevent the machine from starting when the guard is opened.
questions.explanation:
Self-adjusting guards provide barriers that move according to the size of 
the stock entering the danger area.

questions.question: OSHA requires [1910.212(a)(1)] that the employer must provide one or more methods of machine guarding to protect the operator and other employees from hazardous mechanical motion or action. Which of the following IS NOT an example of hazardous mechanical motion or action requiring machine guarding?
questions.explanation:
The problem of vibrating parts usually does not require guarding and is 
solved using vibration dampers.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true in regard to Class A hard hats?
options: These helmets are for general services.
They provide good impact protection but limited voltage protection.
They are used mainly in mining, building construction, shipbuilding, lumbering, and manufacturing.
They provide limited impact protection but good voltage protection.
questions.explanation:
These helmets provide very limited voltage protection and are not 
suitable for electrical work.

questions.question: Which of the following statements IS NOT true in regard to Class B hard hats?
options: Choose Class B helmets if your employees are engaged in electrical work.
They protect against falling objects and high-voltage shock and burns.
The shells are water resistant and slow burning.
They do not have to meet ANSI standards.
questions.explanation:
Class B hard hats must meet ANSI standards. Class B hard hats fall into 
two different categories: ANSI Type I and ANSI Type II. Type I provides protection from electric shock and falling 
objects. Type II provides protection from falling and flying objects and electric shock and burns.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true in regard to Class C hard hats?
options: They protect against falling objects and high-voltage shock and burns.
questions.explanation:
Class C helmets are designed for comfort. They offer limited head 
protection. They protect workers against fixed objects but do not protect against falling objects or electric shock.

questions.question: Which of the following colors are used on the coverings of grounded conductors?
questions.explanation: Conductors that are grounded have a white or natural gray covering.

questions.question: Many combustible gas devices burn the contaminants catalytically. This causes an increase in temperature, resulting in an increase in the resistance of the filament. Which of the following BEST describes the principle used in these devices?
questions.explanation:
The instruments are built on the Wheatstone bridge principle. As the 
temperature increases, the resistance of the filament also increases, causing a decrease in current flow.

questions.question: Which of the following statements in NOT true in regard to cathodic protection?
options: It is used to control the corrosion of a metal surface
It makes the metal surface the cathode of an electrochemical cell
It makes the metal surface the anode of an electrochemical cell
It connects protected metal to a more easily corroded sacrificial metal acting as the anode
questions.explanation:
In this technique, the sacrificial metal corrodes instead of the protected 
metal. One of the major uses of cathodic protection is protecting underground storage tanks against corrosion.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding a ground fault circuit interrupter (GFCI)?
options: It is a fast-acting circuit breaker designed to shut off electric power in the event of a ground fault.
It can shut off power in as little as 1/40 of a second.
It works by comparing the amount of current going to and returning from the equipment along circuit conductors.
It protects the user from line contact hazards.
questions.explanation:
GFCI does not protect against line to line contact. For example, GFCI 
does not protect a person holding two hot wires, a hot and a neutral wire in each hand, or contacting an overhead 
power line.

questions.question: CAD is an acronym for:
questions.explanation:
CAD is an acronym for Computer Aided Design. CAD systems are 
generally comprised of both software and hardware. This combination allows the design of everything from a bridge 
to a ship. Generally, CAD systems also require a high quality monitor to display graphics. Nowadays, CAD software 
is readily available for purchase.

questions.question: The two most common software packages used in occupational health and safety departments are:
questions.explanation:
Word processing and database management is the two most commonly 
used software in occupational safety and health departments.

questions.question: The principle of receiving value (i.e. quality, safety, etc.) for an original purchase of a product is called:
questions.explanation:
The old concept was called caveat emptor or "buyer beware." By 
statutory and common laws, this principle turned into caveat venditor or "seller beware."

questions.question: If a product fails to meet a warranty, then:
options: The manufacturer can be held liable
The consumer must prove unreasonable risk to receive compensation
The consumer must prove negligence in design to receive compensation
questions.explanation:
In this case the manufacturer can be held liable. All consumer products 
are also covered under the concept of strict liability. This means that the manufacturer is responsible for damages 
caused as a result of a defect in his products; no proof of negligence on the part of the consumer is needed.

questions.question: A retailer has made an oral promise concerning a product's life expectancy. Which one of the following best describes this concept?
questions.explanation:
An express warranty exists when statements in regard to certain 
performance characteristics of a product are made either in writing or orally.
