questions.question: You are a CSP working for a midsize company. During a routine inspection, you observe a few minor infractions. Which of the following courses of action would you undertake?
options: Talk to the employees involved and instruct them on how to do the job safely.
Issue a written warning to employees involved and send a copy to the Human Resources department.
Issue a written warning to the employees involved and send a copy to the supervisor.
questions.explanation:
It must be understood that the role of a CSP within an organization is 
advisory in nature both to management and staff. In this case, the best course of action is to notify the supervisor of 
the infractions and request for corrective action.

questions.question: In database systems design, SQL is an acronym for:
questions.explanation:
SQL is an acronym for Structured Query Language. SQL is a 
programming language that is commonly used to request, add, update, or delete data in a database.

questions.question: CAD/CAM is an acronym for which of the following?
questions.explanation:
CAD/CAM is an acronym for Computer Aided Design/Computer Aided 
Manufacturing.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The internet is a network of public and private networks.
The intranet is a private network that is generally inaccessible to outsiders.
The extranet is an intranet, which allows access to outsiders who are permitted.
In peer-to-peer computer networks, the capability of the workstations is generally the same.
questions.explanation:
Statements (a), (b), and (c) are correct. Statement (d) is not. 
The Internet is a worldwide system of interconnected computers that serves private, public, academic, business, 
and government networks. 
An intranet is a private network that usually belongs to a company. An intranet's site looks and acts like any other 
website, except that the firewall surrounding it provides access to only authorized individuals, usually the company's 
employees. 
An extranet, like an intranet, is a private network. It securely shares information with other parties such as a 
company's customers and vendors. An extranet can be looked at as part of a company's intranet in that it provides 
access to authorized users outside the company.

questions.question: In order to find something in the World Wide Web, one must know its URL. URL is an acronym for:
questions.explanation:
URL is an acronym for Uniform Resource Locator. This is a special code 
that tells the browser what kind of site you are visiting. All URLs start with http://. 
URLs are also known as web addresses. In most browsers they are displayed at the top of the page inside an 
address bar.

questions.question: The address of web sites starts with HTTP. This is an acronym for:
questions.explanation:
HTTP is an acronym for Hyper Text Transport Protocol. HTTP is an 
application protocol that is used for distributed hypermedia information systems. This protocol is the most critical in 
communicating data on the World Wide Web.

questions.question: The most basic features of a web browser include the capability to display all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
RealNetworks RealPlayer is a plug-in that can be downloaded from the 
Internet and be used with the web browser. It plays audio and video content in RealMedia format.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding Adobe Acrobat, which can be downloaded from the Internet?
options: Plays flash presentations, containing animations and vector graphics
Displays files in its native Portable Document Format (PDF)
Plays macromedia graphics and multimedia audio
Plays audio and video content in RealMedia format
questions.explanation:
Statement (a) is a characteristic of Adobe Flash Player. Statement (c) is 
a characteristic of Adobe Shockwave, and statement (d) is a characteristic of RealNetworks RealPlayer.

questions.question: Which of the following software can be used as a tool for reading and composing E-mail?
questions.explanation:
SeaMonkey Composer is a simple HTML editor for creating and 
modifying web pages. Mozilla Firefox allows you to display web pages and a variety of web content. Microsoft 
Meeting Space lets you connect to audio, video, and chat conferences on the Internet.

questions.question: Most E-mail programs give the option of creating mail in either plain text or HTML formats. The advantage of creating mail in HTML format is that one can add:
questions.explanation:
(a), (b), and (c) are all advantages of creating E-mail in HTML. Compared 
to plain text, HTML can be customized much more to personal or business needs. This is a major advantage 
because it provides the capability of conveying pictures, colors, emphasized text, and quotations.

questions.question: UNIX workstations are generally used for which of the following applications?
questions.explanation:
UNIX workstations are generally used for CPU-intensive applications, 
such as special effects and graphics.

questions.question: Computer networks fall into two general categories: peer-to-peer networks and client/server networks. All of the following are considered to be advantages of a peer-to-peer network EXCEPT:
options: All workstations can share the same printer.
questions.explanation:
Economy, simplicity, and sharing of hardware are all advantages of peer-
to-peer networks. Lack of centralized control is considered to be a disadvantage of this type of networks.

questions.question: All of the following statements are correct in regard to a spectrophotometer EXCEPT:
options: It can measure the transmission of liquids or solids as a function of wavelength.
It can measure absorption of liquids or solids as a function of wavelength.
The beam can be split in two: one beam that goes through a reference cell, and another beam that goes through a sample cell.
It measures the amount of ionizing radiation as a function of the intensity of radiation.
questions.explanation:
Statements (a), (b), and (c) are true in regard to a spectrophotometer. 
This instrument is not used for measuring ionizing radiation. 
Spectrophotometers measure the amount of light having a certain wavelength that passes through a medium. The 
amount of light absorbed is a measure of the concentration of solute present. For example, the concentration of a 
colored solute in a solution can be determined by the amount of light at a certain wavelength that is absorbed.

questions.question: Many web servers and file servers run on UNIX operating systems. Which of the following statements best describes this operating system?
options: UNIX is a Windows-based program developed by the Microsoft Corporation.
UNIX is an operating system by which your network is physically laid out and developed by Procom Technology.
UNIX is a multi-user, multi-tasking computer operating system. This operating system was developed by AT&T Corporation.
UNIX is a protocol that allows workstations to access Internet electronic centralized servers. This operating system was developed by the XP Corporation.
questions.explanation:
Statement (c) is a correct description of UNIX operating system. 
An operating system allows interaction with all the software and hardware on the computer. With a graphical user 
interface (GUI) such as Windows, the interaction with the computer is accomplished by using the keyboard and 
mouse. With Unix operating systems, the user has the option of using command lines as well as the GUI. 
Unix operating systems in general provide more flexibility and control as compared to Windows operating systems.

questions.question: The frequency of eye injuries in a machine shop with new machines added has been on the rise. Which of the following course of actions is the MOST appropriate?
options: Provide employees with safety glasses with side shields.
Provide employees with face shields to be worn on top of safety glasses with side shields.
Apply engineering controls and ensure that the needed personal protective equipment is used.
questions.explanation:
Every attempt must be made to solve safety problems by using 
engineering and/or administrative controls. However, if engineering and/or administrative controls cannot solve the 
problem, appropriate personal protective equipment that has been matched to the hazards must be selected and 
used.

questions.question: Use of Ground-Fault Circuit Interrupters (GFCI) is an example of which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Use of a GFCI is a good example of engineering control for loss 
prevention. Loss reduction refers to situations where a loss has already occurred and the measures try to minimize 
further losses. For example, when emergency personnel respond to an emergency, loss has occurred and the 
emergency personnel try to minimize further losses.

questions.question: According to OSHA regulations contained in 29 CFR 1910.145, all of the following are examples of safety signs EXCEPT:
options: Signs for pedestrian crossing on a public road
questions.explanation:
Signs for pedestrian crossing on a public road are DOT signs, not OSHA 
safety signs.

questions.question: Workers in many different occupations are exposed to hexavalent chromium. Calcium chromate, chromium trioxide, lead chromate, strontium chromate, and zinc chromate are known human carcinogens. Which of the following types of cancer is associated with overexposure to hexavalent chromium?
questions.explanation:
An increase in incidence of lung cancer has been observed among 
workers in industries that produce chromate and manufacture pigments containing chromate. Measurement of 
chromium in urine is used to determine the extent of exposure to chromium. Occupational exposures occur mainly 
among workers who handle pigments containing dry chromate, spray paints and coatings containing chromate, 
operate chrome plating baths, and weld or cut metals containing chromium, such as stainless steel. Stainless steel 
welding involves the greatest exposure to hexavalent chromium.

questions.question: Which of the following organizations issues health effects certification for tiles and installation materials?
options: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH)
questions.explanation:
Underwriter's laboratories issue the certification. UL was founded in 1894 
by William Henry Merrill. Today, UL provides a wide range of services such as: certification, testing, inspection, and 
auditing to mention a few.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of nanoparticles that are related to adverse health effects:
questions.explanation:
Nanoparticles are able to cross cell membranes and reach the blood and 
various organs because of their very small size. The degree of toxicity posed by nanoparticles depends on their 
chemical composition and on the composition of any chemicals absorbed onto their surfaces. Although there is little 
definitive evidence, the health effects of nanoparticles are likely to also depend on their shape.

questions.question: Which of the following can become combustible dust under specific situations?
questions.explanation:
A combustible dust is defined as any fine material that has the potential 
to catch fire and explode when mixed with air at proper concentrations. Some of these materials, such as aluminum, 
are not combustible under normal conditions, but they can catch fire and explode if the particles are the right size 
and in the right concentration.

questions.question: All of the following are examples of workplaces and industries that have potential for dust explosions EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Dusts can be created during transportation and handling, processing, 
polishing, and grinding and shaping. Dust explosion is of special concern in grain elevators, metal processing 
operations, and some food industries.

questions.question: As compared to a normal fire, dust explosion needs two additional elements known as the dust pentagon. Which of the following is one of these two additional elements?
questions.explanation:
Dispersion or suspension of particles in air and confinement of the dust 
cloud are two additional elements required for a dust cloud explosion.

questions.question: The most important concept in selection of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) is to:
options: Train workers in its proper use
Ensure that it is properly stored
questions.explanation:
Matching PPE to the hazard is the most important step in the selection 
process. Using the wrong kind of PPE can create a false sense of security and increase the probability of an 
accident.

questions.question: OSHA requires (29CFR1910.138) that whenever an employee uses his/her own PPE:
options: The employer is responsible to ensure that it is of the approved type.
The employee assumes responsibility for PPE being of the approved type but employer is responsible for its maintenance and disinfection.
OSHA requires that no employee owned PPE be used in the workplace.
questions.explanation:
When employee-owned PPE is used in the workplace, the employer is 
responsible for ensuring that it is safe and of the approved type. It is also the responsibility of the employer to 
establish adequate measures for maintenance and disinfection of PPE.

questions.question: Workers who are assigned to jobs requiring eye protection and wear prescription glasses must be provided with which of the following?
options: Safety goggles that would fit over prescription glasses
questions.explanation: Any of the actions stated would satisfy the eye protection requirement.

questions.question: Which of the following organizations provide recommended levels of illumination for different work areas?
questions.explanation:
The Illuminating Engineering Society (IES) provides recommended 
values for lighting in different industrial work areas.

questions.question: Goggles with indirect ventilation ports are most appropriate for which of the following situations?
questions.explanation:
Goggles with indirect ventilation ports do not allow entry of liquids and 
are suitable when working with corrosive chemicals.

questions.question: Hard hats must meet the requirements and specification established by which of the following organizations?
questions.explanation:
Hard hats must meet the requirements and specifications established by 
ANSI in Z89.1. These specifications have been adopted by OSHA.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding a respirator wearer in an atmosphere which is considered to be Immediately Dangerous to Life or Health (IDLH)?
options: The buddy system must be used.
The worker must be supplied with an air purifying respirator.
A closed loop SCBA with constant flow regulator is required.
An open loop SCBA with variable flow regulator is required.
questions.explanation:
In IDLH atmospheres buddy system must be used. This means that the 
respirator wearer must be watched by another person who is in a position to provide help in an emergency.

questions.question: Air purifying respirators remove the contaminants from air primarily by which of the following mechanisms?
questions.explanation:
Air purifying respirators remove the contaminants from air on the bed of a 
solid. Removal of a component of a gaseous mixture on a solid is called adsorption. "Absorption" refers to the 
process of removing one or more components of a gas mixture into a liquid.

questions.question: Air purifying respirators must not be used in which of the following situations?
options: Atmospheres containing less than 19.5% oxygen by volume
In atmospheres where contaminants cannot be detected by odor or taste at levels below PEL or TLV
questions.explanation:
Air purifying respirators do not have their own oxygen source and should 
not be used in oxygen deficient atmospheres (less than 19.5%). Breakthrough will occur very quickly in an IDLH 
atmosphere. In the absence of test data, a cartridge respirator cannot be used in an atmosphere where the 
contaminant of interest does not have a warning property such as odor or taste which allows the user to know that 
breakthrough has taken place. The odor threshold must be lower than PEL or Action Level.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding a Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA)?
options: Open circuit SCBA's have a relatively long operating time as compared to closed circuit SCBA's.
Open circuit SCBA's remove CO2 and water from exhaled air.
Positive pressure SCBA's should be used in IDLH conditions.
Closed circuit negative pressure SCBA provide the highest level of protection in IDLH conditions.
questions.explanation:
Positive pressure SCBA's provide a positive pressure inside the face 
mask at all times. This would eliminate the possibility of slightest leaks from the contaminated atmosphere into the 
face mask. This type of respirator is most effective in atmospheres which are considered to be Immediately 
Dangerous to Life or Health (IDLH) or oxygen deficient.

questions.question: Which of the following test methods can be used to check the fit of a respirator?
questions.explanation:
In qualitative test a harmless agent is injected into the air and the user 
uses his/her sense to detect any leaks. In a quantitative test, an instrument is placed inside face-mask which 
actually measures the amount of leakage. In positive pressure, the user exhales into the face-mask and it should 
remain bulged; in negative pressure the face mask should remain collapsed when inhalation takes place.

questions.question: According to OSHA regulations, a Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA) must be inspected at least once every _________ days and after each use:
questions.explanation:
OSHA requires that SCBA's be inspected at least once every 30 days 
and after each use (29CFR 1910.133).

questions.question: Butyl rubber has a solubility parameter of 16. Gloves made of butyl rubber are most effective against which of the following chemicals.
options: A chemical with a solubility parameter of 18
A chemical with a solubility parameter of 28
A chemical with a solubility parameter of 16
A chemical with a solubility parameter of 47
questions.explanation:
The concept of solubility parameter is the extension of the old rule that 
"like dissolves like." The closer the values of the solubility parameters of two chemicals, the more soluble they are in 
each other. In this case, a chemical with solubility parameter of 47 is the least soluble in butyl rubber with a solubility 
parameter of 16.

questions.question: OSHA's Process Safety Management standard applies to all of the following EXCEPT:
options: A process which involves a chemical at or above specified threshold quantities.
A process which involves a flammable liquid on site in one location, in a quantity of 10,000 lb or more.
Hydrocarbon fuels used solely for workplace consumption for fuel.
A process which involves a flammable gas on site in one location, in a quantity of 10,000 lb or more.
questions.explanation:
Hydrocarbon fuels such as propane used solely for workplace 
consumption are exempt from this OSHA standard.

questions.question: The Process Safety Management of highly hazardous chemicals is contained in:
questions.explanation:
The process safety management standard is contained in 29 CFR 
1910.119. Appendix C of 29 CFR 1910.119 contains non-mandatory compliance for process safety management.

questions.question: All of the following are exempt from Process Safety Management standard EXCEPT:
options: A process, which involves a flammable gas in one location in quantities of 10,000 lb or more.
questions.explanation:
This OSHA standard does not apply to retail facilities, oil or gas well- 
drilling or servicing operations, or normally unoccupied remote facilities. This standard applies to any process which 
involves a flammable liquid or gas, as defined in OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard in 29 CFR 1910.1200 
(c), on site in one location, in a quantity of 10,000 lb or more.

questions.question: Under PSM standard an "atmospheric tank" means:
options: A tank, which is designed to operate from atmospheric pressure to 0.5 psig.
A tank, which is designed to operate under atmospheric pressure.
A tank, which is designed to operate at or below atmospheric pressures.
A tank, which is designed to operate between atmospheric pressure and 28 psig.
questions.explanation:
"Atmospheric tank" means a storage tank, which has been designed to 
operate at pressures from atmospheric through 0.5 psig (pounds per square inch gauge). It must be pointed out that 
pressure can be expressed in two different scales, absolute pressure scale and gauge pressure scale. The 
relationship between these scales is: Absolute pressure = Gauge pressure + Atmospheric pressure

questions.question: The term "hot work" under PSM standard includes all of the following operations EXCEPT:
options: Any operation, which involves temperatures exceeding 1000 degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation:
The term "hot work" means work involving electric or gas welding, 
cutting, brazing, or similar flame or spark-producing operations.

questions.question: For existing equipment designed and constructed many years ago with the codes and standard available at that time and no longer in general use, as part of the "process safety information" package of the PSM standard, the employer must do all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Document the codes and standards that were used.
Change the design or install new equipment in compliance with present codes and standards
Document that the design and construction are still suitable for the intended use.
Document that the testing, inspection and operation are still suitable for the intended use.
questions.explanation:
The information pertaining to process equipment design must be 
documented. In other words, what were the codes and standards relied on to establish good engineering practice. 
For existing equipment designed and constructed many years ago in accordance with the codes and standards 
available at that time and no longer in use today, the employer must document which codes and standards were 
used and that the design and construction along with the testing, inspection and operation are still suitable for the 
intended use. Where the process technology requires a design which departs from the applicable codes and 
standards, the employer must document that the design and construction is suitable for the intended purpose.

questions.question: Selection of a "process hazard analysis" methodology or technique will be influenced by all of the following factors EXCEPT:
options: The amount of existing knowledge about the process.
The size and complexity of the process.
Is it a new process or one which has been changed frequently by the inclusion of innovative features?
questions.explanation:
Selection of a PHA methodology or technique will be influenced by many 
factors including: • The amount of existing knowledge about the process. • Is it a process that has been operated for 

a long period of time with little or no innovation and extensive experience has been generated with its use? • Is it a 
new process or one which has been changed frequently by the inclusion of innovative features? • The size and 
complexity of the process.

questions.question: Process chemicals information is part of the "process safety information" package. Which of the following IS NOT expected to be included in the process chemicals information?
questions.explanation:
The information to be compiled about the chemicals, including process 
intermediates, needs to be comprehensive enough for an accurate assessment of the fire and explosion 
characteristics, reactivity hazards, the safety and health hazards to workers, and the corrosion and erosion effects 
on the process equipment and monitoring tools. Current safety data sheet (SDS) information can be used to help 
meet this requirement which must be supplemented with process chemistry information including runaway reaction 
and over pressure hazards if applicable.

questions.question: Under "process technology information" part of the "process safety information" package, employers are encouraged to use diagrams, which help users understand the process. Which of the following IS NOT one of the three general categories of the recommended diagrams?
questions.explanation:
The 3 general categories of recommended diagrams are BLOCK Flow 
Diagrams (BFD), Process Flow Diagrams (PFD), and Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs).

questions.question: OSHA's process safety management standard does not apply to "normally unoccupied remote facilities." Which of the following statements BEST describes this term?
options: A facility which is at least 80- miles away from all cities with a population of 5,000 or more.
A facility, which is operated, maintained or serviced by employees who visit the facility only periodically to check its operation and to perform necessary operating or maintenance tasks.

A facility which is operated, maintained or serviced by employees who visit the facility no more than once every 6 months to check its operation and to perform necessary operating or maintenance tasks.
questions.explanation:
"Normally unoccupied remote facility" means a facility which is operated, 
maintained or serviced by employees who visit the facility only periodically to check its operation and to perform 

necessary operating or maintenance tasks. No employees are permanently stationed at the facility. Facilities 
meeting this definition are not contiguous with, and must be geographically remote from all other buildings, 
processes or persons.

questions.question: Under OSHA's process safety management standard, the term "highly hazardous chemical" means:
options: A substance possessing toxic, reactive, flammable, or explosive properties and specified by the standard.
A substance possessing toxic, reactive, flammable, or explosive properties and specified by the standard and also listed under TSCA.
Toxic chemicals with an LD50 of less than 5000 mg/kg, which are specified by the standard.
Hazardous chemicals listed by OSHA under Hazard Communication Standard (29 CFR 1910.1200).
questions.explanation:
"Highly hazardous chemical" means a substance possessing toxic, 
reactive, flammable, or explosive properties and specified by this standard.

questions.question: Which of the following IS NOT an element of process safety management as defined by OSHA?
questions.explanation:
The 14 Elements of process safety management as defined by OSHA are 
listed below. Hazardous waste management is not an element of the process safety management standard. (a) 
Employee participation. (b) Process safety information. (c) Process hazard analysis. (d) Operating procedures. (e) 
Training. (f) Contractors. (g) Pre-startup safety review. (h) Mechanical integrity. (i) Hot work permit. (j) Management 
of change. (k) Incident investigation. (l) Emergency planning and response. (m) Compliance audits. (n) Trade 
secrets.

questions.question: The "employee participation" element of the process safety management standard is required under which of the following legislative acts?
questions.explanation:
Section 304 of the Clean Air Act Amendments states that employers are 
to consult with their employees and their representatives regarding the employer's efforts in the development and 
implementation of the process safety management program elements and hazard assessments. Section 304 also 
requires employers to train and educate their employees and to inform affected employees of the findings from 
incident investigations required by the process safety management program.

questions.question: Which of the following IS NOT addressed in the "process safety information" element of the process safety management standard?
questions.explanation:
Incident investigation is a separate element of the process safety 
management standard and is not part of the "process safety information" package.

questions.question: "Process technology information" is a component of the "process safety information" package required by the process safety management standard. Which of the following IS NOT expected to be included in the "process technology information"?
options: Maximum inventory limits for the process chemicals.
Limits beyond which would be considered upset conditions.
A qualitative estimate of the consequences or results of deviations from the design intent.
Determination of toxic, flammable, reactive, and explosive properties of the process chemicals.
questions.explanation:
Determination of fire and explosion characteristics, reactivity hazards, the 
safety and health hazards to workers, and the corrosion and erosion effects on the process equipment and 
monitoring tools is part of the "process chemicals information" of the "process safety information" package.

questions.question: The "employee training" element of the process safety management standard must cover all of the following areas EXCEPT:
options: Operating procedures and safe work practices.
How to interpret chemical labels and Safety Data Sheets.
Routine and non-routine work authorization activities.
questions.explanation:
Interpretation of chemical labels and SDS's is required under OSHA's 
Hazard Communication Standard (29 CFR 1910.1200). Under provisions of the process safety management 
standard all employees, including maintenance and contractor employees, involved with highly hazardous chemicals 
need to fully understand the safety and health hazards of the chemicals and processes they work with for the 
protection of themselves, their fellow employees and the citizens of nearby communities. The training must cover 
the following areas: • Operating procedures and safe work practices. • Emergency evacuation and response. • 
Safety procedures. • Routine and non-routine work authorization activities.

questions.question: The training program required under the "employee training" element of the process safety management standard must accomplish all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Develop a training center within the facility.
Define goals and objectives of the training program.
questions.explanation:
Development of a training center is not a requirement of this standard. 
The training program must accomplish the following: • Define employees to be trained. • Subjects to be covered. • 
Define goals and objectives of the training program. • Establish means to determine whether the goals and 
objectives have been achieved.

questions.question: Which of the following IS NOT true regarding the team conducting the process hazard analysis required under the process safety management standard?
options: The team needs to understand the hazard analysis methodology that is going to be used.
The team can vary in size.
The team members must have varied operational and technical backgrounds.
At least one member of the team must have a college degree from an accredited institution in a field related to the process.
questions.explanation:
Possession of a college degree in a field related to the process is not a 
requirement under this standard. The team conducting the PHA, however, needs to understand the methodology 
that is going to be used. A PHA team can vary in size from two people to a number of people with varied operational 
and technical backgrounds. The team leader needs to be fully knowledgeable in the proper implementation of the 
PHA methodology that is to be used.

questions.question: Detailed guidance on the content and application of process hazard analysis methodologies can be obtained from which of the following professional organizations?
questions.explanation:
The Center for Chemical Process Safety (CCPS) of the American 
Institute of Chemical Engineers can provide guidance on process hazard analysis methodologies.

questions.question: The acronym SOP in the process safety management standard is an abbreviation for:
questions.explanation: SOP is an acronym for Standard Operating Practices.

questions.question: Under the "operating procedures" element of the process safety management standard, the employer is required to certify that the operating procedures are accurate and current. This certification must be done:
questions.explanation: The certification must be done annually.

questions.question: Employers who use contractors to perform work in and around processes that involve highly hazardous chemicals must do all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Establish a screening process to hire contractors who can accomplish the tasks safely.
Evaluate contractor's work methods and experiences.
Ensure that the contractor employees have successfully completed the OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training.
Maintain a site injury and illness log for the contractors.
questions.explanation:
This standard does not require HAZWOPER training for contractor 
employees. HAZWOPER is covered in 29 CFR 1910.120.

questions.question: The "pre-startup safety review" component of the process safety management standard requires all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Construction of equipment are in accordance with design specifications.
Operating procedures are in place and are adequate.
A compliance audit has been conducted on the process.
questions.explanation:
Compliance audits are a separate element of the process safety 
management standard and is not required under pre-startup safety review.

questions.question: Which of the following IS NOT required under the mechanical integrity program required by process safety management standard?
options: Written procedures to maintain the ongoing integrity of process equipment.
questions.explanation:
Pre-startup safety review is a separate element of the process safety 
management standard and is not addressed under mechanical integrity.

questions.question: The "mechanical integrity" element of the process safety management standard requires that a list of process equipment and instrumentation for inclusion in the program be developed. This list must include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
A list of process equipment and instrumentation for inclusion in the 
program must be developed. This list must include pressure vessels, storage tanks, process piping, relief and vent 
systems, fire protection system components, emergency shutdown systems, alarms, interlocks, and pumps. This 
equipment list must be prioritized to denote which pieces of equipment require closer scrutiny than others.

questions.question: Determination of the MTBF for various instrumentation and equipment is helpful in creating a sound mechanical integrity program. MTBF is an acronym for:
questions.explanation: MTBF is acronym for Mean Time Between Failures.

questions.question: Which of the following IS NOT required by the "mechanical integrity" element of the process safety management standard?
questions.explanation:
Incident investigation is a separate element of process safety 
management and is not required under mechanical integrity program.

questions.question: Which of the following statements IS NOT TRUE regarding "hot work permit" required under process safety management standard?
options: The permit must document the date(s) authorized for hot work.
The permit must identify the object on which hot work is to be performed.
The permit must document that the fire prevention and protection requirements in 29 CFR 1910.152 (a) have been implemented prior to beginning the hot work operations.
The permit must be kept on file for a period of 5 years
questions.explanation:
The permit must only be kept on file until the completion of hot work 
operations.

questions.question: Under the "management of change" element of the process safety management standard, the employer is responsible to implement written procedures to manage changes. These procedures must assure that all of the following issues are addressed EXCEPT:
options: The technical basis for the proposed change.
Effect of change on compliance audits program.
questions.explanation:
Effect of change on compliance audits program is not addressed in 
"management of change" element of the process safety management.

questions.question: Which or the following statements IS NOT TRUE regarding the "investigation of incidents" element of the process safety management standard?
options: Incident investigation is the process of identifying and underlying the causes of incidents and implementing steps to prevent similar events from occurring.
A report of the findings of the incident investigation team must be shared with the local fire department.
Employers need to develop in-house capability to investigate incidents that occur in their facilities.
A team needs to be assembled and trained in the techniques of incident investigation.
questions.explanation:
This standard does not require that a report of findings of the incident 
investigation be shared with the local fire department.

questions.question: The process safety management standard requires that employers develop and implement an emergency action plan which will facilitate the prompt evacuation of employees due to an unwanted release of a highly hazardous chemical. This plan must address all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Process hazard analysis is a separate element of the process safety 
management standard and is not addressed in the emergency action plan.

questions.question: Under provisions of the process safety management standard, it is the responsibility of the employer to certify that they have evaluated compliance with the provisions of this OSHA standard. This certification must be done at least every:
questions.explanation:
It is the responsibility of the employers to certify that they have evaluated 
compliance with the provisions of this OSHA standard at least every three years to verify that the procedures and 
practices developed under the standard are adequate and are being followed.

questions.question: Under provisions of process safety management standard, the employer is responsible for developing a report of the findings of the compliance audit. Which of the following is true in regard to compliance audit report?
options: Employers must retain each report for a period of at least 3 years.
Employers must retain each report for a period of at least 2 years.
Employers must retain the two (2) most recent compliance audit reports.
Employers must retain each report for a period of at least 4 years.
questions.explanation: Employers must retain the two (2) most recent compliance audit reports.

questions.question: Which of the following IS NOT required by the "compliance audits" element of the process safety management standard?
options: The compliance audit must be conducted by at least one person knowledgeable in the process.
A report of findings of the audit must be developed.
Employers must retain the two (2) most recent compliance audit reports.
Employers must develop complete and accurate written information concerning process chemicals, process technology, and process equipment.
questions.explanation:
These issues are addressed in the "process safety information" element 
of the process safety management standard.

questions.question: Which of the following statements IS NOT TRUE in regard to "trade secrets" element of process safety management standard?
options: Employers must make all information necessary to comply available to those persons responsible for compiling the process safety information and to those assisting in the development of the process hazard analysis without regard to possible trade secret status of such information.

Employers must make all information necessary to comply available to those persons responsible for developing the operating procedures and those involved in incident investigations without regard to possible trade secret status of such information.
The employer cannot require the persons to whom the information is made available to enter into confidentiality agreements not to disclose the information.

Employers must make all information necessary to comply available to those persons responsible for developing emergency planning and response and compliance audits without regard to possible trade secret status of such.
questions.explanation:
The employer can ask the parties involved to enter into a confidentiality 
agreement not to disclose the information.

questions.question: Which of the following acts is considered to be "distracted driving"?
questions.explanation:
An estimated 1 in 4 car crashes involve cell phone use. According to the 
United States Department of Transportation, text messaging while driving creates a crash risk 23 times higher than 
driving while not distracted. Despite these statistics, more than 37% of drivers have admitted to sending or receiving 
text messages while driving, and 18% admit doing so regularly.

questions.question: The Department of Transportation requires that every commercial motor vehicle be inspected. DOT also requires that the original or copy of the inspection report be retained for a period of _________ from the date of inspection:
questions.explanation:
The inspection report must be retained by the motor carrier or other entity 
who is responsible for the inspection for a period of 14 months from the date of inspection.

questions.question: Automatic braking technology used in automobiles uses sensors to detect other vehicles or obstacles. Which of the following is NOT a type of sensor used in this technology?
questions.explanation:
Sensors to detect other vehicles or obstacles can include radar, video, 
infrared, ultra-sonic or other technologies. GPS sensors can detect fixed dangers such as approaching stop signs 
through a location database.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true in regard to Anti-lock Braking System (ABS)?
options: ABS allows the wheels on a motor vehicle to maintain tractive contact with the road surface.
ABS can significantly decrease braking distance on loose surfaces.
Recent versions of ABS not only prevent wheel lock but also electronically control the front-to-rear brake bias.
ABS prevents the wheels from ceasing rotation and avoids uncontrolled skidding.
questions.explanation:
Anti-lock braking system (ABS) is an automobile safety system that 
allows the wheels on a motor vehicle to maintain tractive contact with the road surface according to driver inputs 
while braking, preventing the wheels from locking up (ceasing rotation) and avoiding uncontrolled skidding. 
ABS generally offers improved vehicle control and decreases stopping distances on dry and slippery surfaces for 
many drivers; however, on loose surfaces like gravel or snow-covered pavement, ABS can significantly increase 
braking distance, although still improving vehicle control.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true in regard to Vehicular Accident Reconstruction (VAR)?
options: It is the scientific process investigating, analyzing, and drawing conclusions about the causes and events during a vehicle collision.
The laws of physics and engineering principles are the basis for analysis.
Results from accident reconstruction can be useful in developing recommendations for making roads and highways safer.
questions.explanation:
Vehicular accident reconstruction is the scientific process of investigating, 
analyzing, and drawing conclusions about the causes and events during a vehicle collision. Reconstruction 
personnel are employed to conduct in-depth collision analysis and reconstruction to identify the collision causation 

and contributing factors in different types of collisions, including the role of the driver(s), vehicle(s), roadway and the 
environment. The laws of physics and engineering principles such as the conservation of linear momentum, work-
energy methods, and kinematics are the basis for these analysis and may make use of software to calculate useful 
quantities. 
Results from accident reconstructions are also useful in developing recommendations for making roads and 
highways safer, as well as improving safety aspects of motor vehicle designs.

questions.question: Pressure relief systems use which of the following to reduce or depressurize a system:
options: Comparing the measured value to a set point to generate an error
Acting on a final control element to reduce the pressure or depressurize the system
questions.explanation:
Any automatic control system must first measure the parameter to be 
controlled. The measured value is then compared to a set point value to generate an error. The generated error 
(deviation from the set point) acts on a final control element such as a valve which is loaded with a spring. The 
spring causes the valve to open in case of excessive pressure.

questions.question: In order to accurately conduct noise measurements, sound level meters should be calibrated:
options: Before, during, and after each use.
questions.explanation: Statement (d) ensures accurate noise measurements.

questions.question: Noise level measurements in a machine shop indicate that the TWA in an 8-hour shift exceed the allowable limits. Management decides to reduce the exposure to four hours by job rotation which in turn brings the exposure down to allowable limits. This is an example of:
questions.explanation:
Engineering controls reduce the hazards permanently, and in many 
cases, eliminate the need for personal protective equipment (PPE). An example of engineering control in this case 
would be to place the worker in an enclosure to minimize exposure to excessive noise.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about confined spaces?
options: Have toxic chemicals in their atmosphere
Have limited means for entry or exit
Must be equipped with a rescue ladder
questions.explanation:
A confined space has limited or restricted means for entry or exit and is 
not designed for continuous occupancy. Examples of confined spaces include tanks, vessels, silos, etc.

questions.question: In order to represent the real-world use of hearing protection devices, ANSI recommends that the manufacturer's claim for noise reduction:
questions.explanation:
ANSI recommends that the manufacturer's claim for noise reduction of 
earmuff hearing protection devices be reduced by 40% to represent the actual noise reduction in real-world work 
situations.

questions.question: There are four classes of lasers. Which of the following is true for class 1 lasers?
options: Non-hazardous under normal conditions of use
Capable of ionizing the material through which it flows
Capable of adversely affecting the DNA
questions.explanation:
Class 1 lasers are considered to be non-hazardous unless viewed 
through magnifiers.

questions.question: Which of the following personal protective equipment (PPE) should be worn when working with electricity?
options: Safety glasses and insulated gloves & clothing.
Class B hard hat and insulated gloves & clothing.
Tools that are properly grounded and insulated gloves & clothing.
Non-conducting ladder and insulated gloves & clothing
questions.explanation:
Class B hard hats provide protection against electric shock and must 
meet ANSI standards. Class B hard hats and insulated gloves & clothing must be used when working with 
electricity. The glove rating must match with the work to be performed. Not all gloves can be used to prevent electric 
shock. Ladders and tools are not personal protective equipment.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an active safety device?
questions.explanation:
Active Safety includes set of safety features which reduce the chances of 
an accident or collision in the first place. However, the airbags, seatbelts, and others safety features come into play 
during an accident. Hence, they are called the passive safety systems.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Underwriter's Laboratories (UL)?
options: Sets standards for different product categories and tests products to make sure they meet the standards.
UL approval is required by law.
UL is part of the U.S. Department of Commerce.
questions.explanation:
UL approval is not legally required. It's only common because many large 
companies will not buy equipment that has not passed UL's safety tests. UL is not part of any government agencies 
and is a private safety testing organization. On January 1, 2012, Underwriters Laboratories transformed from a non-
profit organization to a for-profit company in the U.S.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the basic strategy of a safe system approach for road traffic safety?
options: To ensure that in the event of a crash, the impact energies remain below the threshold likely to produce either death or serious injury.
To apply fault tree analysis to identify and eliminate the events that can lead to an accident.
To ensure that the airbags are properly designed and can absorb the force generated as a result of a crash.
questions.explanation:
The basic strategy of a Safe System approach is to ensure that in the 
event of a crash, the impact energies remain below the threshold likely to produce either death or serious injury. 
This threshold will vary from crash scenario to crash scenario, depending upon the level of protection offered to the 
road users involved. For example, the chances of survival for an unprotected pedestrian hit by a vehicle diminish 

rapidly at speeds greater than 30 km/h, whereas for a properly restrained motor vehicle occupant the critical impact 
speed is 50 km/h (for side impact crashes) and 70 km/h (for head-on crashes).

questions.question: A simple definition for hazard, as it applies to system safety, is:
options: A dangerous condition which can interfere with the orderly progress of an activity
questions.explanation:
potential to do harm is the simple and abbreviated version of the definition of 
"hazard." More formally, a hazard is "a potential condition, or set of conditions, either 
internal and/or external to a system, which when activated by a stimulus (set of events or 
conditions that transforms a hazard from its potential state to one that causes harm to the 
system) or series of events which culminate in a loss (accident)."

questions.question: Of the following, which is the LEAST effective way for a manager to maximize his or her safety program?
questions.explanation:
Common elements to maximize a safety program include: written policies, supervisor 
training, auditing, investigation of all hazards and accidents, and formation of safety 
committees. Staff meetings can be on any schedule that allows you to reach your goals.

questions.question: A procedure to make a job safer by identifying hazards in each step of the job and developing measures to counteract those hazards is a:
questions.explanation: A job safety analysis examines job hazards during each step of the job.

questions.question: What is a JSA?
options: A procedure of reviewing methods, hazards, and safety
A private company well-recognized by safety practitioners
questions.explanation:
A job safety analysis is a written procedure for reviewing job methods, uncovering 
hazards, and recommending safe procedures.

questions.question: Which of these is an essential step in performing a JSA?
options: Break the job down into discreet steps
Formally identify the hazards in each discreet step
questions.explanation:
The actual steps in a JSA are to identify the job, break the job down into steps, 
identify hazards, and determine how to control the hazards.

questions.question: Military contractors for weapons research played a major role in developing:
options: Event tree and fault tree analysis
questions.explanation:
Event tree and fault tree analyses were developed for weapons systems in the 1950's 
and 1960's.

questions.question: The industry where system safety techniques first were widely used was the:
questions.explanation:
The aerospace industry developed the basic format of system safety. The government 
contracts issued to these companies required that systems safety be addressed in a 
quantitative manner. Military specifications have been written concerning system safety.

questions.question: The industry where system safety techniques first were widely used was the:
questions.explanation:
The aerospace industry developed the basic format of system safety. The government 
contracts issued to these companies required that systems safety be addressed in a 
quantitative manner. Military specifications have been written concerning system safety.
questions.exclusion_reason: Identical question and choices; retained d2-b-255

questions.question: Risk-based inspection of pressure vessels involves:
options: Performing specific non-destructive examinations (NDEs) on specific intervals to understand the pressure vessel's current condition and to predict how the pressure vessel will degrade over the next inspection interval
Performing the specific ASME-required pressure vessel tests
Performing the specific OSHA-require pressure vessel tests
Determining whether a high-risk inspection is require based on the age of the pressure vessel and the vessel's service
questions.explanation:
Risk-based inspection (RBI) is a strategy gaining ground that considers the holistic 
effect of pressure vessel service against prescriptive requirements for pressure vessel safety. 
Sometimes the results of an RBI program recommend more frequent inspection intervals than 
are required by ASME, and sometimes the results of the RBI program recommend less 
frequent intervals. In many cases, an RBI program recommends tests in addition to those 
required by codes and regulations.

questions.question: In the context of reliability-centered maintenance (RCM), what is a task selection guide?
options: A guide developed to help choose appropriate maintenance tasks based on the service of the equipment
A guide that describes the intervals between maintenance tasks
A guide that describes the actual maintenance tasks to perform on equipment
questions.explanation:
RCM is a method to define an appropriate maintenance strategy based on the 
criticality of the equipment and the effectiveness of maintenance tasks to produce acceptable 
reliability performance. A task selection guide is developed to define the actual maintenance 
tasks and their intervals based on the type of service of the equipment. This information helps 
the maintenance and operations professionals to choose maintenance tasks at appropriate 
intervals.

questions.question: Why would the following types of analyses be routinely conducted? A) Vibration analysis B) Lubricant analysis C) Thermographic analysis
options: To determine how rotating equipment failed
To determine whether additional maintenance is needed on rotating equipment
To predict the day when rotating equipment will fail
To evaluate the overhaul of rotating equipment
questions.explanation:
Though any of these could be true, these types of condition monitoring tasks are 
typically associated with reliability-centered maintenance and help maintenance professionals 
determine when more extensive maintenance is needed on rotating equipment.

questions.question: What is meant when a system is said to be "two fault tolerant?"
options: The system will fail when it sustains two independent failures.
The system will fail when it sustains three independent failures.
The system is designed to tolerate two independent failures and still operate.
The system is designed to tolerate three independent failures and still operate.
questions.explanation:
Fault-tolerance is a method of designing equipment to sustain one or more 
independent failures and still operate (or be able to transition into a fail-safe mode). In this 
case, the system is designed to sustain two independent failures and still function. Fault 
tolerance has nothing to do with when the system will fail (i.e., the system may sustain more 
than three independent failures and still function).

questions.question: The primary reason for an accident investigation is to:
options: Provide OSHA with the accident facts
Prepare insurance forms to recover losses
Correct the conditions that caused the accident
questions.explanation:
The main purpose of an accident investigation is to identify the reason for the 
accident and correct it.

questions.question: A Gantt chart is used in manufacturing to:
questions.explanation:
Gantt charts show how long each production process should take and when it should 
take place. It is widely used in project scheduling.

questions.question: The most appropriate way to display critical quantitative data necessary for an operator to make a decision would be to use a:
questions.explanation:
Of these four choices, the most appropriate way to display critical quantitative data 
would be to use a printer. There are better ways than a printer; however, of the choices 
offered, printing critical quantitative data is the best.

questions.question: Laboratory quality control samples control which type of error?
questions.explanation:
These quality control samples include spiked samples and blanks. This keeps the 
instrument in calibration during the analytical series. Equipment errors are systematic errors.

questions.question: Evaluation of safety and health program effectiveness is based on:
questions.explanation:
Sometimes, attempts to control accidents and their consequences can best be 
described as trial and error, chiefly because adequate measures of the effectiveness of 
controls do not exist in practice. Controls begin with quantifiable criteria measures. The 
degree to which accident control (the underlying purpose of a safety and health program) is 
possible is a function of the adequacy of the measures used to identify the type and 
magnitude of potential injury-producing situations. To do this effectively, a variety of 
quantitative measures are needed.

questions.question: Of the following, what is the greatest benefit to using a computer to process historical, safety-related data (accidents, injuries, illnesses, etc.)?
options: The computer can quickly perform complicated math and generate useful trend data and analyses
The computer can easily generate reports of high quality and consistency for management use
The computer can maintain the names and locations of supervisors for efficient incident report notification
The computer can distribute reports electronically for faster dissemination to employees
questions.explanation:
Though computers clearly assist in all of these areas, its ability to do complicated 
math for trend analyses allows the safety practitioner to rapidly identify trends and address 
these trends with the relevant supervisors and managers.

questions.question: In any study involving a statistical analysis, the main focus is on sets of numerical data. The entire set of data from which your data came is called the:
questions.explanation:
The sample is what you take. You hope (and assume) that your sample is 
representative of the population from which it was drawn.

questions.question: Air sampling data are log normally distributed. To analyze air sampling data using a t- test one must:
options: Use the log of the concentration
Make no changes to use the t-test
questions.explanation:
A t-test is used with a normal distribution. To analyze log normally distributed data, 
one must convert the air sampling data to logarithms to use the t-test. Converting to 
logarithms should result in a normal distribution.

questions.question: Which of the following components are not specifically required in a process hazard analysis? A. Facility inspection procedures B. Facility siting C. Human factors D. The hazards of the process E. An assessment of the worst-case release into the environment of the covered process materials F. The identity of engineering and administrative controls for specific process hazards G. Consequences of failures of engineering controls H. Consequences of failures of administrative controls
questions.explanation:
These items are not specifically required to be assessed in a process hazard analysis; 
however, depending upon the actual analysis, these items may come up.

questions.question: When you are interviewing a person associated with a recent high-consequence incident, what fundamental law of human behavior must you consider at all times?
options: The person being interviewed will tell you what he or she views is in his or her best interests.
The person being interviewed can be subpoenaed to provide you any information you think he or she is hiding.
The person being interviewed will lie to you if you hit upon critical information.
The person being interviewed will only cooperate in the presence of an attorney or other representative.
questions.explanation:
Though the other items may be true from time to time, when conducting an incident 
investigation, remember that the person being interviewed will likely describe things that he 
or she perceives is in her best interest to discuss. This means that if the person being 
interviewed believes that the incident investigation is in his or her best interests, the 
interviewer will likely obtain the information sought. If the person being interviewed believes 
that job reprisals, legal action, or other adverse things will occur, the quality of the 
information obtained during an interview will likely be degraded.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST method for conducting interviews associated with an incident investigation?
options: One interviewer and one witness in a room with audio recording
Three interviewers and one witness in a room
One interviewer and three witnesses in a room
One interviewer and one witness in a room
questions.explanation:
Audio and video recording should always be avoided as this will typically make the 
witness nervous and less likely to be fully open. Having three interviewers is intimidating to 
the witness. Interviewing multiple witnesses at the same time should be avoided since 
frequently, a dominant person will speak for the group. The other witnesses with information 
will reason with themselves that other witnesses in the room have better information - 
particularly if the information is contradictory.

questions.question: A chemical process uses cryogenic liquid ethylene and other additives to produce the product. A process hazard analysis (PHA) of this process determined that a potentially dangerous situation could occur if the liquid ethylene were aligned directly with the flare (the flare is not designed for liquid ethylene). This situation would occur if Automatic Valve AV- 1 and Manual Valve MV-C were opened while liquid ethylene was flowing. The PHA team determined four options to correct this issue. Which is the most desirable corrective action?
options: Create and test a software interlock in the programmable logic controller to prevent AV-1 from opening when MV-C is open and liquid ethylene is flowing (according to Flow Controller FC-1).
Install a flare that can handle liquid ethylene at the flow rate expected when this situation occurs.
Invoke a strictly enforced administrative procedure to physically verify that MV-C is closed before the control room operator is allowed to open AV-1 when flowing liquid ethylene.

Replace AV-1 with a manual valve and require operators to strictly enforce an administrative procedure to physically verify that MV-C is closed before the operator is allowed to open the new manual valve when flowing liquid ethylene.
questions.explanation:
Though all of these corrective actions could work, the most desirable is to install a 
software interlock. A new flare would likely be an expensive solution, and administrative 
controls are always less desirable than engineering controls.

questions.question: A chemical process uses a flammable material under pressure. The flammable material is pumped into a reactor vessel (a pressure vessel). The pressure vessel is designed in accordance with ASME requirements. As a part of the process control, the safety relief valve is used to regulate pressure. When the vessel pressure is too high, the safety relief valve lifts, and a flammable mixture flows to the flare (the flare is designed to handle substantially more load than this). Which of the following statements best describes this process?
options: The process is not designed adequately because flammable materials should not be used under pressure.
The process is not designed adequately because safety relief valves should not be used to control the pressure in any process.
The process is not designed adequately because the products of the reactor should not be relieved to the flare through a safety relief valve.
questions.explanation:
It is considered poor engineering practice to control a process with its safety systems. 
Other process controls and design features should be put in place so that the safety system 
can be used to relieve the system when safety parameters have been exceeded.

questions.question: A quantitative risk analysis (QRA) was performed on a single process. The results of the analysis indicate that the process will fail causing catastrophic consequences once every 10,000 years. Your plant has seven of these processes operating at all times, and your company has 12 other plants similar to this one around the country. Also, your company has three other competitors with similar numbers of facilities with very similar processes. Assuming that the results of the QRA can be extrapolated to the other similar processes throughout the industry, how often should you expect a catastrophic accident in your company's industry related to this process?
questions.explanation:
The results of the QRA are associated with a single process. Your company has 84 
such processes (12 facilities * 7 processes/facility). Your company's competitors bring 
another 252 such processes (84 processes * 3). This is a total of 336 such processes in the 
industry. That means we can expect 336 catastrophic accidents in 10,000 years, or about one 
accident every 30 years.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: Of the following, which is a reason for avoiding quantitative analyses?
options: Probabilities calculated are often so small that many believe corrective action need not be taken
Quantitative analyses are often expensive and frequently require a team of trained professionals to perform the analyses
Quantitative analysis techniques often require the use of personnel capable in mathematical techniques and/or use of a computer
questions.explanation:
All these and more are reasons that quantitative analyses are not always accepted or 
done on product evaluations.

questions.question: The deductive technique that selects the undesired outcome (top-level event) and all possible modes of happenings is the:
questions.explanation:
In the fault tree method, an undesired event is selected and all possible happenings 
that can contribute to the event are diagrammed in the form of a tree. The branches of the tree 
are continued until independent events are reached. Probabilities are determined for the 
independent events and after simplifying the tree, both the probability of the undesired event 
and the most likely chain of events leading up to it can be computed.

questions.question: In developing a safe maintenance guide for robotic workstations, which method, useful for predicting potential injury situations, would apply to determining the combinations of human actions and equipment conditions that could lead to a robot related injury?
questions.explanation:
Fault tree analysis (FTA) begins with defining the unwanted injury event and 
proceeds by graphically constructing the sequences of events and conditions that would lead 
to that event. When failure rates and human reliability values are available, the probabilities 
of the various sequences can be computed. NIOSH Publication No 88-108 Safe Maintenance 
Guide for Robotic Workstations SADT - Structural Analysis and Design Techniques JSA - 
Job Safety Analysis FMECA - Failure Modes, Effects and Critical Analysis

questions.question: Given that incident investigations require resources (time and money), what would be an efficient method to maximize your company's ability to harvest as much information from each incident investigation that is conducted?
options: Perform a formal incident investigation on every incident regardless of complexity and consequence.
Perform a formal incident investigation on every complex incident and on every incident with a high consequence.
Trend all incidents, perform a formal incident investigation on every complex incident, on every incident with a high consequence, and on other incidents that show a trend.
Perform a formal investigation on a randomly selected set of incidents.
questions.explanation:
The key is trending. An incident can be as minor as a process upset leading to 5 
seconds of downtime to a safety-related fatality due to a highly complex sequence of events. 
No company can afford to investigate every incident unless there is a method for choosing 
the incidents that will yield the most information and the most opportunity for improving. In 
some cases, regardless of the complexity, a formal investigation will be commissioned. More 
frequently, however, a company will want to trend incidents and only perform a formal 
incident investigation when the trend indicates that there is a higher-than-acceptable potential 
for a repeat. Trending applies to near misses, as well.

questions.question: What is a chain of custody?
options: A documentation trail describing a detailed history of specific items particularily with respect to who has held custody of the item and the reason that person had custody of the item
A documentation trail describing the manufacturing history or personal history of an item or person
A documentation trail describing the quality review and checklists that were performed on an item
questions.explanation:
A chain of custody is typically associated with incident investigations and describes 
in detail the identity of the person who has held custody of an item and why the person had 
custody of the item.

questions.question: Change analysis is:
options: A method for understanding how an incident occurred
A method for understanding how a change in a system could cause problems later on
A method of understanding how a management system change will affect the system
questions.explanation:
Change analysis is an excellent investigative tool for incident investigation as well as 
a proactive tool for performing risk assessments when a system change is anticipated.

questions.question: The F-statistic is associated with problems involving:
options: ANOVA and inferences about standard deviations
questions.explanation:
When performing an analysis of variance test (ANOVA) the F-statistic is computed. 
Chi-Square tests involve the Chi-Square distribution. Inferences about means usually involve 
the assumption of normal distributions for large samples and the "t" distribution for small 
samples.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT generally considered part of a behavioral observation process?
questions.explanation:
A behavioral observation process generally consists of identifying the behaviors to be 
observed, conducting the observations, and providing feedback on the results. 

E. Scott Geller, The Psychology of Safety

questions.question: Extinction can be accomplished by:
questions.explanation:
Extinction can be accomplished by punishment and withholding positive 
reinforcement. 

Dan Petersen, Safety Management: A Human Approach

questions.question: A Theory Y leader would exhibit which type of management style?
questions.explanation:
Theory Y leaders assume that their employees are intelligent, hard working, and 
willing to learn. They would encourage subordinates to self-manage, take responsibility, and 
share in decision making. This is democratic leadership.

questions.question: To assess your company's loss control performance, several statistics are captured and analyzed. One of these is "Percent of operational personnel that have completed all phases of chemical safety training." This statistic is an example of a(n):
questions.explanation:
Leading indicators (such as risk assessments) provide data on how well the loss 
control system is expected to perform in the future. In this particular case, there is evidence 
that when a lower fraction of operational personnel have been trained, the company's loss 
control performance decreases.

questions.question: The hidden costs of accidents are:
questions.explanation:
There are direct and indirect costs associated with an accident. These costs can be 
thought of as an iceberg, with the direct costs the visible portion of the iceberg and the 
indirect costs the large ice mass below the surface of the water. The indirect costs have been 
estimated to be 4 to 10 times the direct costs.

questions.question: Cost factor equals the total compensation and medical costs incurred per exposure, and is calculated by the following:
questions.explanation: Cost incurred * 1,000 / total work-hours is the formula for cost factor.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: The manual premium for a company under workers' compensation law is:
options: A premium from a manual for that type of company
Premium modified for the company's experience
The premium before experience modification is applied
The premium before automatic debits and credits are applied for safety program actions the company has taken
questions.explanation:
The manual premium is the premium before experience modification is applied. 
Modified premium is manual premium modified by a company's specific experience modifier 
It is also known as the standard premium. If any credits or debits are applied for specific 
program actions, they are usually applied after experience modification is applied.

questions.question: If a company is an assigned risk under a workers' compensation program, it means that the company:
options: Has been assigned a classification for the degree of risk it presents to its employees
Is unable to secure coverage and has been assigned to an insurance company for workers' compensation coverage
Has been assigned to a group that represents the type of products or services it produces
Is a good risk, has low losses, and therefore is assigned a preferred rate
questions.explanation:
Assigned risks are also know as pool risks, or residual market risks. Most assigned 
risks either have higher than anticipated losses, are new companies without any history of 
losses to predict their actual losses, or are in financial difficulty, making them less desirable 
to insure.

questions.question: In workers' compensation systems, the premium a company pays for coverage is a function of:
questions.explanation: Premium is determined by Payroll/$100 * Class Rate * Experience Modification.

questions.question: Which of the following traditional insurance coverages for business is a "no-fault" coverage?
questions.explanation:
Workers' compensation insurance is one of the first types of "no-fault" coverages for 
US businesses. No-fault coverage means that the injured party is compensated no matter who 
is at fault. While some states have sought to bring the concept of no-fault to other coverages 
such as automobile coverage, workers' compensation remains one of the only types of 
insurance that began as a no-fault coverage.

questions.question: In workers' compensation, most insurance is provided by private sector insurance companies. When insurance can only be obtained from the state government, that state is known as:
questions.explanation:
States that operate their own insurance mechanism for workers' compensation are 
known as state fund states.

questions.question: The preferred course for a company's management to meet the consequent risks of product liability is:
options: Regulation of risks through careful statement of conditions of sale and delivery
Transfer of risks through the underwriting of product liability insurance
Reduction of risks through the introduction of effective quality assurance
questions.explanation:
The management of a company must consider what ways or combinations of ways 
are available to meet the consequent risks of product liability. Of the four fundamentally 

different risk alternatives that the company's management may take, the reduction of the 
existing risk through introduction or improvement of quality assurance will give better 
conditions for regulation and transfer of risk.

questions.question: The manufacturer of any product faces an environment in which:
options: Present court rulings favor the company
Product liability is a not a significant financial burden
Product liability claims are generally decreasing
questions.explanation:
The manufacturer of any product faces an environment in which fault without 
negligence exists. Legal history shows a movement from buyer beware to seller beware.

questions.question: Alpha Company sold a product in 1990 that caused an accident in 1999. The company was not insured in 1990, but did acquire Mutual B product liability insurance for the same product in 1992. Which firm is responsible for losses?
options: Alpha Company since it was not insured in 1990
Both Alpha and Mutual B share responsibility
questions.explanation:
Mutual B is likely still responsible for the losses unless specific disclaimers in the 
policy allow Mutual B to remain clear of product liability for products sold prior to the 
underwriting.

questions.question: A tool made by Echo Corporation is sold to Tango Corporation by Wholesale Company. A Tango employee modifies the Echo tool and is subsequently injured using the employee-modified tool. Which firm is potentially liable for damages?
questions.explanation:
All parties involved are potentially liable in this situation. Tango's liability will likely 
not be associated with product liability, but biased toward worker-related injuries (if the 
employee elects to reject a workers' compensation settlement).

questions.question: For potential legal protection, how long should a manufacturer keep product records?
options: Well beyond life of the product
questions.explanation:
Due to product liability claims, a manufacturer should keep product records well 
beyond the intended life of the product.

questions.question: Implied warranty involves:
questions.explanation:
An implied warranty revolves around the implications, made by a manufacturer or 
dealer, that a product is suitable for a particular use.

questions.question: Which of the following is least likely to support a product liability claim?
questions.explanation:
Even customer misuse may be used as valid support for a product liability claim if 
the misuse could have been reasonably anticipated by the manufacturer; however, the other 
three answers are much easier foundations on which to justify a product liability claim.

questions.question: The risk value for a given hazardous event is a measurement that combines all of the following variables EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Unanticipated loss is not a variable for the risk value of a given hazardous event.

questions.question: An insurable pure risk is NOT which of the following?
questions.explanation:
