A business failure does not meet the definition of a pure risk since it is not accidental. 
It is also a single exposure and an event unique to that business.

questions.question: Dealing with the uncertainty and unpredictability of personal injury, property loss, business interruption, and liability is identified with:
questions.explanation:
Risk management is a decision-making process whose objective is to identify the 
proper mix of loss control, risk retention, and risk transfer that the organization should use in 
dealing with its risks of personal injury, property loss, and liability, including the expense and 
revenue losses associated with these exposures.

questions.question: Under workers' compensation laws:
options: The employee has to prove negligence by the employer
The amount of compensation is decided by the employee and employer under arbitration
The employer assumes responsibility and compensation for accidents, regardless of fault
The employee may sue the employer if the compensation provided is not adequate
questions.explanation:
Under workers' compensation laws, the employer assumes responsibility for all 
accidents and compensation to the employee, regardless of fault. The employee does not have 
to prove negligence and is not allowed to sue for damages beyond what is set by the state's 
workers' compensation law.

questions.question: Two valves are in series. Valve "A" has failure rate of 1 x 10-3. Valve "B" has a failure rate of 1 x 10-2. What is failure rate of the system?
questions.explanation:
Since the valves are in series, you must add the failure rates. 
Failure Rate = 1 x 10-2 + 1 x 10-3 
= 1.1 x 10-2
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: A boiler has three valves in series that have failure rates of: 3 x 10-3 8 x 10-4 2 x 10-4 What is the overall failure rate of the system?
questions.explanation:
Add the failure rates of components in series. 
Failure Rate = 3 x 10-3 + 8 x 10-4 + 2 x 10-4 
= 4 x 10-3
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: An airplane landing gear has 4 components in parallel with failure rates of 1 x 10-5, 1 x 10-8, 1 x 10-8, and 1 x 10-9, respectively. What is the approximate failure rate?
questions.explanation:
Multiply the failure rates for parallel construction. 
Failure Rate = (1 x 10-5) (1 x 10-8)(1 x 10-8)(1 x 10-9) = 1 x 10-30
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: The heart of the systems safety approach is the:
questions.explanation:
Hazard analysis is the heart of the system safety approach. An effective hazard 
analysis effort over the life cycle of a system is the spine on which all body components of a 
safety program are attached. Anticipating and controlling hazards at the design stages of an 
activity is the cornerstone of a system safety effort. 
"System Safety Engineering and Management" by Harold E. Roland and Brian Moriarity

questions.question: A product safety factor is defined as:
options: The extra margin of safety over intended use
Amount of product liability insurance needed
questions.explanation:
The product safety factor is that extra margin of safety designed into the product over 
and above its intended use.

questions.question: All of the following are examples of redundant design philosophy EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Series, single parallel, and double parallel are all examples of redundant design 
philosophy.

questions.question: What is critically needed prior to conducting a formal system safety analysis?
questions.explanation:
A system safety analysis must have models of the involved system. Before analysis 
of safety can be made, a model of the system must be constructed.

questions.question: To increase the reliability of a process, which of the following methods would LEAST likely be used?
questions.explanation:
Parallel and series design, as well as redundancy, are all appropriate methods for 
increasing the reliability of a system.

questions.question: What is a bathtub curve?
options: Failure rate analysis showing a spiraling rate of failure
Typical failure rate over the life of a product
Atypical failure rate over the life of a product
questions.explanation: The bathtub curve traces the typical failure rate of a product over time.

questions.question: A procedure analysis is a product evaluation technique that is similar to:
questions.explanation:
The techniques of a procedure analysis are similar to those of a job safety analysis 
except that in a JSA one identifies the actions the employee might take that could injure 
himself/herself, injure a fellow employee, or do damage to the operations. In a procedure 
analysis, the evaluator looks for procedures that the employee might use in the manufacturing 
of a product that could induce a hazard in the product.

questions.question: What is a CMMS?
options: A strategy for managing occupational safety in a construction environment
A computerized data management system for tracking equipment maintenance tasks
A computerized chemical safety management system
A method for managing compliance with Minerals Management Service regulations
questions.explanation:
CMMS stands for computerized maintenance management system. It is designed to 
assist maintenance and operations professionals with tracking equipment maintenance tasks 
and equipment history.

questions.question: What is the fundamental objective that a developer of a form, report, or other written instrument must remember?
options: The needs of the end user of the written instrument
The needs of the one who will read the written instrument
The needs of the ones described by the written instrument
questions.explanation:
A developer must balance these three needs when creating forms, reports, and other 
written instrument.

questions.question: There are several safety-related uses for personal computers. Considering the vast amount of information relating to safety, computers should allow safety practitioners, employees, and supervisors access to anything to mitigate risks. Of the following, what is one of the most critical pieces of safety-related information that company employees should have computer access to?
options: Company occupational accident rates, by plant
Company occupational illness rates, by department
questions.explanation:
Of these, the information that is extremely helpful is the kind which helps in 
PREVENTING future accidents - near miss and lessons learned data. Unfortunately, most 
companies do a very poor job of tracking this type of information, let alone granting 
employees computer access to it. 
The other information is somewhat helpful for employees to have on a computer; however, 
real-time access to historical data is only marginally useful in preventing future accidents.

questions.question: Heinrich's ratio of no-injury accidents to minor injuries to major injuries is:
questions.explanation:
Heinrich wrote that for every 300 no-injury accidents, there are 29 minor injuries 
accidents and 1 major injury accident.

questions.question: In 1931, Heinrich significantly changed the thinking of safety professionals. He:
options: Shifted emphasis from conditions to actions
Suggested the use of JSA to analyze accidents
Applied forensic science to accident analysis
questions.explanation:
In the early 1900's, employers concentrated more on the inspection of the workplace. 
Heinrich suggested that more emphasis be placed on the actions of employees.

questions.question: It is generally accepted that accidents:
options: Are preventable about 50% of the time
Are unexpected events that cannot be controlled
Can generally be prevented, but where absolute prevention is not possible, steps can be taken to reduce accident severity
questions.explanation:
Each of the answers is a history of accident prevention. The prevalent concept in the 
early 1900's was that no more than 50% of all accidents were preventable. In the 1940's, it 
changed to a concept that all were preventable, and finally to today's more realistic theory 
that not all accidents can be prevented, but in those cases where absolute prevention is not 
possible, steps can be taken to reduce the severity of the damage or injury.

questions.question: Your company's chief executive officer feels that she has too many employees reporting directly to her (among whom is you, the safety director). She has asked your opinion about where in the organizational structure is the best place from which the safety function should report? Your opinion is:
options: Safety should report through Human Resources
Safety should report through Procurement Support
Safety should remain on the chief executive officer's staff
questions.explanation:
Safety should report to a function with the authority and the control to correct 
company-wide safety problems. Therefore, the safety function should continue reporting to 
the chief executive officer.

questions.question: Until the widespread availability of inexpensive personal computers, the information associated with safety-related facility and site inspections and surveys was difficult to maintain. Of the following, what is the best use of the personal computer to manage information from these endeavors?
options: Maintaining an up-to-date list of responsible supervisors
Tracking and following up on the results of recommendations and corrective actions
Allowing for consistent documentation and reports
questions.explanation:
Though all of these have benefits, the key advantage to using personal computers is 
the ability to track and verify that recommendations and corrective actions are being 
addressed in a timely fashion. The key purpose of inspections and surveys is to prevent 
accidents, and the implementation of these corrective actions and recommendations is 
management's window to verifying that these identified risks have been addressed.

questions.question: The following clause from the OSH Act of 1970 is known as: "...of employment which are free from recognized hazards that are causing or likely to cause death or serious physical harm to his employees"
questions.explanation:
This clause gives OSHA broad regulatory license. It is known as the "general duty 
clause". If there is a serious hazard for which OSHA does not have a specific standard, and 
OSHA compliance officer can cite the employer using the General Duty Clause, thus 
requiring the hazard to be abated.

questions.question: At one time, a plaintiff could not recover damages unless the injury was due to physical contact. This principle is called:
questions.explanation:
Fright without physical contact is the principle that a plaintiff could not recover 
damages unless the injury was due to physical contact.

questions.question: When an injured person's care for his own safety was less than reasonable for a prudent man under existing conditions, he is considered negligent and the defendant will not be held liable. This principle is called:
questions.explanation:
Contributory negligence is the principle that an injured person's care for his own 
safety was less than reasonable for a prudent man under existing conditions. He is considered 
negligent and the defendant will not be held liable.

questions.question: Every person has a legal duty to exercise due care for the safety of others and to avoid injury to others if possible. This principle is called:
questions.explanation:
Exercise of due care is the principle that every person has a legal duty to exercise due 
care for the safety of others and to avoid injury to others if possible.

questions.question: A standard applying to a particular industry with specifications that relate to individual operations is termed a:
questions.explanation:
A vertical standard pertains only to a particular industry (e.g., OSHA requirements 
for pulp, paper, and paperboard mills).

questions.question: Which of the following statements about regulatory standards is INCORRECT?
options: Regulatory standard are developed by a federal agency such as OSHA
Regulatory standards can be developed by state level agencies
questions.explanation: Regulatory standards are mandatory. If voluntary, they are not standards.

questions.question: The "Whirlpool" decision of the U.S. Supreme Court dealt with:
options: Employee right to refuse life-threatening work
Employee right to refuse a respirator
Employee right to refuse medical exam
Employee right to request an OSHA inspection
questions.explanation:
The "Whirlpool" decision established an employee's right to refuse life- threatening 
work.

questions.question: The first legally upheld workers' compensation law was in which state:
questions.explanation: Wisconsin had the first workers' compensation law.

questions.question: The first state to utilize factory inspectors was:
questions.explanation: Massachusetts was the first state to have factory inspectors in 1867.

questions.question: The most dangerous industry from the 19th to the 20th century was:
questions.explanation:
Mining has been (and still is) one of the most dangerous industries in the United 
States. Fire fighting, construction, and logging also remain high on the list.

questions.question: What was one of the first incentives for management to ensure safe working conditions for employees?
options: The Occupational Safety and Health Act
questions.explanation:
In 1911, the Wisconsin workers' compensation law was the first law of its kind that 
required compensation for injuries which occurred on the job, without regard to fault.

questions.question: Common law requires employers to:
options: Provide a workplace free of hazards
Provide a workplace that is reasonably safe
questions.explanation:
Common law only requires the employer to provide a workplace that is reasonably 
safe.

questions.question: The standard error of the mean:
options: Is always less than the population standard deviation
Cannot be determined if the population standard deviation is not known
Increases as the sample size increases
questions.explanation:
In general, the standard error of the mean is always less than the population standard 
deviation. However, if the sample size is 1, the standard error of the mean is the standard 
deviation. 
The standard error of the mean cannot be determined if the population standard deviation is 
not known is not true because the standard error of the mean can be determined by using a 
point estimate derived from a sample standard deviation. The standard error of the mean 
decreases as the sample size increases.

questions.question: When dealing with outliers in statistical data sets one should:
options: Always eliminate them from consideration since it is obvious that a mistake has been made
Be suspect but always give careful consideration before discarding them
Rerun the experiment or take a new sample
Include them in the analysis since there is no way to determine how they appear
questions.explanation:
There are many sources of outliers including instrument failure, errors in reading 
instruments, poor experimental design, etc. But it is always possible there is something going 
on that would legitimately produce that result. Since they can have a considerable influence 
on the data set they should always be carefully considered before being accepted or 
summarily discarded.

questions.question: Inferential statistics can best be described as:
options: Setting up an experimental design for collecting data to be analyzed
Predicting the probabilities of certain events occurring in a population
questions.explanation:
Predicting the probabilities of certain events occurring in a population is a basic 
definition of inferential statistics. We are concerned with predicting or inferring something 
about a population usually based on a sample.

questions.question: Which of the following measures is likely to be the best measure of central tendency in a skewed (or non-symmetric) distribution?
questions.explanation:
A measure of central tendency is a number which represents the "average" value for a 
set of scores. The MEAN is computed by summing all the scores and dividing by the number 
of scores. The MODE is the most frequently-occurring score in a distribution. The MEDIAN 
is computed by rank-ordering all the scores and taking the one which is sequentially in 
middle. When a distribution of scores is "normal" and not skewed, the mean, median and 
mode are all the same score. When the distribution is skewed, they all differ. Under these 
conditions, it is generally accepted that the median is less affected than the other measures of 
central tendency.

questions.question: What is the best definition regarding percentiles that defines the interquartile range?
options: The range from the 25th to the 75th percentiles
questions.explanation:
The 95th percentile is incorrect. This means that 95% of the subjects fall within this 
percentile. 
The 5th percentile is incorrect. This means that 5% of the group falls within this number.

questions.question: If variable 1 and variable 2 are highly correlated with one another (r = 1.0), this means:
questions.explanation:
Even if two variables are perfectly correlated with one another (r = 1.0), we cannot 
say that one CAUSES the other. For all we know, a third variable may be responsible for the 
observed correlation. A correlation coefficient simply indicates the degree to which two 
variables covary. As such, you can generate correlations between any two measurable things 
(e.g., the amount of rainfall in Burma with the number of baseball tickets sold in New York). 
Such correlations might not be interesting, but it is still possible to compute them even 
though they have no conceivable causal relationship to one another.

questions.question: If two variables (1 and 2) have a correlation of r = -0.09, this would be considered a:
questions.explanation:
Correlation coefficients can range from -1.0 to 1.0. The negative value indicates that 
the correlation is inverted. The correlation of -0.09 indicates that the relationship between the 
two variables is very weak.

questions.question: The mode is defined as:
options: The average of all the numbers in a sequence
The value which appears most frequently in a sequence
The difference between the highest and lowest values in a sequence
The value in a sequence for which there are an equal number of values greater than the value and less than the value
questions.explanation:
The mode is defined as the value in a sequence which appears most frequently. The 
median is the number in the middle of a sequence and average or mean is an arithmetic 
average of the sum of the numbers divided by the number (n) in the set.

questions.question: The median is defined as:
options: The average of all the numbers in a sequence
The number which appears most frequently in a sequence of numbers
The difference between the highest and lowest values in a sequence
The value in a sequence for which there are an equal number of data points greater than the value and less than the value
questions.explanation:
The median is defined as the value in a sequence for which there are an equal number 
of data points greater than the value and less than the value. The mean is the arithmetic 
average of the set and the mode is the number in the set which appears most frequently.

questions.question: The standard deviation is:
options: A measure of the average distance of all observations from the mean
A measure of the average distance of all observations from the median
A constant which accounts for randomness
Not useful when working with normal distributions 5.
questions.explanation:
The standard deviation is a measure of the average distance of all observations from 
the mean.

questions.question: In a normal distribution, approximately 95.4% of the observations will fall between:
options: The median plus or minus one standard deviation
The median plus or minus two standard deviations
The mean plus or minus one standard deviation
The mean plus or minus two standard deviations
questions.explanation:
In a normal distribution, 95.4% of the observations will fall between the mean plus or 
minus two standard deviations.

questions.question: In a normal distribution, about 68.3% of the observations will fall between:
options: The median plus or minus one standard deviation
The median plus or minus two standard deviations
The mean plus or minus one standard deviation
The mean plus or minus two standard deviations
questions.explanation:
In a normal distribution, about 68.3% of observations will fall between the mean plus 
or minus one standard deviation.

questions.question: The geometric mean:
options: Is synonymous with the arithmetic mean
Is used when evaluating log normally distributed data
Is the median of log normally distributed data
questions.explanation:
The geometric mean is used when evaluating log normally distributed data and is 
equal to the median of the log normally distributed data. The geometric mean is the square 
root of the product of all of the data points.

questions.question: Which of the following is TRUE about a normal distribution?
options: It is symmetric around the mean
It can be characterized by the mean and the standard deviation
It is also known as a Gaussian distribution
questions.explanation:
A normal, or Gaussian, distribution is symmetrical around the mean and is 
completely characterized by the mean and standard deviation.

questions.question: What is the advantage of the use of historical control groups in toxicology studies?
questions.explanation:
In the event of a non-statistically significant increase in a rare tumor type in treated 
animals, a low level or lack of occurrence in historical controls gives greater biological 
validity to the finding. Use of only a concurrent control group which is usually smaller might 
have resulted in dismissal of the effect as due to chance alone.

questions.question: Of the following, the LEAST likely principle value of accident statistics is:
questions.explanation:
Accident statistics are used to measure performance, detect trouble spots, and fulfill 
OSHA record-keeping requirements.

questions.question: Descriptive statistics can best be defined as statistics that:
options: Deal with methods of planning the observation
Make generalizations based on sample data
Provide information about individuals rather than groups
questions.explanation:
Descriptive statistics is the branch of statistics that deals with methods that help to 
classify, summarize, and present the results of observations in forms that are comprehensible 
and likely to be suggestive of fruitful hypotheses.

questions.question: What is the preferred method for measuring variability in statistical analysis?
questions.explanation:
The standard deviation is the most widely used measure of dispersion (or variability, 
or spread). The computation of the standard deviation is based on, and is representative of, 
the deviations of the individual observations about the mean of those values.

questions.question: In Boolean logic and its application, the LEAST likely definition for a set is:
options: A group of objects having at least one characteristic in common
A collection of ideas having at least one characteristic in common
A collection of mathematical relationships having at least one characteristic in common
A group of objects having no characteristics in common
questions.explanation:
Boolean algebra was developed originally for the study of symbolic logic. Its rules 
and expressions in mathematical symbols permit complicated propositions to be clarified and 
simplified. In Boolean algebra, a set is a group of objects having at least one characteristic in 
common. The set may be a collection of objects, conditions, events, symbols, ideas, or 
mathematical relationships.

questions.question: A process of examining any system, design, or operation to discover inherent hazards, characterizing them as to the level of risk, and identifying risk-reduction alternatives is called a:
questions.explanation:
A hazard analysis is the process of examining a system, design, or operation to 
discover inherent hazards, characterizing them as to the level of risk, and identifying risk-
reduction alternatives. Of course, there are several TYPES of hazard analysis techniques.

questions.question: A successful research study is characterized by which of the following?
options: The study must include random samples
The study and control groups must show the same results
Variables for the study and control group must be controlled by one person
Evidence of the study must be reproducible by others
questions.explanation:
If results of a study cannot be reproduced by other independent researchers, the study 
has questionable validity.

questions.question: Safety sampling is a technique using statistics to measure:
options: The effectiveness of line manager safety activities
The risk potential for accidental injury/illness
questions.explanation:
Safety sampling measures the effectiveness of line manager safety activities - but not 
in terms of accidents. It measures effectiveness by conducting periodic samplings of how 
safely the employees are working. Safety sampling is based on the quality control principle of 
random sampling inspection. The degree of accuracy is dictated by the number of samples 
taken.

questions.question: In probability, if order is important, a permutation is used. What is the formula for a permutation?
questions.explanation:
The formula for a permutation is: 
P = N! / (N - X)!
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: In probability, if order is not important, a combination is used. What is the formula for a combination?
questions.explanation:
The formula for a combination is: 
C = N! / [X! (N - X)!]
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Evaluate the following to predict which set of circumstances will produce severe injuries if they are not identified and controlled:
questions.explanation:
A number of recent studies have shown that severe injuries are fairly predictable in 
certain situations. One of these involves unusual, non-routine work. This includes the job that 
happens occasionally, or a one-of-a-kind situation. Non-routine work may arise in factory 
operations but normal controls that apply to routine work have little effect in the non-routine 
situation.

questions.question: ALARA is most often applied in:
questions.explanation:
ALARA is the main tenet of health physics. ALARA stands for As Low As 
Reasonably Achievable.

questions.question: PEL's are:
questions.explanation: PEL's are permissible exposure limits and are established by OSHA.

questions.question: A study collected 347 death certificates of former workers. The study found that 22 workers died from a form of cancer where 9.7 would be expected. The remaining workers died of other causes where 337.3 would be expected. Using the chi-square statistic, determine the p level at which this finding is significant.
options: The finding is not significant at any level
The finding is significant at p less than 0.01
The finding is significant at p greater than 0.99
The finding is significant at p less than 0.05
questions.explanation:
X 2 = [(observed-expected)2 / expected] 
= (22 - 9.7)2 / 9.7 + (325 - 337.3)2 / 337.3 
= 16.05 
Referring to the Upper Percentage Points of the X 2 Distribution Table with one degree of 
freedom, 16.046 corresponds to a "p" much smaller than 0.01. 
This means it is very unlikely that the finding was the result of chance and it is thus 
significant at a "p" less than 0.01.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: When using the chi-square statistic, why would one use that portion of the table with values for one degree of freedom?
options: It is the most conservative approach when evaluating cancer risks
Only one of the expected numbers can be determined independently of the total number of outcomes
questions.explanation:
Degrees of freedom is determined by the number of expected outcomes which can be 
determined independently of the total number of outcomes.

questions.question: The statistical correlation coefficient is:
options: A constant used to correlate two dependent variables
The percentage of hood entry loss associated with different ventilation hoods
Used to develop a predictive model between two variables
An index of the extent to which two variables are associated
questions.explanation:
The correlation coefficient is an index of the extent to which two variables are 
associated.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the correlation coefficient?
options: As the correlation approaches 1.0, the association is stronger
questions.explanation:
A correlation of 0 (zero) means there is no correlation, (i.e., the variables show 
complete independence from one another). A negative correlation means the variables are 
inversely related to one another (e.g., as one increases, the other decreases).

questions.question: A correlation coefficient of 0.95 means two variables are:
options: Weakly correlated in an inverse manner
Strongly correlated in an inverse manner
questions.explanation:
The two variables are strongly correlated because the coefficient of correlation 
almost approaches 1.0.

questions.question: A regression equation is used to:
options: Determine the slope of a straight line
Determine the degree of correlation between two variables
Develop a predictive model between two variables
questions.explanation: A regression equation is used to develop a predictive model between two variables.

questions.question: The z-test is used:
options: To measure the distance of a particular value from the mean
questions.explanation:
A z-test is used on normal distributions to measure the distance of a value from the 
mean.

questions.question: The t-test is used:
options: To test the hypothesis that the mean score from a group does not differ from the expected mean
questions.explanation:
A t-test is used with normal distributions to test the hypothesis that the mean score 
does not differ from the mean. It is used to determine statistical significance.

questions.question: In a group of 1,000 adults, 630 are women. What is the probability that a person chosen at random from the group will be a man?
questions.explanation:
If 630 people out of the 1,000 are women then 1,000 minus 630 (370) are men. The 
probability of choosing a man is 
P = 370 / 1,000 = 0.370
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: What is the statistical distribution that considers the probability that an event will occur a specified number of times OR not at all? It is used for events that occur randomly.
questions.explanation: The Poisson distribution is the statistical technique to address this event.

questions.question: Given ignition and that a fire does not terminate (probability = 0.80) and automatic sprinklers do not extinguish the fire (probability = 0.05) and manual suppression does not extinguish the fire (probability = 0.60), what is the probability that the fire will reach full involvement?
questions.explanation:
Use the formula. 
P = ABC = Pterminates * Psprinklers * Psuppression = 0.80 * 0.05 * 0.60 = 0.024
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) "Recombinant DNA Research Guidelines" requires the formation of what type of administrative body?
questions.explanation:
The NIH guidelines require the formation of a Biohazard Safety Committee. This 
Committee serves as a technical resource to investigators, develops biohazard safety manual, 
and reviews research proposals.

questions.question: Who among the following is REQUIRED to be on a process hazard analysis (PHA) team specified in OSHA's process safety management standard (29 CFR 1910.119)? A. At least one operations/maintenance line employee (hourly, non-supervisory) B. At least one operations/maintenance supervisor C. At least one operations/maintenance engineer D. At least one safety representative/safety manager E. At least one person knowledgeable in the PHA methodology used F. At least one person knowledgeable of the process being analyzed G. At least one person capable of representing the company from a legal perspective H. At least one external regulator (OSHA compliance officer, fire marshal, etc.)
questions.explanation:
No corporate positions are specifically required by the standard; however, the 
standard requires a team, and the team must have, at a minimum, one person knowledgeable 
in the PHA methodology (i.e., what-if/checklist, HAZOP, FMEA, etc.) and one person 
knowledgeable of the process being analyzed. Good practice would suggest composing a 
PHA team with the people occupying some of the other positions in this list. 
29 CFR 1910.119 (e)(4)

questions.question: Contract employers have specific responsibilities under the OSHA Process Safety Management Standard. These responsibilities include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Assuring employees are trained in work practices
Assuring employees are instructed in the Emergency Action Plan
Conducting process hazard analyses of contract work
Advising facility employees of unique hazards discovered3
questions.explanation:
The contract employer is not required to perform the process hazard analyses. It is 
the responsibility of the employer that owns the applicable processes to conduct the process 
hazard analyses. The other answers are contract employer responsibilities.

questions.question: Means of egress, as defined by the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) Life Safety Code (NFPA 101) consists of three separate and distinct parts. Which of the following should be excluded?
questions.explanation:
Means of egress is a continuous and unobstructed way of exit travel from any point 
in a building or structure to a public way and consists of three separate and distinct parts, 
namely, exit access, the exit, and exit discharge.

questions.question: Section 5 (a)(1) of the Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) Act:
options: Gives the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) the right of entry
Is commonly called the general duty clause
questions.explanation:
Section 5 (a)(1) of the OSH Act is commonly called the general duty clause and 
specifies the requirement that employers keep their workplaces free from recognized hazards 
that are causing or likely to cause death or serious physical harm.

questions.question: ISO-9000 compliance has now become very popular in the United States and in other countries. What do the standards associated with ISO-9000 address?
options: A company's methods for system quality management
A company's methods for system safety management
questions.explanation:
ISO-9000 standards are designed to enhance a company's quality performance by 
documenting all aspects of the company's operations. Though safety and environmental 

performance enhancements are possible, the focus of ISO-9000 is to enhance quality by 
defining the processes and management systems necessary to produce a company's product. 
ISO-14000 standards deal with environmental management methods. Other ISO standards 
dealing with various aspects of safety management also exist and are expected to become 
more popular in the United States in the future.

questions.question: After establishing the required management systems, to become formally registered as compliant with ISO-9000 or ISO-14000 standards, a company must:
options: Certify in writing to the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) that the company complies with the relevant standards.

Hire an ISO-certified third-party registrar to perform an external audit of the company's facilities at which point the third-party registrar will certify to the ISO that the company complies with the relevant standards (if the company is compliant).

Hire an ISO-trained auditor to perform an external audit of the company's facilities at which point the external auditor will certify that the company complies with the relevant standards (if the company is compliant).
Simply maintain compliance with the relevant ISO standards and submit an annual certification fee to ISO.
questions.explanation:
A registrar formally certified by ISO as a registrar must be retained for the audit and 
subsequent certification to ISO that the company meets ISO requirements.

questions.question: By legislative fiat, who has the responsibility for conducting educational programs to ensure an adequate supply of qualified safety and health professionals?
questions.explanation:
NIOSH, in the Department of Health and Human Services, has in its charter the 
directive to train safety and health professionals and to ensure that an adequate supply of 
these trained professionals are available.

questions.question: By legislative fiat, who trains employers and employees in matters of safety and health?
questions.explanation: This duty is described in the OSH Act at Section 21 (c).

questions.question: In the area of automobile safety, which agency is responsible for reducing accidents on the nation's highways?
questions.explanation: The NHTSA was established in 1970 to oversee the nation's highway safety program.

questions.question: NIOSH is located in this federal agency:
options: Department of Health and Human Services/CDC
Department of Health and Human Services/PHS
questions.explanation:
NIOSH is located within the Department of Health and Human Services, Center for 
Disease Control.

questions.question: OSHA approves:
options: OSHA does not approve personal protective equipment
questions.explanation:
OSHA does not approve any personal protective equipment. NIOSH approves 
respirators, and several ANSI standards address the design requirements for the listed 
personal protective equipment.

questions.question: OSHA standards are promulgated by:
questions.explanation: The Secretary of Labor promulgates OSHA standards.

questions.question: The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) is a part of the ____________.
options: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH)
Department of Health and Human Services
questions.explanation: OSHA is located within the Department of Labor.

questions.question: The Public Health Service (PHS) plays the following important role in occupational safety and health:
options: Many OSHA inspectors are in the PHS
Many NIOSH employees are in the PHS
The PHS has prime occupational safety and health responsibility
questions.explanation: Many NIOSH employees are also commissioned officers in the PHS.

questions.question: What agency governs man-made radionuclide use?
questions.explanation:
The NRC governs radionuclide use if the materials are man-made. If the material is a 
naturally occurring radionuclide, then OSHA has jurisdiction.

questions.question: As established by the OSH Act of 1970, the Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission is part of
options: The Department of Labor Solicitor's Office
questions.explanation:
As part of the separation of power, this commission is part of the Executive Branch of 
the federal government.

questions.question: A manufacturer of lawn, leaf, and brush shredders has just learned that an interlock on the shredder guard is defective and may not shut down the unit when the guard is removed or unintentionally works loose. The company is required by the CPSC to
options: Recall the shredders and fix them
Provide a replacement switch to product owners
Notify the CPSC (Consumer Product Safety Council) of the defect
Place ads in local papers alerting owners of the defect
questions.explanation:
While the other answers may be "good business", the Consumer Product Safety Act 
requires that the CPSC be notified by the manufacturer of such defects.

questions.question: A listing of Nationally Recognized Testing Labs is published by
questions.explanation:
This listing, compiled by OSHA, contains a listing of labs that can test samples 
sent to them for contaminant,s according to the protocols established by the OSH Act or 
adopted by OSHA.

questions.question: Most employers now allow their employees to access the Internet for work- related activities. Which of the following are available on the Internet?
options: CBT safety courses delivered by commercial firms
Codified regulations and laws maintained by their respective government agencies
Discussion groups dedicated to the practice of safety and risk management
questions.explanation:
The Internet provides a huge repository of information that safety professionals can 
use to carry out their duties. This is just a small slice of the information available.

questions.question: Among the most useful modern data storage technologies is a media called "CD-ROM." Each unit of this media can store nearly 640 megabytes of information in an optical format. The format is superior to magnetic media (such as floppy discs, hard drives, and tape) because of the following
options: The CD-ROM is extremely durable and cannot be easily damaged physically
The CD-ROM is never susceptible to data degradation
The CD-ROM is not susceptible to data loss from magnetic fields
One CD-ROM is more compact than an equally-sized hard drive
questions.explanation:
CD-ROMs are not susceptible to data degradation or data loss from magnetic fields 
(such as those near monitors and speakers). CD-ROMs do experience data degradation over 
time, depending upon the quality of the CD-ROMs used. CD-ROMs are quite delicate and 
can easily be scratched or marked if not properly protected. CD-ROMs are actually quite 
bulky when compared to the storage capacity of modern multi-gigabyte hard drives.

questions.question: For a state plan to be approved by OSHA, the state plan must have regulations to cover the safety and health of state and local employees
options: True, except where the state petitions OSHA for relief from this requirement
False, except where OSHA specifically mandates this requirement due to the state's history with developing state plans
questions.explanation:
For OSHA to approve a state plan, OSHA requires the state to cover its own employees 
and those employees of all of its political subdivisions to a level at least as effective as the 
OSHA regulations that cover all other employees. Some states have state plans approved that 
ONLY cover state and local employees while allowing OSHA to maintain its jurisdiction 
over all other employees in the state (currently, these states are Connecticut, New Jersey, and 
New York).

questions.question: AIHA laboratory accreditation is good for how many years?
questions.explanation:
The AIHA Industrial Hygiene Laboratory Accreditation process follows ISO 17025; 
Requirements for the Competence of Testing and Calibration Laboratories. Every two years, 
a multiple day site inspector audits both management and technical requirements for evidence 
and documentation of laboratory best practices. If testing and calibration laboratories comply 
with the requirements of this International Standard, they are deemed to operate a quality 
management system to their testing and calibration activities that also meets the principles of 
ISO 9001.

questions.question: The Accident Prevention Manual is published by the following organization
questions.explanation: The Accident Prevention Manual is published by the National Safety Council.

questions.question: The precursor of the National Safety Council was the.
options: Association of Iron and Steel Electrical Engineers
questions.explanation:
The Association of Iron and Steel Electrical Engineers evolved into the National Safety 
Council.

questions.question: Human errors in a system can be detected using the following system safety technique
questions.explanation:
In using the critical incident technique, those involved in accidents or near misses are 
interviewed. A survey is made of those having similar experiences, and everyone involved is 
asked to describe near misses or mishaps they can recall.

questions.question: The procedure in which a job is broken into its component parts, and each task is analyzed to determine if there is a better, safer way to accomplish the job, is called a
questions.explanation:
A job safety analysis (JSA) is a procedure used by safety professionals and supervisors 
to review job methods and uncover hazards that had either been overlooked or resulted from 
changes in operations and/or personnel. The procedure evolved from military applications in 
World War II.

questions.question: The analysis technique where individuals are interviewed about accidents, near misses, and hazardous conditions is known as a(n)
questions.explanation:
Critical incident technique involves the examination of accidents and near misses to 
find hazards.

questions.question: Electrical fires are one of the most common types of building fires in the United States. What is the most common type of electrical equipment involved in electrical fires?
questions.explanation:
Distribution equipment is the primary cause of most electrical fires since it is often 
hidden and it is usually energized constantly.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate coding method when identifying 15 items, from a human engineering view?
questions.explanation:
Geometric shapes is the most appropriate coding method when identifying 15 items 
from a human engineering view.

questions.question: When designing a task that will be repeated throughout a shift, it should be designed so that it does not consume more than what percent of a persons maximum physical capacity?
questions.explanation: 40% capacity is the acceptable limit on the design of a task that is long-term in nature.

questions.question: Human factors engineers work to change tasks to improve efficiency. When applying these principles to reduce accidents or injuries, the hardest item to change through HFE principals is
questions.explanation:
Humans are the hardest part of the system to change. Therefore, the engineer attempts 
to improve efficiency or safety by working on the other parameters or sub-systems.

questions.question: The procurement/acquisition process is frequently overlooked as a stakeholder in the design of systems. At which point in the design process should representatives from procurement be integrated into the design team?
options: When the system's design intents are well understood
When the system's component specifications are established
When the system is ready to be released for bid or fulfillment
questions.explanation:
Though bringing in representatives from procurement at the very beginning may 
provide some design insight, the best time to integrate procurement into the design process is 
when the actual design intent of the system is well understood. At this point, procurement can 
provide insight on specific component specifications and vendors that can provide the 
required components and services.

questions.question: Shortly following a gas manifold cleaning operation in which alcohol was used, an explosion, followed by fire occurred. A contributing factor could probably be traced to the presence of which of the following materials (besides the alcohol)?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is the oxidizer and it participates in the combustion with the alcohol.

questions.question: System safety and occupational safety considerations are frequently not considered early in a system's design process. Why is this? A. Some design engineers and project managers do not consider system safety and occupational safety issues as design engineering components (i.e., design intent and how to achieve design intent do not require input from system safety and occupational safety professionals). B. As a result of corporate structures, some system safety and occupational safety professionals are not concerned about business outcome and are instead focused only on product safety. C. Some design engineers and project managers believe that early consideration of system safety and occupational safety considerations will result in increased system costs and schedule and are best addressed once the functional design is completed. D. Some design engineers and project managers believe that system safety and occupational safety considerations can be best addresses only after the system is in operation
questions.explanation:
Unfortunately, many project managers and design engineers have no formal training in 
system safety and occupational safety and are unaware of the value (and ultimate savings) 
that can be realized by integrating such considerations early in the project life cycle. Early 
safety consideration can prevent future costly design changes.

questions.question: A primary reason for conducting an accident investigation is to
options: Reduce the cost for workers' compensation
Identify the cause and take actions to prevent recurrence
questions.explanation:
Although there are a variety of accident investigations and analysis techniques, they all 
serve to identify root cause (or multiple root causes) and identify countermeasures that will 
prevent accident recurrence.

questions.question: The LEAST likely root cause of accidents generally is a result of
options: Lack of a safety policy or program
questions.explanation:
Accident causation is very diverse, but generally each accident is a result of a 
combination of factors. The lack of a safety program, per se, is not a root cause. The 
management system allowing no safety program, though, is a primary root cause of accidents.

questions.question: Safety professionals use accident investigations to
options: Identify the hazards that caused the accident
questions.explanation:
Accident investigations are used to determine the root cause(s) of an accident, so that 
issues can be corrected. Although the information in the other answer selections obtained 
during accident investigations may be useful, these are not the primary reasons for 
conducting investigations.

questions.question: In business terminology, what is a tall organization?
options: A company with well-developed management systems
A company with many levels of management
A company with broad market diversification
A company with extensive vertical market mobility
questions.explanation:
A tall organization has many levels of management and a narrow span of control at 
each level. In the United States, the tall organization is being displaced by flatter 
organizational structures.

questions.question: What is a DISADVANTAGE of having an external group evaluate the company's safety program?
questions.explanation:
A real problem with having external groups evaluate the safety program is that they 
may be perceived as "critics" rather than as teammates.

questions.question: What is a DISADVANTAGE of having an internal group evaluate the company's safety program?
questions.explanation:
One main drawback of an internal safety program audit group is that they are less 
likely to be totally objective due to personal friendships and "closeness" to issues.

questions.question: A pattern of behavior associated with a distinctive social position is commonly referred to as a:
questions.explanation:
Each society has many social categories which are referred to as roles, of which, each 
is associated with a particular behavioral pattern.

questions.question: The theory on human motivation which declares that workers are uninterested and unmotivated toward work, and to motivate them to work, a system of rewards and punishment is necessary, applies to:
questions.explanation:
In an attempt to analyze how management personnel view human motivation, 
McGregor evolved the notion that there are two basic ways in which management can view 
the worker: Theory X assumes the worker is essentially uninterested and unmotivated to 
work. Theory Y assumes the worker is basically interested and motivated to work.

questions.question: In occupational safety, ________________ are particularly important from the point of view of hazard identification and recognition through various warning systems:
questions.explanation:
In the man-machine system, man functions as a controller. For many situations, a 
generalized response is given, like expecting a light switch to be turned on with an upward 
movement and off with a downward movement, or turning a dial clockwise to obtain an 
increase. Such responses are called population stereotypes, a behavioral response common to 
nearly everyone in a certain population.

questions.question: Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs: Biological - security - social - ego/status - self- realization. Once a lower need is met, a person seeks the next higher need. All of the following factors complicate hierarchical motivation EXCEPT:
options: Multiple Motivation - People are often motivated by more than one need, for example, seeking recognition from fellow workers and supervisor
Psychosocial Needs - These are continuing needs such as recognition and affection
Conflicting Motives - Some motives can cause conflict, for example, desiring a promotion but fearing responsibilities
Withdrawal Needs - Removes self from the situation, physically or psychologically
questions.explanation: Withdrawal needs is not one of the factors complicating hierarchical motivation.

questions.question: Which of the following technical departments or functions normally perform an FMEA?
questions.explanation:
Reliability engineers are often tasked to perform a failure modes and effects analysis 
(FMEA).

questions.question: The primary purpose of a safety inspection is to:
options: Determine if compliance with governmental codes and regulations are being met
Find out if safety rules are being obeyed
Look for unsafe conditions and practices
questions.explanation:
The primary purpose of a safety inspection is to locate hazards and quickly follow up 
with actions to correct them.

questions.question: Of the following, the least likely reason to perform a health and safety audit is to:
options: Determine if codes, laws, and regulations are being complied with
Assess the over-all program and its conformance to accepted safety and health practices
Determine if company policies, procedures, and standards are being met
Make sure the company is prepared for an OSHA inspection
questions.explanation:
The purpose of an effective health and safety audit is to conduct a systematic, 
objective analysis of a company's health and safety practices that is directed toward well 
defined goals, namely: regulatory compliance, accident/injury/illness risk control, program 
activities, records analysis and company policies. Following the audit, a report is prepared in 
which a written assessment is made along with recommendations to improve health and 
safety management of any significant risks that were identified.

questions.question: Environmental health and safety audits are a means to:
options: Identify weak performers in plant manager roles
Ensure legal and corporate program compliance
Advise top management of compliance status
questions.explanation:
A well run audit program will ensure compliance with corporate and legal 
requirements and advise top management of the situation at the plant. The goal is not to 
identify weak plant managers but rather to identify strengths and weaknesses of the EH&S 
program and to assess the level of compliance. In addition, a compliance assurance plan is 
generated.

questions.question: A safety program evaluation can be defined as:
options: An exercise designed to placate management
A measure of the effectiveness of safety programs
A method to get rid of unsafe supervisors
questions.explanation:
A safety program evaluation is defined as a systematic method of measuring the 
effectiveness of a planned group of activities aimed at improving workplace safety. It is 
important to note that most program evaluations look at both the good and bad aspects of the 
program; in other words, a properly conducted safety program evaluation is a balanced 
evaluation.

questions.question: The main reason for safety inspections is to:
questions.explanation: The main purpose of safety inspections is to identify hazards and to correct them.

questions.question: An in-depth method that may be used to evaluate a safety program is a:
questions.explanation:
A safety audit is a comprehensive examination of the safety program. The audit should 
provide insight into the effectiveness of the program and identify where improvements can be 
made. The American Society of Safety Engineers (ASSE) publicizes a comprehensive safety 
audit process to evaluate and rate a safety program by considering Organization and 
Administration, Industrial Hazard Control, Fire Control and Industrial Hygiene, Supervisory 
Participation, Motivation and Training, Accident Investigation, and Statistics and Reporting 
Procedures.

questions.question: The purpose of an upper limit switch on a hoist is to:
options: Shut down the hoist when the load is too heavy
Prevent the load block from being raised too high
Prevent the running rope from coming off the hoist drum
To ensure that the load is centered over the hoist
questions.explanation:
The purpose of an upper limit switch is to prevent the load block from being raised 
into the hoist mechanism (sheave). When the upper limit switch is near contact by the load 
block, the crane upward movement is automatically shut down in order to keep the load block 
from contacting the sheave.

questions.question: In auditing plant operations, you find a machine operator being exposed to a high noise level (determined through sampling). What is the most expedient method that should be taken to protect the machine operator?
options: Equip the operator with personal protective equipment
Limit the operator's time of exposure
questions.explanation:
For expedience and until such time as engineering or administrative controls can be 
implemented, personal protective equipment must be provided and used to reduce the noise to 
an acceptable level.

questions.question: Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems standard 18001 is a produced by:
questions.explanation:
Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems standard 18001 is a produced 
by BSI. The British Standards Institute led the development of 18001 as a health and safety 
management system standard that is compatible with ISO 9001 and ISO 14001. 

BS OHSAS 18001:2007

questions.question: The British Standards Institute (BSI) developed and published the Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems standard 18001 because:
options: Of 'customer' requests for a management standard that addresses occupational health and safety
Of 'customer' concerns that the ISO management system standards were inadequate
BSI is responsible for assuring that United Kingdom has business standards necessary for global competition
ANSI/AIHA had developed an American standard (ANSI/AIHA Z10)
questions.explanation:
The British Standards Institute (BSI) developed and published the Occupational Health 
and Safety Management Systems standard 18001 because of 'customer' requests for a 
management standard that addresses occupational health and safety. BSI has stated its 
intention to withdraw the standard if an Internal Standard is published covering the subject 
matter. Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems standard 18001 is produced by 
BSI. The British Standards Institute led the development of 18001 as a health and safety 
management system standard that is compatible with ISO 9001 and ISO 14001. 

BS OHSAS 18001:2007

questions.question: The British Standards Institute (BSI) developed and published the Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems standard 18001 to provide for:
options: Organizations to fill a gap, thus providing additional revenue streams to BSI, through the sales of the standard. This will be successful until ISO publishes a similar standard
A structure for an organization to incorporate occupational safety and health into the organizational management process. The standard is designed to work in conjunction with ISO 14001 and ISO 9001

An organizational structure to incorporate occupational safety and health into the organizational management process. The standard was necessary because occupational safety and health program needs are not compatible with ISO 14001 and ISO 9001

A management structure for an organization to accomplish occupational safety and health, providing an independent verification of organizational safety programs that is not negatively influenced by the quality management system objectives
questions.explanation:
The British Standards Institute (BSI) developed and published the Occupational Health 
and Safety Management Systems standard 18001 to provide for a structure for an 
organization to incorporate occupational safety and health into the organizational 
management process. The standard is designed to work in conjunction with ISO 14001 and 
ISO 9001. 
BS OHSAS 18001:2007

questions.question: The Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems standard 18001 concept is based on the recognized quality concept of:
questions.explanation:
The Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems standard 18001 concept is 
based on the recognized quality concept of plan, do, check, act. 
BS OHSAS 18001:2007

questions.question: The planning process of the Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems standard 18001 requires that:
options: An organization or company completes a planning activity on a recurring basis with the organization or company's board of directors
An organization assures daily planning of work activities to assure safe practices are reviewed and implemented
An organization or company to establish processes, implement and monitor all procedures and processes and take corrective action when problems occur
An organization establishes objectives and processes supporting the organizations' occupational health and safety policy
questions.explanation:
The planning process of the Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems 
standard 18001 requires that an organization establishes objectives and processes supporting 
the organizations' occupational health and safety policy. 

BS OHSAS 18001:2007

questions.question: The Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems standard 18001 is a management system standard that is directed at reducing risk through a process of continual improvement. The standard is not a regulation or law. As such:
options: Compliance with OH&S legal requirements is only a piece of an OH&S management system conforming to the Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems standard 18001
Compliance with OH&S legal requirements is only the key factor of an OH&S management system conforming to the Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems standard 18001
Compliance with OH&S legal requirements is irrelevant to an OH&S management system conforming to the Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems standard 18001
Compliance with OH&S legal requirements is generally part of, but not required for an OH&S management system conforming to the Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems standard 18001
questions.explanation:
The Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems standard 18001 is a 
management system standard that is directed at reducing risk through a process of continual 
improvement. The standard is not a regulation or law. As such, compliance with OH&S legal 
requirements is only a piece of an OH&S management system conforming to the 
Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems standard 18001. Section 4.3.2, of the 
standard requires that legal and other requirements be continually identified and taken into 
account when establishing processes, procedures and running an OH&S management system. 
BS OHSAS 18001:2007

questions.question: The ANSI/ASSE Z490.1 standard:
options: Provides the additional depth necessary to integrate the ANSI/AIHA Z10- 2005, American National Standard for Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems into quality and environmental management systems
Is a standard that covers the areas of accomplishing training, including design, development, delivery and evaluation of training
Is the American Society of Safety Engineers' alternative to the American Industrial Hygiene Association's standard on safety management systems
Provides a basis for training that assures compliance with laws and regulations
questions.explanation:
The ANSI/ASSE Z490.1 standard is a standard that covers the areas of accomplishing 
training including design, development, delivery and evaluation of training. 
ANSI/ASSE Z490.1-2001

questions.question: ASSE is the:
options: Association for Safe and Secure Environments
questions.explanation:
ASSE is the American Society of Safety Engineers. ASSE is an organization serving 
its members and the public by providing information and action on occupational safety, 
health and environmental issues and practices. ASSE membership is made up of 
professionals that work to prevent workplace injuries and illnesses, to create safer work and 
leisure environments and to develop safer products to enhancing the quality of life.

questions.question: The ANSI/ASSE Z490.1, American National Standard, Criteria for Accepted Practices in Safety, Health and Environmental Training should be applied to:
options: Organizational safety, health and environmental management organizations
Any training that has the potential to create a hazardous environmental for the students
Organizational safety, health and environmental training plans to assure compliance with laws and regulations
Safety, health and environmental training providers
questions.explanation:
The ANSI/ASSE Z490.1, American National Standard, Criteria for Accepted Practices 
in Safety, Health and Environmental Training should be applied to safety, health and 
environmental training providers. As with all ANSI standards, Z490.1 is voluntary and does 
not guarantee regulatory compliance. 
ANSI/ASSE Z490.1-2001

questions.question: The International Organization for Standardization is:
options: A worldwide federation of national standards bodies
An organization created by the European Union to advance the business needs of the EU
A federation of international government appointed representatives that develop consensus standards for application on a worldwide basis
A federation of government representatives that develop unilateral agreements for the application of business practices across international borders
questions.explanation:
The International Organization for Standardization is a worldwide federation of 
national standards bodies. 
ISO WWW1

questions.question: ISO 19011:2002, Guidelines for quality and/or environmental management systems auditing is designed for:
options: Use by organizations wanting to get independent certification of its management system. ISO 19011 is a requirement for quality management systems under ISO 9001 and recommended for environmental management systems under ISO 14001
Use as guidance for audit programs whether those programs are for internal or external audits
Use as guidance for audits conducted by third party certification organizations to assure valid management system certification
Use by regulators, providing a guide to the application of management system audits to compliance inspections
questions.explanation:
ISO 19011:2002, Guidelines for quality and/or environmental management systems 
auditing is designed for use as guidance for audit programs whether those programs are for 
internal or external audits. 
ISO 19011:2002

questions.question: The ISO 19011:2002, Guidelines for quality and/or environmental management systems auditing provides:
options: Guidelines that are statutory in nature and are not necessarily applicable in all circumstances
Guidelines that, when adopted, need to be applied as specifically designated in order to claim conformance with the standard
Guidelines that should be used differently based on the nature, size and complexity of an organization that is being audited
Guidelines to be applied when conducting combined quality and environmental management system audits
questions.explanation:
The ISO 19011:2002, Guidelines for quality and/or environmental management 
systems auditing provides guidelines that should be used differently based on the nature, size 
and complexity of an organization that is being audited. The guidelines may be applied to 
quality management system audits, environmental management system audits or combined 
management system audits. There is no specific requirement for the guidelines to be 
implemented in order to have a conforming management system. 
ISO 19011:2002

questions.question: ANSI/ISO/ASQ QE 19011S-2004, American National Standard, Guidelines for quality and/or environmental management systems auditing was developed by the ASQ to:
options: Provide for the special needs of the U.S. business community in maximizing U.S. international competition
Assure U.S. business competitiveness with the European Union
Provide U.S. corporations with an auditing program that would accomplish regulatory compliance requirements, as well as management system audits
Provide additional guidance to the International Standard for application to the full range of audit activities
questions.explanation:
ANSI/ISO/ASQ QE 19011S-2004, American National Standard, Guidelines for quality 
and/or environmental management systems auditing was developed by the ASQ to provide 
additional guidance to the International Standard for application to the full range of audit 
activities. 
ANSI/ISO/ASQ QE 19011S-2004

questions.question: Which of the following is not an indicator of the variability of observations in an experiment?
questions.explanation:
The mean is the arithmetic average of the observations; it tells you nothing of the 
spread of the data. The standard deviation is a measure of how the data points differ from the 
average. The range is the high and low limits of the observations, and the confidence interval 
incorporates a probability as well as a measure of variability.

questions.question: Quality control has been labeled as the science and art of identifying and controlling variability. One measure of variability as used in this context is:
questions.explanation:
The variance is a measure of the average squared difference between the mean and the 
individual items in either a sample or a population. Squaring these distances gives weight to 
the variation in distance from the mean and eliminates the negative sign.

questions.question: Which of the following measures of variability is not dependent on the exact value of every measurement?
questions.explanation:
The range is the difference between the largest and smallest value in a group of data. It 
ignores the data between these values.

questions.question: A major objective of safety analysis programs is to:
options: Analyze all accidents including non-injury accidents
questions.explanation:
Safety analysis programs have as their chief objective, the determination of possible 
accidents from systems. They do not rely on past accidents to determine cause. Analyses do 
not determine fault. Analyses are performed on systems, not past accidents or incidents.

questions.question: When designing a safety program for an organization, it is necessary to consider the psychological factors that influence success, such as motivation, emotion, individual differences, and attitudes.
options: Safety programs are not designed for organizations
questions.explanation:
To work effectively with people, it is necessary to understand them. Much of the 
success of a safety program depends upon its acceptance by those to whom it is directed. 
Conversely, program acceptance is dependent upon an understanding of psychological factors 
which influence program success. These have been identified as being: individual 
differences, motivation, emotion, attitudes, and learning processes.

questions.question: One of the primary reasons for the loss of buildings to fire has been an inadequate chain of events for notifying the fire department. Which element of the chain is often at fault in this chain?
options: Deciding to inform the fire department
The correct receipt of the message by the fire department
questions.explanation:
Buildings have been lost because of insufficient attention to the method of notifying the 
fire department.

questions.question: A manufacturing process can by laid out according to the product being produced or according to the process that is used to make several products. An advantage of process layout vs. product layout is:
options: Accounting costs are easier to track
questions.explanation:
These costs are lower because there is less need to transport materials during the 
process.

questions.question: A job safety analysis is a technique to:
options: Establish safety procedures for each job
Determine physical demands of each job
Identify hazards associated with each step of the job
questions.explanation:
A job safety analysis is a procedure to make the job safer by identifying the hazards or 
potential injuries/illnesses associated with each step of the job, in addition to developing a 
solution for each hazard that will eliminate or control the exposure.

questions.question: Approximately ___% of the MALE population has some form of color blindness.
questions.explanation:
About 8% of men and 1% of women are color deficient. Color deficiency is a 
difficulty distinguishing color hue, especially under dim light. Color blindness is the inability 
to discriminate between certain colors, usually red, green, and gray. Very few people (about 3 
in 100,000) are actually totally color blind (see everything as one color in different 
intensities).

questions.question: Common carriers (e.g., airlines, bus companies, and railroads) must exercise a high degree of care (care that a very prudent and cautious person would undertake for the safety of others). This principle is called:
questions.explanation:
Care and great care is the principle behind a high degree of care: that a very prudent 
and cautious person would undertake for the safety of others. Common carriers must exercise 
a high degree of care.

questions.question: A master is liable for any negligence of his servant acting within the scope of employment. This concept is called:
questions.explanation:
Master-servant relationship is the concept that a master is liable for any negligence of 
his servant acting within the scope of employment.

questions.question: Historically, under common law, an employer is obligated to provide employees with all BUT:
questions.explanation:
Under common law an employer has been obligated to provide employees with 
competent (not semi-competent) supervisors.

questions.question: Under the doctrine of comparative negligence:
options: Damage is based on the party that was most at fault
Damage is awarded to the party that was least at fault
Damage is awarded only if a party is not at fault
Damage is apportioned according to the degree of fault of the various parties
questions.explanation:
Damages are awarded and apportioned to the degree of fault of each party in the law 
suit.

questions.question: Failure to exercise a degree of care that an ordinarily careful and prudent person (reasonable man) would exercise is the definition of:
questions.explanation:
This is the classic definition of negligence. There must be a legal duty to use care. A 
breach of that duty and injury or damage is negligence.

questions.question: Manual materials handling injuries include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Carpal tunnel syndrome is a repetitive motion injury, not a materials handling injury. 
Materials handling injuries are from overexerting muscles, tendons, and ligaments, that result 
in musculoskeletal injuries or trauma from falling objects or being caught between objects.

questions.question: With repeated exposure to noise of sufficient intensity, a permanent threshold shift (PTS) will gradually appear first at ________ Hz.
questions.explanation:
As the number of years of noise exposure increases, the hearing loss between 3,000 Hz 
and 6,000 Hz becomes more pronounced.

questions.question: A temporary depression of the hearing is called a:
questions.explanation: A temporary depression of the hearing is called a temporary threshold shift, or TTS.

questions.question: Administrative work practice controls for heat stress include acclimatization. This requires exposing the worker to the work environment for how long?
options: Two hours per day for 1 to 2 weeks
Four hours per day for 1 week
questions.explanation:
Experience has shown that workers do not tolerate a hot job very well initially, but 
develop tolerance rapidly, and full endurance by working in the heat for about two hours per 
day for a period of one to two weeks. A worker acclimatized to heat will have a lower heart 
rate, a lower body temperature, a higher sweat rate, and more dilute sweat.

questions.question: One of the most helpful groups to determine potential product problems with an existing product is:
questions.explanation:
The service department is often the first group to know about emerging problems, 
especially with new products.

questions.question: The process of eliminating unsafe acts is referred to as:
questions.explanation:
Extinction is the process of eliminating a behavior, including unsafe acts. 

Dan Petersen, Safety Management: A Human Approach

questions.question: What kind of industrial hazard can lead to an accident resulting in either death OR an accident with no severe lasting effects?
questions.explanation:
Depending on a number of conditions (e.g., skin thickness, surface moisture, part of 
body involved, duration of current flow through the victim, etc.), an electric shock can result 
in either death or no lasting effect except for body burns that generally heal.

questions.question: The most critical step in any safety program evaluation is:
options: The development of the evaluation protocol checklist
Walking-through the survey with the responsible supervisor before formally conducting the evaluation
Appointing a competent evaluation team leader
questions.explanation:
A safety program evaluation will fail or succeed based on the quality of the evaluation 
protocol/checklist. The protocol determines the areas to be examined, the level of detail, and 
the questions to be asked.

questions.question: A common injury to the wrist involving the median nerve which produces tingling and numbness is:
questions.explanation:
Carpal tunnel syndrome is an injury/inflammation of the carpal tunnel of the wrist. The 
median nerve is compressed resulting in numbness and tingling in areas served by the median 
nerve. Other symptoms are also common, i.e., pain and sometimes muscle atrophy.

questions.question: A condition which results from exposure to welding fumes that is characterized by accumulation of metal oxides in the lung without apparent physical symptoms is called:
questions.explanation:
