Siderosis is a pigmentation of the lung due to iron oxide exposure. The pigmentation 
can be marked but there seems to be no physical detriment. However, some siderosis patients 
present with chronic bronchitis and dyspnea. Differential diagnosis is difficult.

questions.question: Metal fume fever is a delayed type of disease with flu-like symptoms. It has been associated with exposure to all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Metal fume fever has been shown to be caused by exposure to freshly generated 
(nascent) fumes of zinc and magnesium and their oxides. Although zinc and magnesium are 
the most common causes, copper has been known to cause metal fume fever also.

questions.question: As one ages there is a vascular and neural degeneration of the inner ear. This results in a decrease in hearing ability. This condition is called:
questions.explanation: Presbycusis is the decrease in hearing that is associated with aging.

questions.question: To assess your company's loss control performance, several statistics are captured and analyzed. One of these is "Number of lost time cases experienced during the past year." This statistic is an example of a(n):
questions.explanation:
Lagging indicators (such as historical statistics) provide data on how well the loss 
control system has performed and is useful for understanding how well a management system 
change affected loss control performance. However, lagging indicators are not as useful for 
predicting future loss control performance.

questions.question: Which of the following ergonomically related orthopedic problems leads to the greatest cost?
questions.explanation:
Statistics indicate that low back pain is responsible for more lost time than any other 
ergonomically related problem. About one third of all disabling injuries are due to manual 
handling of objects.

questions.question: In injury epidemiology, the term incidence rate is often used. Incidence rate is the number of _____ that occurred in a given period of time divided by the sum of the exposed time.
questions.explanation:
Incidence rate is the rate of development of new cases of a specific disease over a 
given time period. The denominator is normally person-hours worked or some other similar 
measure such as person-years, etc.

questions.question: There are a number of management standards published by ISO. ISO is an acronym for:
questions.explanation:
ISO is an acronym for the International Organization for Standardization. ISO is a non-
governmental organization. 
ISO World Wide Web

questions.question: The ISO Quality Management Standards are found in which series of standards?
questions.explanation:
The ISO Quality Management Standards are found in the ISO 9000 series. ISO 9001, 
Quality Management Systems - Requirements is the best known. The ISO 14000 series 
covers Environmental Management. 18000 series is not in the ISO standards. OHSAS 18001 
and 18002 are Occupational Safety and Health Management Standards generally considered 
to have originated from England. 
ISO World Wide Web

questions.question: An EMS, referred to in ISO 14004, is a system for:
questions.explanation:
ISO 14004 discusses guidelines for an Environmental Management System (EMS). 
ISO World Wide Web

questions.question: The ISO 9000 series of standards set forth and describe:
options: A regulatory framework that assures a corporation has a valid quality management system
A standardized list of expectations of high quality companies for use by governing bodies
A simple set of rules that can be followed by company officials to assure that employees accomplish quality work
A set of management practices recognized by international consensus
questions.explanation:
The ISO 9000 series of standards sets forth an internationally recognized series of 
standards that have been developed through a consensus process. The ISO 9000 series 
specifically identifies good quality management practices. 
ISO World Wide Web

questions.question: The ISO 9001:2008 standard provides:
options: A set of management system requirements that can be achieved and measured
A set of specific operating methodologies that companies must implement
A model organizational structure that will assure quality products and services
A method for auditing organizations to measure the organizational quality level
questions.explanation:
ISO 9001:2008 sets forth a system of requirements that an organization must achieve 
to be considered conformant with the standard. The standard does not specify how the 
organization must achieve the requirements or what the organizational structure must be. 
ISO World Wide Web

questions.question: The American National Standards Institute (ANSI) is:
options: The United States Government representative to international boards of inquiry and regulation
A United States government organization that certifies standards
questions.explanation:
The American National Standards Institute (ANSI) is a 501(c)3 private, not-for-profit 
organization in the United States. ANSI oversees the creation, promulgation and use of 
standards and guidelines that impact every sector of businesses. ANSI is also involved in 
accreditation programs related to conformance to standards - including globally-recognized 
programs like the ISO 9000 (quality) and ISO 14000 (environmental) management systems. 
ANSI World Wide Web

questions.question: The American National Standards Institute (ANSI) oversees the development of national standards affecting businesses in the United States. ANSI's standards development process focuses on:
options: The selection of key experts for standards committees to assure scientifically sound standards are promulgated
The use of European Union approved methods to achieve global dominance of key industries
The use of consensus and broad based public involvement to achieve balanced and high quality standards
The use of standards to further the business interests of ANSI member companies
questions.explanation:
The American National Standards Institute (ANSI) oversees the development of 
standards affecting businesses in the United States. ANSI's standards development process 
focuses on the use of consensus and broad based public involvement to achieve balanced and 
high quality standards. The ANSI standards development process is designed to withstand 
scrutiny. 
ANSI World Wide Web

questions.question: The American National Standards Institute (ANSI):
options: Serves as the Head of ISO and chairs the IEC
Is not involved in international standards, as it is a United States based organization
Provides oversight for all ISO standards development
Is the US representative to ISO and IEC
questions.explanation:
The American National Standards Institute (ANSI) is the U.S. representative to ISO 
and IEC. ANSI is the U.S. representative of the two major non-treaty international standards 
organizations, the International Organization for Standardization (ISO), and the International 
Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) [via the U.S. National Committee USNC)]. 
ANSI World Wide Web

questions.question: AIHA is the:
options: Agency International for Hygiene and Assessment
Agency Industrial and Health Audits (from ISO)
questions.explanation:
AIHA is the American Industrial Hygiene Association. AIHA is an international, 
membership organization serving professionals that practice industrial hygiene. AIHA is the 
sponsor of the ANSI/AIHA Z10, American National Standard for Occupational Health and 
Safety Management Systems. 

AIHA World Wide Web

questions.question: The ANSI Z10 standard is:
options: The American National Standard Criteria for Accepted Practices in Safety, Health, and Environmental Training
The American National Standard for Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems
The American National Standard version of the ISO 140001, Environmental Management Systems
The American National Standard equivalent of the ISO 9001, Quality Management Systems
questions.explanation:
The ANSI Z10 standard is the American National Standard for Occupational Health 
and Safety Management Systems. Z10 is the equivalent to the British Standards Institute, BS 
OHSAS 18001. 
AIHA World Wide Web

questions.question: The objective of the ANSI/AIHA Z10, American National Standard for Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems is which of the following?
options: Provide a framework of auditing tools to measure the level of success of an organizations occupation safety and health programs
Set forth a strict set of practices and processes that must be implemented that will allow an organization to be certified as having an occupation safety and health management system
Provide organizations with a model to allow them to integrate occupational health and safety management into their overall business management system
Establish a framework for organizations to manage occupational health and safety irrespective of the success or failure of the business
questions.explanation:
The objective of the ANSI/AIHA Z10, American National Standard for Occupational 
Health and Safety Management Systems is to provide organizations with a model to allow 
them to integrate occupational health and safety management into their overall business 
management system. 
AIHA World Wide Web

questions.question: The ANSI/AIHA Z10, American National Standard for Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems provides a system of:
options: Detailed specifications to be implemented in each organization adopting the standard
Strict auditing specifications for management system certifications
A template for occupational safety and health consultants to use in establishing consulting businesses
Principles with broad applicability to different organizations
questions.explanation:
The ANSI/AIHA Z10, American National Standard for Occupational Health and 
Safety Management Systems provides a system of principles with broad applicability to 
different organizations. Management system standards must be capable of being used by a 
wide variety of different organizations, as such, they are performance based, not prescriptive. 

AIHA World Wide Web

questions.question: ANSI, or the American National Standards Institute:
options: Approves standards developed sponsors, granting approval once specific standards development criteria are verified
Promulgates and publishes standards that are intended to be used by local governments in the development of regulations
Promulgates and publishes standards that are developed in cooperation with various sponsoring organizations
Works closely with the American National Standards Verification Board to assure the standards that it develops meet the specific criteria required of ANSI standards
questions.explanation:
ANSI, or the American National Standards Institute, approves standards developed 
sponsors, granting approval once specific standards development criteria are verified. ANSI 
does not develop standards and does not provide interpretations. Standards are developed 
under the direction of sponsors. Standards may be approved by ANSI only after ANSI has 
verified that the requirements for due process, consensus and other criteria have been met in 
the development process. 
ANSI World Wide Web

questions.question: The ANSI/AIHA Z10, American National Standard for Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems purpose is to:
options: Establish performance criteria for management acceptance of risk to employees and the public
Establish a tool for continual improvement of occupational safety and health performance
Establish a tool to assist organizations with regulatory compliance
Establish a minimum level of performance for organization health and safety programs in the international environment
questions.explanation:
The ANSI/AIHA Z10, American National Standard for Occupational Health and 
Safety Management Systems purpose is to establish a tool for continual improvement of 

occupational safety and health performance. 
ANSI/AIHA Z10-2005

questions.question: The ANSI/AIHA Z10, American National Standard for Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems concept is based on the recognized quality concept of:
questions.explanation:
The ANSI/AIHA Z10, American National Standard for Occupational Health and 
Safety Management Systems concept is based on the recognized quality concept of plan, do, 
check, act. 
ANSI/AIHA Z10-2005

questions.question: There are 10 plants in a manufacturing company. Four are to be picked at random to send a representative to safety planning meetings. How many different combinations of plant representation are possible at the meeting?
questions.explanation:
Because order is NOT important, this is a combination (instead of a permutation). 
Combinations = N! / [X! (N-X)!] 
(where N is the total number of plants and X is the number of plants chosen for 
representation at the safety planning meetings) 
Combinations = 10! / [4! (10-4)!] = 3,628,800 / (24 * 720) = 210
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: In manual materials handling, methods for eliminating the need to bend include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Using lift tables, work dispensers, and other mechanical aids
Raising the work level to an appropriate height
Providing materials and tools in front of the worker
questions.explanation:
Although providing materials and tools in front of the worker helps to prevent twisting 
motions, to avoid bending motions the work needs to be at the proper height. This can be 
accomplished through mechanical means (lift tables), raising the work level, or lowering the 
worker to the level of the work.

questions.question: Human factors engineering or ergonomics is concerned with fitting the worker to a task or the task to the worker. A man/machine system is considered a closed loop system. Which one of the following does NOT make up the closed loop system?
questions.explanation:
The closed loop system is made up of reactions, machine, data input, and senses of 
man.

questions.question: Human factors engineering is fitting the worker to the task or the task to the worker. Man is better at all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Sensitive to a wide variety of stimuli
questions.explanation: Machines are better at exerting large forces smoothly.

questions.question: Human factors engineering is a technical discipline which concerns any of the following EXCEPT:
options: Design of the workplace to reduce mistakes and accidents
Design of tools to promote comfort
questions.explanation:
Human factors, also referred to as ergonomics, human engineering, bioengineering, 
and biomedics is a technical discipline mainly concerned with optimizing the relationship 
between people AND their work environment.

questions.question: A safety program begins by:
options: Assuring compliance with all OSHA standards
Soliciting support of the facilities department
questions.explanation:
Management must develop a policy statement that clearly defines management's 
support for safety and the safety-related roles of each member of the organization.

questions.question: When an employee's exposure to an airborne, breathable chemical cannot be reduced to permissible safe levels through engineering controls, then the LEAST acceptable exposure control alternative is:
questions.explanation:
Administrative controls are methods for controlling employee exposures to 
contaminants or excess noise by limiting the duration of an individual's exposure by job 
rotation, work assignment, or time periods away from the contaminant or noise source. 
Personal protective equipment, such as a respirator, is the last alternative that should be 
considered to reduce exposures.

questions.question: Safety directors should _______ as many levels of management as possible.
questions.explanation:
The fact that the safety director's manager is interested in safety and supportive of the 
director is more important than the level he/she reports at. It is important that the company's 
upper management support safety and encourage safety. If the safety function reports at a 
high level in a company that does not value safety, the level of reporting will not matter. 
Access to managers throughout an organization will assist the safety director in developing 
an accepted, consistent, effective safety program.

questions.question: Typically, the product safety engineer is a separate entity of which organization?
questions.explanation:
Generally the product safety engineer is a separate entity or of the risk management 
department organization. For a simple product or process, the product safety engineering 

organization may be one person. If the organization is large or complex, several people may 
be needed, even with specializations.

questions.question: The system safety responsibility in many company organizations is placed in the:
questions.explanation:
The system safety responsibility in many company organizations is placed in the 
product assurance department because it is an organizational method of establishing a close 
relationship among common disciplines such as reliability, maintainability, quality assurance, 
and human factors engineering.

questions.question: Ozone has a propensity to form free radicals in the body. A toxicologic phrase utilized to describe this phenomena is:
questions.explanation:
Ozone's propensity to form free radicals is termed radiomimetic. Webster's 3rd New 
International Dictionary defines radiomimetic as "producing, especially, biological effects 
similar to those produced by radiation."

questions.question: Numerous LIFESTYLE factors have been shown to impact the toxicity of chemicals. For example, ________ is known to potentiate both the carcinogenic and noncarcinogenic effects of asbestos.
questions.explanation:
Epidemiologic studies have shown that smoking dramatically increases the risk of 
developing fibrotic lung disease (asbestosis and bronchiogenic carcinoma). Mesothelioma, 
another tumor type associated with asbestos exposure, has an uncertain relationship to 
cigarette smoking.

questions.question: Accidental contact with 60 Hz current of 5 to 25 mA can cause the following:
questions.explanation:
Victims may become paralyzed with accidental contact with 60 Hz of current in the 
range of 5 to 25 mA.

questions.question: Electrical shock intensity and effects will depend on the:
questions.explanation:
Electrical shock intensity and effects depends on the current path, frequency, and 
duration.

questions.question: Special hazard terminology has been developed for cranes and derricks. What is the correct term for an undetected hazard, created as a result of the crane's design or by the crane's use?
questions.explanation:
A dormant hazard is an undetected hazard created either by the crane's design or crane 
use. Armed and active are other types of crane and derrick hazards.

questions.question: Which of the following are safety devices installed in boilers to relieve pressure?
questions.explanation:
Fusible plugs are designed to relieve pressure and to indicate certain conditions that 
contribute to low water (which causes pressure build-up). Safety valves will automatically 
relieve excess pressure or vacuum, that would otherwise damage equipment or result in injury 
to personnel. The selection, fabrication, installation, testing, and replacement of safety valves 
and fusible plugs should be in accordance with the ASME code.

questions.question: Which is the preferred guard for power presses performing piercing, blanking, and stamping operations?
questions.explanation:
The fixed guard is considered preferable to all other types and should be used in every 
case unless it has been definitely determined that this type is not at all practical. The fixed 
guard at all times prevents access to the dangerous parts of the machine. Besides power 
presses, fixed guards are also on guillotine cutters, drilling machines, gear trains, milling 
machines, and sheet flattening machines.

questions.question: Guarding by means of a rail enclosure which restricts access to a machine is called:
questions.explanation:
Guarding by means of a rail enclosure which restricts access to a machine is called 
fencing.

questions.question: Which of the following statements describes ergonomics/HFE? I. Engineering something for the population that will use it II. Designing a system so that machines, human tasks, and the environment are compatible with the capabilities and limitations of people III. Designing the system to fit the characteristics of people rather than retrofitting people into the system
questions.explanation:
Ergonomics/HFE is a multidisciplinary activity dealing with interactions between man 
and his total working environment plus stresses related to such environmental elements as 
atmosphere, heat, light, and sound, as well as workplace tools and equipment.

questions.question: Placing importance on individual differences, a work station or system should be designed to fit _______ % of the population:
questions.explanation:
When a system is designed which is directed at the average individual, much of the 
population will not be able to use the system efficiently because each person differs from the 
other; in other words, there is variability in the population. A better approach when 
designing a system is, instead of setting the standards to fit the average, design it to fit all but 
the upper 5% and the lower 5%. The system will then fit 90% of the population.

questions.question: Anthropometry provides the safety engineer with data about:
options: Lifting capabilities of males and females
questions.explanation: Anthropometric data provided specific data about the dimensions of the human body.

questions.question: The most effective time to apply the principles of ergonomics is:
questions.explanation:
The most effective use of the principles of ergonomics is when planning a new 
operation or planning changes to an existing operation.

questions.question: Ergonomics attempts to:
options: Redesign the product to be made more efficiently
Redesign tasks to fit the capabilities of males
Redesign tasks to fit the capabilities of humans
Redesign jobs to reduce the number of tasks required
questions.explanation:
The engineer attempts to redesign individual tasks in jobs so that a higher percentage 
of the human population can safely perform the tasks.

questions.question: It is widely recognized that an important aspect of hand tool use is often overlooked. This aspect is:
questions.explanation:
Tenosynovitis is often called a "training" disease. Inexperienced or new workers often 
exert more force than necessary when using certain hand and power tools. Training in proper 
methods of tool use and encouraging workers to alternate hands when using selected hand 
tools (a design consideration, too) is encouraged.

questions.question: What three concepts characterize ergonomics?
options: Human performance, ergonomic design, systems integration
Physical demands, mental demands, emotional demands
questions.explanation: These concepts can be rephrased as work, engineering, and technology management.

questions.question: Good engineering controls for manual materials handling tasks are based on which of the following principles?
questions.explanation:
Good engineering controls involve designing the workplace to fit the worker, one of 
the definitions for ergonomics. The key scientific areas that have been studied for the purpose 
of developing ergonomic guidelines for workplace design include: anthropometry, 
biomechanics, epidemiology, and physiology.

questions.question: Work operations, reach, operator's position, and posture are all best analyzed by:
questions.explanation: A human factors engineer would utilize these variables to conduct studies.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct when isolating equipment through lockout/tagout?
options: Pulling a fuse on electrical equipment to guarantee a dead circuit
Disconnecting the main power source to fully disable most machines
Tightly shutting a high pressure valve before starting maintenance work
Physically locking the main power source and labeling it
questions.explanation:
The incorrect answers fail to adequately eliminate the hazard. Additional actions 
require physically "locking out" the energy source(s) and labeling it with a warning tag. 
29 CFR 1910.147

questions.question: How does a ground fault circuit interrupter work?
questions.explanation:
The GFCI operates by sensing small amounts of current going to ground. There are 
various types of GFCI's with different tripping currents.

questions.question: After a recent hazardous materials spill of hydrochloric acid, you have been asked to analyze the contents of a catch basin in which some of the spilled acid was collected. After collecting a 65 mL sample from the catch basin, you precisely separate the samples into two 30.0 mL pipettes. Next, you test the remaining 5 mL with PH paper and see that it clearly indicates a pH of around 1. You decide to perform an acid/base titration to determine the precise molarity, or molar concentration of the material in the catch basin. You prepare a 0.100 Molar solution of sodium hydroxide and titrate both of your 30.0 mL samples. The first sample requires 50.55 mL of sodium hydroxide for neutralization, and the second sample requires 50.45 mL. What is the molarity of the hydrochloric acid in the catch basin?
options: the pH paper indicated that the material in the catch basin is actually basic
questions.explanation:
First of all, the indication of 2 on the pH paper implies an acidic liquid; therefore, an 
acid/base titration using sodium hydrochloric acid is appropriate. Sodium hydroxide and 
hydrochloric acid neutralize one another on a one-to-one basis (the one H+ ion from HCI 
reacts with the one OH- ion in NaOH, and the one Na+ ion in NaOH reacts with the one CI- 
ion in HCL). Because of this one-to-one relationship, we can determine the molarity by using 
this simple identity: M1V1 = M2V2. M1 is 0.100 M of which 50.5 mL (average) was used to 
neutralize 30.0 mL (V2) of acid of unknown molarity (M2). (M1V1)/V2 = M2 (0.100 M * 50.5 
mL)/30.0 mL = M2 = 0.168 M
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: A design which allows the system to function safely until corrective action is possible is called:
questions.explanation:
Fail-operational is a design which allows the system to function safely until corrective 
action is possible.

questions.question: When derating an electronic part, which of the following techniques is not appropriate?
questions.explanation: Decreasing the MTBF is not an appropriate technique for derating an electronic part.

questions.question: The scientific study of how, when, where, and why an illness distributes itself over time in a population describes:
questions.explanation:
Epidemiology is a science that investigates the distribution and causes of disease. 
Epidemiologists study the interplay between the physical environment, biological effects, and 
social phenomena that relate to human health and illness in the workplace.

questions.question: A group of foundry workers are exposed to an air temperature of 105ºF. Which control would be least appropriate?
questions.explanation:
The principal heat load in a foundry is radiant. It is highly unlikely that foundry air 
will have much moisture. All other methods may have some net benefit.

questions.question: TLV's for gases and vapors are estimated on what unit basis?
questions.explanation:
TLV's for gases and vapors are expressed in parts per million, which is a 
volume/volume ratio, and milligrams per cubic meter, which is a weight/volume ratio.

questions.question: It is necessary for a maintenance worker to enter a confined space where a potential atmosphere immediately dangerous to life or health (IDLH) may be present. Which of the following respirators should the worker use?
options: NIOSH-approved full face chemical cartridge respirator with cartridges rated for the chemical hazard
NIOSH-approved full face demand SAR (Supplied Air Respirator)
NIOSH-approved full face pressure demand SCBA (Self Contained Breathing Apparatus)
NIOSH-approved half face cartridge respirator with HEPA cartridges
questions.explanation:
A pressure demand SCBA or pressure demand SAR is required in a known or 
suspected IDLH atmosphere. A demand SAR may sometimes allow contaminants to be 
sucked into the mask which may have a negative pressure with respect to the outside 
atmosphere. A pressure demand SCBA constantly supplies air to the face piece (to ensure 
that a negative pressure is never experienced inside the face piece). Cartridge respirators are 
not permitted in known (or suspected) IDLH atmospheres. 29 CFR 1910.134 (d)(2)

questions.question: The basic safety precaution for people who work in confined spaces or in dangerous atmospheres is:
options: Use of safety harnesses and life lines
questions.explanation:
The basic safety precaution for people who work in confined spaces or in dangerous 
atmospheres is the "buddy system". With the buddy system, no worker enters a dangerous 
atmosphere until someone else has been designated to take responsibility for his/her safety. 
While one worker goes into a confined space or other dangerous area, the buddy stays in a 
safe place nearby, alert at all times for danger and ready to act in an emergency. (Usually the 

buddy is suited up in protective equipment, as is the worker, ready to help the worker out in 
case of trouble).

questions.question: A mechanical filter respirator is designed to prevent entrance of __________ into the respiratory system.
questions.explanation: Mechanical filters can only remove particles, they cannot remove gases or vapors.

questions.question: Air-purifying and atmosphere-supplying are:
questions.explanation:
Respirators can be placed in two categories: a) air-purifying, and b) atmosphere-
supplying. Most air-purifying respirators use chemical cartridges to remove contaminants 
from the outside atmosphere to a concentration acceptable for breathing. Atmosphere-
supplying respirators include SCBA and SAR. These respirators have an independent supply 
of breathable air for the respirator-wearer. There is no such thing as an OSHA-approved 
respirator.

questions.question: Barrier creams:
options: Reduce contact of potential irritants with the skin
Are preferred to gloves in most cases
questions.explanation:
Barrier creams, as their name implies, form a protective barrier between the skin and 
the chemical. They are not neutralizing agents for chemicals.

questions.question: In which of the following situations may an air-purifying respirator be worn safely?
options: Odor threshold is greater than the allowable level
Odor threshold is equal to the allowable level
Odor threshold is less than the allowable level
Odor threshold is at least 4 times the allowable level
questions.explanation:
To wear an air purifying respirator safely, the worker must be able to detect the 
material at a safe level. If the odor threshold is greater than the allowable level (e.g., the odor 
threshold is 20 ppm, while the allowable level is 10 ppm), the worker will not know the 
material is getting through until PEL/TLV levels are reached or exceeded.

questions.question: The risk of developing active pulmonary tuberculosis is substantially increased by which of the following?
options: Exposure to free crystalline silica dust
questions.explanation:
Exposure to free silica dust is a risk factor for pulmonary tuberculosis. The fibrosis 
caused by the silica may make the lung more susceptible to tuberculosis.

questions.question: Which of the following would be most effective in reducing dermatitis in electroplaters?
questions.explanation:
The best method of protecting oneself from dermatitis is to prevent all contact with the 
offending agent. Therefore, gloves is the best answer.

questions.question: When an internal explosion occurs, it causes the shape of the enclosure to change from:
questions.explanation:
When an internal explosion occurs, it causes the shape of the enclosure to change from 
rectangular to elliptical. Adequate strength is one requirement for the design of an 
explosionproof enclosure; a safety factor of 4 is generally used. To prevent failure of the 
enclosure, openings are designed to relieve the pressure of the expanding gases.

questions.question: You suspect that a worker's exposure has exceeded the TLV-C for a certain chemical. Unfortunately you do not have a device to measure instantaneous exposures. You do have a longer term measurement device. What do you do? Note: Substance does not cause an immediate reaction.
options: Take an 8-hr sample and back calculate
Take as short as sample as possible
Do not measure and assume the TLV-C was exceeded
questions.explanation:
If instantaneous monitoring is not feasible, then the TLV-C can be assessed by 
sampling over a 15-min period - except for those substances that may cause immediate 
irritation when exposures are short. 
ACGIH TLVs and BEIs

questions.question: Pressure testing is a potentially ___________ test.
questions.explanation: Pressure testing may actually destroy the object being tested.

questions.question: How many footcandles of illumination are necessary for work that requires fine assembly?
questions.explanation:
500 footcandle is necessary for the performance of visual tasks of low contrast and 
very small size over a prolonged period of time (e.g., fine assembly, very difficult inspection, 
etc.). 5 footcandles is very low light, and is not appropriate for most working environments. 
50 footcandle is a typical office environment lighting level, and 5,000 footcandle is well 
beyond the lighting necessary for the task described.

questions.question: As a safety professional, you are asked to provide guidance in the layout of a 5,000 square-foot, high-hazard facility to be occupied by up to 15 laboratory scientists. The expected configuration of the process equipment presents the need for a dead end corridor in the means of egress arrangement. Based on NFPA 101 (Life Safety Code), what will be your suggestion regarding the maximum permitted length of the anticipated dead end corridor?
questions.explanation:
Dead ends are not permitted in high hazard occupancies with an area of more than 200 
square feet or an occupant load of more than 3 people. NFPA 101 7.11.4 (Life Safety Code)

questions.question: Delegation of authority and chain of command are characteristic of a:
questions.explanation:
The formal structure has a system of objectives that defines roles and responsibilities 
of the participants. Delegation of authority means authorizing individuals within the structure 
with defined rights and responsibilities resulting in a "chain of command".

questions.question: All have been identified as "megatrends" by John Naisbett EXCEPT:
options: Transition from industrial to information society
questions.explanation:
Naisbett predicted a number of changes including the movement from centralization to 
decentralization in government and business.

questions.question: Heinrich's domino theory of accidents includes:
options: Social, fault, unsafe act, accident, injury
questions.explanation: Heinrich's domino theory involved social, fault, unsafe act, accident, injury.

questions.question: An effective fire loss control program must include objectives that prevent loss of life and personal injury, prevent inception of fire, protect property and:
options: Incorporate the use of fire resistive building materials
Effect controls that limit the fire load (amount of combustibles)
questions.explanation:
In any fire loss control program there is a necessity for a plan that protects against a 
business interruption. Generally, there is a condition of insurance that you reduce the loss 
resulting from a business interruption by resuming complete or partial operations on the fire 
damaged premises and/or making use of other property and materials at other facilities.

questions.question: Political and socioeconomic factors are NOT important considerations in which of the following processes?
questions.explanation:
Risk assessment is the scientific discipline involved in characterizing and quantifying 
the magnitude of potential harm to human health from the presence of a particular agent in 
the environment. Unlike risk management, risk assessment does not consider economic 
impact.

questions.question: What does the management term "line function" mean?
options: An employment function for which the enterprise exists
An employment function to support the work for which the enterprise exists
An employment function associated with a manufacturing assembly line
An employment function providing direct supervision
questions.explanation:
A line function is a position or role directly involved with the main enterprise of the 
company. For example, "pigment mixer" would be a line function in a paint manufacturing 
plant. A staff function, on the other hand, is a position or role that supports the line functions. 
For example, "security guard" is a staff function for a paint manufacturing plant to ensure the 
protection of the facilities and people involved in manufacturing paint.

questions.question: A manager who utilizes an external reward and punishment system to affect performance is a _________ manager.
questions.explanation:
Theory X holds that people must be motivated to work by external reward and 
punishment.

questions.question: A manager who utilizes the inherent motivation that is present in all humans is a ________ manager.
questions.explanation: Theory Y managers utilize the goal-orientation of the worker to achieve results.

questions.question: The tendency for an individual who finds himself in a frustrating circumstance and reverts to an earlier form of behavior - such as putting on a temper tantrum - is called:
questions.explanation:
Regression is the tendency for an individual who finds himself in a frustrating 
circumstance to revert to an earlier form of behavior.

questions.question: The tendency for an individual to give up or withhold any sense of emotional or personal involvement in the situation is called:
questions.explanation:
Resignation is the tendency for an individual to give up, or withhold any sense of 
emotional or personal involvement in the situation.

questions.question: Human performance is a function of:
questions.explanation: Human performance is a function of (aptitude + training) * motivation.

questions.question: It is possible to reduce incidents involving human error by:
options: Furnishing workers with personal protective equipment
Providing training and education to workers and line supervisors
questions.explanation:
It is generally agreed that the majority of incidents leading to an accident are attributed 
to unsafe acts rather than unsafe conditions. Although general estimates of the mental and 
emotional states that cause accidents (like indifference, resentment of authority, disregard of 
danger, undue haste, anger, impatience, boredom, etc.) are not reliable, there is consensus that 
effective training and education will prevent many of the human errors (unsafe acts) that arise 
from mental and emotional states.

questions.question: Workers' compensation represents a significant business expense for employers. To a large extent, employers can influence the cost of this coverage by:
options: Obtaining a low rate prospective experience rating plan
Obtaining a low rate retrospective experience rating plan
questions.explanation:
One of the objectives of the workers' compensation system is to encourage safety in 
the workplace. A credit rating is awarded for better than average injury/illness accident 
prevention OR a debit rating is charged against the premium for one that is worse than 
average. Injury rates and the experience modification rating are used to estimate charges. By 
lowering the experience modification rate one can lower their insurance premium.

questions.question: The acronym CAD/CAM has become very important to manufacturing. What does CAD stand for?
questions.explanation:
CAD/CAM stands for computer aided design and computer aided manufacturing. 
CAD/CAM is used to make manufacturing more cost effective, more time efficient, and to 
increase overall product quality.

questions.question: A safety professional is asked to evaluate a procedure to address a high pressure steam fitting leak. He or she should ensure that which of the following safety-related caution steps is included prior to repairs being made?
options: Ensure system is shut down, bled, locked out, and tagged out
Wrap line with electrician's tape before making repairs
questions.explanation:
The correct caution step is to verify that the system is properly bled and to ensure that 
the lock out/tagout procedures have been implemented.

questions.question: In organizing and implementing a successful safety and loss control program, it is essential that you:
options: Get top management support and participation
Acquire an environmental health and safety staff
Promulgate a formal safety policy and program
questions.explanation:
An effective safety program must begin at the top. Only top management can assign 
the responsibility for safety and loss control and ensure its performance. Also, top 
management can implement the controls in the workplace environment along with worker 
operations that will control accidents.

questions.question: All of the following are examples of staff functions EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Commanding is a line function and, therefore, not an example of a staff function.

questions.question: A supervisor's job responsibilities include the "3-E's" principles. Which of the following would NOT be included under the "3-E's"?
options: Making sure employees comply with safety rules and procedures
Instructing employees how to work safely
Determining ways for eliminating injury/illness potential from the job
questions.explanation:
The supervisor's job involves: 
ENGINEERING - to determine the most effective way of doing the job and designing the 
injury/illness potential out of the job. 
EDUCATION - to instruct the employee in the right method, and through training, improve 
job skill, knowledge, and behavior. 
ENFORCEMENT - to ensure the employee follows the prescribed work practice and 
complies with safety rules and procedures.

questions.question: Within a PERT network, slack time is defined as:
options: The difference between the length of time scheduled for an event and the length of time required for completion
The longest path between critical events
questions.explanation:
Slack time within the PERT network is defined as the difference between the length of 
time scheduled for an event and the length of time required to complete the event.

questions.question: The critical path in a PERT network is defined as:
options: The start time between the longest tasks
The longest time path between beginning and end events
The shortest time path between beginning and end events
questions.explanation:
The critical path in a PERT network is the longest time path between beginning and 
ending events. Critical path defines the sequence of events that control the amount of time 
needed to complete the effort described by the PERT network.

questions.question: The responsibility for IMPLEMENTING a company's safety and health policy is that of:
questions.explanation:
Top management is responsible for setting the company's policy on safety. Top 
management sets clear-cut restrictions and regulations appropriate to the type of operation, 
processes, and company size to keep employees at all levels aware of what is required of 
them in regard to safety. Line and operating management are responsible for implementing 
this policy and are accountable to top management. Together they are accountable for the 
safety and health program. The safety professional is the technical expert and can provide 
advice and counsel on potential implementation plans, but does not generally implement 
them.

questions.question: Responsibility for safety in day-to-day operations belongs to:
questions.explanation:
The line supervisor is the key person who plays an important role as the link between 
management and the worker. The worker follows the line supervisor's orders, and each 
worker is responsible for the quality and quantity of their own work.

questions.question: It is generally accepted that the most effective safety program places safety responsibility on the:
questions.explanation:
If a supervisor is held responsible for safety performance, he or she will have a 
personal interest in the program.

questions.question: The success of the system safety effort depends on:
questions.explanation:
The success of the system safety effort depends on definitive statements of safety 
objectives and requirements by the managing activity and their translations into functional 
hardware and software.

questions.question: Relatively new developments in human resources management include:
questions.explanation:
New developments include flex-time (flexible working hours), job-sharing (two or 
more workers sharing the same job), and work sharing (during downtime, hours are taken 
away from everyone to prevent layoffs).

questions.question: System engineers seek to drive down the probability of causing a death to users of a system. What is this probability?
questions.explanation:
To the average person, accidents with the probability of death of 10-6 or less per person 
per year are not of great concern to the average person. Hence, many systems safety experts 
are attempting to design products or processes to a level that is "ten to the minus six" level of 
performance, or one in a million. 
NOTE: the probability of being killed in a motor vehicle accident hovers consistently around 
10-4.

questions.question: The design, development, and delivery of a new product can be called:
questions.explanation:
The design, development, and delivery of a new product can be called a manufacturing 
system. The system incorporates accidental loss consideration involving system integration of 
a Machine/Environment (occupational safety) with subsystems pre-production safety and 
quality reviews (product safety).

questions.question: What is the most critical period in crisis management?
questions.explanation:
It is generally considered that the first 24 hours of any crisis are the most critical during 
the life of the crisis. Management's function is to explain the problem, control rumors, and 
control panic.

questions.question: What is the value of an investment that will be worth $10,000 after 5 years, given that the interest rate during this period is 10%?
questions.explanation:
This question requires calculating the time value of money. Find the present worth of 
the future investment value as follows: 
Use the formula: P = F(1 + i)-n 
P = F(1 + i)-n 
= $10,000 (1 + 0.10)-5 
= $6,209
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Organizations allocate costs into various categories to aid decision making. Often, these costs are determined as a percent or ratio of manufacturing costs. Examples include raw materials, direct labor, indirect materials, selling costs, distribution costs, and other costs. In calculating return on investment of ergonomic controls, a key expense used to determine the cost-benefit of controls is:
options: Direct costs of accidents inflated over time to determine present value of future workers' compensation injury dollars
The cost of capital associated with purchase and installation of controls
Depreciation costs and pretax operating expenses after controls are implemented
Profit and quality loss as a result of increased absenteeism and poor employee morale
questions.explanation:
While all are important, the cost of capital (interest lost from the initial investment) is 
often ignored. Knowledgeable financial managers will consider the cost of capital when 
calculating their desired return on investment of a capital expenditure. The challenge of the 
practitioner is to keep this in mind when determining cost-benefit of controls and, when 
possible, to quantify productivity efficiency and productivity enhancements to help support 
action plans.

questions.question: At an annual interest rate of 6.0%, what must the total return on a $50,000 investment be over 3 years to break even?
questions.explanation:
This is a compound interest problem. If invested and left alone, the $50,000 would be 
worth $53,000 after year 1; $56,180 after year 2; and $59,551 at the end of year 3. 
This is found as follows: 
$50,000 * 1.06 = $53,000 
$53,000 * 1.06 = $56,180 
$56,180 * 1.06 = $59,551
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: It is estimated that the total cost to the country from an OSHA regulation is $20 million the first year and $5 million in each subsequent year. If the regulation is estimated to save 5 lives per year, what is the cost per life saved over a 10 year period, not considering the time value of money?
options: One cannot put a value on human life
questions.explanation:
To get the cost per life, first calculate the total cost of the regulation. 
The total cost of the regulation is $20 million for the first year plus (9 * $5 million) for each 
of the subsequent years. This is $65 million. 
Then calculate the total lives saved. The total number of lives saved is (10 years * 5 lives per 
year) = 50 lives. 
Then divide the total cost by the total lives saved. 
Thus, the cost per life saved is $65 million / 50 lives = $1.3 million/life.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: If an investment of $20,000 is made to buy ergonomic tools, and these tools should prevent $10,000 per year in injury-related costs, when will the investment pay for itself, assuming an annual interest rate of 10%?
options: At the end of the first year
questions.explanation:
This question requires calculating the time value of money. Find the present worth of 
the future savings as follows: 
Present worth of at the end of each year: 
PW = F (1 + i)-n 
PW(1) = $10,000 (1 + 0.10)-1 
= $9,090.90 
PW(2) = $10,000 (1 + 0.10)-2 
= $8,264.46 
PW(3) = 10,000 (1 + 0.10)-3 
= $7,513.15 
PW(1) + PW(2) = $17,355.36 
PW(1) + PW(2) + PW(3) = $24,868.51 
The tools will pay for themselves at some time during the third year. Remember that PW(1) + 
PW(2) is the present worth at the END of Year 2.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: A company's finance department requires that all investments pay for themselves within 24 months. You have recommended that $50,000 in material handling equipment be installed to prevent $35,000 in material handling injuries per year. Will the finance department approve your request, assuming an annual interest rate of 8%?
options: Only if the payback is extended to 36 months
questions.explanation:
This question requires calculating the present worth of the future savings. That is, what 
is the present value of $35,000 in loss that will be prevented each year over the next two 
years required by this finance department. 

PW(1) = $35,000 (1 + 0.08)-1 
= $32,407 
PW(2) = $35,000 (1 + 0.08)-2 
= $30,006 
Total savings after 2 years = PW(1) + PW(2) = $62,413 
Since the present value of the savings is greater than the cost, your request should be 
approved.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: The finance department requires that all investments pay for themselves in 24 months. You have recommended that $50,000 in material handling equipment be installed to prevent $35,000 in injuries per year. Will the finance department approve your request if the annual interest rate is 12%?
options: Yes if the payback period is extended to 48 months
questions.explanation:
This question requires calculating the present worth of the future savings (in this case, 
the accident costs of $35,000 per year). 
PW(1) = $35,000 (1 + 0.12)-1 
= $31,250 
PW(2) = $35,000 (1 + 0.12)-2 
= $27,902 
Total savings = PW(1) + PW(2) = $59,151 which is STILL greater than $50,000. Therefore, 
this request ought to be approved, too.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: In conducting a safety and health audit you ask for workers' compensation cost data. You find the location's experience modification rate to be 0.55. How would you rate the location's safety and health performance with respect to this measure?
questions.explanation:
The experience modification is developed from the location's injury/illness frequency 
and severity rate and the industry rate. If the plant had the same experience as the industry as 
a whole, the experience modification rate would be 1.0. Since this plant had an experience 
modification rate of 0.55, it would be considered excellent.

questions.question: Workers' compensation insurance premiums are determined by three rating systems namely, retrospective rating, experience rating, and:
questions.explanation:
The first step in the rate making process is to determine a basis for potential loss. With 
workers' compensation, it is obtained from the payroll (i.e., the number of employees), the 
number of hours worked, and pay rate. Different types of work entail various degrees of 
hazard. For example, an office worker will be insured with less risk than a machine operator 
based on their job classifications. Similar industries have similar or matching classifications. 
Manual rates are governed by the experience of the industry and are reported annually by 
insurance carriers.

questions.question: As the manager of the safety and health function, you have access to cost data relating to insurance, medical, wages, and operations. How would you determine the total cost of an injury or illness?
options: Sum the insured and non-insured costs
Combine insurance cost for medical and compensation paid to claimant
Determine the direct cost and multiply it by four
Determine the direct cost and add 25%
questions.explanation:
Accident costs include both those that are insured and those that are not insured. The 
insured costs include medical and compensation costs paid to the claimant by the insurance 
company. The non insured costs include time lost by others who observed or rendered 
assistance at the time of the accident, time lost to investigate the accident, time to train a 
replacement, cost for damaged materials, etc.

questions.question: In one year, a company with 65 employees recorded in their Form OSHA No. 300: 7 injury cases with lost workdays, 2 injury cases without lost workdays, and 2 illness cases without lost work days. The total hours worked by all employees is 130,000. What is the incidence rate of recordable injuries for that year?
questions.explanation:
Computation of incidence rate for OSHA-recordable cases: 
= (No. of recordable cases * 200,000) / Total employee hours 
= (11 cases * 200,000 hr/yr) / 130,000 
= 16.92 cases/yr 
The OSHA incidence rate is based on 100 employees working 2,000 hours per year. This is 
the basis for the 200,000 hr/yr in the equation.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: In one year, a company with 65 employees recorded in their Form OSHA No. 300: 7 lost workdays from injuries, 2 injury cases without lost workdays, and 2 illness cases without lost work days. The total hours worked by all employees was 130,000. What is the incidence rate of lost workday injuries for that year?
questions.explanation:
Computation of incidence rate for lost workday cases: 
= (No. of lost workday cases x 200,000)/Total employee hours 
= (7 cases x 200,000 hr/yr) / 130,000 hr 
= 10.77 cases/yr 
The OSHA incidence rate is based on 100 employees working 2,000 hours per year. This is 
the basis for the 200,000 hr/yr in the equation.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Determine the OSHA-recordable injuries incidence rate for a company if the firm sustained 40 OSHA-recordable injuries in a year in which the 750-person firm worked 1,500,000 hours.
questions.explanation:
Computation of incidence rate for OSHA-recordable cases: 
= (40 cases * 200,000 hr/yr) / 1,500,000 hr 
= 5.3 cases/yr
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: A worker can perform a certain task in 16 hours. The part of the task the worker can do in H hours is:
questions.explanation:
In one hour, the worker can do 1/16 of the total task. In H hours, the worker can do H 
times (l/16) = H / 16 of the task.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: Just-in-time (JIT) inventory control seeks to:
options: Minimize the amount of raw material inventory in the facility at any time
Provide line employees with exactly what they need when they need it
Minimize procurement anomalies by establishing standard schedules (based on need) for delivering raw materials/spare parts
questions.explanation:
JIT inventory control also helps to reduce overhead costs by reducing 
storage/warehousing requirements. JIT requires a company to fully understand its production 
and maintenance system so that optimizations can be made while enhancing quality.

questions.question: Zero-based budgeting means:
options: Developing a budget without considering the value of last year's budget
Creating a budget with no basis
questions.explanation:
The essence of zero-based budgeting is starting at "zero", determining which programs 
are critical, and assessing how much each program actually costs. Last year's budget is not 
relevant, except as a data point. True zero-based budgeting sometimes shows that some 
programs are under-funded, while others are not critical or are duplicative.

questions.question: Crew Resource Management (CRM) is a technique to properly use all of the operations professionals on a team to reliably meet mission objectives. It is derived from efforts to make aircraft cockpit crews more team-oriented versus the highly authoritarian environments in which cockpit crews formally found themselves. Of the following, which dynamic human environment is the best candidate for applying the principles of CRM?
options: Offsite incident command staff-onsite incident command staff during an emergency
questions.explanation:
Incident command could greatly benefit from applying the principles of CRM. In this 
environment, all of the incident command professionals have the same goal; however, 
culture, work habits, and other non-relevant issues can cloud the efficient exchange of 
information to meet the mission objectives.

questions.question: Theory X management assumes the following:
options: The worker is basically uninterested in work
Worker must be motivated to work
questions.explanation:
Theory X management holds that workers must be made to work by a set of external 
rewards and punishments. Work is not a natural condition.

questions.question: Theory Y management assumes the worker is:
questions.explanation:
Theory Y management holds that the worker is interested and motivated to work, as 
opposed to Theory X.

questions.question: According to contemporary motivation theory, the strongest motivator is:
questions.explanation:
Current theory holds that recognition of achievement is the single most important 
motivator.

questions.question: The LEAST effective means for involving employees in process safety management at a facility is through:
options: Review and input to the program
questions.explanation:
An individual reward and discipline program does less to encourage involvement than 
employee training, committees, and review/input to the program. The latter three allow 
employees to become informed and involved up-front in decisions that affect their safety and 
health.

questions.question: Responsibility for safety at the operational level rests with:
questions.explanation:
Line supervisors are responsible for safety. Safety management is among the other key 
aspects of a supervisor's job duties.

questions.question: What functions do corporate safety groups normally NOT perform?
questions.explanation:
Corporate safety groups do not normally investigate plant accidents. They frequently 
review the findings, root causes, and corrective actions generated from a formally conducted 
incident investigation, though.

questions.question: It can be difficult to get non-users of seat belts to wear them because:
options: The positive consequence of wearing them is future and uncertain
The negative consequences of wearing them are immediate and certain
questions.explanation:
Since the positive consequences of wearing seat belts (i.e., prevent injury) is future and 
uncertain, and the negative consequences of wearing them are immediate and certain 
(uncomfortable and it takes time), some people may be motivated not the wear them. 

E. Scott Geller, The Psychology of Safety

questions.question: In behavioral terms, safety management can be considered a continuous fight against human nature because:
options: Positive consequences of unsafe behavior tend to be immediate and certain
Negative consequences of unsafe behavior tend to be uncertain
questions.explanation:
The positive consequences of unsafe behavior tend to be immediate and certain, for 
example, more comfort in not wearing personal protective equipment. In addition, the 
negative consequences of unsafe behavior, such as having an accident, are uncertain. 

E. Scott Geller, The Psychology of Safety

questions.question: Why is it a good idea to have a formal safety and health statement of policy?
options: Safety and health should be of primary concern to everybody
It is the starting point for all activities in the safety and health program
It expresses management's attitude toward safety and health
It publicizes the safety and health function
questions.explanation:
The formal safety and health statement of policy is an endorsement of top 
management's commitment and support. It is management's expression of the direction to be 
followed.

questions.question: A good company safety policy will include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
A company safety policy should include: responsibilities, accountabilities, authority, 
scope, intent, and standards. Though accident history is interesting, a company's safety policy 

should not dwell on specific past events, but should indicate management's expectations 
toward future safety-related performance.

questions.question: What is the principle focus of an in-plant medical program?
questions.explanation: The focus of medical programs is on the prevention of occupational disease.

questions.question: The concept of "hierarchy of needs" was developed by:
questions.explanation:
Maslow's hierarchy of needs is a critical component of many management theories 
dealing with human needs.

questions.question: A supervisor's attitude toward safety and health _________ influence on those that he or she supervises.
questions.explanation:
A supervisor's attitude is of critical importance to an employee's perception of job 
safety and health.

questions.question: There are several management theories of motivation, such as Theory X and Theory Y. Which one of the following is NOT true?
options: Theory X - The worker is uninterested and unmotivated to work
Theory Y - The worker is interested and motivated to work
Job Enrichment Theory of Herzberg - Work environment, benefits, and work conditions are all-important
Job Enrichment Theory of Herzberg - Work must be meaningful, must provide recognition, give responsibility, and allow for professional growth in order to motivate the worker
questions.explanation:
Job Enrichment Theory of Herzberg - Work environment, benefits, and work 
conditions are all-important incorrectly identifies Herzberg's Job Enrichment Theory. 

Herzberg believed that hygiene issues (such as work environment, benefits and work 
conditions) are necessary before motivation and resultant productivity increases can occur but 
do not result in motivation. Instead, workers are motivated by work that is meaningful, 
provides recognition, gives responsibility, and allows for professional growth.

questions.question: The process of determining safety goals, allowing supervisors a chance to perform, providing assistance along the way, and rewarding them according to their progress is known as:
questions.explanation:
Safety by Objectives is the process of determining safety goals, allowing supervisors a 
chance to perform, providing assistance along the way, and rewarding them according to their 
progress.

questions.question: The key to effective line safety performances are management procedures that fix:
questions.explanation:
To be effective, line managers must be accountable for safety performance. 
Accountability is critical.

questions.question: In the study of traditional management, the term "Span of Control" is used to indicate:
options: The control of many by one
The number of personnel under one supervisor
The number of supervisors that should be in control
The number of supervisors actually in control
questions.explanation: Span of control is the number of personnel that directly report to a single supervisor.

questions.question: The best way to create acceptable new responses to environmental stimuli is to:
questions.explanation:
Rewarding a desired response is the best way to encourage the response in the future. 

Dan Petersen, Safety Management, A Human Approach

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT generally considered positive reinforcement?
questions.explanation:
Money, praise, and recognition are forms of positive reinforcement. 
Dan Petersen, Safety Management: A Human Approach

questions.question: Total quality management (TQM) is an overall commitment to continuously improve quality performance at all levels. All of the following concepts apply EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Central thinking is not a concept of TQM, although acting as one voice is a concept of 
TQM.

questions.question: Communication means conveying a message and having it understood. Retention of the safety message is best retained when it is:
options: Presented orally at a rate of 120 words/min
Presented orally at a rate of 450 words/min with body movement
Presented orally at a rate of 120 words/min with visual aids
Presented orally at a rate of 120 words/min with hand and face gestures
questions.explanation:
We learn 87% through our eyes and only 7% through our ears. (The remaining 6% 
balance occurs from other senses, e.g. touch and smell.) Also, there are differences in the 
rates of listening versus talking and understanding. The average speech rate is 120 

words/min, while the rate of understanding is 450 words/min. Adding visual aids to an oral 
presentation increases the rate of learning and retention of the message presented.

questions.question: A management technique frequently used to explore options and to determine the most remote contingencies is:
questions.explanation:
Brainstorming is normally used to fully develop a situation's potential impact. It 
normally involves several people in a setting designed to draw out all ideas. The ideas are 
then sorted out and prioritized, and action plans are developed. The unstructured nature of 
this activity tends to produce more creative ideas. A trained facilitator is often used.

questions.question: The goal of ergonomic/human factors engineering (HFE) may be any of the following EXCEPT:
options: Control stresses affecting worker's psychic comfort
questions.explanation:
Ergonomics and human factors engineering in the United States is a multidisciplinary 
activity. It deals with interactions between individuals and their total working environment, 
plus stresses relating to such environmental elements as atmosphere, heat, light, and sound, in 
addition to workplace tools and equipment.

questions.question: One of the current principles of safety management states that the key to effective line safety performance is having management procedures that:
options: Identify and correct unsafe acts and or conditions
Improve worker attitude through education and training
Engineer the hazard out of operations
questions.explanation:
Fixing accountability is based on the belief that a line manager will achieve results only 
in those areas in which he or she is being measured. It has long been felt by professional 
safety practitioners that the lack of procedures for fixing accountability is safety's greatest 
failing.

questions.question: One of the principles of safety management states that certain sets of circumstances can be predicted to produce severe injuries. Which of the following circumstances does NOT apply?
options: Accidents occur by chance and cannot be predicted
questions.explanation:
The old approach to safety states that once an accident occurs, the severity of injury is 
dictated by chance. Modern thinking asserts that certain sets of circumstances can be 
predicted to produce severe injuries. Essentially, we can attack severity directly instead of 
hoping the severe accident frequency is low.

questions.question: In what ways should safety be managed differently from other company functions?
questions.explanation:
The management of a safety program should not differ from any other program - set 
goals, plan, organize, and execute the plan to achieve the goals. The more the safety 
program's goals and management style are understood, the more support there will be for the 
program.

questions.question: What is the key to effective safety management?
questions.explanation:
Management must hold supervisors accountable for the unsafe acts committed by the 
employees they supervise. Accountability produces interest and attention. The result is a 
more effective program.

questions.question: What is the most important factor in accident prevention?
questions.explanation:
The most critical element of any accident prevention program is management support. 
Without this support the program cannot succeed.

questions.question: Which of the following is the first step in establishing an effective process safety management program?
options: Writing a process safety management program
Establishing a company culture centered on safety
questions.explanation:
An effective process safety management program cannot be achieved without first 
establishing a culture in which safety is a priority and is part of the daily routine of the 
employee. The hazard analysis and written program will not be implemented, and employee 
training is not effective without the commitment of the work-force or management.

questions.question: What is the primary reason for a company to institute a fleet safety program?
questions.explanation:
The primary reason for a company to institute a fleet safety program is to prevent 
accidents. As a result of preventing accidents, the number of liability claims will decline and 
insurance costs should decrease.

questions.question: There are similarities and differences between motor-vehicle safety and industrial safety. Which similarity stands out?
questions.explanation:
A statement of management's intent bears the same importance in motor-vehicle 
accident control as it does in industrial safety. Generally, the policy spells out: Management's 
statement that safety on the road is important; the company safety program includes the 
driver; the driver will support the program: and specific safety responsibilities will be 
assigned to management. Motor-vehicle safety is different from industrial safety in two ways: 
On-the-road employees are not under constant supervision as they would be in a plant, nor 
can the driving environment be controlled as effectively as it can be within an industrial 
setting.

questions.question: A generic process of evaluating competing courses of action by examining the dollar costs of certain abatement actions versus the dollar value of the benefits received is called:
questions.explanation:
Cost-benefit analyses are generic processes for evaluating competing courses of action 
by examining the dollar costs of certain actions versus the dollar value of the benefits 
received.

questions.question: A measure of the projected dollar loss per unit (or prorated per unit) calculated by dividing the total risk exposure by the total number of units produced is called:
questions.explanation:
Unit risk exposure is a measure of the projected dollar loss per unit (or prorated per 
unit) and is calculated by dividing the total risk exposure by the total number of units 
produced.

questions.question: The ratio of the risk exposure to the project cost is called:
questions.explanation: Risk exposure ratio is the ratio of the risk exposure to the project cost.

questions.question: If a company is using self insurance to handle risk, the company:
options: Is using the insurance of the employees to cover their risk
Is buying the insurance from a state plan
questions.explanation:
The company is not insured and must "fund" their own insurance plan. Self insurance 
can be used for various types of risks, including worker's compensation, but often the state 

will require the company to be in good financial health to use this approach, or be bonded for 
the exposure.

questions.question: Your company manufactures and fills small propane cylinders that are used for torches, camp stoves, and gas-powered lanterns. This product is packaged and distributed to wholesalers and retailers using a combination of transportation options including the company's own fleet of trucks. Your company is responsible for the:
options: Safe containerization of the product shipped via the company fleet. For other modes of shipment, safe containerization is the responsibility of the receiver of the cylinders
Development of safe containers and transportation specifications for the product
Safety of manufacturing, handling, and storage of the product within the facility, and the safe containerization for shipment
Safety of manufacturing. The shipper is responsible for containerization
questions.explanation:
The company is responsible for safety in manufacturing and for safe containerization 
for shipping no matter who does the shipping.

questions.question: As an effective manager, how would you discipline an employee's first minor safety rule infraction?
questions.explanation:
The most logical way to deal with a minor rule infraction is some sort of oral reprimand 
for the first offense. Ignoring it will not cause a change in employee behavior, and a formal 
reprimand/suspension will likely cause employee dissention.

questions.question: How can a Safety Director LEAST influence line accountability for safety?
options: Put safety in the supervisor's appraisal
Have safety affect the supervisor's income
questions.explanation:
All of the above actions will make line supervisors accountable for the safety of their 
group. However, "putting a supervisor on warning" will cause an adversarial relationship 
which benefits no one. Once accountability is assigned, improvement in performance is 

attained more readily. This is true in any line function. Human nature is to pay attention to 
those things that will be measured.

questions.question: What is the reason that line employees fail to report near misses to supervisors and/or safety staff?
options: Fear of job reprisals from reporting
Fear of peer pressure from reporting
Perception that nothing ever happens to near miss reports
questions.explanation:
There are several other reasons why employees do not report near misses. A critical 
component to an effective loss control program is removing these barriers to reporting near 
misses. Without effective near miss reporting, a loss control program will have difficulty 
evolving beyond reactive assessment.

questions.question: In biosafety nomenclature, which agent Class is the most hazardous?
questions.explanation:
Biosafety agents range from Class 1 (safest) to Class 4 (most hazardous). Class 5 
agents are foreign animal pathogens regulated by the USDA.

questions.question: The color to indicate fire or danger is:
questions.explanation: Red is the color used to denote fire or danger. 29 CFR 1910.144 (a)(1)

questions.question: The basic color used for designating caution is:
questions.explanation:
Yellow is the basic color for designating caution. Applications include: aisle marking, 
"caution" signs, construction tractors and bulldozers, handrails, guardrails, marking for low 
beams, pipes, and projections. ANSI Z53.1 (1967) 
29 CFR 1910.144 (a)(3)

questions.question: The color used to identify physical tripping hazards is:
questions.explanation:
Black/yellow is normally used to identify physical tripping hazards. 29 CFR 1910.144 
(a)(3)

questions.question: The color generally utilized to denote information is:
questions.explanation: Blue is the color utilized to denote information.

questions.question: What color is generally used to identify moving machine parts?
questions.explanation: Orange is used to identify moving machine parts.

questions.question: What color is generally used to identify safety facts or first aid?
questions.explanation: Green is the universal symbol for safety and first aid.

questions.question: NFPA 704 provides a diamond shaped diagram shown for inherent hazards of a chemical. What does the color blue indicate?
questions.explanation: The color blue stands for health hazard.

questions.question: NFPA 704 provides a diamond shaped diagram shown for inherent hazards of a chemical. What does the color yellow indicate?
questions.explanation: The color yellow relates to a reactivity hazard.

questions.question: NFPA 704 provides a diamond shaped diagram shown for inherent hazards of a chemical. What does the color red indicate?
questions.explanation: The color red indicates a flammability hazard.

questions.question: ANSI A-13.1 provides a scheme for the identification of piping systems. What is the standard color used to identify protective materials?
questions.explanation: Bright blue is the standard color used to identify protective materials.

questions.question: ANSI Z-35.1 provides the specifications for industrial accident prevention signs. What is appropriate to indicate caution against lesser hazards?
options: Light blue background color, black lettering
questions.explanation:
Yellow background color with black lettering is appropriate to indicate caution against 
lesser hazards.

questions.question: ANSI A-13.1 provides a scheme for the identification of piping systems. What standard color is used to identify dangerous materials?
questions.explanation:
Yellow is the standard color used to identify dangerous materials according to ANSI 
A-13.1.

questions.question: Rank the order of traditional hazard warning terms from most serious to least serious.
questions.explanation:
