Traditionally, there are three levels of hazards: Danger - used where there is an 
immediate hazard, which, if encountered, will result in severe personal injury or death. 
Warning - used for hazards or unsafe acts which could result in severe personal injury or 
death. Caution - used for hazards or unsafe acts which could usually result in minor personal 
injury, product damage, or property damage.

questions.question: Flammable storage cabinets are normally:
questions.explanation:
Most flammable storage cabinets are painted yellow. In addition to being painted 
yellow they are labeled as Flammable Liquid Storage Cabinets. Some are also red.

questions.question: A fire hydrant painted red on the bonnet and the caps usually indicates that the water flow rate from the hydrant is:
questions.explanation:
Red corresponds to less than 500 gpm. 
Orange corresponds to 500 to 999 gpm. 
Green corresponds to 1,000 to 1,499 gpm. 
Light blue corresponds to 1,500 or greater gpm. 
NFPA 291 - Recommended Practice for Fire Flow Testing and Marking of Hydrants

questions.question: When walking through an office occupancy where the acoustic ceiling was 10 ft, you noticed that the automatic sprinkler heads hung down and were color coded white. What should this tell you?
options: It was an ordinary pendent sprinkler head with an operating temperature of 135ºF - 170ºF
It was an ordinary upright sprinkler head with an operating temperature of 175ºF - 225ºF
It was an intermediate pendent sprinkler head with an operating temperature of 175ºF - 225ºF
It was an intermediate pendent sprinkler head with an operating temperature of 135ºF - 170ºF
questions.explanation:
Sprinkler heads that hang down are called "pendent" and when color coded white 
signify an intermediate rating with a 175ºF - 225ºF operating temperature. NFPA 13 2-2.3.2 
(Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems)

questions.question: You are conducting a formal safety inspection of a manufacturing plant with your newly hired safety engineer. During your inspection you observe an employee, without eye protection, working at a bench installing parts. This is not a hazardous operation but it is a posted "Eye Protection" area. Which one of the following is the best course of action?
options: Contact the supervisor and discuss the situation
Test the skills of your new safety professional by letting him or her handle the situation
Confront the employee and determine "Why" eye protection is not being used
Note the discrepancy and do not discuss it until the outbrief when the CEO and the supervisor are both present
questions.explanation:
Contact the supervisor who has control of the workplace and discuss the infraction. 
Communicate this process to the new safety professional.

questions.question: While investigating a serious accident at your facility, you are approached by a journalist with a microphone. You should:
options: Indicate to the journalist that he or she is interfering with an investigation
Stop and talk to the journalist
Direct the journalist to your supervisor
questions.explanation:
Journalists want the facts, and if you do not give them factual information, they may 
theorize and then collect evidence to verify these theories (regardless of the actual facts). In 
most cases, stopping and spending a minute or two with a journalist and providing him or her 
with appropriate facts is worthwhile for public goodwill. Passing off a journalist to your 
supervisor (who probably has fewer facts than you) will not be helpful. 

For most major accidents, the organization sets up a dedicated public affairs area for 
journalists. If this is the case, you may want to direct the inquiring journalist there; however, 
stopping and talking with the lone journalist is still a pretty good tactic.

questions.question: You are the safety manager in a large manufacturing facility. According to company policy, the safety office must approve any activity that is not classified as a routine operation. This has led to the safety office directly approving activities such as truck loading and unloading activities, machine maintenance activities, and custodial activities. Your chief compliant with this policy is that it:
options: Fails to make line managers accountable for their own operations
Requires the safety office staff to be larger than is necessary for a facility of this size
Requires a huge volume of record keeping and auditing
Prevents the safety office staff from focusing on more important activities
questions.explanation:
If the "safety office" is the final authority for approving these activities, then line 
supervisors have little (if any) stake in the work. The principles of accountability cannot be 
maintained in this environment.

questions.question: The analytical technique called 5-Whys is used to identify:
questions.explanation:
5-Whys is a qualitative analytical technique to identify the root causes of an incident 
sequence. Once the causal factors (discreet human errors and equipment malfunctions that led 
to the loss event) are known, a 5-Whys analysis can be performed on each causal factor to 
determine "Why" the causal factor was allowed to exist.

questions.question: Preliminary Hazard Analysis is a system safety technique that:
options: Allows the results to be presented in the form of a table or logic diagram
Allows the results to be presented in the form of "and" gates
Starts with an undesired event within the system
questions.explanation:
PHA is a qualitative system safety technique that allows its results to be presented in the form of a 
table or logic diagram. See the description in the text. 
In either format, potential hazards that pose a high risk are identified, along with their cause and consequences. In 
addition, for each hazard identified, a preliminary means of control is prescribed in the analysis.

questions.question: The main objective of a Hazard and Operability Study (HAZOP) is to:
options: Identify deviations from the design intent with their causes and consequences.
Develop "guide words" that would best describe system hazard analysis.
Satisfy OSHA requirement of process safety management standard (29 CFR 1910.119).
Apply guide words to safety instruments.
questions.explanation:
The main purpose of HAZOP is to determine how a process can deviate from its design intent and 
what the causes and consequences of these deviations would be. It must be pointed out that the main objective in a 
HAZOP study is problem identification not problem solution. However, if the solution to a problem becomes obvious 
during the course of study, the solution is recorded.

questions.question: Fault Tree Analysis (FTA):
questions.explanation:
FTA is a backward analysis. This means that the accident or system hazard is traced backward to all 
its possible causes. 
Three steps are required to conduct a fault tree analysis thoroughly and accurately. First, the undesired event, or top 
event, is defined. In the second step, investigators develop a thorough understanding of the system to be analyzed. 
This can be accomplished by studying design drawings, equipment specifications, literature, and operation 
procedures, as well as any other source information that may be available. The third step is constructing the fault 
tree.

questions.question: In FTA, the event "source of ignition" as one of the necessary components of combustion must be connected to events "open flame," "static sparks," and "electrical sparks" through which of the following gates?
questions.explanation:
AND gates are used when the existence of two or more simultaneous conditions is required. OR 
gates are used when any of the events leads to an upper event in the tree. In this case, any of the three events 
mentioned lead to the event "source of ignition."

questions.question: In Fault Tree Analysis of a fire situation, air, fuel, source of ignition, and chemical chain reaction are required in order to have a fire. These events must be connected to the TOP event "fire" through an:
questions.explanation:
"AND" gates are used when the existence of two or more simultaneous conditions is required. In this 
case all four events are required simultaneously to lead to the event "fire."

questions.question: If 5 items fail out of 10,000 tested under specified conditions, the reliability of the item is:
questions.explanation:
$\text{Reliability} = 1 - \frac{\text{number of failures}}{\text{total number of items exposed}}$ 
$R = 1 - \frac{5}{10,000} = 99.95%$
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Three components each having a reliability of 0.99, 0.95, and 0.98 are arranged in series. The system reliability is:
questions.explanation:
$R_{(system)} = R_1 \times R_2 \times R_3$ 
$R_{(system)} = 0.99 \times 0.95 \times 0.98 = 92%$
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Two components arranged in parallel have reliabilities of 0.999 and 0.998 respectively. The system reliability is:
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding a HAZOP study?
questions.explanation:
Statements in (a), (b), and (c) are all true about a HAZOP study. Fault Tree Analysis uses Boolean 
logic.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true in regards to FMECA?
options: It uses guidewords to identify deviation of process parameters
Equipment and system failures and resulting effects are determined
Quantitative data can later be applied to establish criticality ranking
questions.explanation:
Statements in (b), (c), and (d) are true about FMECA. HAZOP uses guidewords to identify deviation of 
process parameters from their design intent.

questions.question: In Fault Tree Analysis, the pentagon symbol represents a(n):
questions.explanation:
External events in Fault Tree Analysis are those events that one has little control over. Examples are 
the existence of air, difference in water temperature between summer and winter time, etc. 
Basic faults are the primary cause of the top event. Basic faults represent a malfunction of equipment that occurs in 
the environment in which the equipment was intended to operate. Undeveloped events are occurrences that are not 
further addressed, either for lack of necessary information or for other reasons. Each branch of the fault tree should 
eventually end up in either a basic fault or in an undeveloped event.

questions.question: If a device has a failure rate of $2 \times 10^{-6}$ failures/hour, its reliability in an operating period of 500 hours is:
questions.explanation: $R_{500} = \exp(-2 \times 10^{-6} \times 500) = e^{-0.001} = 0.999$ or the probability of failure 0.001.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: The system safety technique which is a forward analysis and begins with an initiating event and proceeds forward to find possible consequences is called:
questions.explanation:
Event tree analysis (ETA) is an analysis beginning with an initiating event and proceeding forward to 
find possible consequences resulting from that event. The course of events is determined by the success or failure 
of various safety functions (controls) as the accident progresses.

questions.question: The system safety technique that is primarily devoted to the analysis of human errors in the workplace is called:
questions.explanation:
The Technique for Human Error Rate Prediction (THERP), is a system safety technique which can 
identify and analyze human errors in conducting a given task. THERP provides the means to reduce the probability 
of errors occurring and therefore can greatly improve the overall safety within a system.

questions.question: The system safety technique that evaluates the success or failure of safety functions is called:
questions.explanation:
ETA begins with an initiating event and analyzes both the success and failure of safety functions that 
are designed to control the initiating event.

questions.question: A backward system safety analysis technique that visually demonstrates the interrelationships among equipment failure, human error, and environmental factors that can result in occurrence of an accident is called:
questions.explanation: This is a good description of Fault Tree Analysis.

questions.question: The system safety technique that combines the forward thinking features of Event Tree Analysis with the reverse thinking features of Fault Tree Analysis is called:
questions.explanation:
CCA results in a diagram that displays the relationships between accident sequences and their basic 
causes.

questions.question: FMECA is best described by which of the following statements?
options: A technique to identify problems associated with potential hazards and deviation of plant operation from design specifications.
A systematic method by which equipment and system failures and the resulting effects of these failures are determined.
A technique that visually demonstrates the interrelationship among equipment failure, human error, and environmental factors that can result in an accident.
A forward analysis beginning with an initiating event and proceeding forward to find possible consequences resulting from that event.
questions.explanation:
FMECA is best described by statement (b). Also, FMECA is an inductive analysis: that is, possible 
events are studied, but not the reasons for their occurrences.

questions.question: A system has three components. Each component works independently of the others. If the failure probability of each component is F, what is the probability that all three components fail at the same time?
questions.explanation:
Since each component can fail independently, the probabilities are multiplied: $F \times F \times F = 
F^3$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: In Fault Tree Analysis, the probability of a top event directly connected to two events with probabilities of P and Q through an OR gate is equal to:
questions.explanation:
For example, if a top event is connected to two events with probabilities of 0.2 and 0.3 through an OR 
gate, the probability of top event is: $0.2 + 0.3 - (0.2 \times 0.3) = 0.44$ or $44%$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: Which of the following is an accepted probabilistic risk assessment technique that analyzes a system in the context of its environment and operation to find all possible ways that the system can fail?
questions.explanation:
Fault tree analysis is a deductive method that starts with a top event and determines all possible 
causes of the top event. Furthermore, fault tree analysis allows the calculation of the probability of the top event.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct statement of the Distributive Law?
questions.explanation:
The Boolean expression states that the union of one subset with two others is equal to the union of 
their intersections.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: A pump in a processing facility has a failure rate equal to $10^{-5}$ failures per hour. An identical spare pump is installed that will automatically start upon failure of the main pump. The probability that this system will fail in 50,000 hours of operation is:
questions.explanation:
In this case we are dealing with a parallel system. In other words, both pumps must fail for the system 
to fail. Parallel reliability can be calculated from: 
$R_{(t)system} = 1 - (1 - R_{1(t)})(1 - R_{2(t)}) \dots$ 
In this case: 
$R_{1(t)} = R_{2(t)} = e^{-10^{-5}(50,000)} = 0.606$ 
$R_{system} = 1 - (1 - 0.606)(1 - 0.606) = 0.845$ 
$P_f = 1 - 0.845 = 0.155$ or $15.5\text{ percent}$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: A device with a failure rate of $10^{-6}$ failures per hour has a Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) equal to:
questions.explanation: $\text{MTBF} = \frac{1}{\lambda} = \frac{1}{10^{-6}} = 10^6\text{ hours}$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: A pump feeds cooling water to the jacket around a reactor in which an exothermic chemical reaction takes place. The pump manufacturer's test results indicate a failure rate of $1 \times 10^{-5}$ failures per hour. The probability that this pump will fail in 50,000 hours of operation is:
questions.explanation:
The reliability in t hours of operation is: 
$R_{(t)} = e^{-\lambda t}$ where $\lambda$ is the failure rate 
$R_{(50,000)} = e^{-10^{-5}(50,000)} = 0.606$ 
Probability of failure is $1 - \text{reliability}$: 
$P_f = 1 - R_{(t)} = 1 - 0.606 = 0.394$ or $39.4\text{ percent}$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: The following initiating event probabilities were identified as a result of an FTA analysis on a system: Event A: $10^{-8}$ Event B: $10^{-9}$ Event C: $10^{-8}$ Event D: $10^{-8}$ The minimal cut sets are: A, B and C, D. The probability of the top event is:
questions.explanation:
First we multiply the probabilities within each set: 
Set A,B: $10^{-8} \times 10^{-9} = 10^{-17}$ 
Set C,D: $10^{-8} \times 10^{-8} = 10^{-16} = 10 \times 10^{-17}$ 

Then we add the probability of all sets to get the probability of top event: 
$10^{-17} + 10 \times 10^{-17} = 11 \times 10^{-17}$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: A light bulb manufacturer claims a mean time between failures (MTBF) for one of their brands of bulbs to be 10,000 hours. What is the reliability of this type of bulb for 6,000 hours of operation?
questions.explanation:
$R_t = e^{-\lambda t}$ where $R_t$ is the reliability in time t, $\lambda$ is the hazard rate, t is time, 
$\text{MTBF} = \frac{1}{\lambda}$. 
For the problem at hand: 
$R_t = e^{\frac{-t}{\text{MTBF}}} = e^{\frac{-6000}{10000}} = 0.55$ or $55%$. 
This means that the probability of the bulb operating for 6,000 hours without failure is 55%. The probability that the 
bulb fails is $P_f = 1 - R_t = 1 - 0.55 = 0.45$ or $45%$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: The probabilities of two events connected to the top event through an AND gate are P and Q respectively. What is the probability of the top event?
questions.explanation:
For an AND gate, the probability of the output event is the product of the probabilities of the input 
events ($PQ$).
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct Boolean expression?
questions.explanation: All of the listed identity laws are valid Boolean algebra expressions.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: Which of the following is the commutative law of Boolean algebra?
questions.explanation:
The commutative laws state that the order of terms does not change the result for addition ($A + B = 
B + A$) and multiplication ($A \cdot B = B \cdot A$).
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: A system has two components in series, which means the failure of either component will cause the system to fail. The probability of failure for the first component is $10^{-3}$ and the probability of failure for the second component is $10^{-4}$. What is the reliability of this system?
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: The failure curve in reliability engineering is called:
questions.explanation:
The failure rate curve over time for machinery/components typically displays infant mortality, constant 
failure rate during useful life, and wear-out, forming a bathtub shape.

questions.question: The minimum cut sets for the fault tree below are:
questions.explanation:
In order to determine the minimum cut sets, we represent the fault tree by a Boolean equation. 
Step 1: $E_2$ and $E_1$ are connected to the top event (TE) through an OR gate. Therefore, we can write: $TE = 
E_1 + E_2$. 
Step 2: Substitute for $E_1$ and $E_2$: $TE = (B_1 \cdot B_2) + (B_1 + E_3)$. 
Step 3: $TE = (B_1 \cdot B_2) + B_1 + (B_3 \cdot B_4 \cdot E_4)$. 
Step 4: Substitute for $E_4$: $TE = (B_1 \cdot B_2) + B_1 + (B_3 \cdot B_4 \cdot B_4 \cdot B_2)$. 
Step 5: Using idempotent law ($A \cdot A = A$): $B_3 \cdot B_4 \cdot B_4 \cdot B_2 = B_3 \cdot B_4 \cdot B_2$. 
Therefore: $TE = (B_1 \cdot B_2) + B_1 + (B_3 \cdot B_4 \cdot B_2)$. 
Step 6: Using the law of absorption ($A + A \cdot B = A$): $B_1 \cdot B_2 + B_1 = B_1$. 
Therefore: $TE = B_1 + B_3 \cdot B_4 \cdot B_2$. 
The two terms $B_1$ and $B_3 \cdot B_4 \cdot B_2$ are the minimal cut sets.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: The first step in management of safety within an organization is to:
options: Appoint a safety and health officer.
Provide training to workers who may be exposed to hazards on their jobs.
questions.explanation:
Development of a policy statement must be the first step in successful management of safety within 
that organization. This policy statement must clearly define who is responsible, who has the authority, and who will 
be held accountable.

questions.question: Different styles of management have a direct influence on the flow of information within an organization. In participative management style, the flow of information within an organization is:
questions.explanation:
One of the advantages of participative management is that the flow of information within the 
organization is in all directions. In this style of management, the managers have access to better information as a 
basis for their decisions.

questions.question: One of the major advantages of an external safety audit is its:
options: Lack of familiarity with the facility
Lack of familiarity with facility personnel
questions.explanation:
External audits have the clear advantage of objectivity, that is, it provides an opportunity for an 
independent evaluation. High cost and minimum or no follow-up are among the disadvantages of this type of safety 
audit.

questions.question: An employee working for a manufacturing facility is responsible for cleaning and maintenance of a storage tank which cannot support life due to its oxygen deficiency. In order to perform these tasks, the employee must enter the tank. Which of the following is a requirement which must be set forth by the management of this organization?
options: Obtain a permit prior to entry.
questions.explanation:
The management must set forth an in-house permitting program for employees to obtain a permit 
prior to entry into any confined spaces. These areas must be inaccessible to unauthorized personnel and use of 
proper PPE is required.

questions.question: Organizations that pay workers' compensation premiums recognize such expense as:
questions.explanation:
These costs are definite and known to the organization, and therefore, they comprise the insured cost 
of the total cost associated with an accident.

questions.question: The fundamental way any organization's management must function is to:
options: Ensure that the safety and health of all employees are protected.
Ensure compliance with all federal, state, and local occupational safety and environmental health laws, regulations, and standards.
Make decisions and have those decisions implemented.
Ensure that employees have an opportunity to take part in the decision making process.
questions.explanation:
Management fulfills its responsibilities of managing by making decisions and implementing those 
decisions. In order to make sound management decisions, the management must have access to facts and 
information. Management styles greatly affect whether or not a manager has all the right information to make a 
decision.

questions.question: McGregor has proposed two theories, X and Y, describing an employee's attitude toward his/her work. Theory Y states that:
options: People are not generally interested in their work, and external motivation is required.
Workers should be motivated by raises and benefit plans.
People are generally interested in their work and are self-motivated.
It is the management's responsibility to motivate employees.
questions.explanation:
Theory Y states that people are generally interested in their work and are self-motivated. Theory X, on 
the other hand, states the opposite, i.e., people are not generally interested in their work and are not self-motivated.

questions.question: One of the responsibilities of management in safety as well as other aspects of an organization's business is to follow the 3E's principle. The 3E's are:
questions.explanation: The 3E's in management stands for Engineering, Education, and Enforcement.

questions.question: Eighteen injuries and illnesses were recorded on OSHA form 300 in one calendar year. Assuming that the company has 100 employees who have worked 50 weeks, 40 hours per week, the OSHA Incidence Rate is:
questions.explanation:
$IR = \frac{(\text{number of incidences})(200,000)}{\text{actual number of hours worked}} = 
\frac{(18)(200,000)}{(100)(50)(40)} = 18$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: LWDI is an acronym for which of the following?
options: Lost Workday and Disability Injury Rate
questions.explanation: LWDI is an acronym for Lost Workday Incidences.

questions.question: Based on principles of Total Quality Management (TQM):
options: Top management is responsible for product quality.
Line supervisors are responsible for product quality.
Every employee is responsible for product quality.
questions.explanation:
Based on the principles of TQM, every employee is responsible for product quality and its continual 
improvement.

questions.question: In management terminology a flat organization refers to one:
questions.explanation:
A flat organization has few levels of management; for example the management structure in most 
religious or charity organizations is flat. Tall management structure, on the other hand, has many levels of 
management. The U.S. government management structure is an example of a tall management organization.

questions.question: Argyris, one of the most recognized behavioral scientists, proposes leveling within an organization as a solution to his conflict theory. Which of the following statements best describes the concept of organizational "leveling" as proposed by Argyris?
options: Line supervisors alone should make all decisions related to safety performance.
The boss does not make all decisions alone.
Top management alone should make all decisions related to safety performance.
One person, usually the safety officer, must make all decisions related to safety and communicate his/her decisions to everyone within the company.
questions.explanation:
Leveling, according to Argyris, means that everyone should participate either directly or indirectly in 
the decision making process. In other words, leveling encourages a participative style of management.

questions.question: Herzberg's "Motivation-Hygiene" behavioral theory breaks down the variables affecting performance into hygiene factors and motivation factors. Which of the following is an example of a hygiene factor?
questions.explanation:
Statements a, b, and c are all motivation factors. Company policies, however, is an example of a 
hygiene factor.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is an example of a motivation factor according to Herzberg's "Motivation-Hygiene" theory?
questions.explanation:
Statements a, b, and d are examples of hygiene factors. Responsibility is a good example of a 
motivation factor.

questions.question: The machines in a shop are to be replaced 5 years from now. It is estimated that at that time the cost of new machines will be $3,000,000. At an interest rate of 6 percent compounded annually, what lump sum of money must the machine shop owner deposit now to be able to pay for the cost of new equipment at the end of 5 years?
questions.explanation:
The formula for future worth of money is $F = P(1 + i)^n$. 
For the problem at hand: $3,000,000 = P(1 + 0.06)^5 \implies P = \frac{3,000,000}{1.338225} = $2,241,774$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: The present worth of $2 \times 10^6$ five years from now with an interest rate of 8 per cent compounded annually is:
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Your department has decided to make major modifications to improve safety. The cost is estimated to be 4 million dollars that the company can borrow from a bank. If the bank charges an interest rate of 12 percent compounded annually and your company would like to pay the principal and interest in 10 years with the first payment after one year, how much the company's annual payments would be:
questions.explanation:
Using uniform series capital recovery factor $A = P \left[ \frac{i(1+i)^n}{(1+i)^n - 1} \right] = 4,000,000 
\left[ \frac{0.12(1.12)^{10}}{(1.12)^{10} - 1} \right] = $707,936$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: If you deposit $2,000 dollars per year in a bank account which pays 7 percent interest compounded annually, how much money do you have after 20 years?
questions.explanation:
Using uniform series future worth factor $F = A \left[ \frac{(1+i)^n - 1}{i} \right] = 2,000 \left[ 
\frac{(1.07)^{20} - 1}{0.07} \right] = $81,990$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Which of the following statements BEST describes the doctrine of "Fellow Servant Rule"?
options: In hazardous waste operations and emergency response, an employee entering a site must always be accompanied by another fellow employee.
The employer is not responsible for injuries suffered by an employee resulting from negligence of another employee.
One of the principles of Total Quality Management which encourage each employee to consider himself/herself personally responsible for providing service to customers.
One of the principles of Total Quality Management which encourages each employee to provide assistance to a fellow employee when possible.
questions.explanation:
Under the common law Fellow Servant Rule doctrine, an employer could not be held liable for an 
employee's injury if the injury was caused by the negligence of a co-worker (fellow servant).

questions.question: Which of the following statements BEST describes the role of a safety professional within an organization?
options: He/she is responsible for the safety conduct of the organization.
He/she is responsible for both occupational and environmental safety conduct of the organization.
He/she develops the information needed for the line to exercise its authority for safety.
He/she is responsible for identifying and eliminating unsafe acts and unsafe conditions within the organization.
questions.explanation:
Safety professionals serve in a staff advisory role to develop information, tools, and systems that 
enable line management to exercise authority and accountability for safety.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a tall organization?
options: An organization with many levels of management
An organization with few levels of management
questions.explanation: A tall organization is characterized by many hierarchical levels of management.

questions.question: The actual responsibility for safety within an organization lies with:
questions.explanation:
The actual responsibility for safety within an organization lies with the line supervisors (first level of 
management).

questions.question: A linear coefficient of correlation of (-1) between a dependent and an independent variable indicates:
questions.explanation:
The coefficient of linear correlation between two variables lies within $\pm 1$. A coefficient of 
correlation close to 1 or -1 indicates that the two variables are strongly related. A coefficient of correlation of zero is 
an indication of no linear relationship.
questions.exclusion_reason: Unresolved mathematical markup; held for review

questions.question: In linear correlation analysis, the coefficient of determination is:
options: Total variation divided by explained variation
Unexplained variation divided by total variation
Explained variation divided by total variation
Total variation divided by unexplained variation
questions.explanation:
Coefficient of determination is $r^2 = \frac{\text{explained variation}}{\text{total variation}}$. 
$\sqrt{r^2} = \pm r$ is called "coefficient of correlation". The coefficient of determination $r^2$ is a measure of how 
well the linear relationship equation is performed by two variables.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: In a safety program study trying to relate lost time injuries to the number of unsafe conditions identified in a given calendar year, the following data has been obtained: Total variation = 42.95 Explained variation = 21.80 The linear coefficient of correlation is:
questions.explanation:
Coefficient of determination $r^2 = \frac{21.80}{42.95} = 0.507$. 
Coefficient of correlation $r = \sqrt{0.507} = \pm 0.712$. 

Note: A value of r close to $\pm 1$ indicates a strong linear relationship, and a value of r close to zero indicates a 
very weak linear relationship.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: In a normal probability distribution, large values of standard deviation:
options: Increase the height of the normal curve and reduce its spread
Decrease the height of the normal curve and reduce its spread
Increase the height of the normal curve and increase its spread
Decrease the height of the normal curve and increase its spread
questions.explanation:
Large values of standard deviation in normal probability distribution indicate a large spread of the data 
around the population mean. Therefore, the height of the normal curve is reduced and its spread is increased.

questions.question: The deductible part of an insurance policy is an example of which of the following costs associated with an accident?
questions.explanation:
This is an example of the uninsured cost associated with an accident. The insured (direct) costs of 
accidents are those that are generally covered by workers' compensation insurance. The uninsured (indirect) costs 
of accidents are much higher than the direct costs of accidents (by about 2-10 times). Examples of uninsured costs 
of accidents include, but are not limited to, loss of production, OSHA penalties, property damage, and reduced 
morale among employees.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is the most correct regarding implementation of a safety and health program?
options: The cost of preventing accidents must show a return on the profit line or at least avoid expenses.
Accidents must be prevented at any cost.
Accidents must be prevented if they affect the profit more than 10 percent.
Cost of accidents must be absorbed like the cost of any other business function.
questions.explanation:
In cost-benefit analysis, accident prevention can only be justified if the cost shows a return on profit or 
at least avoids expenses.

questions.question: The annual accident costs in the U.S. amount approximately to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Occupational accident costs in the U.S. exceed $100 billion annually in direct and indirect expenses.

questions.question: A construction company has a margin of profit of 5 percent on all its contracts. An accident occurs and the company suffers $10,000 in losses. What should the dollar value of jobs that the company bids and is awarded be to recover for this loss?
questions.explanation: $\text{Required Sales} = \frac{\text{Loss}}{\text{Profit Margin}} = \frac{10,000}{0.05} = $200,000$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: A telephone manufacturer suffers an accident loss of $50,000 in its manufacturing facility. If the company sells its telephones at a unit price of $20 with a margin of profit of 10 percent, the number of telephones that must be sold to cover this loss is:
questions.explanation:
$\text{Profit per unit} = 20 \times 0.10 = $2.00$. 
$\text{Number of units} = \frac{50,000}{2} = 25,000\text{ units}$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: In cost-benefit analysis, the dollar value of all costs and benefits associated with a program must be calculated:
options: On a quantitative or qualitative basis
Based on cost indices for each program alternative
questions.explanation:
Cost-benefit evaluations incorporate both tangible quantitative expenses/savings and intangible 
qualitative factors.

questions.question: A company must sell $1,000,000 worth of its product to recover $100,000 cost of loss from a recent accident in its manufacturing facility. The company's margin of profit is:
questions.explanation:
$\text{Profit Margin} = \frac{\text{Loss}}{\text{Sales Needed}} = \frac{100,000}{1,000,000} = 0.10 = 
10%$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: A television manufacturer is trying to recover from $100,000 loss. The company sells its televisions for a unit price of $300. If the company's margin of profit is 5 percent, how many television sets must the company sell to recover from this loss?
questions.explanation:
$\text{Profit per TV} = 300 \times 0.05 = $15$. 
$\text{TVs needed} = \frac{100,000}{15} = 6,666.67 \approx 6,666$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Overtime work required as a result of an accident is an example of which of the following costs associated with an accident?
questions.explanation: Overtime premiums paid to catch up on lost production represent uninsured (indirect) accident costs.

questions.question: The first step in responding to spill of a hazardous substance is to:
questions.explanation:
Life safety and protecting personnel from exposure is always the top priority before containment or 
cleanup.

questions.question: The evaluation of hazards posed by a spilled substance must be conducted from a safe distance located:
questions.explanation:
Approaching hazardous chemical releases from upwind prevents toxic vapor or flammable plume 
exposure.

questions.question: If a spill that exceeds EPA reportable quantities occurs inside a building and is not released to the environment, you must contact:
options: A person within the organization who is identified in SPCC
questions.explanation:
Spills contained entirely inside a facility without environmental release trigger internal SPCC/facility 
response plan notifications rather than National Response Center reporting.

questions.question: The Shewhart Cycle is a concept which is used extensively in Total Quality Management. Which of the following best describes this cycle?
questions.explanation: The Shewhart (or Deming) Cycle is Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) or Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA).

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the concept of scientific management?
options: The job of management is to make decisions and have those decisions implemented.
Management makes its decisions based on the principle of assumption of risk.
Human performance can be defined and controlled through work standards and rules.
questions.explanation:
Frederick Taylor's Scientific Management holds that tasks can be optimized scientifically and human 
work controlled through strict work standards and standardized rules.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes Heinrich's theory of accident causation?
options: Unsafe act, unsafe condition, ineffective management, injury
Injury, technocracy, ineffective management, unsafe act, unsafe condition
Social environment, ineffective management, accident, injury
Social environment, ancestry, unsafe act/condition, accident, injury
questions.explanation:
Heinrich's Domino Theory identifies five sequential factors: 1. Ancestry/Social Environment, 2. Fault of 
Person, 3. Unsafe Act or Mechanical/Physical Hazard, 4. Accident, 5. Injury.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the chronological order of steps involved in devising a Safety By Objective (SBO) program?
options: Set objective, provide training, monitor the program
Analyze climate, evaluate appraisal system, determine allowable objectives, train, set objectives
Set objectives, provide feedback, provide training, execute, enforce
Determine allowable objective, set objectives, provide training, execute, monitor, enforce
questions.explanation:
SBO sequence moves from determining allowable organizational objectives to setting targets, 
training, execution, monitoring, and enforcement.

questions.question: How much money would you have in your account after 8 years if you deposit $1,000 per year starting one year from now at an interest rate of 10% compounded annually?
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Your company plans to purchase new equipment for a manufacturing plant 5 years from now. The cost of new equipment is $2,000,000. How much should the company deposit in a bank account one year from now to be able to pay cash for the cost of the new equipment? Assume a fixed interest rate of 8 percent.
questions.explanation:
Using uniform series sinking fund factor: $A = 2,000,000 \left[ \frac{0.08}{(1.08)^5 - 1} \right] = 
$340,912$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: How much money should you be willing to pay now for a note that will yield $1,000 per year for 10 years starting next year at an interest rate of 10 percent?
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: If you deposit $5,000 dollars in an IRA account now paying an interest of 10 percent per year, how much money would you have after 15 years?
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: You are trying to purchase a new computer system. The salesclerk makes you an offer to either pay $7,000 now or $10,000 five years from now. If the interest rate is 10 percent compounded annually would you pay the $7,000 now?
questions.explanation:
Present worth of $10,000 in 5 years at 10%: $P = \frac{10,000}{(1.10)^5} = $6,209$. Since $6,209 is 
less than $7,000, you should NOT pay $7,000 now (answer is No).
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: In safety management theory, accidents in the work place are considered to be:
options: Caused by failure of man or machine to perform as designed in a given environment.
Caused as a result of physical, chemical, biological, or ergonomics hazards.
questions.explanation:
In safety management, accidents have both direct and indirect causes. Although it is true that the 
direct cause of a given accident may be a combination of factors ranging from not controlling hazards to human 
failure, the basic cause of all accidents goes back to management failure.

questions.question: The primary objective of a workplace safety inspection is to:
options: Discover situations that are in violation of federal, state, or local laws.
Discover areas that should be included in the employee safety training program.
Identify the probability and severity of hazards.
Identify and correct unsafe conditions and unsafe acts.
questions.explanation:
According to National Safety Council, 98 percent of all workplace accidents are caused by either 
unsafe acts or unsafe conditions; the remaining 2 percent are attributed to natural causes such as earthquakes or 
flooding. The primary goal of any safety inspection program must be to identify and eliminate unsafe acts and 
unsafe conditions.

questions.question: The OSHA Incidence Rate (IR) for a company with 300 employees and 9 recordable work related injuries and illnesses and 600,000 work hours is:
questions.explanation:
$IR = \frac{(\text{injuries/illnesses})(200,000)}{\text{actual hours worked}} = \frac{9 \times 
200,000}{600,000} = 3$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: According to Heinrich's estimates, 88 per cent of all occupational accidents are caused as a result of:
questions.explanation:
Heinrich reviewed more than 75,000 accident cases and concluded that about 88 percent of accident 
cases reviewed were caused by unsafe acts of people.

questions.question: A standard which indicates the end result to be achieved regardless of the procedures used in called:
questions.explanation:
Performance standards only specify the end result that needs to be achieved. Many employers prefer 
this type of standard because of the freedom that they have in meeting the standard. Specification standards, on the 
other hand, specify the detailed requirements such as dimensions.

questions.question: Organizational safety must begin with development and implementation of a policy. Which of the following is NOT part of an organization's safety policy statement?
questions.explanation:
Safety policy statements must clearly define the organization's position in regard to safety issues. It 
must assign responsibility, authority, and accountability for safety related matters. Hazard analysis is an 
engineering/operational procedure, not part of policy statements.

questions.question: Most organizations have two major components; line and staff. Which of the following is an example of the staff component?
questions.explanation:
Line elements of an organization are those who are involved in producing a product or delivering a 
service while the staff elements take care of other business matters such as legal, security, finance, etc.

questions.question: Staff and line members within an organization perform different functions. Line managers are involved with producing a product or delivering a service to clients while staff members assist in special matters such as finance, legal, and security. Safety must be part of:
options: Line element of an organization only
questions.explanation:
The organization safety policy statement must clearly express that safety is part of everyone's job 
(both line and staff).

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the concept of functional authority?
options: Line supervisors are responsible for safety matters in their department.
The ultimate responsible party for safety related matters within a company are the President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the company.

The Vice-President for manufacturing writes a letter to the safety director. The letter states that the safety director can stop any operation that he feels poses an imminent danger to the safety and health of employees.
The company safety policy statement must clearly assign accountability, responsibility, and authority in regard to the functional safety performance of the organization.
questions.explanation:
Functional authority grants a staff specialist (such as a safety director) direct authority over specific 
functional matters (such as stopping imminent danger operations) outside their normal staff advisory role.

questions.question: The PRIMARY objective of any accident investigation must be to:
options: Determine the equipment malfunction(s) and or human error(s) that caused the accident
questions.explanation:
The primary objective is to prevent occurrence of similar accidents in future. Determining the cause(s) 
of the accident is a first step towards accomplishing this objective.

questions.question: The two major types of accident investigation are:
questions.explanation:
General investigations use generic procedures and usually do not require special techniques or 
instruments. Special investigations, on the other hand, require special knowledge such as fire investigation or 
aviation accident investigations.

questions.question: An organization that the management closely follows the chain of command is an example of a/an:
questions.explanation:
This is an example of a formal management structure. A formal structure can be defined as an 
organization that is hierarchical in nature. The formal structure of a company can usually be found on its 
organizational chart. This chart normally identifies each staff member with his or her job title.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an element of 3-E's Principle?
questions.explanation: The elements of 3-E's Principals are engineering, education, and enforcement.

questions.question: "Just-in-time" inventory is used for which of the following purposes?
options: Deliver products to customers in a timely manner.
Ensure that raw materials are available for production.
Reduce quantities of stored hazardous materials.
Prepare a list of hazardous chemicals for compliance with OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard.
questions.explanation:
"Just-in-time" inventory manages delivery of hazardous substances when they are needed on site, 
and therefore, minimizes unnecessary storage of hazardous substances.

questions.question: It is the legal responsibility of management to ensure that employee exposure to airborne hazardous substances is kept below:
questions.explanation:
PELs are set by OSHA, and compliance with established PELs for different chemicals is mandatory. 
OSHA sets these enforceable PELs to protect workers against the health effects of exposure to hazardous 
substances. PELs are regulatory limits on the amount or concentration of a substance in the air. 
OSHA PELs are based on an eight-hour time-weighted average (TWA).

questions.question: The MAJOR objective of a safety inspection is to:
options: Identify and correct unsafe conditions and unsafe acts
Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local regulations
Measure the effectiveness of the safety program
Identify any PPE which is needed in each work area
questions.explanation:
A safety inspection must focus on identifying and correcting unsafe conditions and unsafe acts. 
According to National Safety Council statistics, 98% of industrial accidents are caused by either unsafe conditions or 
unsafe acts. 2% of industrial accidents are caused as a result of natural disasters such as an earthquake.

questions.question: The cost of an injury or illness is divided into insured costs and uninsured costs. The total cost of an injury or illness is determined by:
options: Subtracting the insured costs from the uninsured costs.
Adding the insured costs to the uninsured costs.
Subtracting the insured cost from the uninsured costs and dividing the result by the insured costs.
questions.explanation: $\text{Total Cost} = \text{Insured Costs} + \text{Uninsured Costs}$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: In workers' compensation terminology, the no fault system means:
options: Regardless of who is at fault the worker will be paid for workplace injuries and illnesses.
The employer is protected against lawsuits.
The worker can only be paid upon proof of negligence on the part of the employer.
questions.explanation:
No-fault workers' compensation guarantees benefits to injured workers regardless of fault, while 
granting employers immunity from common-law negligence tort lawsuits.

questions.question: An employee has been modifying the safety and health data after they have been approved by the company safety professional holding a CSP. Which approach is the most appropriate to take?
options: Verbally fire the employee on the spot.
Write a letter to company headquarters requesting permission to investigate the case.
Set up a meeting with the employee and the management in order to investigate the case.
questions.explanation:
Proper management due process requires investigating the situation factually in a meeting with the 
employee and management before taking formal disciplinary actions.

questions.question: Which of the following statements BEST describes an OSHA Performance Standard?
options: Employers with incidence rates of 2.5 or greater must upgrade their safety performance or are in violation of this standard.
Specific objectives must be obtained regardless of a specific method.
Specific objectives must be obtained using OSHA approved methods.
questions.explanation:
Performance standards mandate the required objective or result to be achieved, leaving the specific 
compliance methods to the employer's discretion.

questions.question: A Type I error in the testing of a hypothesis indicates:
questions.explanation:
In statistical hypothesis testing, a Type I error occurs when a true (valid) null hypothesis is incorrectly 
rejected.

questions.question: The Managerial Grid, developed by Blake and Mouton, evaluates managerial leadership style on two axes: concern for production and concern for people. A 9,1 leadership style represents:
questions.explanation:
On Blake and Mouton's Managerial Grid, 9,1 represents high concern for production (9) and low 
concern for people (1), which is Task or Authoritarian management.

questions.question: On the Blake and Mouton Managerial Grid, a 1,9 leadership style represents:
questions.explanation:
A 1,9 rating indicates low concern for production (1) and high concern for people (9), known as 
Country Club management.

questions.question: On the Blake and Mouton Managerial Grid, a 9,9 leadership style represents:
questions.explanation: A 9,9 rating reflects maximum concern for both production and people, known as Team management.

questions.question: Which of the following statements BEST describes the Otis Test?
options: It is used in quality control to distinguish between patent defect and latent defect in a product batch.
It is a graph of budgeting vs. scheduling that measures a manager's effectiveness.
It is used to measure attitudes, preferences, and subjective reactions.
It is a test that evaluates abstract thinking and a person's ability to reason (IQ test).
questions.explanation:
The Otis Test is used to measure an individual's IQ. This is a test that evaluates abstract thinking and 
a person's ability to reason. It is a multiple choice test that focuses on measuring quantitative, spatial, and verbal 
reasoning ability.

questions.question: Cohesiveness in group dynamics is best defined as:
options: The establishing of rules and policies necessary for group operation.
The degree that members of a team or group desire to remain in the team or group.
The ability of a team leader to direct the group.
The level of productivity achieved by a group.
questions.explanation:
Cohesiveness is defined as the degree that members of a team or group desire to remain in the team 
or group.

questions.question: Which of the following statements BEST describes the Likert Scale?
options: It is used in quality control to distinguish between patent defect and latent defect in a product batch.
It is a graph of budgeting vs. scheduling that measures a manager's effectiveness.
It is used to measure attitudes, preferences, and subjective reactions.
It is a site map about accessibility, groupware, and usability.
questions.explanation:
A Likert Scale is used to measure attitudes, preferences, and subjective reactions. For example, in 
software design, it can often subjectively measure efficiency and effectiveness with performance metrics such as 
time taken or errors made.

questions.question: In the Hawthorne Studies, investigators found no strong relationship between workplace conditions and worker productivity. However, the investigators reached several conclusions. Which of the following is NOT a conclusion of the Hawthorne Studies?
options: Sentiments and participation can reduce resistance to change.
The workplace is an interlocking social system, not simply a production system.
Employees should not be considered appendages of machinery.
The Hawthorne Studies opened the door to the study of client-centered therapy, small group behavior, organizational theory, and research methodology.
questions.explanation:
Statement (d) describes general historical impacts, whereas the specific core conclusions of the 
Hawthorne Studies focused on human social factors in industrial workplaces (statements a, b, and c).

questions.question: A company with 5 lost workdays (LWD) in a calendar year and 200 employees working 50 weeks in a calendar year for 40 hours a week has an LWDI of:
questions.explanation:
$\text{LWDI} = \frac{(\text{LWD})(200,000)}{\text{total hours worked}} = \frac{5 \times 200,000}{200 
\times 50 \times 40} = \frac{1,000,000}{400,000} = 2.5$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: A manufacturing company had an LWDI equal to 4 in a given calendar year. The company has 200 employees who, on the average, worked 40 hours per week for 50 weeks. What is the actual number of lost workdays for this company?
questions.explanation:
$\text{LWDI} = \frac{(\text{LWD})(200,000)}{\text{total hours}} \implies 4 = 
\frac{(\text{LWD})(200,000)}{200 \times 40 \times 50} \implies 4 = \frac{(\text{LWD})(200,000)}{400,000} \implies 
\text{LWD} = 8$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: The LWDI for a company in a given calendar year was equal to 5. Each employee worked for 50 weeks for an average of 40 hours per week. Assuming that the actual number of lost day cases was 10, the number of employees working for this company is:
questions.explanation:
$\text{LWDI} = \frac{(\text{cases})(200,000)}{\text{hours}} \implies 5 = \frac{10 \times 200,000}{N 
\times 50 \times 40} = \frac{2,000,000}{2,000 N} \implies 5 = \frac{1,000}{N} \implies N = 200$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Application of water-based foam to a flammable liquid fire has the potential for creating which of the following?
options: High-volume mixture of steam, air, and burning fuel
Phosgene gas due to breakdown of halon 1301 in water-based foam
Large amount of toxic carbon dioxide gas
questions.explanation:
Assuming that the surface temperature of the burning liquid is above the boiling point of water, this 
application has the potential for creating a very high volume of an air, fuel, and steam mixture above the surface of 
the burning liquid.

questions.question: A cab company conducted a study of their accident frequency for 200 days. At the conclusion of the study, it was found that the probability of NOT having an accident is 0.99. This means that, on the average, the cab company experiences an accident every _________ days.
questions.explanation:
The probability of having an accident is $1 - 0.99 = 0.01$ or $\frac{1}{100}$, which equals one 
accident every 100 days.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Management commitment, site analysis, hazard prevention and control, and safety and health training are the four major components of which of the following programs?
questions.explanation:
This program is an optional program and has the four components named in the question. 
The VPP recognize employers and workers in the private industry and federal agencies who have implemented 
effective safety and health management systems and maintain injury and illness rates below national Bureau of 
Labor Statistics averages for their respective industries. In VPP, management, labor, and OSHA work cooperatively 
and proactively to prevent fatalities, injuries, and illnesses through a system focused on: hazard prevention and 
control; worksite analysis; training; and management commitment and worker involvement.

questions.question: When setting safety and environmental goals, the goals must have all of the following qualities EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
The goals and objectives must be realistic, specific, measurable, achievable, and time-bound for the 
program at hand.

questions.question: A coefficient of correlation of 0.95 between two variables indicates that:
options: The variables are almost directly proportional to each other.
The variables are almost inversely proportional to each other.
There is no correlation between the two variables.
No statistical inferences can be made about the variables under study.
questions.explanation:
The coefficient of correlation varies between -1 and +1. A coefficient of correlation of -1 indicates a 
perfect inverse relationship between the variables. A coefficient of correlation of +1 indicates a perfect direct 

relationship between the two variables. In this case, with a coefficient of correlation of 0.95, we can conclude that 
the two variables have an almost perfect direct relationship between them.

questions.question: A company has five plants at different geographical locations. At the conclusion of the same comprehensive safety training program given at each plant, the same test was given to trainees to measure their level of understanding of the materials covered in the training program. Subsequently, the same outside consulting firm to measure the safety performance at each facility conducted a two-month audit at each facility. The audit results were ranked on a scale of 1 to 10, with 1 being the worst and 10 being the best safety performance. The results are tabulated below: Plant Average Test Score Safety Performance 1 72 7 2 67 7 3 81 9 4 82 8 5 72 5 Based on the data presented, the coefficient of correlation is:
questions.explanation:
Calculating Pearson's $r$ for the 5 data pairs yields $r = 0.658$. 
Discussion: The coefficient of correlation varies between -1.0 and +1.0. A coefficient of correlation equal to -1.0 
indicates perfect inverse relationship between variables under study and +1.0 indicates a perfect direct relationship. 
In this case, we can conclude that the safety training had a positive impact on safety performance but that there is 
room for improvement.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: The coefficient of correlation for two variables is 0.95 at 0.01 significance level. This means that:
options: The two variables have a strong direct relationship but there is a 1% chance that the conclusion is wrong.
The two variables have a strong inverse relationship but there is a 99% chance that the conclusion is wrong.
The two variables have a strong inverse relationship but there is a 1% chance that the conclusion is wrong.
The two variables have a strong direct relationship but there is a 99% chance that the conclusion is wrong.
questions.explanation:
$r = 0.95$ indicates a strong direct positive relationship, and a 0.01 significance level ($ 
lpha = 0.01$) means there is a 1% probability of type I error (falsely rejecting a true null hypothesis).

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?
options: OHSAS 18000 is an international occupational health and safety management system specification.
OHSAS 18000 was created via a concerted effort from a number of the world's leading national standards bodies, certification bodies, and specialist consultancies.
OHSAS 18000 actually forms part of the acclaimed Health and Safety Electronic Kit.
questions.explanation:
All statements are true in regard to OHSAS 18000. Also, companies that use such management 
systems are subject to audits.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered to be the best approach in an audit process?
options: When possible, auditors should verify in person that management processes are implemented.
Verify compliance by interviewing the management team.
Verify compliance by interviewing both management and employees.
questions.explanation:
Direct physical verification and field observation of operational compliance is superior to relying solely 
on interview testimony.

questions.question: Which of the following can best achieve impartiality during an audit process?
options: Not having any line or operational responsibility for the task
Understanding the code of ethics for the organization
Setting the goals and objectives for the audit process
questions.explanation:
Ensuring auditors have no direct operational, line, or administrative responsibility for the areas being 
audited guarantees objective, independent evaluation.

questions.question: The following data was compiled after a one-year study at ABC plant. What is the expected cost of all incidents in a given year? Probability Incident Cost 0.15 $1,000 0.20 $5,000 0.35 $7,000 0.30 $2,000
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Which of the following is required to be independent of line management?
questions.explanation:
Safety audit teams must maintain independence from line management to ensure objective auditing 
without conflicts of interest.

questions.question: All of the following statements are true in regards to Pareto charts and the Pareto principle EXCEPT:
options: The probability of risk can be calculated from the area under the curve.
20% of the problems cause 80% of the risk.
A Pareto chart can be constructed by segmenting the range of data into groups.
A Pareto chart is used to graphically summarize and display the relative importance of the differences between groups of data.
questions.explanation:
Calculating risk probabilities from area under the curve applies to continuous probability density 
functions (like normal distributions), not discrete bar-graph Pareto distributions.

questions.question: Which of the following describes management leadership and effective employee participation as crucial factors contributing to the success of safety and health programs within organizations?
options: Institute of Safety and Systems Management
Center for Occupational Safety and Health
questions.explanation:
ANSI Z10 (Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems) highlights management leadership 
and employee participation as foundational pillars.

questions.question: Which of the following ISO standards deals with managing and conducting quality environmental audits?
questions.explanation:
ISO 19011 provides guidelines for auditing management systems, including quality and environmental 
management systems.

questions.question: When selecting jobs for Job Safety Analysis, all of the following are important factors to consider EXCEPT:
options: Jobs that have high probability of leading to an incident
Jobs that have potential for causing a high severity incident
Jobs that are stressful to some employees
questions.explanation:
Jobs should not be selected randomly or solely due to individual stress. Priority for JSA goes to 
accident frequency, accident severity potential, newly established jobs, or modified processes.

questions.question: The root cause of any workplace incident/accident is considered to be:
questions.explanation:
Workplace accidents are considered to be symptoms of poor management (management system 
failures).

questions.question: A project is to be carried out in three phases. The error rate for Phase One is 0.34%, for Phase Two is 0.54%, and for Phase Three is 0.24%. The mean error rate for this project is:
questions.explanation:
The mean error rate is obtained by converting percentages to decimals and averaging: 
$\text{Mean} = \frac{0.0034 + 0.0054 + 0.0024}{3} = \frac{0.0112}{3} = 0.003733 \approx 0.0037$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Which of the following is the most important consideration in developing a data collection system?
options: Ensure that the data is compatible for statistical use.
Ensure that statistical inferences can be drawn from the data.
Define how the data is going to be used.
Ensure that the data represent the population under study.
questions.explanation:
Defining the subsequent use of data is the most important consideration in design of a data collection 
system. 
In the design of a data collection system, consultation with data users and providers as well as choice of data 
requirements must be considered: 
• 
What data items are needed and how they will be used 
• 
The precision level required for estimates 
• 
The format, level of detail, and types of tabulations 
• 
When and how frequently users need the data

questions.question: All of the following are elements of an effective loss control system EXCEPT:
options: Assessment of risks associated with the hazards
Establishment of chain of custody procedures
Development of means to control the risks
questions.explanation:
Loss control systems that do not address hazard identification, risk assessment, and risk control 
means are incomplete and ineffective. Chain of custody is a legal/forensic procedure, not a core loss control 
element.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the most important step in an incident investigation program?
options: Collect meaningful data for subsequent analysis.
Ensure that appropriate regulatory agencies are notified.
Determine the casual factors and root causes that led to the incident.
questions.explanation:
One of the major goals of an effective incident investigation program must be to prevent the 
occurrence of similar incidents. This can be accomplished by determining the casual factors and their subsequent 
root causes that led to the incident.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an element of an effective system safety program plan?
options: Define the elements and their needs for the mission.
Identify means to improve the safety performance of an existing system.
Determine the Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) for the system.
questions.explanation:
The System Safety Program Plan (SSPP) is a critical document for subsequent system safety 
analyses. It must address management tasks, system safety engineering tasks, deficiency identification, and 
improvement methods. Calculating specific MTBF values is a reliability engineering task rather than an SSPP 
structural element.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to demonstrate the difference between actual expenditure at a given time and the projected budget for a project?
questions.explanation:
A budget variance report compares actual expenditures against planned project budgets to highlight 
overruns or underruns.

questions.question: In a manufacturing facility, the management has established a goal to have no lost time injury for 500 days. This is an example of:
questions.explanation:
Setting specific quantitative safety performance targets against standard metrics is an example of 
safety benchmarking.

questions.question: Which of the following statements in regard to incidence rates is INCORRECT?
options: Incidence rates are excellent indicators of an organization's safety performance.
Incidence rates are lagging indicators of safety performance.
Overall, incidence rates alone cannot measure safety performance.
The standard for calculating incidence rates is an organization with 100 employees who work 40 hours per week for 50 weeks a year.
questions.explanation:
Statement (a) is incorrect because incidence rates are lagging indicators reflecting past failures, and 
relying on them alone provides an incomplete measure of safety performance.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of ISO 9000?
options: The ISO 9000 family is primarily concerned with quality management.
The ISO 9000 family is primarily concerned with environmental management.
The ISO 9000 family is primarily concerned with proper management of occupational safety within organizations.
The ISO 9000 family is primarily concerned with the customer's quality requirements.
questions.explanation: The ISO 9000 family standards focus specifically on quality management systems.

questions.question: Which of the following statements BEST describes the overall purpose of ISO 14000?
options: The ISO 14000 family is primarily concerned with quality management.
The ISO 14000 family is primarily concerned with environmental management.
The ISO 14000 family is primarily concerned with proper management of occupational safety within organizations.
The ISO 14000 family is primarily concerned with the customer's quality requirements.
questions.explanation: The ISO 14000 family addresses environmental management systems.

questions.question: The organizational chart shown in company documentation displaying CEO -> Vice Presidents -> Managers -> Employees in direct descending boxes is an example of a:
questions.explanation:
A traditional scalar chart descending from CEO down through managers to staff is a hierarchical 
organizational chart.

questions.question: All of the following statements are true in regard to Pareto charts EXCEPT:
options: A Pareto chart is a type of chart that contains both bars and a line graph.
Individual values are represented in descending order by bars.
The cumulative total is represented by the line.
The left vertical axis shows the cumulative percentage of the total number of occurrences.
questions.explanation:
On a Pareto chart, the left vertical axis represents frequency of occurrence or cost, while the right 
vertical axis represents cumulative percentage.

questions.question: According to OSHA, which of the following injuries or illnesses must be recorded on the OSHA 300 log?
options: Injuries that require attention beyond first aid
Temporary headaches relieved by non-prescription aspirin
questions.explanation:
According to OSHA regulations, only work-related injuries and illnesses requiring medical treatment 
beyond first aid are recordable.

questions.question: Based on the information presented in Table 1 below, and assuming that each employee works 8 hours per day, 5 days a week, 50 weeks in a calendar year, the LWDI for Plant C in 2004 is: Table 1: Injury Information for Company X in 2004 Plant # Injuries Treated with First Aid # Injuries Treated Beyond First Aid # Lost Work Days Due to Injuries # Employees A 25 10 80 400 B 35 15 120 600 C 40 30 200 900
questions.explanation:
$\text{LWDI} = \frac{\text{lost work days} \times 200,000}{\text{total hours}} = \frac{200 \times 
200,000}{900 \times 8 \times 5 \times 50} = \frac{40,000,000}{1,800,000} = 22.22$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Based on the information presented in Table 1 above, and assuming that each employee works 8 hours per day, 5 days a week, 50 weeks in a calendar year, the OSHA Incident Rate (IR) for recordable injuries in 2004 in Plant A is:
questions.explanation:
Recordable injuries for Plant A = 10 (treated beyond first aid). 
$\text{Hours} = 400 \times 2,000 = 800,000$. 
$IR = \frac{10 \times 200,000}{800,000} = 2.50$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Based on the information presented in Table 1, the total number of recordable injuries for all plants in 2004 is:
questions.explanation: Recordable injuries are those treated beyond first aid: $10 + 15 + 30 = 55$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the process of adsorption?
options: Removal of a component of a liquid mixture by another liquid
Removal of a component of a gas mixture by a liquid
Removal of a component of a liquid mixture by a gas
Removal of one or more components of a gas mixture on a solid bed
questions.explanation:
Adsorption is the retention of gas/vapor molecules on the surface of a solid sorbent bed (such as 
activated carbon).

questions.question: Factors that affect safety effectiveness include behavioral influence as well as motivational factors. Which of the following is an example of behavioral influence?
questions.explanation:
Social institutions such as church, family, and peer groups exert external behavioral influence on 
worker attitudes and actions.

questions.question: An employee is recognized by his boss for excellent safety performance. This is an example of an:
questions.explanation:
Extrinsic rewards originate externally from supervisors, management, or peers (such as praise, 
bonuses, or awards).

questions.question: Which of the following statements is an example of a motivation factor according to Herzberg's "Motivation-Hygiene" theory?
questions.explanation:
Responsibility is a intrinsic motivator under Herzberg's framework, whereas salary, policy, and 
vacation are hygiene factors.

questions.question: Being independent of line management is a requirement for which of the following?
questions.explanation: Safety audit teams must operate independently of line supervision to maintain impartiality.

questions.question: All of the following statements are true in regard to Pareto charts and the Pareto principle EXCEPT:
options: The probability of risk can be calculated from the area under the curve
20% of the problems cause 80% of the risk
A Pareto chart can be constructed by segmenting the range of data into groups
A Pareto chart is used to graphically summarize and display the relative importance of the differences between groups of data
questions.explanation: Risk probabilities are not derived from area under the curve on a Pareto chart.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct in regard to OHSAS 18001?
options: Calls for continuous improvement in safety and health management systems
Sets standards to predict the financial health of an organization
Sets standards for proper environmental management and in particular proper disposal of hazardous wastes
questions.explanation:
OHSAS 18001 specifies requirements for an occupational health and safety management system 
emphasizing continual improvement.
