questions.question: Which of the following statements is true in regards to cost-benefit analysis?
options: Cost-benefit analysis calculates the benefits and costs of competing alternatives.
The analysis can be performed by calculating the cost-to-benefit ratio.
The analysis can be performed by calculating the benefit-to-cost ratio.
questions.explanation:
All statements are true in regards to cost-benefit analysis. 
Cost-benefit analysis considers the equivalent dollar value of costs to benefits among competing projects. If the 
costs exceed the benefits the project is not considered worthwhile to pursue. Many components of costs and 
benefits lend themselves to simple analysis. However, there are other components for which intuition fails to offer an 
accurate method of measurement.

questions.question: Hazard and Operability (HAZOP) studies are conducted to identify the deviations of process parameters from their design intent. A team conducts a HAZOP study. Which of the following IS NOT true in regards to HAZOP team leaders or their functions?
options: The HAZOP team leader must be completely familiar with the process and its safety features.
The HAZOP team leader must be able to assist in brainstorming the process.
The HAZOP team leader must be able to document the findings of each brainstorming session.
The HAZOP team leader must be able to prepare a sound HAZOP report.
questions.explanation:
Although a HAZOP team leader must in general be familiar with the 
process, complete familiarity with the process is not a requirement. One of the responsibilities of the team leader is 
to form a multidisciplinary team that is completely familiar with the process and its safety features.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered to be an environmental risk assessment technique?
questions.explanation: All are techniques used in environmental risk assessment.

questions.question: The risk assessment process must be conducted in the following order:
options: Hazard accounting, hazard identification or risk evaluation, risk characterization
Hazard identification, risk evaluation, risk characterization, hazard accounting
Hazard identification, hazard accounting, risk characterization, risk evaluation
Hazard identification, hazard accounting, risk evaluation, risk characterization
questions.explanation:
Statement (c) describes the correct order for environmental risk 
assessment.

questions.question: Residual risk is defined as equal to inherent risk less the effect of controls. Which of the following is NOT one of the three types of controls that are commonly used to reduce inherent risk?
questions.explanation:
Preventive controls focus on reducing the probability of risk occurring. 
Detective controls attempt to identify the occurrence of risk. If detective controls are applied before the occurrence 
of risk, they reduce the likelihood of occurrence. If they are applied after the occurrence of risk, they reduce the 
consequences of the risk. Remedial controls attempt to reduce the consequences of a risk that has occurred.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is not true in regard to a management oversight risk tree (MORT)?
options: It can be used to predict the adequacy of control elements already in place to prevent accidents.
MORT uses similar symbols and logic to those used in fault tree analysis.
MORT does not look at what happened during an accident, but traces causal factors back to management systems to identify why events happened.
It is very effective in identifying the underlying management root causes of hazards.
questions.explanation:
MORT has the capability to analyze what happened during an accident. It 
is a comprehensive, analytical, and disciplined method for determining the causes and contributing factors of an 
incident.

questions.question: Pure risk is defined as risk that can only produce negative outcomes. Speculative risk is defined as risk that can produce both positive and negative outcomes. Which of the following is not an example of pure risk?
questions.explanation: Gambling can offer winnings as well as losses.

questions.question: You are a CSP in charge of safety for a petrochemical plant. A reactor explodes and 4 workers are killed and 3 are severely injured. The local newspapers and TV personnel pour into the plant and want information from you. Which of the following courses of actions would be most appropriate for you to take?
options: Try to tell them everything that you know.
Stay in the background and provide information to management.
Try to blame the accident on unavoidable causes.
questions.explanation:
In situations like this, the safety professional should stay in the 
background and provide adequate information to management (unless specifically directed by management to get 
directly involved).

questions.question: As a safety and health professional in a midsize company, you have established a safety and health program. One of the employees in the production department has consistently been ignoring safety rules and policies. You have discussed the matter with his supervisor without getting any results. You should:
questions.explanation: The best course of action is to inform the personnel department.

questions.question: All of the following must be considered in developing a safety and health program for an organization EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
PPE is not a consideration in developing a safety and health program. It 
is a consideration after the program has been developed.

questions.question: Formal hazard analysis techniques can be divided into two general categories. Which of the following is the correct description of these two categories?
questions.explanation:
Formal hazard analysis techniques are often divided into two general 
categories, inductive and deductive. 
In inductive hazard analysis (bottom up), future behavior is based on experience which is hypothetical, and the 
conclusion is generally more than just the sum of observations. In deductive hazard analysis (top down), future 
behavior is concluded from a number of premises which may be true or false.

questions.question: According to Berlo, the communication process is made up of seven steps. Which of the following is NOT one of the seven communication steps suggested by Berlo?
questions.explanation:
According to Berlo, the communication process is made up of seven 
steps; the communication source, encoding, the message, the channel, decoding, the receiver and feedback.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered to be a valid approach in safety programs that primarily focus on behavior modification?
options: Provide training to eliminate or reduce the number of unsafe conditions.
Provide reward and/or praise for working safely.
questions.explanation:
Training on eliminating unsafe conditions is not considered to be a 
behavioral modification approach to enhance safety programs.

questions.question: All of the following are examples of situations that knowledge of the risks involved may not lead to safe behaviors EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Knowledge of the risks involved in handling toxic chemicals usually leads 
to safe behaviors.

questions.question: All of the following are steps involved in conducting Job Hazard Analysis EXCEPT:
options: Determine the steps involved in each job
Identify hazards related to each task
Quantify the results using minimum cut sets
Determine how hazards can be mitigated
questions.explanation:
Minimum cut sets are used in Fault Tree Analysis. A minimal cut set is 
the smallest combination of component failures which, if they all occur, will cause the top event to occur. 
By definition, a minimal cut set is thus a combination (intersection) of primary events sufficient for the top event. The 
combination is a "smallest" combination, in that all the failures are needed for the top event to occur. If one of the 
failures in the cut set does not occur, then the top event will not occur (by this combination). 
Any fault tree will consist of a finite number of minimal cut sets that are unique for that top event. The one-
component minimal cut sets, if there are any, represent those single failures that will cause the top event to occur. 
The two-component minimal cut sets represent the double failures that together will cause the top event to occur.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true in regard to Root Cause Analysis?
options: It combines the forward thinking pattern of PHA with the backward thinking pattern of FTA to predict the failure of safety functions that could lead to an undesirable event.
It is the process by which the cause and effect relationship of an event, usually with undesirable consequences, are analyzed.
It is a process by which the members of a team engage in brainstorming sessions to find out the deviation of process parameters from their design intent.
It is best suited for predicting human errors by breaking a job into several steps and analyzing each step separately.
questions.explanation:
Root Cause Analysis (RCA) is the process by which the cause and effect 
relationship of an event, usually with undesirable consequences, are analyzed. The goal of conducting an RCA is to 
find a solution that ensures that the undesirable event does not happen. 
RCA uses a specific set of steps to find the main cause of a problem. This gives the analyst an opportunity to 
determine a) what happened, b) why it happened, and c) what to do in order to prevent its recurrence. 
In RCA, the causes of a problem can be physical (for example, a control valve failed to open), human error (the 
technician failed to perform a scheduled maintenance on the control valve), and/or organizational causes (for 
example, no one was assigned to do maintenance and everyone thought someone else was assigned to do it).

questions.question: Which of the following IS NOT considered an essential step in the process of risk management?
questions.explanation:
The fourth step in the process of risk management is management and 
control of the risk and feedback on the effectiveness of the process.

questions.question: In the process of risk assessment, both the probability and severity of risk must be addressed. This can be done either graphically, with one axis showing the probability and the other axis showing the severity, or in the form of a table. This representation of risk data is called:
questions.explanation:
The representation of risk data in graphical or tabular form is called a risk 
matrix. For example, a typical risk matrix plots Probability on one axis and Severity on the other. 
Point A represents a relatively low probability and low severity risk. However, Point C has a high probability and high 
severity. Determining the acceptability or nonacceptability of risks is a management decision.

questions.question: Which of the following techniques is most helpful to top management in placing priorities on corrective actions to eliminate or reduce risks?
questions.explanation:
The benefit obtained from risk reduction must be justified through 
benefits to the organization.

questions.question: All of the following are steps which must be undertaken in a risk assessment process EXCEPT:
options: Decide on who and what may be harmed and how
Evaluate the risks and decide on control measures
The person in charge of the risk assessment process must attend risk assessment training
questions.explanation:
The other steps involved in the risk assessment process are to record the 
findings and implement them, then review the assessment and update if necessary.

questions.question: In proper risk assessment, a cost-benefit analysis must be performed. Both tangible and intangible costs must be considered. All of the following are examples of tangible costs associated with a project EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Energy costs are considered an intangible cost for a project. Tangible 
costs typically include things a business can buy directly for specific costs, such as labor, materials and space.

questions.question: A measure of the combined probability and severity of potential harm to one or more resources as a consequence of exposure to one or more hazards is the correct definition of:
questions.explanation:
Risk is defined as the simple product of probability and severity. In order 
to reduce risk, the probability or severity or both must be reduced. For example, consider an exothermic (heat 
generating) reaction in a chemical reactor where the heat of reaction is removed by pumping a coolant through the 
jacket around the reactor. If the coolant pump fails, heat will accumulate in the reactor leading to a runaway reaction 
and explosion. Installation of a spare pump would reduce the probability of losing coolant flow to the reactor 
because two pumps must fail at the same time.

questions.question: The process of determining the degree of threat that is posed by one or more hazards is called:
questions.explanation:
Risk may be assessed either subjectively (non-quantitatively) or 
numerically (quantitatively).

questions.question: The process of minimizing or eliminating accidental losses by anticipating and preventing the occurrence of unplanned events is called?
questions.explanation:
Risk control incorporates a wide range of elements including worker 
safety. Once the hazards are identified and the risk assessed, risk should be managed and controlled. Engineering 
and administrative measures are used to control risk. For example, use of enclosures to protect workers is an 
example of engineering control and measures such as job rotation is an example of administrative control.

questions.question: The professional assessment of all loss potentials in an organization's structure and operations leading to the establishment and administration of a comprehensive loss control program is called:
questions.explanation:
Risk management's goal is to eliminate or to reduce losses to an 
acceptable minimum at the lowest possible cost.

questions.question: "Risk homeostasis" is a theory that:
options: A person may operate at a given risk level regardless of the safeguards provided
Deals with non-industrial risks such as smoking
Deals with risk of hazards encountered off the job such as climbing a ladder at home
questions.explanation:
For example, a worker who feels he/she is protected by a back-belt may 
attempt to lift even more with the belt than he/she would without it.

questions.question: Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) is:
options: Used to determine the deviation in process parameters from their design intent
A qualitative system safety technique that identifies the consequences of success or failure of safety functions in a system.
questions.explanation:
Fault tree starts with an undesirable event and traces backward to all 
possible causes. Failure mode effect analysis (FMEA) is also a bottom up system safety technique. Event Tree 
Analysis (ETA) is a system safety technique that determines the consequences of success or failure of safety 
functions in a system.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the concept of safety and health "benchmarking"?
options: Benchmarking cannot be applied to ALL aspects of a safety and health program.
Benchmarking does not necessarily require management commitment but it does require employee involvement.
Any information that is exchanged does not have to be comparable with partner's information.
Safety and health benchmarking compares an organization's safety and health performance with similar organizations.
questions.explanation:
Benchmarking requires both management commitment and employee 
involvement. Information that is exchanged must be comparable to the other organization's information and 
arrangements for confidentiality issues must be made.

questions.question: In performing a Job Safety Analysis (JSA), several factors affect prioritizing different jobs for analysis. All of the following are factors which affect the prioritization of jobs for analysis EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Complexity of an operation is not considered to be a factor in prioritizing 
a job for Job Safety Analysis.

questions.question: All the following statements are correct about Job Safety Analysis (JSA) EXCEPT:
options: JSA breakdowns a job into several steps.
JSA identifies the hazards associated with each step.
JSA can be used to educate employees on safe practices.
JSA can quantify the accident probabilities.
questions.explanation:
JSA breaks down a job into many steps and identifies the hazards 
associated with each step and their means of control. This technique can be used to educate employees on safe 
work practices. It must be pointed out that the priority for JSA should be assigned to those jobs that have a relatively 
high probability of leading to an accident which has severe consequences.

questions.question: In conducting a Job Safety Analysis, the priority should go to which of the following jobs?
options: Jobs with the highest injury or illness rates.
Jobs with the potential to cause severe or disabling injuries or illnesses.
Jobs in which one simple human error could lead to a severe accident or injury.
questions.explanation:
A job hazard analysis can be conducted on many jobs in the workplace. 
Priority should go to the following types of jobs: 
• 
Jobs with the highest injury or illness rates. 
• 
Jobs with the potential to cause severe or disabling injuries or illnesses, even if there is no history of 
previous accidents. 
• 
Jobs in which one simple human error could lead to a severe accident or injury. 
• 
Jobs that are new to the facility operation or have undergone changes in processes and procedures. 
• 
Jobs complex enough to require written instructions.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the "Casual Analysis?"
options: To find the root cause of a problem instead of finding the symptoms.
Helps to uncover the facts that lead to a certain situation.
questions.explanation:
Cause refers to a reason. The purpose of causal analysis is trying to find 
the root cause of a problem instead of finding the symptoms. This technique helps to uncover the facts that lead to a 
certain situation.

questions.question: Under what conditions is Level A protection preferred over Level B protection?
options: Where heat stress is a factor.
Where the highest level of skin protection available is needed.
Where the highest level of respiratory protection available is needed.
Where there is a high potential for fire/explosion.
questions.explanation: Level A protection provides a higher level of skin protection than Level B protection.

questions.question: Water principally extinguishes fire by:
questions.explanation:
All four answers legitimately describe how water extinguishes a fire. Of these, though, 
cooling the fuel surface has the most impact.

questions.question: Building fire safety is achieved by all of the following EXCEPT.
options: Managing the impact of fire through building design
Taking measures to control products of combustion.
questions.explanation:
Building fire safety may be achieved either by fire ignition prevention or, if a fire does 
occur, by managing its impact through building design. Ignition prevention is accomplished 

by separating igniters from ignitable materials. The products of combustion that must be 
considered by the building designer can be categorized as thermal (flame and heat) and non-
thermal (smoke and gases).

questions.question: A combustible liquid is best defined by one of the following:
options: Any liquid having a flash point above 100 0F and below 140 0F.
Any liquid having a flash point at or above 100 0F.
Any liquid having a flash point above 140 0F.
Class II liquids having flash points at or above 100 0F and below 140 0F.
questions.explanation:
A combustible liquid is any liquid having a flash point at or above 100ºF. Flammable 
and combustible liquids are subdivided into classes. Combustible liquids are: Class II - flash 
points at or above 100ºF and below 140ºF Class III- flash points at or above 140ºF. NFPA 30 
- Flammable and Combustible Liquids Code

questions.question: A flammable liquid is best defined by one of of the following:
options: Any liquid having a flash point below 73 0F and boiling point below 100 0F.
Any liquid having a flash point below 100 0F and vapour pressure exceeding 40 psi(a) at 100 0F.
Any liquid having a flash points at or above 100 0F and below 140 0F.
Any liquid having a flash point below 73 0F and boiling point at or above 100 0F.
questions.explanation:
A flammable liquid is any liquid having a flash point below 100ºF and having a vapor 
pressure not exceeding 40 psi(a) at 100ºF. Flammable and combustible liquids are subdivided 
into classes with Class I having a flash point below 100ºF, Class II having flash points at or 
above 100ºF and Class III having flash points above 140ºF. NFPA 30 - Flammable and 
Combustible Liquids Code

questions.question: Flame spread rating is a measure of a materials’ surface burning characteristics. Which test is employed?
questions.explanation:
The 25 ft Steiner Tunnel Test, also known as ASTM E-84, NFPA 255, and UL 723 
was developed at Underwriters Laboratories. Due to the need for some method for control of 
interior finishes, the Steiner Tunnel Test was recognized and adopted by ASTM & NFPA as 
an official standard in 1958.

questions.question: The chemistry of fire is depicted by a fire triangle. Which of the following does not apply?
options: Air heat and fuel comprise the three elements of the triangle.
All three elements must be present to sustain combustion.
The combustion process will cease when any one of three elements is removed.
The heating process will cease when the ignition source is removed.
questions.explanation:
An ordinary fire (extinguished using conventional methods) results from the 
combination of air (oxygen), fuel, and heat. Take one away and the combustion process will 
stop.

questions.question: Tuberculation is:
options: Growth of tuber or other organic matter.
questions.explanation:
Tuberculation is caused by internal pipe corrosion and/or a build-up of rust. 
Tuberculation cannot be detected without an internal inspection. Build-ups in valve may be 
an indication that the same is happening within the pipes. Such a build-up can significantly 
change the volume of water delivered by a system.

questions.question: One of the key elements of a good fire prevention program in industry is .
questions.explanation:
While all contribute to an effective program, a good housekeeping program can 
prevent many fires in the workplace. These practices maintain control over many common 
exposures that can lead to or contribute to the spread of fires.

questions.question: Overloading an electric circuit is a known fire hazard. This hazard exists due to the heat produced by the overload situation that can be a source of ignition. Overloading a circuit is a greater hazard because.
options: The heat breaks down the electrical insulation which can lead to short circuits.
The device connected to the circuit can fail due to a brown-out condition.
The heat from the circuit can ignite the insulation of the wire.
questions.explanation:
Overloaded circuits, over time, will cause the insulation to fail, which can lead to short 
circuits and arcing. Arcing then becomes a significant ignition source.

questions.question: A command post established for managing a hazardous chemical spill should contain, at a minimum, all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
A command post is set up away from the spill area, therefore the spill cleanup 
equipment needs to be at the spill scene, not at the command post.

questions.question: How often should direct monitoring instruments used for emergency response be checked or calibrated?
questions.explanation:
Emergency response instrumentation need to be calibrated or response checked (bump 
tested) prior to and after each use. Instruments should be maintained, calibrated and used in 
accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. It is critical for responders to use direct 
monitoring instruments that are operating properly and providing valid results.

questions.question: What is the most effective component in a fire prevention program for welding or cutting?
options: Cutting and welding hot-work permit system
questions.explanation:
A permit system which allows safety professionals to preview all cutting and welding 
work is very successful in eliminating fires.

questions.question: "Design for building fire safety" represents a systematic approach to the six principal types of fire safety strategies. Three of these are prevention, slowing of initial growth and spread, and detection. Of the following, which is NOT one of the other three strategies?
questions.explanation:
Alarming is not a specific major strategy as defined by the National Fire Protection 
Association.

questions.question: Which does a combustible gas indicator best measure?
questions.explanation:
Combustible gas meters, as the name implies, only measure those substances which are 
flammable. Hence, the correct answer is petroleum solvent vapors.

questions.question: A flammable gas detected in a confined space registers 10% by volume of the atmosphere. How many parts per million (ppm) does this equal?
questions.explanation:
To convert any gas concentration to parts per million, simply multiply the percentage 
expressed as a decimal by 1,000,000. In this problem, 0.10 x 1,000,000 ppm = 100,000 ppm.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: A hot wire combustible gas meter should not be used in an atmosphere containing:
questions.explanation:
Silicone vapors rapidly poison the platinum filament in hot wire combustible gas 
meters. Poisoning can occur when silicone vapors are at very low concentrations (e.g., as low 
as 1 ppm).

questions.question: An explosion meter reads 10%. What does this mean?
options: Concentration is 10% of the lower explosive limit
Concentration is 10% of the upper explosive limit
questions.explanation:
Explosion meters read in percentage of the lower explosive limit. For example if a 
compound's LEL were 10%, then a 10% reading on an explosion meter indicates an actual 
concentration of 1%.

questions.question: Problem(s) you may encounter with the use of a hot wire combustible gas meter with a platinum catalyst is that the catalyst may become:
questions.explanation:
The primary problem with "hot wire" type combustible gas detectors is poisoning of 
the catalyst. Platinum catalysts are subject to poisoning by silicone vapors at concentrations 
as low as 1 ppm. This silicone vapor poisoning renders the platinum catalyst inactive. 

A secondary problem that is less prevalent today because of advances in meter construction 
(primarily the coating of the reference bead of the detector with glass), is that un-coated 
reference beads can become "active" with aging, not inactive.

questions.question: An instrument that detects a mixture of flammable vapors when air is passed over a heated electric filament is called a:
questions.explanation:
A combustible gas indicator is the instrument which operates on this principle. A 
Wheatstone bridge is the actual internal mechanism which provides the instrument with data.

questions.question: In some combustible gas meters, an electrical circuit consisting of a series of resistors is used to measure the mixture of combustible gas to air. The resistors are balanced and one leg of the circuit, called a hot wire, is exposed to the suspect atmosphere. If a combustible mixture is present, catalytic combustion increases the resistance of the wire and causes an imbalance. The circuit is called a:
questions.explanation: The circuit is called a wheatstone bridge.

questions.question: A combustible gas meter works on the principle of:
questions.explanation:
The combustible gas meter works on the wheatstone bridge principle. A wheatstone 
bridge is an electronic circuit that is capable of detecting very small changes in current flow 
via changes in resistance from the heat released from the actual combustion of 
flammable/combustible materials.

questions.question: The resistance of a wheatstone bridge ________ when a flammable mixture is oxidized as it passes over a catalyst, releasing heat. The heat causes the resistance in the circuit to increase.
questions.explanation:
The resistance increases. Most combustible/flammable gas detectors use this 
phenomenon to quantify the presence of combustible/flammable materials in an atmosphere.

questions.question: CHEMTREC is an arm of the Chemical Manufacturers Association (CMA) that provides:
options: Hazard profiles of chemicals in non-emergency situations
Information system consultants to the semiconductor industry
questions.explanation:
CHEMTREC is a highly successful program of the CMA to assist in response to 
HAZMAT incidents.

questions.question: Fires have various stages of burning. All the following are true EXCEPT:
options: Incipient Stage - No visible smoke, flame, or significant heat is developed, but a significant amount of combustion particles are generated over a period of time
Smoldering Stage - The quantity of combustion particles decreases to the point where they become almost invisible
Flame Stage - The point of ignition occurs and flames start
Heat Stage - Large amount of heat, flame, smoke, and toxic gases are produced
questions.explanation:
Smoldering Stage - The quantity of combustion particles increases to the point where 
they become visible (smoke).

questions.question: In the theory of fire extinguishment, all of the following are believed appropriate EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Per the NFPA Fire Protection Handbook, all but extinguishment by fire break, are 
appropriate.

questions.question: The level of protection that chemical protective clothing offers is affected by all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Durability is not one of the factors that affect protection levels for chemical protective 
clothing (CPC).

questions.question: Of the following, the most effective way to control heat stress is by:
options: Deploying administrative work practices and controls
questions.explanation:
Heat stress is usually controlled by engineering methods, administrative work 
practices, or by the use of personal protective equipment. 
ENGINEERING METHODS are procedures which may be used to reduce the stress of a hot 
environment. Examples include general ventilation, spot cooling, local exhaust ventilation, 
air conditioning, cooling fans, and radiant heat shields. 
ADMINISTRATIVE WORK PRACTICE controls include acclimatizing to heat, a work-rest 
program, rotation of workers, education, and training. 
PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT for heat stress is ordinarily used only when a 
worker must remain in a hot environment long enough to cause unacceptable high heat strain 
without protection.

questions.question: A one story steel framed factory building with a metal roof, concrete floor, and masonry exterior/interior walls represents what type of construction?
questions.explanation:
A standard classification of buildings into five major types based on the fire-resistance 
ratings of their component parts was developed by NFPA to help prevent confusion of terms 
used in various building codes and by insurance companies. Non-combustible construction is 
made entirely of non-combustible materials that either fail to meet the full requirements for 
fire-resistive construction or are without fireproofing protection for the structural steel 
elements.

questions.question: What category, by property class, has the highest incidence of fatal fires (fires that take 50 or more lives per incident)?
questions.explanation:
From 1900, 98 fires caused 50+ deaths. Of these 98, 68 were in the industrial 
environment, and 59 of these were in mine fires or explosions.

questions.question: The traditional method of describing fire growth has been through fire loads reflected in:
questions.explanation:
Occupancy classifications include consideration for special hazards and ordinary 
hazards. Fire load considers flame spread.

questions.question: Water damage from fire fighting is a major cause of damage from fires. What is the most important consideration to reduce damage from water?
options: The water tightness of the floor
The number and location of floor drains
The use of less water to fight the fire
The use of lifts to raise critical equipment off the floor
questions.explanation:
Floor drains reduce water damage more than any other approach, especially during 
salvage operations after the fire.

questions.question: A tank truck has been involved in a fire. By the time you arrive, the label on the truck only indicates that the material has a pH of 12. What does this tell you?
questions.explanation:
A pH of 12 is a basic solution. A pH less than 7 is acidic, a pH equal to 7 is neutral, 
and a pH greater than 7 is basic.

questions.question: In one type of explosimeter, a series of resistors is balanced and a portion of the circuit is exposed to air containing a combustible gas. The combustion causes an imbalance. The circuit is called a:
questions.explanation:
A common circuit used to measure differences in current flow and hence resistance is 
the Wheatstone bridge. In this circuit the resistances are balanced, then one part of the circuit 

is exposed to an external atmosphere containing flammable gases. This unbalances the circuit 
because the heat of combustion from the hot wire interacting with the flammable gas results 
in a measurably higher resistance.

questions.question: An MFL wall is:
options: An interior partition that acts as a barrier to the spread of fire
A fire resistant wall designed to prevent the horizontal spread of fire
A self supporting wall designed to maintain its integrity if the structure on either side completely collapses
A concrete block, floor to ceiling, wall that protects one fire zone from the other
questions.explanation:
A maximum foreseeable loss (MFL) wall is a fire resistant wall designed to prevent the 
horizontal spread of fire into adjacent areas and by insurance carrier decree, must be self 
supporting and designed to maintain its integrity if the structure on either side completely 
collapses. The MFL wall insures that a total fire loss would not extend beyond the wall.

questions.question: If the flowing pressure at a fire extinguishing nozzle is 75 psi, what is the velocity discharge in ft/sec?
questions.explanation:
The solution involves two pressure formulas: 
- Torricelli's Law for efflux from a container 
and 
P = 0.433 * h 
V = velocity in ft/sec (unknown) 
g = acceleration due to gravity (32 ft/sec2) 
P = 75 psi 
Solving for "h" (head in feet). 
75 psi =( 0.433 )h 
173.2 feet = h 

V = 105.3 ft/sec
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: Which of the following has the most potential for fire and explosion?
questions.explanation:
The range of flammable limits for acetylene (2.5% to 81% acetylene in air) is greater 
than that of other commonly used gases, with consequently greater hazard.

questions.question: Means of egress components in a two-story office building include one 34 in. wide door, a 44 in. wide stairway and a 44 in. wide door. What is the capacity of this exit?
questions.explanation:
The most restrictive egress component is the 44" wide stairway. The component with 
the least capacity determines the egress capacity. 
COMPONENT 
CAPACITY FACTOR 
CAPACITY 
Door 34 in. 
0.2 in/person 
170 persons 
Stair 44 in. 
0.3 in/person 
147 persons 
Door 44 in. 
0.2 in/person 
220 persons
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: If the public water supply at street level is 95 psi(g), what is the gauge pressure at a hose outlet located on the roof of a 50 ft high office building?
questions.explanation:
The pressure exerted by a 50 ft high column: 
P = 62.4 lb/ft3 * 50 ft 
= 3,120 lb/ft2 
Converting to lb/ft2 to psi: 
P = 3,120 lb/ft2 * (1 ft / 12 in)2 
= 21.7 psi 
Subtract this from supply pressure at street level 
Pressure = 95 psi - 21.7 psi 
= 73.3 psi 
NOTE: These are gauge pressures.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Class C fires involve:
questions.explanation:
Class A fires involve ordinary combustibles such as paper and cardboard. Class B fires 
involve flammable or combustible liquids. Class C fires involve live electrical equipment. 
Class D fires involve combustible metals.

questions.question: A motor rated to operate in a flammable/explosive atmosphere is explosion proof due to:
options: It's ability to contain internal explosions
It's being constructed exclusively of bronze
It's ability to operate at the non-sparking point of the fan curve
questions.explanation:
Explosion proof motors are designed to prevent explosions occurring inside the motor 
from propagating to the external environment.

questions.question: At a construction site, an approved/rated storage cabinet may hold no more than ______ gal of flammable materials or ______ gal of combustible materials.
questions.explanation:
An approved/rated cabinet may hold up to 60 gal of flammable materials or 120 gal of 
combustible materials. No more than three such cabinets may be located in a single storage 
area. 
29 CFR 1926.152 (b)(3)

questions.question: Chlorinated hydrocarbon solvents involved in a fire may generate:
questions.explanation:
Phosgene (COCl2) may be generated during the thermal decomposition of chlorinated 
hydrocarbons.

questions.question: Indicate the flammable solvent:
questions.explanation:
Chlorobenzene is a flammable solvent. The other solvents are chain hydrocarbons with 
chlorine substitution. Normally, this indicates a tendency towards non-flammability, but in 
this case a chlorinated solvent is also a flammable solvent.

questions.question: One class of organic chemicals that form potentially explosive peroxides is:
questions.explanation:
Aged ethers can form explosive peroxides. These peroxides may frequently occur as 
visible crystal growths in the ether solution.

questions.question: Which of these metals is combustible?
questions.explanation:
Examples of metals which are considered combustible other than magnesium include 
titanium, zirconium, sodium, and potassium. Fires involving these metals are Class D fires.

questions.question: A fire protection standpipe 110 ft high is filled with water. What is the gauge pressure at the bottom of the pipe?
questions.explanation:
To determine the pressure at the bottom of the pipe, obtain the density of water from 
the OHST/CHST Examination Reference Handout and multiply it by the height of the 
standpipe. Convert the units to obtain pounds per square inch (psi). 

Water has a density of 62.4 lbs./ft3. 

110 ft (62.4 lbs./ft3)(1 ft/12 in.)2 = 47.67 psi 

To obtain the absolute pressure, add 14.7 psi to the gauge pressure.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Fire loads depend on the occupancy and the materials used in their operations. An occupancy that contains mostly paper and wood, such as an office, would have a heat of combustion of:
questions.explanation: A fire load of 7,000 to 8,000 Btu/lb can be expected in this environment.

questions.question: If a fire pump is to obtain water by the suction process, how far can the pump be expected to raise the water from its source to the pump?
questions.explanation:
Regardless of pump size, 25 ft is about the limit a pump can raise water by the suction 
process.

questions.question: When reviewing the effectiveness of compartmentalization as a delay or prevention of the propagation of fire from one area to another, you must consider inherent fire resistance, the details of construction, and:
options: The speed of reaction of the suppression system
The penetrations of the walls and floors
questions.explanation:
One of the major causes of propagation from one area to another are the penetration of 
walls and floor such as doors, ducts, stairs, utility chases, etc.

questions.question: The fire point is the lowest temperature at which a liquid in an open container will evolve vapors fast enough to support continuous combustion. That temperature is usually:
options: A few degrees below the flash point
A few degrees above the flash point
questions.explanation:
The fire point is usually slightly above the flash point in order to create a mixture 
between the lean limit and the rich limit thereby creating a flammable mixture.

questions.question: A catastrophic hazard in large steel foundries that utilize below the floor casting pits is:
options: Loss of power in the electrical system during a pour
Explosions from water in the pit that turns to steam when molten metal is poured into the mold
Pouring metal into a collapsed mold
questions.explanation:
While all are significant hazards, water in a mold cavity can cause a significant 
explosion when the molten metal is poured into the mold cavity.

questions.question: The number of hours during which the required fire flow should be available varies from:
questions.explanation:
The time varies from 2 to 10 hr, although most water authorities place an upper limit 
of 2 to 4 hr on water supply duration because of economics.

questions.question: You have a need to determine the rate of flow of water from hydrants in the area of your building. You have been told by the water department that the pressure, or velocity head, of the hydrant in front of your building is 49 psi when measured at the 2.5 inch hydrant butt with a pitot tube and gauge. The k factor for this type of hydrant is 167.8. What is the water volume?
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: An alarm system that transmits water flow alarms from sprinklers and supervisory signals to a central system that is constantly staffed by the owner's security force is the description of a:
questions.explanation:
A proprietary system is a normally closed-circuit system with electromechanical 
devices used to transmit signals to the central supervisory station located in or near the 
building or groups of buildings being protected. The central supervisory station is constantly 
staffed by qualified personnel hired by the building owner or occupant.

questions.question: Smoke detectors work best where:
options: Smoke generation will be difficult to detect
Smoke will be generated by the products of combustion
There is the potential for substantial fumes to be generated
The products of combustion generated by fire are invisible
questions.explanation:
Smoke detectors respond to the particles of combustion that occur in the second fire 
phase. Smoke detectors operate on lighting principles. When smoke enters a light beam, it 
triggers a reaction; the more smoke that enters, the faster the response.

questions.question: The main disadvantage of most heat detectors is:
options: Their false alarm rate is high
They are slow in detecting fire
questions.explanation:
Of the four kinds of fire detectors in use, heat detectors are the slowest in detecting 
fires. They are widely used because they are the least expensive fire detector and have the 
lowest false alarm rate.

questions.question: Which of the following smoke detectors will accurately detect most fires more rapidly than the others?
questions.explanation:
Ionizing detectors sense fire at the earliest practical detection stage. They sense both 
visible and invisible products of combustion which enters a chamber containing positive and 
negative plates and a very minute amount of radioactive material that ionizes the air in the 
chamber. The movement of ions between plates sets up a small current that triggers an alarm.

questions.question: Smoke detectors which detect the products of combustion are known as what type of detector?
questions.explanation:
Combustion produces products that can be detected by the ionizing detector before 
smoke is visible.

questions.question: Smoke detectors which react to light reflected off smoke from a fire are known as what type of detector?
questions.explanation:
Photo-electric detectors essentially work when smoke passes through the detector and 
light is reflected back into the photo cell of the detector.

questions.question: A water motor gong is powered by:
options: Domestic water lines opened electrically by a smoke detector
Water flowing through the sprinkler system
questions.explanation:
Water flowing through a sprinkler system will power the gong, whether the sprinkler is 
actuated by a fire or has a substantial leak.

questions.question: The oldest type of automatic fire detection device in use today is the:
questions.explanation:
Eutectic metals are designed to melt (fuse) at a specific temperature. A fusible link is 
one of the oldest types of heat detectors, and the heat detector is the oldest type of automatic 

fire detection device. It is the type of fire detection used in most sprinkler heads, auto-closing 
fire doors, automatic lid closers, and some alarms. The development of sprinklers began in 
the 1860's.

questions.question: Eutectic metals are used in:
questions.explanation:
Eutectic metals are metal alloys designed to melt at a specific temperature. They are 
usually made from tin, lead, cadmium, or bismuth, and melt rapidly at a predetermined 
temperature.

questions.question: The type of smoke detector that contains a small amount of radioactive material as part of its operating mechanism is the:
questions.explanation:
Ionizing detectors use radiation to ionize smoke particles so that the particles conduct 
electrical current, thus operating the alarm. The other types listed are photo-electric smoke 
detectors that use light as the basis of their operation.

questions.question: What fire extinguishing agent contains halogenated hydrocarbons?
questions.explanation:
Halon is composed of halogenated hydrocarbons (CFC's) which react with 
stratospheric ozone.

questions.question: What type of closed-head sprinkler system requires a fire detection device in the affected area to activate?
questions.explanation:
The best answer is a pre-action system. A dry-pipe system relies on sprinkler head 
operation to trigger water flow. A deluge system uses a fire detection device but the heads are 
already open.

questions.question: The flowing pressure at a fire extinguishing nozzle is 50 psi. What is the velocity of discharge in ft/sec?
questions.explanation:
Use the formula Q = 12.1

Q = 12.1

= 12.1 * 7.07 
= 85.5 ft/sec
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: All of the following are decomposition products of Halon 1301 EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Ethylene is a gaseous olefin compound resulting from the cracking of either selected 
petroleum fractions or natural gas.

questions.question: All the following secondary hazards should be considered as a result of discharge of Halon 1301 EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Heat is not a secondary hazard as a result of discharge of Halon 1301.

questions.question: What is one of the major decomposition products produced when Halon is used as an extinguishing agent.
questions.explanation:
Hydrogen fluoride is produced when Halon (BrCF3) is exposed to temperatures over 
900ºF.

questions.question: Halogenated hydrocarbons appear to be effective in suppressing fires by:
options: Producing free radicals that consume free radicals that the fire is producing
Suppressing the production of free radicals by the heat of the fire
questions.explanation:
These seem to work by producing free radicals that then combine with free radicals 
being produced by the fire. The elimination of these free radicals then starve the fire.

questions.question: Water is a particularly effective extinguishing agent because:
options: Water is the cheapest of the extinguishing agents available
Water has a high latent heat and expands 1,700 times when vaporized thereby excluding oxygen
Water acts faster than other extinguishing agents
questions.explanation: Both of these characteristics make water effective in fighting most fires.

questions.question: Which of the following extinguishing systems or extinguishing agents are frequently used in areas with electrical hazards (such as switch rooms in manufacturing plants)?
questions.explanation:
Carbon dioxide (CO2) systems are primarily used because they will not create 
additional fire hazards or damage the electrical equipment.

questions.question: A fire emanating from a compressed gas cylinder can be effectively halted _____________ .
questions.explanation:
The only way to really halt a compressed gas fire is to shut off gas flow. Temporarily 
extinguishing the fire may be dangerous if flow is not stopped. The unburned gas can then 
accumulate and possibly explode.

questions.question: The handling of ethyl ether involves severe explosion hazards because of its:
questions.explanation:
Ethyl ether has a LOW flash point and a HIGH vapor pressure. Ethyl ether has a 
dangerous propensity to form highly unstable explosive peroxides when in contact with air

questions.question: On pressure demand SCBA's there is an alarm to let the wearer know that the air supply has decreased to _______ of full.
questions.explanation:
All pressure demand units are required by NIOSH-MSHA to have an alarm to alert the 
user that the air supply has decreased to 20-25% of full.

questions.question: The "hot zone" is:
options: The area closest to a radiation leak
The area around a spill/release into which untrained personnel may not enter
The area where responders and most equipment are decontaminated before entering the "cold zone”
The area where only firefighters can enter
questions.explanation:
The "hot zone" (exclusion zone), is that area around a spill/release into which 
untrained, unequipped individuals may not enter.

questions.question: In responding to a spill of a material that is labeled "ORM-A ", what would be your main concern?
questions.explanation:
ORM-A refers to a Department of Transportation (DOT) classification of "other 
regulated materials" that do not meet the definition of other DOT hazard classes. ORM-A 
materials have anesthetic, irritating, noxious, toxic, or other similar properties that can cause 
extreme annoyance or discomfort to passengers or crew in the event of leakage during 
transportation.

questions.question: A hazardous location, because of the presence of combustible dust requires electrical protection that meets the requirements of:
questions.explanation:
Class II locations are those in which suspended combustible dust may be present in 
quantities sufficient to produce explosive or ignitable mixtures; or be electrically conductive; 
or be ignitable by a malfunction of electrical equipment. NFPA 70 Article 500-6 (National 
Electric Code)

questions.question: When applied to electrical apparatus, the term "explosionproof" means:
options: Capable of excluding the intrusion of explosive gas or vapor
Capable of containing an internal explosion
questions.explanation:
NFPA 70 (National Electric Code) defines "explosionproof apparatus" as, "Apparatus 
enclosed in a case that is capable of withstanding an explosion of a specified gas or vapor that 
may occur within it and of preventing the ignition of a specified gas or vapor surrounding the 
enclosure by sparks, flashes, or explosion of the gas or vapor within, and that operates at such 
an external temperature that a surrounding flammable atmosphere will not be ignited 
thereby." NFPA 70 Article 100-A (National Electric Code).

questions.question: You are a safety professional in a plant that manufactures a flammable, solvent based ink. The wiring in the processing area should be:
questions.explanation:
Wiring complying with Class I, Division 1 is required. This high level of protection is 
required because flammable solvents are used. The vapors can travel and find a source of 
ignition when inadequate protection is installed. NFPA 70 Article 500-5 (National Electric 
Code)

questions.question: If a spill occurs in an enclosed space, and the maximum airborne concentration of the spilled material reaches 18,000 ppm, how many room air changes would be needed to drop the airborne concentration of the spilled material to its TLV- C of 1.0 ppm?
questions.explanation:
C = Ci (-Vw/Vi) 
Vw/Vi= ln [Ci /C] 
Ci = 18,000 ppm 
C = 1.0 ppm 
Vw/Vi = ln [18,000 / 1] 
= 9.8
