questions.question: According to NFPA, water fire extinguishers require periodic hydrostatic testing:
questions.explanation:
NFPA requires hydrostatic testing of water extinguishers every 5 years. The NFPA 
Fire Protection Handbook is a comprehensive reference covering all aspects of fire 
extinguishers. NFPA 10 - Standard for Portable Fire Extinguishers

questions.question: The major cause of fire-related deaths is attributed to:
questions.explanation:
Statistics maintained by the National Safety Council (NSC) and the National Fire 
Protection Association (NFPA) show carbon monoxide to be the leading cause of fire-related 
deaths. Carbon monoxide, a gas, inhibits blood cells from carrying oxygen to the body 
tissues.

questions.question: What is the leading source of industrial fires?
questions.explanation:
In an analysis of 25,000 industrial fires reported to FM from 1968-77, electrical 
malfunctions were the leading cause of industrial fire.

questions.question: Which activity requires the higher level of personal protection?
questions.explanation:
The potential exposure during spill stoppage is greater since the situation is not 
controlled and the responder has to go to the source of the spill, which may have the greatest 
exposure potential.

questions.question: EPA specifies levels of protection for chemical protective clothing. One ensemble includes liquid-splash protective suit, pressure-demand full face piece SCBA, inner chemical resistant gloves, chemical resistant safety boots, two-way radio, hard hat. This is an example of what level?
questions.explanation:
Level A is more stringent than Level B in that a vapor protective suit is required 
instead of a liquid-splash protective suit.

questions.question: The products produced when water is electrolyzed are:
questions.explanation:
A controlled electrical charge on a container of water will convert the water to 
hydrogen gas (H2) and oxygen gas (O2).

questions.question: In the treatment of cyanide poisoning which of the following is administered first?
questions.explanation:
Administration of sodium nitrite results in the formation of methemoglobin, which acts 
as a competitor of cytochrome a3 for cyanide. Since the affinity of methemoglobin for 
cyanide is greater than for cytochrome a3, the result is dissociation of the cyanide-
cytochrome complex and resumption of oxidative metabolism. Sodium thiosulfate converts 
cyanide to thiocyanate.

questions.question: At a distance of 5 miles, an office building has an angle of elevation of 2º (neglecting the curvature of the earth). Find the height of the building.
questions.explanation:
5 miles is equal to 26,400 ft. 
Draw a right triangle. 
Tan 2º= Opposite side / Adjacent side 
= Opp / 26,400 ft 
Opposite side = tan 2º * 26,400 ft 
= 922 ft
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: An instantaneous exposure excursion to ammonia ranging up to 250 ppm should:
options: Not be considered when the TWA is calculated
Be regarded as a measurement artifact
questions.explanation:
An excursion of this magnitude for a fast acting irritant would be considered 
unacceptable. For more information see the ACGIH TLVs and BEIs publication.

questions.question: Given a challenge atmosphere of 150 ppm and a quantitative fit test result of 3 ppm measured inside the respirator, what is the protection factor (PF) for that respirator?
questions.explanation:
To calculate the PF: 
PF = outside concentration / inside concentration 
PF = 150 ppm / 3 ppm 
= 50
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: A closed 500 l cylinder holds a gas at 200 psi(a) at 20ºC. If the cylinder is involved in a fire and increases in temperature to 260ºC, what is the gas pressure in the cylinder assuming an ideal gas?
questions.explanation:
(P1 V1) / T1 = (P2V2) / T2 
Remember to use absolute temperatures. 
(200 psi * 500 l) / 293ºK = (P2 * 500 l) / 533ºK 
P2 = 364 psi
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: A chemical with a molecular weight of 88 evaporates from a chemical process. Where would it most likely accumulate?
questions.explanation:
For gases, density is proportional to molecular weight. Air has an approximate 
molecular weight of 29. Therefore the gas should sink.

questions.question: The reaction of oxygen and organic compounds yielding sudden and rapid combustion is known as a:
questions.explanation:
A hypergolic reaction is a violent reaction occurring when a fuel and oxidizer are 
mixed. The mixing of liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen is also an example of this reaction.

questions.question: If the velocity of a reaction through the reacting material reaches sonic or supersonic speed, the reaction is called a:
questions.explanation:
The explosion that results when the velocity of reaction through the reacting material 
reaches sonic or supersonic speed is called a detonation.

questions.question: A sudden and violent release of large amounts of gas is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An explosion is the sudden and violent release of large amounts of gas.

questions.question: Which hydrocarbon has the lowest auto-ignition temperature?
questions.explanation: Decane is the hydrocarbon with the lowest auto-ignition temperature.

questions.question: Flammable limits and range is defined as:
options: The range in which flammable liquids cannot ignite
The range in which flammable liquids can auto-ignite
The range in which liquids form flammable mixtures with maximum concentrations of vapor in air or oxygen
The range in which gases or vapors form flammable mixtures with air or oxygen
questions.explanation:
Flammable limits and range is defined as the range in which gases or vapors form 
flammable mixtures with air or oxygen. There is a minimum concentration of vapor in air or 
oxygen below which propagation of flame does not occur on contact with a source of 
ignition.

questions.question: The vapor-air density is defined as:
options: The weight of a vapor-air mixture resulting from the vaporization of a flammable liquid at equilibrium temperature and pressure conditions as compared with the weight of an equal volume of air under the same conditions
The weight of a volume of a pure gas compared to the weight of an equal volume of dry air at the same temperature and pressure
The density of a solid or liquid substance is the ratio of the weight of the substance to the weight of the same volume of another substance
A hazard which exists wherever material that will burn or oxidize readily is available
questions.explanation:
The vapor-air density is defined as the weight of a vapor-air mixture resulting from the 
vaporization of a flammable liquid at equilibrium temperature and pressure conditions as 
compared with the weight of an equal volume of air under the same conditions.

questions.question: Methane (CH4) is composed of carbon (atomic weight of 12.011 g/mol) and hydrogen (atomic weight of 1.008 g/mol).What is the molecular weight of methane?
questions.explanation:
One carbon atom (12.011 g/mol * 1) + four hydrogen atoms (1.008 g/mol * 4) = a 
molecular weight of 16.043 g/mol.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Methane (CH4) is composed of carbon (atomic weight of 12.011 g/mol) and hydrogen (atomic weight of 1.008 g/mol).What is the specific gravity of methane?
questions.explanation:
Molecular weight of methane is: 
MW = (1 * 12.011 g/mol) + (4 * 1.008 g/mol) 
= 16.043 g/mol 
SG = MW of substance / MW of air 
= (16.043 g/mol) / (29 g/mol) 
= 0.5532 

(A molecular weight of 29 is used for air. This is the weighted average of the gaseous 
components of air.)
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Methane (CH4) is composed of carbon (atomic weight of 12.011 g/mol) and hydrogen (atomic weight of 1.008 g/mol).What is a primary concern, from a fire safety viewpoint, in large spills of liquid methane?
options: The gas has a specific gravity of less than 1.0 which will cause it to rise rapidly
The gas will spread over a wide area with little dilution
The gas will dilute quickly to reach its explosive concentration
questions.explanation:
Even though the specific gravity is less than one, when spilled in large quantities, the 
gas is cryogenic (cold) making it heavier than air. As the gas warms, it will spread over a 
wide area with little dilution.

questions.question: Find the vapor-specific gravity at 100ºF and atmospheric pressure for a flammable liquid which has a specific gravity of 2.3, and has a vapor pressure at 100ºF of 3.0 in Hg.
questions.explanation:
vasg = (ps)/P + (P - p)/P 
Where: 
p = vapor pressure of the liquid 
s = specific gravity of the liquid 
P = the pressure of one atmosphere in the same units as "p" 
1 atm = 29.92 in Hg 
vasg = [(3.0 in Hg * 2.3) / 29.92 in Hg] + [(29.92 in Hg - 3.0 in Hg) / 29.92 in Hg] = 0.2306 
+ 0.8997 = 1.1303
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: How many kilowatts are required to raise 1 lb of water 1ºF in 1 sec?
questions.explanation:
1 Btu is the heat required to raise 1 lb of water 1ºF. 
1 Btu = 2.930 x 10-4 kW-hr 
There are 3,600 seconds in an hour. 
(2.930 x 10-4 kW-hr)(3,600 sec/hr) = 1.054 kW
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: An explosion of hydrogen in a battery recharging area is an example of a propagating reaction. Such a reaction is always:
questions.explanation: Propagating reactions always require a source of ignition and are therefore exothermic.

questions.question: The term combustion usually refers to an exothermic, or heat producing, chemical reaction of a substance and:
options: A substance with a similar molecular weight
questions.explanation: Oxygen is required to support conventional combustion

questions.question: Water reactive materials are:
options: Materials that are chemically reactive with water
Materials that are chemically reactive with water while being heated
Materials that are chemically reactive with water under pressure
Materials that are chemically reactive with water while being heated under pressure
questions.explanation:
Water reactivity describes the sensitivity of materials to water without requiring heat 
or confinement.

questions.question: Decontamination procedures include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Incineration is a form of disposal, not decontamination.

questions.question: The decontamination stations should be set up in:
options: Between the warm zone and the hot zone
questions.explanation:
Decontamination stations should be set up in the warm zone, which is the area between 
the contaminated area (hot zone) and the cold zone, where contamination should not occur. 
The decontamination line is the last point where decontamination will occur, at the entrance 
to the cold zone from the warm zone.

questions.question: In responding to a spill of hazardous materials, which of the following is NOT a good source of information for prompt hazard recognition?
questions.explanation: The hazardous waste manifest does not contain hazard information.

questions.question: If the identity of the material in a pipe were unknown, one could determine the hazard of the pipe material by referring to all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Other employees familiar with the processes
questions.explanation: The MSDS can only be used if the identity is already known.

questions.question: The skill of prompt hazard recognition is so important because:
options: The responders can protect themselves and others
It allows plant management to understand the situation
Communication with the media is most efficient
questions.explanation: The first concern is the health and safety of the responder.

questions.question: Under what circumstances would you want to designate a decontamination team for a spill response?
options: Only with spills greater than 55 gallons
Only with spills greater than 25 gallons
Only in catastrophic spills greater than 1,000 gallons
questions.explanation:
In very simple defensive measures, decontamination may not be necessary, but 
typically at least one person should be assigned this responsibility for spill response 
situations.

questions.question: The first physiological signs of exposure to an oxygen-deficient atmosphere are increased rate and depth of breathing. This condition is called:
questions.explanation:
Hypoxia, the first physiologic sign of an oxygen deficiency, is characterized by an 
increased rate and depth of breathing.

questions.question: The first consideration when you are the first person approaching an active spill is:
questions.explanation:
The first consideration for first responders is their own safety and that of others. They 
are to determine what needs to be done to protect people.

questions.question: Supplied air respirators (SAR's) can be used in IDLH atmospheres under any of the listed conditions EXCEPT:
options: Employee is equipped with auxiliary escape air
Supply line are less than 300 ft in length
Maximum inlet air pressure is less than 125 psi(g)
Airflow into the face piece is 3 cfm
questions.explanation: NIOSH respirator requirements require a face piece air flow rate of 4 cfm.

questions.question: A respirator that uses various chemical substances to purify inhaled air which contains certain contaminant gases and vapors is defined as a:
questions.explanation:
A chemical cartridge air-purifying respirator is a respirator that uses various chemical 
substances to purify inhaled air which contains certain contaminant gases and vapors.

questions.question: Protective garment materials have all of the following general considerations EXCEPT:
options: They are permeable to some degree
They are resistant to all chemicals
Some chemicals have no acceptable garment
No single material is resistant to all chemicals
questions.explanation:
There is no material that can protect against all chemicals due to the many different 
chemical forms that are used in today's manufacturing. All materials have some level of 
permeation.

questions.question: What is permeation?
options: A chemical's ability to pass through a material
A chemical's ability to dissolve another material
A chemical's ability to pass through living tissue
questions.explanation: Permeation is a chemical's ability to pass through a material.

questions.question: Chemical protective clothing (CPC) can introduce all of the following hazards to an emergency responder EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
CPC can cause discomfort to the wearer, especially heat stress, and many 
physiological stresses during use. An SCBA is worn which supplies Grade D breathing air.

questions.question: An oil refinery worker was attempting to repair a pipe from which gas had been escaping. He became dizzy, noticed a pressure in his head, and then passed out. A fellow worker who went to his aid was also rendered unconscious. Both victims began convulsing and were hospitalized. The first victim appeared to be recovering but at approximately 72 hours after the exposure, developed severe pulmonary edema and died. The second victim recovered completely within 36 hours and was back at work within a week without lasting effect. What is the most logical chemical agent to cause this?
questions.explanation:
The most logical choice, given the fact that the incident takes place in an oil refinery, 
is hydrogen sulfide poisoning. Hydrogen sulfide interferes with cytochrome oxidase leading 
to tissue hypoxia.

questions.question: A semiconductor operator is exposed to a variety of agents when a diffusion furnace tube explodes during a process step. Upon admittance to the emergency room, the unconscious worker is found to have a bronze hue to his skin. Subsequent lab test indicate a number of lysed red blood cells. What is the causative agent?
questions.explanation:
The lysed red blood cells and bronze hue of the skin is highly indicative of arsine 
poisoning. This gas breaks apart the red blood cell. It is an extremely toxic chemical.

questions.question: Several young male agriculture pesticide formulation workers complained to the company physician about an inability to have children. Medical examination revealed little or no sperm and the decrease or loss of spermatogenic cells. What is the likely chemical cause?
questions.explanation:
1,2-dibromo-3-chloropropane (DBCP) is a potent male reproductive toxin. It is also a 
suspect human carcinogen.

questions.question: A biotechnology technician dropped a bottle of compound X and saturated his right leg, the right side of his stomach and his chest. Fellow employees removed his shirt and washed his upper body. The technician then walked across the street to a physician's office. However within 15 minutes of arriving, the technician collapsed and died. Subsequent autopsy revealed first and second degree burns on his body's right side. There was edema of both lungs, kidneys, pancreas, and spleen. What was the agent?
questions.explanation:
Phenol is a systemic poison absorbed through the skin. The removal of the shirt and 
subsequent washing of the chest did not remove the phenol from the victim's lower body and 
a subsequent acute poisoning occurred.

questions.question: How long should eyes or skin be flushed immediately after exposure to a hazardous chemical?
questions.explanation: A general rule is to wash with copious amounts of water for at least 15 minutes.

questions.question: Which group of specially trained employees, who have been delegated by their employer, are most qualified to respond to an emergency in which a drum of hazardous substance has ruptured?
questions.explanation:
The HAZMAT team has been given the proper training that covers the necessary 
information to control and handle chemical substances, spills, and leaks safely, including 
information on the proper personal protective equipment and procedures that safeguard 

employees against hazards and toxic substances exposure. In this example, the only choice 
that explicitly has the required knowledge would be the HAZMAT team - hazardous 
materials response team.

questions.question: What type of canister respirator would you use if you were working in a parking garage with a gas fired engine?
questions.explanation:
Gas fired engines emit carbon monoxide as a by-product; the correct canister color for 
carbon monoxide is blue. Black is for organic vapors, green is for ammonia, and red is for all 
types of contaminants.

questions.question: The movement of liquids or vapors through a garment material that occurs on a molecular level is called:
questions.explanation:
Permeation involves sorption of the chemical into the surface of the material, diffusion 
through the material, and desorption on the opposite side. Penetration is the passage of 
vapors or liquids through zippers, seams, holes, etc.

questions.question: A one pound cylinder of Cl2 (chlorine) fell off a lab bench and broke. The contents leaked into a sealed room of 60 ft x 30 ft x 15 ft. What is the concentration if the lab is at STP?
questions.explanation:
First calculate the volume of the room. 
Vol = 27,000 ft3 (one ft3 is equal to 28.3 l) 
= 764,640 l 
Next calculate the mass of chlorine released. 
1 lb Cl2 = 454.5 g Cl2 
The molecular weight of Cl2 is 71 g/mol 
454.5 g(1 mol/71 g) = 6.4 mol 
6.4 moles(22.4 l/mole) = 143.4 l Cl2 
ppm = Va/Vb x 106 (gives the concentration in ppm where Vb is the volume of the room) 
= (143.4 l Cl2 / 764,460 l) x 106 ppm/l 
= 187.5 ppm Cl2
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: What is the dose of a chemical called that will kill 100% of the test animals?
questions.explanation:
The common terminology for this chemical dose is LD100 (i.e., the lethal dose for 
100% of animals tested).

questions.question: The minimum temperature at which a liquid gives off sufficient vapor to form an ignitable mixture with air near the surface of the liquid is called the:
questions.explanation:
The auto ignition temperature is the temperature at which the liquid will self ignite 
with no external spark, and is used to determine the flash point. The ignition point is not a 

"defined" fire term. The fire point is similar to the flash point except that the flammable 
substance is able to sustain self burning without a continued spark or ignition source.

questions.question: Reducing the oxygen concentration and raising the heat capacity of the atmosphere is the primary extinguishing mechanism of:
questions.explanation:
Carbon dioxide also works like inert agents to extinguish a fire. Halocarbons work 
through inhibiting the chain reaction of the fire process. Halon is banned for new 
installations. Wet chemicals inhibit the chain reaction of a fire and produce an emulsion 
effect that smothers the fire.

questions.question: Inside a flammable liquid storage room, the minimum portable fire extinguisher requirement is:
options: A 20 lb carbon dioxide adjacent to any dispensing station within the room
A multipurpose ABC dry chemical, located inside the room, adjacent to the entrance door
A fire hose, with fog nozzle, mounted on a column, inside the room
extinguisher must be located outside the room
questions.explanation:
In a hazardous location of this nature, the recommended practice is for the fire 
extinguishing equipment to be located outside the room.

questions.question: The maximum travel distance to an exit in an industrial occupancy fully protected with automatic sprinklers is:
questions.explanation:
The travel distance to at least one exit shall not exceed 200 ft in industrial occupancies 
NOT equipped with a sprinkler system or exceed 250 ft in industrial occupancies protected 
throughout by an approved, supervised sprinkler system. NFPA 101 40.2.6.1 (Life Safety 
Code)

questions.question: For a dust explosion to occur in a storage silo, which of the following conditions must be met:
options: Oxygen must be present in a concentration that will sustain rapid combustion
The dust must be well mixed with the oxygen at a concentration above the LEL
An ignition source must be present
All of above conditions must be met
questions.explanation:
A dust explosion compares with a deflagration in which gases spread through the 
burning material by conduction, convection, and radiation at a rate less than the velocity of 
sound. For it to occur, all conditions, including enclosed space, must be met.

questions.question: Class "B" fire doors are used to protect openings in:
questions.explanation:
Class B openings are in enclosures of vertical communication through buildings, such 
as stairs and elevators. Doors for protection of these openings have a fire protection rating of 
1 to 1.5 hours.

questions.question: "Bonding" a flammable liquid dispensing can refers to the process of:
options: Attaching it to a grounding strap
Connecting it to other conductive objects
questions.explanation:
"Bonding" refers to the connection of conductive objects by means of a conductor to 
minimize potential electrical differences between the objects. "Grounding" is the process of 
connecting the conductive objective to the ground. In flammable liquid dispensing, both 
"Bonding" and "Grounding" are important.

questions.question: A detonation has the following features EXCEPT:
options: Blowout panels and rupture disks can vent explosion
Blowout panels and rupture disks are useless
questions.explanation:
Due to the supersonic nature of the pressure front after a detonation, blowout panels 
and rupture disks are useless. 

When materials explode they usually propagate as a deflagration of a detonation. A 
deflagration is a low speed propagation and is effectively an expansion of gases. An 
expansion or flow of gases can be directed through venting and thus serious damage can be 
prevented through adequate venting. A detonation, on the other hand, results in a shock wave 
that cannot be redirected. The shock wave will impart its energy on any surface that is in its 
path, thus venting is practically useless for protection against damage from a detonation. 

National Fire Protection Association, Fire Protective Handbook, (15th ed. ) Section 3/Chapter 
2 subparagraph A.

questions.question: You are a safety professional for a company that occupies several three-floor office buildings at its corporate headquarters location. Life safety is a concern, and the company insists that recognized life safety standards are not only enforced at its high- hazard plants, but also deployed across all corporate headquarters facilities. What is the minimum width permitted for the common corridors and passageways that lead to exits in the corporate headquarters buildings?
questions.explanation:
44 in. is the minimum permitted width of corridors and passageways that lead to 
means of egress. NFPA 101 39.2.3.2 (Life Safety Code)

questions.question: Your office area in your building is about 10,000 ft2. During an office inspection, someone asks you how many fire extinguishers are needed. The current extinguishers in place are class 2A extinguishers. What is your answer?
questions.explanation: Four are needed, since each one can cover 3,000 ft2 in an office occupancy.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: There are different types of standpipe systems in buildings. Type I systems are meant to be used by:
questions.explanation: These systems are for use by the fire department personnel.

questions.question: One of the specific concerns for fighting fires where oxidizing agents are present is that these agents:
options: Limit the use of water as an extinguishing agent
questions.explanation:
These agents provide the fire with a source of oxygen even when extinguishing agents 
are used.

questions.question: Assume you are building a five-story building and will place the heating unit in the basement. If the vent is to pass through the floors and roof, what must you do to the vent?
options: Install fire suppression equipment in the vent
Increase the size of the vent by a factor of 1.2
Install the vent in one-hour rated fire resistive walls
Install the vent in two-hour rated fire resistive walls
questions.explanation: Two hour walls are needed when the building is four stories or more in height.

questions.question: When water supply pipes change direction due to installation requirements, the installer must often use what technique to prevent damage to the system when in use?
options: Use of plastic or rubber pipe
questions.explanation:
Thrust blocks are used at tees, plugs, and bends to absorb loads imposed by water 
moving in the pipe.

questions.question: In normal areas the spacing between fire hydrants should not exceed:
questions.explanation:
In normal areas, 800 ft is the normal spacing. In congested areas, 500 ft may be used. 
NFPA Fire Protection Handbook

questions.question: How often should private hydrants be opened and closed to ensure proper water flow and drainage?
questions.explanation:
Annual flow testing is recommended for private hydrants. NFPA 25 - Standard for the 
Inspection, Testing, and Maintenance of Water-Based Fire Protection Systems

questions.question: Your company is planning a new corporate office and training center. This center will include a large meeting room that can be subdivided into smaller meeting rooms with movable walls. What is one of the commonly overlooked items when designing such facilities?
options: The facility needs to be classified as a place of assembly
Emergency exit provisions must be made for each area subdivided by movable walls
The facility may be used by the public
Generally these facilities have cooking facilities that must be treated as a restaurant
questions.explanation:
Often overlooked is the need to provide emergency egress from areas subdivided by 
movable walls, particularly when several scenarios of subdivision are possible.

questions.question: All of the following statements are true EXCEPT:
options: Dust-ignition proof equipment is designed to keep ignitable amounts of dust from entering the enclosure
Dust may accumulate on electrical equipment, causing overheating of the equipment, as well as the dehydration and gradual carbonization of organic dust deposits
Overheated equipment may malfunction and cause a fire
Equipment must be designed to operate at the ignition temperature of the specific dust involved even when blanketed
questions.explanation:
Equipment must be designed to operate below the ignition temperature of the specific 
dust involved even when blanketed.

questions.question: Ignition of flammable vapors, dusts, or fibers by discharge of static electricity can be prevented by any of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Static electricity is non-flowing electricity commonly generated by friction and the 
effects of the positive and negative charges which have the potential to spark. The static 
charge which already exists can be removed or allowed to dissipate itself. The acts or 
conditions which can accomplish this are the same as those which permit the separation of 
charges to occur. Ignition is prevented by the actions employing humidification, ionization, 
grounding, and bonding. Flammable vapors, dusts, or fibers cannot be insulated.

questions.question: In Class II hazardous locations there are three groups: E, F, and G. Special designs are required to prevent dust from entering into the electrical equipment enclosure. All of the following are true EXCEPT:
options: Assembly joints and motor shaft openings must be tight enough to prevent dust from entering the enclosure
The design must take into account the insulating effects of dust layers on equipment and must ensure that the equipment will operate below the ignition temperature of the dust involved
If conductive combustible dusts are present, the design of equipment must take the special nature of these dusts into account
Equipment that is dust-ignition proof is generally not acceptable for use in Class III locations
questions.explanation:
Equipment that is dust-ignition proof is generally acceptable for use in Class III 
locations, since the same design considerations are involved. NFPA 70 Article 500-3 
(National Electric Code)

questions.question: As a safety professional, you are asked to recommend a fire detector for use in a Class I, Division 2 work area. Which of the following would you select?
questions.explanation:
The bulb detection system is completely mechanical thereby avoiding the use of 
electricity and a potential source of ignition in an area where volatile flammable liquids or 
gases are used.

questions.question: An average of one gallon of toluene is evaporated every hour in a continuous process drying oven operating at sea level. Assuming that the toluene completely mixes throughout the oven, what is the minimum exhaust ventilation rate required by code to prevent an explosive concentration? The code does not permit the concentration of flammable vapors in the oven to exceed 25% of the LEL at any time. The LEL for toluene is 1.1% at the oven's operating temperature The specific gravity of toluene is 0.87 (water is 1.0) The specific vapor density of toluene is 3.1 (dry air is 1.0) The density of water at STP is 8.328 lb/gal The density of air at STP is 0.075lb/ft3 The basic equation to determine the required ventilation to maintain a system at a discrete LEL is: Ventilation Rate = (Density of Water at STP)/(Density of Air at STP)(Specific Gravity of Solvent)/(Specific Vapor Density of Solvent) [(100% - LEL)/LEL] Solvent Evaporation Rate
questions.explanation:
First, realize that the given equation gives you the required ventilation to MAINTAIN 
the LEL. We need to know the required ventilation rate at 25% of the LEL. Therefore, we 
will have to multiply the result from the given equation by a factor of 4 (100% of LEL/25% 
of LEL = 4). Also note that we require the answer in standard cubic feet per MINUTE. Since 
the evaporation rate is gallons per hour, we will have to convert to gallons per minute. 
Carefully track the units when solving this equation, and remember that specific gravity and 
specific vapor density have no units. 

Minimum Rate = 4(8.328 lb/gal / 0.075 lb/ft3)(0.87 / 3.1) [(100% - 1.1%) / 1.1%] (1 gal/hr) (1 
hr/60 min) 
Minimum Rate = 4 * 111.04 ft3/gal * 0.281 * 89.91 * 0.0167 gal/min 
Minimum Rate = 187 ft3/min 

NFPA 86 Section 7 - Standards for Ovens and Furnaces
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: The water level of a rectangular fire pond, 75 ft * 42 ft, is to be raised 4 in.. How many gallons are needed?
questions.explanation:
V = 75 ft * 42 ft [4 in / (12 in / 1 ft)] 
= 1,050 ft3 
There are 7.5 gallons in 1 cubic foot (ft3) 
V = 1,050 ft3 * 7.5 gal/ft3 
= 7,875 gal
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Water spray is an acceptable extinguishing method for all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
The extinguishing properties of water include cooling, smothering, emulsifying, and 
diluting. The application of water in spray form or combination nozzles and sprinklers is 
considered to be an efficient method for extinguishing fire. However, using water to 
extinguish a burning metal fire may cause an explosion.

questions.question: Halon 1301 is a clean extinguishing agent that leaves no residue. It has a "B" and "C" extinguishing classification, intended primarily for use on sensitive electronic equipment such as computer operations. In a 10,000 ft2 computer room, what concentration of Halon 1301 would be needed to prevent combustion?
questions.explanation:
For Halon 1301 to be effective, the ventilation systems must be stopped so that the 
designed concentration of 6% will effectively extinguish the fire. In a total flooding system, 
human exposure should be limited to one minute if the concentration is as high as 7% to 10%.

questions.question: It is considered good practice to avoid all unnecessary exposure to Halon 1301 and to prohibit exposure above:
questions.explanation:
It is considered good practice to avoid all unnecessary exposure to Halon 1301 and to 
prohibit exposure above 15%.

questions.question: On a loading dock in Minnesota, you would most likely find the following type of sprinkler system:
questions.explanation: Dry-pipe systems are used where there is a possibility of freezing.

questions.question: In a fire sprinkler system, what is the purpose of a check valve?
options: To limit water pressure to the sprinkler system
To check the flow and send an alarm to the central station
To prevent water from entering a dry pipe system
To prevent the sprinkler system from flowing back into a public water system
questions.explanation:
In some cases due to health requirements, two check valves may be needed in a 
system, but normally one is sufficient to prevent sprinkler system water from returning to the 
public water supply system.

questions.question: If an SCBA is worn in an atmosphere that is immediately dangerous to life and health; he/she must:
options: Have a standby worker with a canister respirator
questions.explanation:
In the event of an emergency, a safety harness and lifeline is the means of quickly 
removing the person from the hazardous atmosphere.

questions.question: What type of breathing air is used for supplied air respirators?
questions.explanation:
Class D breathing air is considered safe for supplied air respirators. Class D breathing 
air has specific levels of oxygen, hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide, and carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Which of the following SCBA systems is required for IDLH atmospheres?
questions.explanation:
Pressure demand SCBA's provide a continuous flow of positive pressure air to the face 
piece of the respirator. The demand/negative pressure demand respirators supply air to the 
face piece only upon inhalation. Gas masks are not SCBA's.

questions.question: Class B portable fire extinguishers are rated by the size of the fire that a novice can extinguish and are identified by a red square containing the letter "B". The numeral preceding the "B" in the rating indicates:
options: Number of seconds it will take to dispense the contents of the extinguisher
Number of times the extinguisher may be used
Number of square feet of burning liquid that can be extinguished
Number of times the unit is effective compared with one gallon of water
questions.explanation:
The numeral preceding the letter "B" indicates the number of square feet of burning 
liquid that the novice can extinguish with that extinguisher. For example a 20B rating 
indicates the novice can extinguish 20 ft2 of burning liquid fire.

questions.question: Class A portable fire extinguishers are identified by a green triangle containing the letter "A." What does the rating number appearing before the "A" signify?
options: The time in seconds it takes to dispense the contents of the extinguisher
The time in minutes it takes to dispense the contents of the extinguisher
The ability to extinguish a fire as compared to one gallon of water
e number of square feet of paper waste that can be extinguished
questions.explanation:
The number preceding the letter "A" rates its ability to extinguish a fire as compared to 
one gallon of water. For example, a "4A" rating means the unit is four times as effective as 
one gallon of water, or conversely, it has the same effectiveness as four gallons of water.

questions.question: As a safety professional, you must recommend how to safely store the following quantities of flammable and combustible liquids: Class I - 35 gallons Class II - 35 gallons Class III - 50 gallons
options: Provide two (2) approved metal storage cabinets
Disburse the materials throughout the assembly area
Provide one (1) approved metal storage cabinet
questions.explanation:
NFPA 30 states that not more than 120 gallons of Class I, Class II and Class IIIA 
liquids may be stored in a storage cabinet. Of this total, not more than 60 gallons may be of 
Class I and Class II liquids.

questions.question: In a 25 ft high assembly area designed for fire safety, a 6 ft metal curtain has been affixed to the bar joists. What is the LEAST likely fire safety purpose?
options: Delays and limits the horizontal spread of heat, gases, and smoke
Assists in making the venting more effective
Provides a horizontal confinement to obtain a stack effect
Delays and limits the vertical spread of heat, gases, and smoke
questions.explanation:
The metal curtain is a draft curtain that functions to delay and limit the horizontal 
spread of heat, gases, and smoke by providing a horizontal confinement to obtain a stack 

effect. The placement of draft curtains makes the venting more effective in that the volume of 
hot gases and smoke discharged by thermal updrafts through a vent varies directly with the 
height of the gas or smoke column.

questions.question: The term central station alarm or central station system is used to describe a type of alarm system that communicates trouble at a premises to those who will respond. These systems:
options: Directly notify the local fire department
Notify a constantly attended location operated by a company that notifies appropriate authorities
Notifies emergency personnel that work at the facility
Notifies a central point in the facility so that a designated person can call the fire department
questions.explanation:
This type of alarm system notifies a continuously attended facility operated by a 
company whose purpose is to alert appropriate authorities.

questions.question: The best fire protection system advisable in a plant where water damage would result in a serious product loss would be:
questions.explanation:
Pre-action fire protection systems are designed to eliminate the danger of water 
damage and to counteract the operational delay of conventional dry pipe systems. In pre-
action systems, the water supply valve is actuated independently of the opening of sprinklers.

questions.question: Confronted with having to extinguish a small Class A fire in an office where only the following extinguishing agents were present, which would you select?
questions.explanation:
A multipurpose dry chemical is effective because it provides a rapid knock-down of 
flames and forms a fire-retardant coating that prevents reflash. CO2 may blow the contents 
around, leaving embers which can reflash.

questions.question: Which class of fire extinguisher is best for extinguishing a paper fire?
options: Class "C" (blue circle with "C" in the circle)
Class "D" (yellow star with "D" in the star)
questions.explanation:
Class "A" fire extinguishers are used on paper or wood fires. Class "B" fire 
extinguishers are used on burning flammable and combustible liquids. Class "C" fire 
extinguishers are used on fires involving energized electrical equipment. Class "D" fire 
extinguishers are used on fires involving combustible metals.

questions.question: Spark arresters are required on chimneys in certain applications. In which of the following applications is a spark arrester not required but is desirable?
options: On all heating equipment burning liquid fossil fuels
questions.explanation:
Spark arresters are required on refuse burners and incinerators. Arrestors are desirable 
(but not required) when burning solid fuels. They are not needed on liquid or gas fuels.

questions.question: The best way to extinguish a chimney fire serving a wood burning stove or heater is to:
options: Close the damper and doors reducing the air supply
Use water in the fire box
questions.explanation:
Close the damper to cut off oxygen to the fire. If it does not totally cut off the air, it 
will reduce the intensity of the fire.

questions.question: One of the most effective forms of area protection from fires in combustible oil quenching operations is:
options: Draining the oil to a tank
Automatic water spray systems over the tanks
questions.explanation:
The best protection is water sprays since they reduce heat, reduce oxygen, and protect 
the building from oil fires. The other controls can also be used but are not generally as 
effective as water spray.

questions.question: The mixing room for a spray painting operation should be located:
options: In the flammable liquids storage room
In the spray painting room or booth
Adjacent to an outside vented wall
questions.explanation:
The best location is in a separate room located on an outside wall of the building so 
that explosion venting can be provided. It should be isolated from the rest of the building by 
fire-resistive construction.

questions.question: High piled combustible storage presents a challenge to sprinkler systems. Above what height are special in-rack sprinkler system design considerations necessary?
questions.explanation:
12 ft is considered the upper range for piled combustibles without utilizing special 
system design techniques that can get water to a potential fire.

questions.question: Your company is a grocery wholesaler and is planning a new warehouse with storage racks 60 ft high. What is one of the primary reasons you will recommend a sprinkler system that includes in-rack sprinklers?
options: In-rack sprinklers are required by code and will reduce the fire insurance costs
In-rack sprinklers are cheaper to install than other types of systems and are easy to protect from damage
Water requirements can be reduced when in-rack sprinklers are installed in addition to general building sprinklers
High rack storage of commodities on pallets and in boxes will create significant flues through which fire will propagate
questions.explanation:
In-rack storage creates flues in the storage area, particularly between pallets of goods 
stacked side-by-side. In-rack sprinklers will knock down the fire sooner and will probably 
reduce water damage from fire suppression. They will cost more to install but will protect the 
building and the contents.

questions.question: Who is LEAST responsible for ensuring that each container of a hazardous chemical shipped to a facility is labeled?
questions.explanation:
The chemical manufacturer, importer, or distributor must ensure that hazardous 
chemical containers are labeled.

questions.question: SCBA is:
questions.explanation: This is the common acronym for self-contained breathing apparatus.

questions.question: A truck driver transporting hazardous materials must know the following:
options: Rest stops along the intended route
questions.explanation: The truck driver is legally obligated to know the nature of the cargo being transported.

questions.question: What type of respirator is best for initial response during an emergency?
options: Organic vapor/acid gas cartridge full-face air-purifying respirator
questions.explanation:
A positive pressure SCBA is recommended until the type and level of hazardous 
chemicals have been identified.

questions.question: In responding to a spill, one would use SCBA in the following situations EXCEPT:
options: When the oxygen level is below 19.5%
When the concentration of the material is greater than the protection factor for other levels of respiratory protection
When the hazards or concentrations are unknown
When oxygen deficiency is not a factor, and the maximum concentrations of airborne hazardous chemicals are within the limits of appropriate NIOSH- approved air-purifying respirators
questions.explanation:
If oxygen deficiency is not a problem, then a properly selected air-purifying respirator 
may be used.

questions.question: You are recommending that your organization purchase an expensive digital trunked radio system for emergency response to replace the single frequency system currently being used. Your manager is looking at several other systems with similar features and capabilities and wants to compare them from only a cost-basis. He has asked you to give him the total cost of the system in today's dollars. Your company uses an annual interest rate (compounded annually) of 8.5% to perform these types of small capital project comparisons. Based on the data provided in the Table below, what is the total system cost assuming a useful life of 15 years? Note that the maintenance agreement and utility costs are assessed at the end of the first year. Cost of 8 portable radios and one base station $25,000 Cost of antenna and transmitter (and facilities) $55,000 Cost of electrician labor and materials $17,500 Cost of computer aided dispatch computers $10,000 Annual maintenance agreement cost $12,500 Annual utilities above those from current system $2,500 Anticipated total system salvage value in 15 years $7,500
questions.explanation:
This is a present value problem with an annuity and a future value. 
The capital cost of the system is $25,000 + $55,000 + $17,500 + $10,000 = $107,500 
The annual costs are ($12,500 + $2,500) for 15 years. The present value of this annual cost 
(annuity) is 
PV = A [(1 + i)n - 1] / [i (1 + i)n] = $15,000 (1.08515 - 1) / (0.085 * 1.08515) = $124,564 
The present value of the salvage value of $7,500 is 
PV = FV (1 + i)-n = $7,500(1.085)-15 = $2,206 
The TOTAL cost of this option is therefore the present value of all of the costs MINUS the 
present value of the salvage value. 
Total Cost = $107,500 + $124,564 - $2,206 = $229,858
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula/advanced calculation or diagram/table-dependent question

questions.question: What color is used to identify ionizing radiation?
questions.explanation: A magenta field identifies areas with ionizing radiation.

questions.question: Both DOT and NFPA systems use _____________ coloring to identify an oxidizing material.
questions.explanation:
Although systems employed by DOT and NFPA for identifying hazardous materials 
are similar, their purposes differ as does their color coding, with the exception of yellow for 
oxidizing materials and red for flammable materials.

questions.question: What does a "3" in the health section of a HMIS label mean?
options: Moderate health hazard - use reasonable precautions
Very hazardous to health - avoid all routes of exposure
questions.explanation:
The HMIS is the hazardous materials identification system commonly used to identify 
chemicals. The rating scale is 0-4, 0 being the least hazardous and 4 being the most 
hazardous. Materials are rated for reactivity, flammability, and health hazards

questions.question: The NFPA 704 diamond has four classes of materials by position and color on the diamond. The classes are:
options: Health hazard, flammability, reactivity, and specific hazards
Explosivity, health, flammability, and specific hazards
Health hazards, flammability, reactivity, and corrosivity
questions.explanation:
The four classes of materials and colors on the National Fire Protection Association 
704 (NFPA 704) diamond are: 
 
health hazard-blue 
 
flammability-red 
 
reactivity-yellow 
 
and specific hazards-white.
questions.exclusion_reason: Unreliable symbol extraction; held for review

questions.question: HMIS labels contain the following information:
options: Health, fire, reactivity, personal protective equipment
Toxicity, fire, reactivity, personal protective equipment
questions.explanation:
The Hazardous Materials Information System (HMIS) uses a standard label for 
communicating hazards on health, fire, reactivity, and recommended PPE.

questions.question: On vehicles used for transporting hazardous cargo, placards are used as a warning. A placarded vehicle must have at least how many identical placards?
questions.explanation:
Placards are used to warn others of hazardous cargo. Placards are signs put on the 
outside of a vehicle to show the hazard class of the cargo. A placarded vehicle must have at 
least four identical placards. They are put on the front, rear, and both sides. Placards must be 
readable from all four directions. There are 19 DOT-specification placards. They are 10¾ 
inches square, turned upright on a point (in the shape of a diamond).

questions.question: A hazardous chemical shipment Bill of Lading must have the NFPA 704 label.
options: Depends on the type of hazard
questions.explanation:
The Bill of Lading must have the hazard class, chemical ID number, and the quantity 
of the transported chemical, but the NFPA 704 label is not required.

questions.question: Aspects of the NFPA 704 labeling system include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: May be used without a supplementary manual
questions.explanation:
The NFPA 704 system is easy to understand, may be used without a supplementary 
manual, and summarizes the worst hazards.

questions.question: Disadvantages of the NFPA 704 labeling system include:
questions.explanation:
The summarized information on the NFPA 704 label is frequently inadequate for 
emergency response and other applications where detailed, accurate hazard information is 
essential.

questions.question: In the NFPA 704 diamond symbol, the top number indicates the degree of ________ risk of a certain chemical.
questions.explanation:
The NFPA 704 diamond symbol is used to denote the health, flammability, and 
reactivity risk of a substance. The top number in the red-background area indicates the degree 
of flammability hazard, the left number in the blue-background area indicates the degree of 
health hazard, the right number in the yellow-background area indicates the degree of 
reactivity hazard, and the symbol in the lower, white-background area of the diamond 
indicates special hazards such as water reactivity, radioactivity, etc.

questions.question: Planning for spills, explosions, etc. is considered:
questions.explanation: Emergency planning includes planning for spills, explosions, etc.

questions.question: Your company has an emergency brigade established under 29 CFR 1910.156. As your plant has expanded, the roles and capabilities of your company's fire brigade have also expanded. To promote community goodwill and to provide an opportunity to interact with the local volunteer fire department, your company is seeking an opportunity to provide its fire suppression, rescue, and emergency medical services to the community within the local fire district. What is a common method for outlining the roles, responsibilities, and communication channels between your company's fire brigade and the community fire district should this be agreeable to the community?
questions.explanation:
These types of agreements are called mutual aid agreements. The terms of these 
agreements detail what (if any) compensation will occur as a result of a request for an 
emergency response by both parties as well as chains of command, communication channels, 
and other policy-related information.

questions.question: In the development of emergency response plans, which of the following is the most critical factor that needs to be addressed?
options: How to protect people, property, and the environment
questions.explanation:
The most important factor to consider is how to protect life, property, and the environment. Although 
emergency equipment, personnel, and response to multiple emergencies must be addressed in the plan, none of 
them is the most important factor in the development of the emergency response plan.

questions.question: Strict liability is the absolute legal responsibility for an injury that can be imposed on the wrongdoer without proof of carelessness or fault. Which of the following IS NOT part of what the plaintiff must prove in product liability cases?
options: That the defect proximately caused the injury
That the product did not work as expected
That the defect rendered the product unreasonably dangerous
questions.explanation:
This statement is related to implied warranty. Implied warranty is the assurance that a product will 
work if it is used for a reasonably expected purpose.

questions.question: Based on a Factory Mutual Engineering Corporation study of 25,000 fires over a period of 10 years, the leading cause of industrial fires is:
questions.explanation: This study indicated that about 23% of all industrial fires are electrical in nature.

questions.question: The leading cause of civilian fires is:
questions.explanation: An estimated 35% of civilian fires are caused with cigarettes as their ignition source.

questions.question: The standards developed by the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) for fire prevention and protection are called:
questions.explanation:
NFPA standards for fire protection are called National Fire Code. Life Safety Code is an element of 
the National Fire Code. 
The NFPA 101 Life Safety Code is designed with the goal of protecting people in case of a fire in a building. It takes 
into account the building's construction, occupancy, and protection features. This NFPA code has provisions for 
means of egress, fire protection features, alarms, sprinkler systems, emergency lighting, and smoke barriers for all 
types of occupancies.

questions.question: Auto-ignition temperature is the minimum temperature at which a material would burn in the absence of an ignition source. This temperature is:
options: Depending on the material, it could be higher or lower than ignition temperature
questions.explanation:
Auto-ignition temperature is higher than ignition temperature. This phenomenon occurs as a result of 
oxidation of fuel which would generate heat and raise the temperature. Higher temperatures would cause higher 
oxidation rates and even more heat would be generated. This process would continue until the material reaches its 
auto-ignition temperature. Paint and oil soaked rags have caused many fires in this way. Flammables should never 
be exposed to temperatures above their auto-ignition temperature.

questions.question: In order for combustion reactions to start and proceed, which of the followings are needed simultaneously?
options: Fuel, heat, source of ignition, and air
Fuel, chemical chain reaction, oxygen, source of ignition
Fuel, auto-ignition temperature, air, source of ignition
questions.explanation:
Fuel, air, and ignition source are obvious elements of combustion. However, we also need chemical 
chain reaction (formation of free radicals) for the combustion reactions to take place. Actually, halon and dry 
chemical fire extinguishing agents put out a fire by stopping the chemical chain reactions.

questions.question: Two cylinders of hydrogen and five 55 gallon drums of gasoline burn completely in a storage area made of non-combustible material. Assuming that the density of gasoline is 4 lbs./gallon, its heating value is 20,000 Btu/lb., and that there are 15 lb of hydrogen in each cylinder with a heating value of 55,000 Btu/lb., the amount of heat released is:
questions.explanation:
$5\text{ drums} \times 55\text{ gal/drum} \times 4\text{ lb/gal} \times 20,000\text{ Btu/lb} = 22 \times 10^6\text{ Btu}$ 
released from gasoline. 
$2\text{ cylinders} \times 15\text{ lb/cylinder} \times 55,000\text{ Btu/lb} = 1,650,000\text{ Btu}$ released from 
combustion of $\text{H}_2$. 
Total Btu released $= 23.65 \times 10^6\text{ Btu}$.
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: A drum of solvent is on fire in a storage room. Assume that heat is transferred from the outer surface of the drum having a temperature of $1,500^\circ\text{F}$ to the wall having a temperature of $1,000^\circ\text{F}$ by convection. If the heat transfer coefficient is $80\text{ Btu/hr/ft}^2/^\circ\text{F}$, the rate of heat transfer is: (Assume a heat transfer area of $50\text{ ft}^2$.)
questions.explanation:
Convection is the mechanism of interphase heat transfer, i.e., heat transfer between two different 
phases. If we have a surface at temperature $T_1$ that is transferring heat to the surrounding air at a temperature 
$T_2$, this heat is transferred by convection because the transfer is between a solid phase and a gaseous phase. 
$$Q = HA(T_1 - T_2)$$ 
Where: 
$Q$ is the rate of heat transfer, $A$ is area, $T$ is temperature, $H$ is the heat transfer coefficient. 

For the problem at hand: 
$$Q = 80(50)(1,500 - 1,000) = 2 \times 10^6\text{ Btu/hr}$$

questions.question: A flammable liquid storage area made of 1 foot-thick brick walls having a thermal conductivity of $0.4\text{ Btu/hr/foot}/^\circ\text{F}$ is on fire. Assuming that heat is transferred from one of the walls having a temperature of $800^\circ\text{F}$ and an area of $100\text{ ft}^2$ to the other side of the wall, which has a temperature of $200^\circ\text{F}$, the rate of heat transfer in Btu/hr is:
questions.explanation:
The equation for heat transfer by conduction is: 
$$Q = K \frac{A}{L} (T_1 - T_2)$$ 
where: 
$Q$ is the rate of heat transfer 
$K$ is thermal conductivity 
$A$ is area through which heat is being transferred 
$T_1, T_2$ are temperatures 
For the problem at hand: 
$$Q = \left(\frac{0.4}{1}\right)(100)(800 - 200) = 24,000\text{ Btu/hr}$$

questions.question: A drum of carbon disulfide ($\text{CS}_2$) is on fire. The combustion products would most likely be:
options: Sulfur oxides, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide
Hydrogen sulfide, water, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide
Twice as much hydrogen sulfide as CO and $\text{CO}_2$ combined
questions.explanation:
Most carbon in the fuel is converted to carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide. Sulfur in the fuel is 
oxidized to mostly sulfur oxides.

questions.question: A water reactive chemical is defined as one that would produce either a flammable gas or a toxic gas when it comes into contact with water or moisture. Which of the following compounds is a water reactive chemical?
questions.explanation:
Potassium reacts with water and produces hydrogen gas which is highly flammable. Potassium 
cyanide reacts with water and generates hydrogen cyanide which is a highly toxic gas.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most important consideration to prevent fire loss in a flammable liquid storage area?
options: Use of pre-action automatic sprinkler system
questions.explanation:
Although statements (b), (c) and (d) are important considerations in fire prevention and protection, the 
most important consideration is compatible storage such as separating ignitors from ignitables.

questions.question: In most fire situations there is not enough oxygen available for conversion of carbon in the fuels to carbon dioxide, and as a result, large amounts of carbon monoxide are produced. CO has been the primary killer in most fires. This gas can cause fatalities because:
options: It in the most toxic of all gases produced in a fire.
It is more reactive with blood than oxygen.
It reacts with oxygen in the lungs and causes asphyxiation.
questions.explanation:
Carbon monoxide which is produced during a fire as a result of incomplete combustion of carbon 
containing materials is about 210 time more reactive with blood than oxygen. Therefore, CO deprives the body of 
oxygen and causes death by a form of asphyxiation. Inhalation of air containing 0.4% carbon monoxide can cause 
death in less than one minute.

questions.question: The gaseous products of combustion have a vapor density of less than 1. This means that air in a fire situation is at:
questions.explanation:
Vapor density is defined as the ratio of density of a gas or vapor to the density of air at a given 
temperature. A vapor density of less than 1 indicates that the gas is lighter than air and would rise in air, a vapor 
density of greater than 1 indicates that the gas is heavier than air and would sink in air. For the problem at hand, fire 
gases rise in air, and therefore, air would be collected at the low spots.

questions.question: The following data is available for vapor pressure of acetone as a function of temperature. Temperature ($^\circ\text{F}$) 130$^\circ$ 120$^\circ$ 110$^\circ$ 100$^\circ$ 90$^\circ$ Vapor Pressure (mm Hg) 760 740 720 700 695 When atmospheric pressure is $740\text{ mm Hg}$, the vapor pressure of acetone is also $740\text{ mm Hg}$ at $120^\circ\text{F}$. This means that the boiling point of acetone at $740\text{ mm Hg}$ is:
options: Vapor pressure is a measure of the volatility of a liquid and has nothing to do with boiling point.
questions.explanation:
Boiling takes place at the temperature where liquid vapor pressures equals the ambient (atmospheric) 
pressure. Vapor pressure of a liquid always increases with an increase in temperature.

questions.question: Acetone is a highly flammable liquid (flash point $= 0^\circ\text{F}$) and has a specific gravity of 0.79. From the data presented, and in the absence of other information, which of the following statements is true regarding a mixture of acetone and water?
options: Acetone would float on top of water.
The mixture has a flashpoint of less than $0^\circ\text{F}$.
Data presented is not sufficient to determine whether acetone would float or sink in water.
questions.explanation:
Gases have relatively high values of diffusion coefficient. Therefore, vapor density alone would dictate 
whether a gas would rise or sink in air. In dealing with liquids, however, we need two pieces of information in order 
to decide whether a liquid would float or sink in water. The information required is specific gravity and solubility. 
Specific gravity is the ratio of density of a liquid to the density of water. If two liquids are insoluble in each other, the 
liquid with the smaller value of specific gravity would float on top of the other liquid. However, when two liquids are 
soluble in each other, they become dissolved and form a uniform solution regardless of their specific gravities.

questions.question: Water has a vapor pressure of $20\text{ mm Hg}$ at room temperature and acetone has a vapor pressure of $180\text{ mm Hg}$ at room temperature. This indicates:
options: Water evaporates more slowly than acetone.
At a given pressure, acetone has a lower boiling point compared to water.
questions.explanation:
Vapor pressure is a measure of force exerted by the vapor to the inside surface of its container. Vapor 
pressure is also a measure of the volatility of a liquid. The higher the vapor pressure, the more volatile the liquid. 
Boiling takes place when atmospheric pressure and vapor pressure are equal.

questions.question: Fire point is defined as the lowest temperature at which enough vapor is generated to support continuous combustion in presence of an ignition source. Fire point is:
options: Depending on the material can be higher, lower, or the same as flash point
questions.explanation:
Flash point is the lowest temperature at which a liquid gives off enough vapor to support combustion. 
The liquid would not continue to burn at its flash point. Fire point temperature requires sustained combustion and is 
always higher than flash point temperature.

questions.question: Mishandling of flammable liquids and gases have been responsible for approximately 18 per cent of all industrial fires. In order to safely handle these materials, one has to understand their properties. Flammable liquids are incompressible while flammable gases are compressible. A container with a volume of $100\text{ ft}^3$ is filled with gasoline. The container is under 100 psi pressure. If this container breaks, the volume of gasoline spilled is approximately:
questions.explanation:
Liquids are incompressible. This means that pressure changes have very little effect on the liquid 
volume.

questions.question: A cylinder of hydrogen having a volume of $5\text{ ft}^3$ is under 1,000 psig pressure. The valve on the cylinder breaks releasing hydrogen to atmosphere. The volume of hydrogen released is approximately:
questions.explanation:
$P_1 = 1,000\text{ psig}$ 
$V_1 = 5\text{ ft}^3$ 
$P_2 = 14.7\text{ psia}$ 
$$P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2$$ 
$P_1 = 1,000 + 14.7 = 1,014.7\text{ psia}$ (We must use absolute pressure) 
$$(1,014.7)(5) = 14.7 V_2$$ 
$$V_2 = 345.13\text{ ft}^3 \approx 345\text{ ft}^3$$ 
Note 1: Gases are compressible which means that the volume of gas is a very strong function of pressure. Note that 
due to pressure reduction the volume increased from $5\text{ ft}^3$ to $345\text{ ft}^3$. 
Note 2: In using gas laws be sure to use absolute pressure (gauge pressure + atmospheric pressure) and absolute 
temperature.

questions.question: A Lower Flammability Limit (LFL) of 10% for a gas or vapor means that the gas would support combustion at:
options: Concentrations above 10% but below the UFL
questions.explanation:
LFL is defined as the lowest concentration by volume of a gas in air which would support combustion. 
UFL is the highest concentration of a gas in air (by volume) that would support combustion. A gas or vapor can only 
support combustion at concentrations with air that fall between its LFL and UFL. It should be pointed out that both 
LFL and UFL are functions of ambient pressure and temperature.

questions.question: Fifty gallons of gasoline is spilled from a drum. The specific gravity of gasoline is 0.8 and its vapor density is 2.5. The volume of vapor that can be generated from the spill is approximately:
questions.explanation:
Vapor volume can be estimated from: 
$$V = \frac{(\text{S.G.})(111)}{\text{V.D.}}$$ 

Where: 
$V$ is volume of vapor generated per gallon of liquid vaporized in cubic feet 
$\text{S.G.}$ is liquid specific gravity 
$\text{V.D.}$ is vapor density. 
$$V = \frac{(0.8)(111)}{2.5} = 35.52\text{ ft}^3\text{/gal}$$ 
$$35.52\text{ ft}^3\text{/gal} \times 50\text{ gal} = 1,776\text{ ft}^3$$

questions.question: Methyl alcohol has a vapor volume of $80\text{ ft}^3$ per gallon and a lower flammability limit of 6% by volume in air. questions.explanation:

Volume of room $= 15 \times 15 \times 10 = 2,250\text{ ft}^3$ 
Partial volume of methyl alcohol $= \frac{40}{2250 + 40} = 0.0174$ 
Concentration $= 1.74 \times 10^{-2}$ or $1.74%$ (which is below LFL of 6%).

questions.question: Materials that are classified as oxidizers must be separated from flammables because:
options: They can produce heat and act as a source of ignition.
If mixed with flammables may cause a fire in the absence of a source of ignition.
They can release oxygen or catalyze the combustion reactions.
questions.explanation:
Compounds which are classified as oxidizers are those which can either release oxygen or catalyze 
the combustion reactions (such as chlorine). In either case, oxidizers would make an ongoing fire much worse and 
must be separated from flammables. They can also react with flammables and raise the temperature to above 
ignition temperature.

questions.question: Fire resistance rating is a rating for buildings that:
options: Determines how long a structure withstands a fire.
Has units of minutes or hours.
questions.explanation:
"Fire resistance rating" is an indication of how long a given structure can withstand a fire to give the 
occupants a chance to evacuate the building before commencement of fire fighting procedures.

questions.question: A storage area made of concrete stores 20 drums of gasoline each containing $200\text{ lb}$ of gasoline. The heat of combustion for gasoline is $20,000\text{ Btu/lb}$. The fire load for this storage area is:
questions.explanation:
$$20 \times 200 \times 20,000 = 80,000,000 = 8 \times 10^7\text{ Btu}$$ 
In calculating the fire load, it is assumed that all combustibles will burn and release their heating value.

questions.question: Fixed temperature heat detectors are not suitable for fires that have the potential for developing quickly because:
options: They can only respond to rate of rise of temperature.
The air reaches a higher temperature before the device.
In a quick fire heat does not transfer to the device properly.
They can only detect heat coming from a fixed temperature.
questions.explanation:
There is a time lag before the device temperature reaches the temperature of air surrounding it. Due 
to this limitation these fire detectors are not suitable for fast developing fires.

questions.question: Most fixed temperature heat detectors use:
questions.explanation:
Fusible metal is selected to melt at a given temperature. This would activate an alarm or sprinkler 
system. The insulation in continuous wire detector is selected in such a way to melt at a given temperature. This 
closes an electrical circuit which could initiate other actions. Bi-metallic strips consist of two metals with different 
coefficient of thermal expansion. This would cause the metal to expand at different rates resulting in bending of the 
strip which can initiate other actions.

questions.question: Rate of rise fire detectors:
options: Are suitable for fast developing fires
Respond to changes in ambient temperature and pressure
questions.explanation:
Rate of rise detectors respond to how fast temperature in the surrounding would rise. These detectors 
are suitable for fires that can develop rather quickly.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describe the operation of a rate compensation fire detector?
options: Is more sensitive to thermal lag than a fixed temperature device
Temperatures that rise rapidly are detected sooner
questions.explanation:
These detectors respond to temperatures that rise rapidly and have exceeded a pre-set fixed 
temperature. 
A rate compensated detector operates when the ambient air temperature reaches a predetermined level, regardless 
of the rate at which it increases. The detector will operate at its design temperature during slow-building fire 
conditions or will respond promptly during rapid fire buildup.

questions.question: Ionization fire detectors respond to:
questions.explanation:
Ionization detectors ionize the air and make it conductive. Smoke particles decrease this conductivity 
and initiate a subsequent action such as alarm or activation of sprinkler system.

questions.question: A dry powder fire extinguishing agent can be used on:
questions.explanation:
The term "dry powder" refers to extinguishing agents designed for metal fires (class D). It should be 
pointed out that a given dry powder is not suitable for all metal fires. Therefore, class D fire extinguishers must have 
a plate on the extinguisher that specifies what type of metal fires the extinguishing agent is suitable for.

questions.question: Which of the following gases is expected to be produced from use of Halon 1202 on a fire?
questions.explanation:
Halon 1202 has two atoms of fluorine and 2 atoms of bromine and its use on a fire would most 
probably produce hydrogen fluoride and hydrogen bromide. 
The four-digit rating of Halon fire extinguishers defines the makeup of the molecule as follows: 
• 
The first numeral is the number of carbon atoms 
• 
The second numeral is the number of fluorine atoms 
• 
The third numeral is the number of chlorine atoms 
• 
The fourth numeral is the number of bromine atoms 
Therefore, Halon 1202 has one carbon atom, two fluorine atoms, and two bromine atoms. This indicates that Halon 
1202 can be made from methane ($\text{CH}_4$, a highly flammable gas) by substituting two hydrogen atoms with 
fluorine and the remaining two hydrogen atoms with bromine ($\text{CF}_2\text{Br}_2$).

questions.question: The main parameter characterizing mechanical foam agents is:
questions.explanation:
Mechanical foams are defined by their expansion ratio which is the final volume of foam to original 
foam solution volume prior to addition of air. Foams are further subdivided into: low expansion up to (20:1), medium 
expansion (20 to 200:1), and high expansion (200 to 1000:1).

questions.question: Foam fire extinguishing agents can put out a fire in a flammable liquid spill by:
options: Forming a blanket on the liquid and removing oxygen
Interfering with the chemical chain reaction necessary for combustion reactions
questions.explanation:
Foams form a vapor seal blanket on the surface of the flammable material. The water used in foams 
provides cooling.

questions.question: Foam fire extinguishing agents should never be used on:
questions.explanation:
Foam should never be used on class C (electrical) fires because many foams are conductors of 
electricity and the user may receive injury or fatal shock.

questions.question: The primary mechanism by which carbon dioxide fire extinguishing agents put out a fire is by:
options: Reducing the oxygen concentration in the atmosphere surrounding the fire.
Forming a blanket and eliminating oxygen.
questions.explanation:
$\text{CO}_2$ extinguishing agent dilute the atmosphere immediately surrounding the fire to 
concentrations below its Lower Flammability Limit (LFL).

questions.question: Carbon dioxide extinguishing agents should not be used on which of the following materials on fire?
questions.explanation:
Carbon dioxide is not effective on fires in materials that contain their own source of oxygen such as 

organic peroxides. Fires involving reactive metals such as magnesium, sodium, and potassium can not be 
extinguished by $\text{CO}_2$ because $\text{CO}_2$ becomes decomposed.

questions.question: Considering that helium and nitrogen are both inert gases with thermal capacities of 5.0 and $7.8\text{ Btu/mole}/^\circ\text{F}$ respectively, which of the following statements is correct?
options: Helium would be more effective than nitrogen as an extinguishing agent on a fire to provide inerting.
Nitrogen would be more effective than helium in extinguishing a fire.
A 50/50 mixture of nitrogen and helium would be better than either helium or nitrogen alone.
Helium or nitrogen cannot extinguish a fire.
questions.explanation:
Inert gases such as nitrogen and helium extinguish a fire by combination of two mechanisms: by 
reducing the concentration of oxygen to values below the LFL, and also by reducing the temperature of the 
flame/vapor mixture to values below the adiabatic flame temperature. In this case both nitrogen and helium would 
contribute equally to the first mechanism (inerting). However, nitrogen due to its higher value of the thermal capacity 
contributes more than helium to reduction of the flame temperature, and therefore, is more effective in putting out a 
fire compared to helium.

questions.question: Ordinary dry chemical fire extinguishing agents can be used on which of the following classes of fires:?
options: Class B, C, and D fires
Class A, B and D fires
questions.explanation:
"Ordinary Dry Chemical" agents are designed for use on Class B (flammable liquids, gases, and 
greases). On the other hand, "Multi-purpose Dry Chemicals" are suitable for use on Class A, B, and C fires.

questions.question: One of the major problems associated with use of large quantities of dry chemical agents on a fire is:
options: Breakage of foam layer causing re-ignition
Depletion of the protective ozone layer in the atmosphere
questions.explanation:
Dry chemical extinguishing agents are made of non-toxic chemicals. Use of large quantities of these 
agents on fire could cause temporary breathing difficulty and serious interference with visibility.

questions.question: A dry powder extinguishing agent can:
options: Also be used on Class C fires
Not be designed for radioactive metal fires
Put out those metal fires for which it is designed
questions.explanation:
Dry powder fire extinguishing agents can only be used for extinguishing fires in the metals for which 
they are designed.

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of class D fire extinguishing agents?
questions.explanation: All have been used to smother metal fires.

questions.question: All of the following extinguishing agents can be used to extinguish a Class A fire EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Dry powder can only be used on metal fires. Dry chemical can stop a Class A fire by both cooling and 
interfering with the chemical chain reactions. Halon can extinguish a Class A fire by interfering with chemical chain 
reaction. Carbon dioxide dilutes the mixture of fuel vapor and oxygen to values below LFL.

questions.question: Which of the following are types of gas-sensing fire detector systems?
questions.explanation:
The semiconductor fire-gas detectors respond to gases which have either oxidizing or reducing 
capabilities by creating electrical charges in a semiconductor. The catalytic type has an element which catalyzes 
oxidation of combustible gases and detects the resulting temperature rise associated with the oxidation reactions.

questions.question: The major reason behind unsatisfactory performance of sprinkler system has been:
questions.explanation:
Approximately 35% of sprinkler failures have been caused by shutting the water supply to them during 
a fire.

$$P = \rho \frac{g}{g_c} h$$ 
Where:
