questions.question: Which of the following diagrams demonstrates the operation of a regular dry pipe sprinkler system?
options: Water Tank ($P_2$) -> Valve (closed) -> Sprinkler Pipe ($P_1$, air under pressure, $P_1 > P_2$)
Water Tank -> Valve -> Sprinkler Pipe (air under pressure)
questions.explanation:
Regular dry pipe automatic sprinkler systems are connected to a supply of air or nitrogen under 
pressure. Heat from a fire causes a valve to open and reduce the pressure on air or nitrogen supply to a value that 
water pressure on the supply side of the system causes the valve to open and establish flow of water to the sprinkler 
heads.

questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) is (are) true regarding deluge type automatic sprinkler systems?
options: Sprinklers are opened in response to pressure reduction in air or nitrogen tank.
Use 15% carbon dioxide to deluge the protected area.
All sprinkler heads are open at all times.
questions.explanation:
In "deluge" type sprinkler systems the sprinkler heads are open at all times. The deluge valve 
responds to a fire detection system. When the valve is opened the water flows into and out of the sprinklers deluging 
the protected area.

questions.question: Fire extinguishment by water spray is accomplished by:
questions.explanation:
Water spray provides cooling and smothering by steam. Emulsification and dilution are also 
contributing factors.

questions.question: The total pressure loss due to friction in 1,000 ft. of a pipe which has an inside diameter of 8 inches and a coefficient of friction of 150 with a flow rate of 1,000 gpm is approximately:
questions.explanation:
The formula for calculation of frictional losses in a piping system is: 
$$P_d = \frac{4.52 Q^{1.85}}{C^{1.85} d^{4.87}}$$ 
where: 
$P_d$ is pressure loss due to friction in psi/ft. 
$Q$ is flow rate in gpm 
$d$ is pipe inside diameter in inches 
$C$ is coefficient of friction 
For the problem at hand: 
$$P_d = \frac{4.52 (1000)^{1.85}}{(150)^{1.85} (8)^{4.87}} = 6.04 \times 10^{-3}\text{ psi/ft.}$$ 
For 1,000 ft. of piping, the total loss is: 
$$1,000 \times 6.04 \times 10^{-3} = 6.04\text{ psi}$$

questions.question: Water with a density of $62\text{ lb per cubic foot}$ is flowing through an 8 inch diameter horizontal piping system. The head loss across a 1,000 ft. section of this piping system is 70 ft. The residual pressure at point A is 50 psi and the velocity at point A is $6\text{ ft/sec}$. If the velocity at point B is $45\text{ ft/sec}$, the value of residual pressure at point B is:
questions.explanation:
This problem is solved by Bernoulli's Theorem: 
$$\frac{V_A^2}{2g} + \frac{P_A}{\rho} + Z_A = \frac{V_B^2}{2g} + \frac{P_B}{\rho} + Z_B + h_L$$ 
where: 
$V$ is velocity 
$P$ is residual pressure 
$\rho$ is density 
$Z$ is elevation 
$h_L$ is head loss 
$g$ is acceleration of gravity ($32.2\text{ ft/sec}^2$) 

For the problem at hand: 
$$\frac{6^2}{2 \times 32.2} + \left(\frac{50\text{ psi}}{62\text{ lb/ft}^3}\right) \left(\frac{144\text{ in}^2}{1\text{ 
ft}^2}\right) + 0 = \frac{45^2}{2 \times 32.2} + \frac{P_B}{62} + 0 + 70$$ 
$$0.559 + 116.129 = 31.444 + \frac{P_B}{62} + 70$$ 
$$116.688 = 101.444 + \frac{P_B}{62}$$ 
$$\frac{P_B}{62} = 15.244 \implies P_B = 945.13\text{ psf}$$ 
$$P_B = \frac{945.13}{144} = 6.56\text{ psi} \approx 6.5\text{ psi}$$

$$Q_2 = \frac{2000}{0.91287} = 2,190.89\text{ gpm} \approx 2,190\text{ gpm}$$

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct classification for flammable liquids?
questions.explanation:
Class IA: Flash point below 73°F; boiling point below 100°F 
Class IB: Flash point below 73°F; boiling point at or above 100°F 
Class IC: Flash point at or above 73°F, but below 100°F 
Combustible liquids are also classified into three groups: Class II, IIIA, IIIB.

questions.question: The maximum amount of Class 1A flammable liquid that can be stored in a laboratory unit with a sprinkler system is:
questions.explanation:
Only NFPA 45-approved amounts of flammable liquids shall be stored in laboratory units outside of 
flammable liquid storage rooms.

questions.question: Not more than _________ gallons of Class I, Class II, and Class IIIA liquids shall be stored in an approved flammable storage cabinet.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 120 gallons. Also, no more than 60 gallons of the total shall be Class I and 
Class II liquids.

questions.question: All of the following are true in regards to a jockey pump EXCEPT:
options: A jockey pump is a small pump used to keep a pressure on a fire main.
The jockey pump keeps a high positive pressure on the discharge side of fire pumps.
It is a spare pump used to provide cooling for highly-exothermic chemical reactions.
If you put packing in the stuffing box of a fire pump, the pump will run almost continually to compensate for the packing leakage.
questions.explanation:
Statements (a), (b), and (d) are all true in regards to jockey pumps. The purpose of a jockey pump is 
to maintain water pressure in the pipes in a predetermined range when there is no fire. This helps the main fire 
pump to not run all the time and also prevents the sprinklers go off randomly.

questions.question: A fire water supply system delivers 8,000 gallons per minute (gpm) when the pressure drops from 85 psig to 40 psig. What is the flow rate if the pressure drops from 85 psig to 25 psig?
questions.explanation:
The formula to solve this problem is: 
$$Q_2 = Q_1 \left[ \frac{(S - R_2)^{0.54}}{(S - R_1)^{0.54}} \right]$$ 
Where: 
$Q_2$ is the final flow rate 
$Q_1$ is the initial flow rate 
$S$ is the initial pressure 
$R_1$ is the initial residual pressure 
$R_2$ is the final residual pressure 
For the problem at hand: 
$$Q_2 = 8000 \left[ \frac{(85 - 25)^{0.54}}{(85 - 40)^{0.54}} \right] = 8000 \left[ \frac{60^{0.54}}{45^{0.54}} \right] = 
8000 \left( \frac{9.13}{7.82} \right) = 9,344.52\text{ gpm}$$
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Sodium azide solution can result in serious explosion hazards if the waste is disposed in a sink made of _________.
questions.explanation: Sodium azide solution in contact with brass, lead, or copper can cause serious explosion hazards.

questions.question: Fire detection and alarm systems use distinctly different signals that are automatically transmitted to an approved central station, remote supervising station, or proprietary supervising station. Which of the following is NOT a signal used in these systems?
questions.explanation: The three types of signals used in fire detection are supervisory, alarm, and trouble.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a mode of heat transfer?
questions.explanation:
Conduction, convection, and radiation are the three modes of heat transfer. Combustion is a chemical 
reaction.

questions.question: Hazardous locations are classified by the National Electric Code (NEC) as Class I, Class II, and Class III locations. Class III locations are those in which there may be:
questions.explanation: Class III locations are those in which there may be ignitable fibers.

questions.question: Which of the following color coding is used for a sprinkler head designed for a maximum ceiling temperature of $300^\circ\text{F}$ ($149^\circ\text{C}$)?
Which of the following is NOT true in regard to Halon fire extinguishing agents?
options: Halons are made by halogenating a hydrocarbon.
Halons stop the spread of fire by chemically disrupting combustion.
The only disadvantage of Halons is that they leave a residue on the equipment after putting out the fire.
Halon is rated for Class B and Class C fires, but is also effective on Class A fires.
questions.explanation:
Halons are made by halogenating hydrocarbons. Although hydrocarbons are flammable, the 
halogenated hydrocarbons lose their flammability characteristic as they become more halogenated. Halons are 
especially effective for electrical fires in sensitive electronic equipment, because they leave no residue and therefore 
do not damage the equipment.

questions.question: The term boiling liquid expanding vapor explosion (BLEVE) refers to which of the following?
options: An explosion caused by a flammable liquid at its boiling point
The failure of a container holding a liquid above its boiling point, which may result in an explosion
The volume of vapor expanding over the surface of a flammable liquid, which may result in an explosion
questions.explanation:
BLEVE is best described by statement (b). The consequences of BLEVE include overpressure blast 
wave, fireball, and vessel fragment hazards.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true in regard to ionization smoke detectors?
options: They have a small amount of radioactive material between two electrically charged plates.
They ionize the air and cause current to flow between the plates.
Smoke disrupts the flow of ions, thus reducing the flow of current, which in turn activates the alarm.
questions.explanation:
Another type of smoke detector is photoelectric. This type aims a light source into a sensing chamber 
at an angle away from the sensor. Smoke enters the chamber, reflecting light onto the light sensor, triggering the 
alarm.

questions.question: Which of the following statements BEST describes the term hypergolic?
options: The ignition of a fuel when it comes into contact with an oxidizer without the presence of an outside source of ignition
A flammable liquid that can create a hyperbola-shaped fireball when on fire.
An above-standard goal-oriented safety, health, and environmental program
The angle of incidence of a hyperbola-shaped dome in construction safety
questions.explanation:
Oxidizers, such as hydrogen peroxide, have excess oxygen in their molecules and can release this 
excess oxygen. If the reaction between an oxidizer and fuel can generate enough heat to raise the mixture 
temperature to above its auto-ignition temperature, no outside source of ignition is needed to cause a fire. 
Flammables must be separated from oxidizers.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a pyrophoric material?
questions.explanation:
Pyrophoric materials are substances that ignite instantly upon exposure to oxygen. No source of 
ignition is needed. They can also be water-reactive, which produces heat and hydrogen.

questions.question: The first step in responding to spills of hazardous material should be to:
questions.explanation:
Although identifying the substance determines the most effective clean up procedure and protective 
equipment needed, the first step is to ensure that people are protected. This includes both responders and other 
people.

questions.question: Employees who use portable fire extinguishers can often put out small fires or control a fire until additional help arrives. Before an emergency occurs, employers must decide whether employees are authorized to use fire extinguishers or must immediately evacuate (29 CFR 1910.38). Which of the following statements is NOT true in regard to portable fire extinguishers intended for emergency response?
options: Selection and distribution of portable fire extinguishers must be based on the class, size, and degree of workplace fire hazards.
Mounting, location, and identification of the extinguishers must be done in such a way so they are readily accessible in an emergency and will not subject employees to potential injury.
Ensure that the travel distance from employee to the nearest extinguisher is 100 feet or less.
Maintain fire extinguishers. Maintenance includes monthly visual inspections, hydrostatic testing, annual internal examinations, and all associated documentation.
questions.explanation:
The Occupational Safety and Health Administration require the following for portable fire extinguisher 
to be used in an emergency (29 CFR 1910.157): 
• 
Select and distribute portable fire extinguishers based on the class, size, and degree of workplace fire 
hazards. 
• 
Mount, locate, and identify the extinguishers so they are readily accessible in an emergency and will not 
subject employees to potential injury. 
• 
Provide only approved portable fire extinguishers. 
• 
Maintain fire extinguishers. Maintenance includes monthly visual inspections, hydrostatic testing, annual 
internal examinations, and all associated documentation. 
• 
Ensure that the travel distance from employee to the nearest extinguisher is appropriate for the fire class. 
The travel distance for class A extinguishers cannot exceed 75 feet. The maximum travel distance for class 
B is 50 feet and there is no maximum travel distance specified for class C extinguishers.

questions.question: In an Emergency, employee alarm systems alert employees to begin implementing emergency action. All of the following are true in regard to alarm systems EXCEPT:
options: Provide a distinctive and perceivable alarm system for emergency action.
Ensure that all equipment used for alarm systems is approved.
Ensure that all equipment used for alarm systems has spare components.
Test alarms once a week. Follow special safety requirements for testing.
questions.explanation:
Employee alarm systems alert employees to begin implementing emergency action. OSHA requires 
the following: 
• 
Provide a distinctive and perceivable alarm system for emergency action or safe evacuation. 
• 
Ensure that all equipment used for alarm systems is approved and spare components are available. 
• 
Test alarms at the frequency required. Follow special safety requirements for testing or restoring alarms.

questions.question: To prepare for any contingency, an emergency action plan establishes procedures that prevent fatalities, injuries, and property damage. Possible emergency scenarios based on the nature of the workplace and its surroundings must be identified. A written emergency action plan must also be prepared. The plan must include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: The fire and emergency reporting procedures
Procedures for emergency evacuation, including the type of evacuation and exit routes.
Procedures for those who remain to operate critical operations prior to Evacuation.
The name, telephone number, and other relevant information of outside emergency personnel who are expected to respond to onsite emergencies.
questions.explanation:
OSHA requires the employer to: 
• 
Identify possible emergency scenarios based on the nature of the workplace and its surroundings. 
• 
Prepare a written emergency action plan. The plan does not need to be written and may be communicated 
orally if there are 10 or fewer employees. At a minimum, the plan must include: The fire and emergency 
reporting procedures; Procedures for emergency evacuation, including the type of evacuation and exit 
routes; Procedures for those who remain to operate critical operations prior to evacuation; Procedures to 
account for employees after evacuation; Procedures for employees performing rescue and medical duties; 
and Names of those to contact for further information or explanation about the plan.

questions.question: Process safety management (PSM) of highly hazardous chemicals focuses on preventing or minimizing consequences from a catastrophic release of toxic, reactive, flammable, or explosive chemicals. Successful PSM emergency planning relies on implementing requirements from 29 CFR 1910.38 and/or 1910.120(q). All of the following are elements of a sound PSM emergency plan EXCEPT:
options: Conduct a reliability analysis for each component of covered processes, and update and revalidate the analysis every 2 years.
Incorporate emergency shutdown actions and operations into the written operating procedures for each process.
Implement an emergency action plan for the facility as described in 29 CFR 1910.38.
Maintain the mechanical integrity of PSM emergency systems and alarms.
questions.explanation:
OSHA's Process Safety Management Standard (29 CFR 1910.119) requires the employer to: 
• 
Conduct a Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) for each covered process, and update and revalidate the PHA 
every 5 years. 
• 
Incorporate emergency shutdown actions and operations into the written operating procedures for each 
process. Include conditions that require emergency action and the qualified operator responsible for 
performing these procedures. 
• 
Implement an emergency action plan for the facility as described in 29 CFR 1910.38. 
• 
Maintain the mechanical integrity of PSM emergency systems and alarms. 
• 
If employees are expected to handle an emergency release rather than promptly evacuate, implement an 
emergency response plan according to 1910.120(q). 
• 
Provide proper response and personal protective equipment for emergency responders under the plan.

questions.question: Emergency planning and response are required safety and health program elements that help minimize employee exposure and injury in hazardous waste sites. All of the following are elements of a sound emergency response plan for hazardous waste site emergencies EXCEPT:
options: If employees are to immediately evacuate in an emergency, develop an emergency action plan in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.38.
Identify emergency response personnel and responsibilities in the site program's organizational structure.
Identify the name and telephone numbers of federal, state, and local emergency response personnel.
Identify personal protective equipment (PPE) and other equipment for emergency response in the emergency response plan.
questions.explanation:
OSHA requires the employer to do the following: 
• 
If employees are to immediately evacuate in an emergency, develop an emergency action plan in 
accordance with 29 CFR 1910.38. 
• 
If employees may assist in handling the emergency, then the following requirements apply: As a separate 
section of the site safety and health plan, develop a written emergency response plan. The plan must be 
implemented before site operations begin and should be integrated with those of other local, state, and 
Federal agencies. Identify emergency response personnel and responsibilities in the site program's 
organizational structure. Include emergency response training details in the comprehensive site work plan. 
Identify personal protective equipment (PPE) and other equipment for emergency response in the 
emergency response plan. Install alarm systems that meet requirements of 29 CFR 1910.165. Share site-
specific emergency response procedures with contractors and subcontractors. Under certain circumstances, 
emergency response personnel may qualify for the medical surveillance program.

questions.question: In responding to hazardous substance emergencies, if the employer has decided that employees may assist in handling the emergency, a written emergency response plan must be developed and implemented. This plan must include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Personnel roles, lines of authority, training, and communication
Exclude employees with disability from taking part in emergency operations
questions.explanation:
Depending on the type of emergency and disability, some employees with disability may be able to 
help in handling an emergency.

questions.question: When an employer establishes a fire brigade to respond to workplace fires, it must meet organizational, training, and personal protective equipment requirements. All of the following are procedural, program, and/or equipment requirements that the employer must meet EXCEPT:
options: Prepare and maintain a fire brigade written organizational statement and document fire brigade member training information in the organizational statement.
Ensure employees expected to fight fires are physically capable to perform assigned duties.
Inspect and maintain fire-fighting equipment monthly. Inspect respirators and fire extinguishers annually. Remove and replace damaged equipment.
Supply protective clothing with components to protect the head, body, and extremities at no cost to the employees.
questions.explanation:
The employer must do the following: 
• 
Prepare and maintain a fire brigade written organizational statement. Document fire brigade member training 
information in the organizational statement. 
• 
Ensure employees expected to fight fires are physically capable to perform assigned duties. 
• 
Inspect and maintain fire-fighting equipment annually. Inspect respirators and fire extinguishers monthly. 
• 
Supply protective clothing with components to protect the head, body, and extremities at no cost to the 
employee. 
• 
Ensure fire brigade members are provided with and use compliant respirators.

questions.question: All of the following are true in regard to emergency respirators EXCEPT:
options: Clean and disinfect emergency respirators at least once every six months.
Select and provide respirators suitable for the intended purpose.
When respirators are required, establish and implement a written respiratory protection program that includes procedures for proper respirator use in emergency.
Ensure that emergency respirators are properly stored and inspected.
questions.explanation:
OSHA requires the employer to do the following: 
• 
Select and provide respirators suitable for the intended purpose. 
• 
When respirators are required, establish and implement a written respiratory protection program that 
includes procedures for proper respirator use in emergency situations. Update the program when changes in 
workplace conditions affect respirator use. 
• 
Clean and disinfect emergency respirators after each use. Ensure that emergency respirators are properly 
stored and inspected. Certify emergency-only respirators by a certification tag or other proper 
documentation method. 
• 
For entry into Immediately Dangerous to Life and Health (IDLH) environments, provide retrieval equipment 
or equivalent means for rescue of employees. Maintain required personnel and communications for 
emergency rescue. 
• 
For interior structural firefighting, ensure that at least two employees who remain in contact with one another 
enter the structure.

questions.question: Which of the following is true in regards to workplace violence?
options: Workplace violence is any act or threat of physical violence, harassment, intimidation, or other threatening disruptive behavior.
It ranges from threats and verbal abuse to physical assaults and even homicide.
In most workplaces where risk factors can be identified, the risk of assault can be prevented or minimized.
questions.explanation:
Workplace violence is any act or threat of physical violence, harassment, intimidation, or other 
threatening disruptive behavior that occurs at the work site. It ranges from threats and verbal abuse to physical 
assaults and even homicide. It can affect and involve employees, clients, customers and visitors. 
In most workplaces where risk factors can be identified, the risk of assault can be prevented or minimized if 
employers take appropriate precautions. One of the best protections employers can offer their workers is to 
establish a zero-tolerance policy toward workplace violence. This policy should cover all workers, patients, clients, 
visitors, contractors, and anyone else who may come in contact with company personnel. 
By assessing their worksites, employers can identify methods for reducing the likelihood of incidents occurring. 
OSHA believes that a well written and implemented Workplace Violence Prevention Program, combined with 
engineering controls, administrative controls and training can reduce the incidence of workplace violence in both the 
private sector and Federal workplaces.

questions.question: A comprehensive crime prevention assessment should ask all of the following EXCEPT:
options: What is the prevailing attitude toward security?
Who is responsible for the overall security program?
What kind of physical safety systems are presently used in other organizations?
questions.explanation:
Other pertinent questions include: 
• 
What is your target potential? 
• 
What resources are available locally and how rapid are the response times for fire, police and ambulance? 
• 
What kind of physical security systems and controls are presently used? 
• 
Do the available security resources, policies and procedures meet the potential threat?

questions.question: All of the following are guidelines that can increase security except:
options: Install key-card access systems at main entrances and on other appropriate doors.
Issue access control badges, with recent photographs, to all employees and authorized contractors.
Upgrade perimeter control systems with intercoms and closed circuit monitoring devices.
Provide master and extra keys to all employees
questions.explanation:
The master and extra keys should be locked in the security office. Other guidelines that can increase 
security include the following: 
• 
Issue access control badges, with recent photographs, to all employees and authorized contractors. 
• 
Upgrade perimeter control systems with intercoms and closed circuit monitoring devices. 
• 
Keep master and extra keys locked in a security office.

questions.question: According to OSHA regulations, companies with _________ or more employees must have a written emergency action plan.
questions.explanation:
OSHA requires that companies with 10 or more employees develop a written emergency action plan. 
Smaller companies may communicate their emergency action plan to their employees orally.

questions.question: Emergency procedures, including the handling of any toxic chemicals, should include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Escape procedures and escape route assignments.
Special procedures for employees who perform or shut down critical plant operations.
Systems to account for all employees after evacuation and for information about the plan.
Procedures for segregation of toxic chemicals based on their toxicity level.
questions.explanation:
Emergency procedures must also address rescue and medical duties for employees who perform 
them as well as means for reporting fires and other emergencies.

questions.question: OSHA requires that the employer designates an emergency response coordinator and a backup coordinator. Duties of the coordinator and employer include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Determining what emergencies may occur and seeing that emergency procedures are developed to address each situation.
Directing all emergency activities including evacuation of personnel.
Ensuring that outside emergency services are notified when necessary.
Ensuring that a member of the local fire department and police serve on the emergency committee.
questions.explanation:
The emergency response coordinator must also be able to direct the shutdown of plant operations 
when necessary.

questions.question: You are a supervisor in the manufacturing department of a company. You observe an employee ignoring the department's safety rules. Which of the following is the most effective disciplinary action against the employee?
options: Immediately inform the HR department in writing
Suspend the employee and provide training
Provide the employee with a written warning
Use verbal reprimand first, and if the behavior continues, issue a written warning followed by suspension and eventual termination.
questions.explanation: This would be the best course of action to follow.

questions.question: A rating of four in the blue section of NFPA 704 system indicates:
questions.explanation:
In NFPA 704 system, red indicates flammability, blue indicates health hazards, yellow indicates 
reactivity, and the color white is reserved for communicating special information such as a material being an oxidizer 
or water reactive. In each section, there is a rating between zero and four with zero indicating no hazards and four 
indicating extreme hazards.

questions.question: In fire-fighting operations, water can extinguish a fire by which of the following mechanisms?
questions.explanation:
Water has an excellent evaporative cooling effect on a fire. Water should never be used on certain 
class B (flammable liquids), class D (metal fires), and class C (electrical) fires. If a flammable liquid is insoluble in 
water and also lighter than water, it would float on top of the water and spread the fire. Use of water on electrical 
fires could pose a fatal shock hazard.

questions.question: The most important step in prevention of workplace violence is:
options: A clear non-harassment policy by the management.
Isolation of employees who have a tendency to harass others.
questions.explanation:
Management commitment and a clear non-harassment policy is the most important step in prevention 
of workplace violence.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST tool for minimizing loss of life during a fire?
questions.explanation: Use of automatic sprinkler systems has proven to minimize loss of life during fires.

questions.question: When transferring flammable or combustible liquids between containers, which of the following safety measures must be undertaken?
options: Provide electrical grounding for the larger container.
Bond the containers with an electrical conductor.
The only safety measure to follow for this situation is elimination of all sources of ignition.
questions.explanation:
Bonding the containers together does not eliminate the buildup of static charges. However, it makes 
the potential difference between the containers equal so there is no driving force for the flow of static charges which 
could act as a source of ignition.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the BEST classification for welding and cutting operations?
questions.explanation:
Hot work is any work that involves burning, welding, using fire, or spark-producing tools, or that 
produces a source of ignition. Examples of hot work include welding and cutting operations.

questions.question: Which of the following organizations mandates lockout/tagout programs for service or maintenance of certain types of equipment?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is OSHA.
questions.exclusion_reason: Duplicate question content; retained d1-s-9

questions.question: What is the first thing to do when a water sample comes into a lab?
options: Take the pH of the sample
Log in and assure chain of custody of the sample
questions.explanation:
Log in the sample. Good laboratory procedures dictate that the sample be 
immediately logged in as soon as possible after arriving at the lab.

questions.question: What is the major factor in determining the required sample volume?
questions.explanation:
The analytical sensitivity is the determining factor when calculating the required 
sample volume.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a typical VOC?
questions.explanation:
Vinyl Chloride is a typical Volatile Organic Compound (V.O.C.) found in 
contaminated water. Arsenic is a metal, Aldrin I s pesticide and carbonic acid is an inorganic 
compound. Volatile organic compounds (VOC) generally means any compound of carbon 
which participates in atmospheric photochemical reactions, excluding carbon monoxide, 
carbon dioxide, carbonic acid, metallic carbides or carbonates, and ammonium carbonate.

questions.question: Why is vapor density important is assessing the hazard of a spilled chemical?
options: The concentration of the vapor will determine the hazard
The vapor can cause visual problems for responders
Vapor density is not an issue in assessing hazard
It will determine the behavior of the vapor at the spill scene
questions.explanation: Vapor density will determine if the vapor will sink into low areas or dissipate.

questions.question: Water is poured into a cylindrical tank at the rate of 9 in3/min. How much time is required to fill the tank if its radius is 3 in. and its height is 14 in.?
questions.explanation:
The volume of a cylinder = π r2 height 
V = π (3 in)214 in = 396 in3. 
Since the rate of flow is 9 in3/minute, the time required to fill the tank is (396 in3)/(9 in3/min) 
= 44 min
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: A wind rose is:
options: A graphical representation of yearly wind direction
A graphical representation of stack discharges
questions.explanation:
Wind roses are graphical representations of wind direction. They are important in 
determining prevailing wind direction

questions.question: In reviewing designs for product safety, all of the following environmental consideration(s) must be dealt with EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
The environment must be considered in designs for product safety because: 
 
the ambient environment (temperature, humidity, corrosivity) will affect the condition 
and operation of the product 
 
the operation of the product (noise, particles, toxic vapors, liquid effluent) would, 
without proper controls, pollute the environment 
 
product disposal, should it contain hazardous materials (mercury, lead, beryllium) has 
the potential to contaminate soil and groundwater. Aesthetics are not part of a product 
safety environmental assessment.
questions.exclusion_reason: Unreliable symbol extraction; held for review

questions.question: Elements of a hazardous waste manifest include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
A manifest does not require an insurance company number. It does require manifest 
number, EPA ID number, and total quantity of waste.

questions.question: Which of the following common law causes of action is NOT used to pursue legal remedies in hazardous waste/hazardous materials, or "toxic tort", damage suits?
questions.explanation:
Negligence, nuisance and trespass, and strict liability for ultra-hazardous activities 
are legal instruments that are available to plaintiffs in toxic tort suits for damages from 
hazardous materials/wastes releases or exposure.

questions.question: A Phase I environmental site assessment typically includes the following activities EXCEPT:
options: Inspect the property, review environment records, and assess chemical handling and disposal practices
Aerial photo search and review of past ownership
Determine whether the subject or surrounding properties are identified on any government lists of contaminated sites, or lists of sites requiring investigation, clean- up, and/or enforcement.
questions.explanation:
Phase I environmental site assessments, a common term for the initial investigation 
in industrial property transfers, includes the listed activities and others as well, except for 
aerial analysis of the hydrogeology.

questions.question: Phase I environmental assessments should include, but are not limited to:
options: Historical review of the uses(s) and improvement(s) made to the subject site
An investigation of subject and neighboring properties with respect to environmental enforcement actions and/or listing on federal or state contaminated property lists
Evaluation of whether present or past owners or tenants have managed hazardous materials or wastes on-site
questions.explanation:
Phase I environmental site assessments, as state of the art is currently defined, should 
include each of the above listed activities.

questions.question: In the RCRA program, UTS refers to:
questions.explanation:
Universal treatment standards are one of the key regulatory reforms of the Land 
Disposal Restrictions program found at 40 CFR 268. The universal treatment standards are 
the regulatory mechanism whereby a single ("universal") maximum allowable concentration 
is established for each regulated constituent in wastes that are hazardous at the point of 
generation, regardless of the waste code(s) carried by the waste. In other words, the 
concentration limit for the constituent chromium for land disposal purposes would be the 
same regardless of whether the waste was F006 or K051. Distinctions are still made between 
wastewater and non-wastewater forms of particular waste codes. The universal treatment 
standards were introduced in the so-called Phase II LDR final rule, appearing in the 
September 19, 1994 Federal Register, at 59 FR 47982-48110. The UTS are found at 40 CFR 
268.48, appropriately entitled "Table UTS - Universal Treatment Standards". The Phase II 
rule went into effect on December 19, 1994.

questions.question: A TLV-TWA is defined as:
options: A time-weighted average concentration for a normal 8-hour workday and 40 hour work week to which all workers can be exposed continuously, day after day, without effect.
A time-weighted average concentration for a normal 8-hour workday and 40-hour work week, to which nearly all workers can be repeatedly exposed, day after day, without adverse effect
questions.explanation:
TLV-TWA is a time weighted average concentration for a normal 8-hour workday 
and 40-hour work week, to which "nearly" all workers can be repeatedly exposed, day after 
day, without "adverse" effect.

questions.question: TLV-STEL is the concentration to which workers can be exposed for a short period of time without suffering from the following, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Dermatitis is not a factor in definition of the TLV-STEL, and therefore, employees 
may suffer from some dermatitis. A STEL exposure should NOT result in irritation, chronic 
or irreversible tissue damage, and narcosis of sufficient degree to increase the likelihood of 
accidental injury, impair self-rescue, or materially reduce work efficiency (provided that the 
8-hour TWA-TLV was not exceeded).

questions.question: A STEL is defined as a ____ minute TWA exposure which should not be exceeded at any time during the workday.
questions.explanation:
Exposures above the TLV-TWA up to the short term exposure limit (STEL) should 
be no longer than 15 minutes. The 15-minute STEL is a time weighted average exposure 
which should not be exceeded even if the 8-hour TWA is within the TLV- TWA.

questions.question: Exposures up to the TLV-STEL should not be longer than 15 minutes and should not occur more than:
questions.explanation:
Employees should not be exposed to the 15 minute STEL more than four times per 
day. There should be at least an hour between successive exposures.

questions.question: TLV-C stands for:
questions.explanation:
The Threshold Limit Value-Ceiling is the concentration that should not be exceeded 
during any part of the working exposure period.

questions.question: Excursions in worker exposure levels may exceed __ times the TLV-TWA for no more than __ minutes during a workday.
questions.explanation:
Excursions in worker exposure levels may exceed 3 times the TLV-TWA for no 
more than 30 minutes during a workday. This is based upon a geometric standard deviation of 
2.0, in which 5% of all values will exceed 3.13 times the geometric mean.

questions.question: Hazardous waste determinations are to be performed at what point in time?
options: Prior to seeking off-site disposal approvals
questions.explanation:
The EPA, in both recent rulemakings regarding listings and characteristics of 
hazardous wastes, as well as in the Land Disposal Restrictions rulemakings, has made their 
position regarding the importance of point of generation determinations quite clear. The 
determination may need to be redone after any on-site treatment, but such treatment does not 
alter the need for hazardous waste determinations to be performed at the point of generation 
for any wastes undergoing treatment on-site.

questions.question: The EPA considers all of the following pollutants "criteria pollutants" EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Hydrogen sulfide is not a criteria pollutant.

questions.question: Acronyms are used extensively in the various regulatory programs as a form of shorthand. Which of the following acronyms is NOT associated with the CWA program?
options: SPCC (Spill Prevention Control and Counter Measures)
questions.explanation:
National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) is associated with the Clean Air 
Act program. POTW, SPCC, and BAT are all terms associated with the Clean Water Act 
program.

questions.question: The "Superfund" law primarily addresses:
questions.explanation:
The Superfund law was written to force clean-up of sites contaminated with toxic 
materials. Sites are prioritized and those of highest priority are listed on the NPL (National 
Priorities List). Money is set aside to clean these sites up if the responsible parties cannot be 
found or refuse to clean it up.

questions.question: Drivers of any size vehicle transporting hazardous materials that require placarding must pass the pre-trip skills and written test to obtain a:
questions.explanation:
Under the terms of the Commercial Motor Vehicle Act, anyone driving a vehicle 
weighing more than 26,000 pounds, transporting more than 15 people including the driver, or 
transporting hazardous materials that require placards, must pass the pre-trip skills and 
written test to obtain a commercial driver's license (CDL).

questions.question: Which of the following agencies has an interest in safety and health matters and regulates selected chemical substances and mixtures?
questions.explanation:
The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) was established by the Toxic 
Substances Control Act (TSCA) in 1976 to regulate selected chemical substances and 
mixtures being manufactured, processed, distributed, imported, and disposed of, if they are 
considered an unreasonable risk to health and the environment.

questions.question: A firm makes a plated device that it installs on the purchaser's property. The device discharges a water effluent. Which of the following agencies govern the device operation?
questions.explanation: Normal operation of the device would be governed by EPA and OSHA.

questions.question: The Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) is enforced by the:
options: The Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) is enforced by the:
questions.explanation: The EPA enforces TSCA.

questions.question: The key element of RCRA designed to track hazardous waste from "cradle to grave" is the:
questions.explanation:
The manifest system was developed by RCRA to track hazardous waste from 
originator to final resting place.

questions.question: A manifest serves the following purposes:
options: It is a shipping document for hazardous wastes
It is a tracking document for hazardous wastes
It is a certificate of destruction for hazardous wastes
questions.explanation:
The manifest serves both shipping paper requirements under DOT regulations, and 
acts as a tracking document under RCRA regulations. The manifest is not a fail-safe 
document, however, and does not absolve the generator of CERCLA liabilities. At best the 
manifest merely indicates that the waste actually was received by the designated facility.

questions.question: The mandatory shipping document for hazardous waste purposes is:
options: Uniform hazardous materials bill of lading
questions.explanation:
The uniform hazardous waste manifest (EPA Form 8700-22) is the mandatory format 
for hazardous waste shipping documents. The actual forms are to be obtained from states 
mandating the use of state issued uniform hazardous waste manifests, or when the state is not 
involved in manifest distribution, from commercial printers following the mandatory format 
with the appropriate number of pages (minimum of 4).

questions.question: An industrial wastewater stream has high levels of dissolved copper that must be reduced before discharge. The wastewater is chemically treated to remove the copper. Which of the following will NOT drive the reaction to remove more copper?
options: Removing one of the products as a precipitate
Removing one of the products as a gas
Reducing the concentration of one of the reactants
Removing one of the products as a slightly ionized substance
questions.explanation:
Reducing reactant concentration tends to retard the chemical reaction process. On the 
other hand, if a product is removed, the chemical equilibrium is perturbed, and the reactants 
will continue to react until a new equilibrium is achieved.

questions.question: Which of the following chemicals is not a solvent in the operation described?
questions.explanation:
To be a solvent, the chemical must dissolve something. Epoxies in coremaking form a 
resin matrix (i.e., a polymer) that binds sand together - no solvent

questions.question: The greenhouse effect is due to a disruption in which geochemical cycle?
questions.explanation: The greenhouse effect is caused by a disruption in the global carbon cycle.

questions.question: In assessing mobility and persistence of hazardous constituents upon release to the environment, the following factors are of interest EXCEPT:
options: Octanol-water partition coefficient (Kow) and soil-sorption coefficient (Koc)
questions.explanation:
Electrofluorescence is not a factor considered in mobility and persistence. The other 
answers are of value in predicting the fate, transport, and persistence of chemicals released to 
the environment.

questions.question: tank farm is being designed and will be located in a geographical location that receives extensive rainfall. The tank farm will house four hazardous materials: fuel oil, ethanol, acetone, and sulfuric acid. To ensure that corporate safety and environmental protection policies are followed, you have been asked to provide input on the layout of the containment dikes. Because of the soil, no dike can be higher than 4.5 ft. Due to the potential for heavy rains, company policy requires a 25% overage be designed into the capacity of any given diked volume. What are the minimum dimensions of the diked area necessary to protect acetone tanks C and D?
questions.explanation:
Answer this question one step at a time. 

Step 1: Find the capacity of the larger tank. Dikes must be able to fully contain a release of 
the largest tank in the diked area. Tank C is the larger tank. Assume that its capacity is the 
same as the volume of a cylinder. The diameter of Tank C is 60 ft an d its height is 24 ft. Its 
volume is therefore 
V =  [(60 ft)2 / 4] 24 ft 
= 67,858 ft3 

Step 2: The next step is to determine the required capacity of the diked area. The dike must 
contain a complete loss of the largest tank plus a rainfall overage of 25%. Therefore, the 
actual capacity of the dike is 25% higher than the volume of the largest tan k. 
Total Volume = 1.25 * 67,858 ft3 
= 84,823 ft3 

Step 3: Unfortunately, we cannot use the volume occupied by the other tank in the diked area 
(Tank D). We DO assume that the volume occupied by Tank C is available, though. To 
calculate the unavailable dike volume occupied by Tank D, simply assume that Tank D is a 
cylinder of 4.5 ft high (the height of the dike) and calculate the volume of this 4.5 ft high 
cylinder. 
Volume Tank D = [(50 ft)2 / 4]4.5 ft 
= 8,836 ft3 

Step 4: Calculate the Net Volume. This is the Total Volume plus the Volume of Tank D. 
Net Volume = 84,823 ft3 + 8,836 ft3 
= 93,659 ft3 

Step 5: Calculate the required surface area necessary to cover this volume. We are allowed a 
dike height of 4.5 ft; therefore, the required surface area is the Net Volume divided by the 
dike height. 
Surface Area = 93,659 ft3 / 4.5 ft 
= 20,813 ft2 

Step 6: To calculate the preliminary minimum dimensions, simply take the square root of the 
Surface Area. This will give us the preliminary minimum dimensions in the form of a square. 
Minimum Dimension = 
ft2 
= 144.3 ft * 144.3 ft 

Step 7: Verify that these dimensions are compatible with tank separation requirements. Tank 
C must be at least 50 ft from Tank D. Assume that all other tanks in this tank farm can be 
placed sufficiently far away from Tank C in their own diked areas to meet minimum 
separation requirements. 
Tank C has a diameter of 60 ft, and Tank D has a diameter of 50 ft. The minimum separation 
distance is 50 ft. Therefore, when adding these gross dimensions, you find that the vertical 
dimension (with respect to the graphic) of 144.3 ft is insufficient. If the two tanks were built 
right on the upper and lower dikes, they would only be separated by 34.3 ft. An additional 

15.7 ft in the vertical dimension is required to account for minimum separation. 

Step 8: The minimum vertical dimension is therefore 
Vertical Dimension = 144.3 ft + 15.7 ft 
= 160 ft 

Step 9: Calculate the new horizontal dimension (with respect to the graphic). The Net 
Volume is still 93,659 ft3. The new horizontal dimension is therefore: 
Horizontal Dimension = 93,659 ft3 / 160 ft / 4.5 ft 
= 130 ft 
Finally, the minimum dimensions of this diked area are 160 ft vertically * 130 ft horizontally. 

NOTE: Always go through the process of determining the preliminary minimum dimensions. 
If Tank C and Tank D contained fuel oil instead of acetone, for example, the preliminary 
minimum dimensions would have been the actual minimum dimensions.

a complete loss of Tank G plus a rainfall overage of 25%. Therefore, the actual capacity of the dike is 
25% higher than the volume of Tank G. 
Total Volume = 1.25 * 39,270 ft3 
= 49,087 ft3 

Step 3: Since there are no other tanks in this diked area, we can immediately calculate the required 
surface area to cover this volume by dividing the volume by the dike height of 4.5 ft. 
Surface Area = 49,087 ft3 / 4.5 ft 
= 10,908 ft2

ft2

Step 5: Verify that these dimensions are compatible with the tank separation requirements. Tank G 
must be at least 80 ft from Tank F. Assume that Tank E is sufficiently far away from Tank G to meet

its diked area, it would still be too close to Tank F by 24.6 ft (104.4 ft - 50 ft - 80 ft + 1 ft). (The 1 ft

Therefore, the minimum horizontal dimension (with respect to the graphic) is

Step 6: Calculate the new minimum vertical dimension (with respect to the graphic) based on the

Minimum Vertical Dim. = 49,087 ft3 / 129 ft / 4.5 ft = 84.6 ft

questions.question: All of the following agents can contribute to indoor air pollution EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Although PCB's have caused problems in building contamination, they have a low 
vapor pressure and do not cause indoor air quality problems, unless burned. Carbon dioxide, 
formaldehyde, and asbestos are common indoor air pollutants that are caused by building 
materials and occupants.

questions.question: Which of the following sources of indoor air pollution in an office environment can be lethal?
questions.explanation:
Airborne microorganisms circulated from water-cooling systems (Legionella 
Pneumophila) have caused Legionnaires Disease from acute exposures. Formaldehyde and 
carbon dioxide require concentrations well beyond those found in offices to be lethal. Poor 
ventilation would require reductions in oxygen level below 19.5%, which is unlikely in an 
office environment.

questions.question: Methods to control Legionnaires disease include the following EXCEPT :
options: Locate make-up air intakes upwind from cooling towers
Periodic cleaning of cooling water systems
questions.explanation:
Continuous feed biocides can cause resistant strains of bacteria in the cooling system. 
It is best to alternate biocides to prevent resistance. Prevention of cooling tower aerosols into 
the building makeup air will prevent bacteria from entering the ventilation system. Complete 
periodic cleaning and sampling of the cooling water systems have proven effective.

questions.question: What capacity of outdoor (fresh) air does the American Society of Heating, Refrigerating, and Air Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE) recommend in its 62-1989 Standard for an office environment?
questions.explanation:
ASHRAE, in its 62-1989 Standard, recommends 20 cfm/person of outdoor air for 
acceptable indoor air quality in an office environment. This value has been chosen to control 
carbon dioxide and other contaminants with an adequate margin of safety and to account for 
health variations among people, varied activity levels, and a moderate amount of smoking.

questions.question: Secondary containment should be considered for all EXCEPT:
options: Chemical and waste loading and unloading areas
Virgin product storage areas and tanks
questions.explanation:
Secondary containment of chemical and waste storage and transfer areas is a best 
management practice and should be seriously evaluated even where not currently required by 
federal, state, or local regulations. Immersion heaters present a fire hazard in electroplating 
operations but do not require secondary containment

questions.question: Secondary containment is considered:
options: Unnecessary if hazardous waste tanks and containers are frequently inspected and when releases are directed away from storm sewers
questions.explanation:
Regardless of regulatory requirements, secondary containment is recommended as a 
best management practice. Secondary containment manages the risks and costs associated 
with chemical releases. Requirements for secondary containment can be found in both RCRA 
and CWA regulations. The fines, clean up costs, and litigation expenses associated with oil 
and chemical releases indicate the necessity for secondary containment.

questions.question: How is asbestos disposed of?
questions.explanation: Asbestos waste is commonly landfilled.

questions.question: What type of facility would be least likely to generate lab packs?
questions.explanation:
Except for semiconductor manufacturing facility, all of the above facilities would use 
a wide variety of small quantities of chemicals and would then require lab packs.

questions.question: Why are temperature inversions important in air pollution?
options: They increase reaction of the chemicals with ozone
questions.explanation: Temperature inversions serve to concentrate air pollutants near the ground.

questions.question: The level of radon exposure in a home considered by the EPA to be the maximum acceptable level is:
questions.explanation:
The EPA has recommended the level of 4.0 picocuries/l air as a maximum safe level 
of exposure to radon in the home environment.

questions.question: Maximum contaminant levels (MCL's) are regulatory thresholds for:
options: Effluent quality under the Clean Water Act
Air emissions under the Clean Air Act
Allowable drinking water pollutant concentrations under the Safe Drinking Water Act
questions.explanation:
MCL's represent maximum permissible levels of specified contaminants in water 
which is delivered to any user of a public water supply system.

questions.question: Primary MCL's refer to:
options: Concentrations of regulated drinking water contaminants that are protective of human health with a margin of safety
Maximum levels of contaminants allowable in public water systems
Workplace exposure limits for airborne contaminants
questions.explanation:
Primary maximum contaminant levels (MCL's) are the maximum permissible levels 
of specific contaminants in water which is delivered to any user of a public water supply 
system. Answer 1 refers to maximum contaminant level goals (MCLG's). MCL's are 
sometimes used as groundwater cleanup goals in the RCRA and CERCLA programs.

questions.question: MCLG's refer to:
options: Non-enforceable concentrations of drinking water contaminants that are protective of health with a margin of safety
Non-enforceable standards addressing the aesthetic qualities of drinking water, such as appearance, odor, and taste
Regulatory standards for small public water supply systems
questions.explanation:
Maximum contaminant level goals (MCLG's) under the Safe Drinking Water Act 
(SDWA) are non-enforceable health-based standards, and are used in developing legally 
enforceable MCL's. Aesthetic qualities of drinking water are addressed by non-enforceable 
secondary MCL's.

questions.question: Industrial dischargers to a POTW should be concerned when a POTW violates its NPDES permit because:
options: Potential bans on new sewer connections
Potential additional or more stringent retreatment requirements
Potential liability for contamination of sewage treatment plant sludge
questions.explanation:
Industrial dischargers to the sewer to a publicly owned treatment works (sewage 
treatment plant) should be very concerned when the POTW violates its NPDES permit for all 
of the above listed reasons, as well as for the real potential for increased scrutiny of its own 
operations by federal, state, and local officials, and environmental groups. Increased 
enforcement activity and citizen suits are likely to follow.

questions.question: Chemical analysis of the products of combustion will almost always show the presence of what element in the molecules?
questions.explanation:
Since oxygen is required to support normal combustion, the products of combustion 
would contain oxygen in combination with other elements.

questions.question: Which of the following general classes of insecticides is the most persistent in the environment?
questions.explanation:
The carbamate and organophosphate insecticides are degraded relatively rapidly in 
both the environment and the mammalian body compared to the organochlorine insecticides. 
Organochlorine pesticides are relatively persistent in the environment. DDT was an 
organochlorine pesticide

questions.question: What type of emergencies would you expect to find at a TSD site?
options: Those dealing with fire and similar life threatening conditions
questions.explanation:
Treatment, storage, and disposal (TSD) sites are required by OSHA, TSCA, and 
CERCLA to have an emergency response plan for all emergencies involving hazardous 
substances. OSHA's HAZWOPER Standard, 29 CFR 1910.120, is the standard that details 
program requirements.

questions.question: All of the following EXCEPT ___________ are components of photochemical air pollution.
questions.explanation:
Photochemical air pollution arises from a series of atmospheric reactions - NO2 
absorbs UV light giving rise to NO and O radicals which in turn react to produce O3 (ozone). 
Ozone and NO can react to regenerate NO2. Thus the reaction is cyclic. Sulfur dioxide is not 
part of the photochemical smog problem.

questions.question: Beer's Law refers to:
questions.explanation:
Beer's Law is A = kC, where A is the absorbance of a solution, C is the concentration 
of analyte, and k is a constant whose value depends on the wavelength of the radiation, the 
nature of absorbing system, and the optical path length, or cell thickness.

questions.question: The phenomena of biomagnification of heavy metals is due to the:
questions.explanation:
The food chain serves to concentrate heavy metals in the uppermost predators as the 
lower forms add to their heavy metal loading.

questions.question: What does BOD stand for?
questions.explanation:
BOD stands for Biochemical Oxygen Demand. This is the quantity of oxygen used in 
the aerobic stabilization of wastewaters.

questions.question: A cyclone scrubber is put on-line with an Electrostatic Precipitator (ESP). The efficiency of the cyclone is 80% while the ESP is 95%. Assuming the cyclone is last, what is the overall system efficiency?
questions.explanation:
Efficiency = 95% + (80 * 5%) 
= 99% efficiency

questions.question: A fluid system with a Reynolds number significantly below 2,000 implies what about a fluid system's flow characteristics?
questions.explanation:
The Reynolds number is a dimensionless number used to model whether the flow is 
turbulent or laminar. If the Reynolds number is less than 2,000 the flow will have laminar 
characteristics. If it is greater than 2,000 the fluid system is considered turbulent .

questions.question: A liquid with a pH of 1 is:
questions.explanation:
A liquid with a pH of 1 is highly acidic. Basic and alkaline are synonyms of a liquid 
with a pH greater than 7. A liquid with a pH of 7 is neutral.

questions.question: A chemical compound capable of forming multiple chemical bonds to a metal ion is called a:
questions.explanation:
A chelating agent is a chemical compound capable of forming multiple chemical 
bonds to a metal ion.

questions.question: A substance that affects the change in hydrogen ion concentration (pH) otherwise produced by adding acids or bases to a solution is called a:
questions.explanation:
A buffer is a substance that reduces the change in hydrogen ion concentration (pH) 
otherwise produced by adding acids or bases to a solution.

questions.question: Which one of the following correctly balances the following reaction: NaOH + H2SO4?
questions.explanation:
This is an example of an acid base neutralization reaction. The resulting salt from this 
reaction is sodium sulfate. To properly balance the full reaction equation, two sodium 
hydroxide molecules react with one sulfuric acid molecule to yield Na2SO4 + 2 (H2O).

questions.question: All the following are true about ketones EXCEPT:
options: Ketones have one or more carbonyl groups (C = O)
Methanol, a small-chain ketone, can cause blindness
Long term exposure to ketones can adversely affect the brain and nervous system
Ketones are commonly used as solvents
questions.explanation: Methanol is not a ketone; it is an alcohol.

questions.question: Which one of the following equations is NOT balanced?
questions.explanation:
Only one molecule of Na2O reacts with one molecule of water to produce 2 
molecules of NaOH.

questions.explanation:
mole is the equivalent of one gram-molecular weight. Since the molecular weight of 
water is 18 g/mol, 25 grams is equivalent to 25 g / (18 g/mol) = 1.39 mol.

questions.question: One atmosphere is equivalent to how many pounds per square inch pressure?
questions.explanation: One atmosphere is equivalent to 14.7 pounds per square inch pressure.

questions.question: The most prevalent all-around solvent is:
questions.explanation:
Water is the most prevalent all-around solvent. It is nontoxic, nonflammable, and 
with proper additives, forms a solvent system that works well even with many organic 
materials.

questions.question: A fiber is defined as having an aspect ratio (length to diameter) greater than:
questions.explanation: Fibers are particles which have a length that is at least three times its width.

questions.question: Gas chromatography (GC) is an excellent separation technique for many organic compounds found in the industrial environment. Which of the following is often performed after GC to identify the compound?
questions.explanation:
GC/MS is commonly performed to separate and identify the compound of interest. 
GC separates a mixture based on differences in boiling point and solubility. Differences in 
these properties produce differences in retention times in the GC column separating the 
mixture. MS fractures and ionizes each compound into a recognizable pattern.

questions.question: The conversion of ammoniacal nitrogen to nitrate ion through the aeration of activated sludge is called:
questions.explanation:
In the sewage treatment process, nitrification converts ammoniacal nitrogen to nitrate 
ion during the aeration of waste water.

questions.question: Two nuclei of the same element that have the same charge but different masses are called:
questions.explanation: Isotopes of the same element have the same charge but different nuclear masses.

questions.question: Normally formless fluids that occupy the space of enclosure and which can be changed to the liquid or solid state by increased pressure and decreased temperature are called:
questions.explanation:
Gases are normally formless fluids that occupy the space of enclosure and can be 
changed to the liquid or solid state by increased pressure and decreased temperature.

questions.question: Which aliphatic hydrocarbon features double carbon bonds?
questions.explanation:
Alkenes (olefins) are unsaturated hydrocarbons with one or more double bonds. 
Alkanes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with only single carbon bonds. Alkynes are 
unsaturated hydrocarbons with one or more triple bonds.

questions.question: The tendency of a liquid to vaporize at room temperature is its:
questions.explanation:
Volatility is the tendency or ability of a liquid to vaporize. Ethanol and gasoline are 
examples of volatile liquids because of their tendency to evaporate rapidly.

questions.question: The latent heat of vaporization of water is:
questions.explanation:
970 Btu/lb is the latent heat of vaporization of water. It takes a relatively large 
amount of heat to vaporize water.

questions.question: A chemical breakdown due to heat is known as a:
questions.explanation: Pyrolysis is the breakdown of materials due to heat.

questions.question: The pressure at which a vapor is at equilibrium is called the:
questions.explanation:
Vapor pressure is the pressure at which molecules escaping from a liquid are equal to 
the number of molecules returning to the liquid from the vapor.

questions.question: In the last 15 years, air pollution emissions have:
questions.explanation:
In the last 15 years many air pollutants, like automobile emissions, have been 
substantially reduced. For example, an automobile purchased in 1990 emitted approximately 
4% of that of a similar 1970 model. Another example is sulfur dioxide, the main ingredient of 
acid rain that is emitted from coal-burning electric utilities. Compared with 1977, the emitted 
rate of SO2 is now 20% lower. Much of this can be attributed to regulations that require 
controls like after-burners and scrubbers.

questions.question: The greatest single contributor to urban air pollution is:
questions.explanation:
Cars and trucks are major sources of carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, and volatile 
organic compounds that interact in the presence of sunlight to produce ground-level ozone 
pollution commonly referred to as smog. Researchers allege the automobile is responsible for 
approximately 40% of urban smog nationally and a great deal more in some areas of 
California.

questions.question: Background concentrations in contaminated soil investigations refer to:
options: Constituent concentrations in samples from areas not affected by the activity being monitored
The maximum allowable incremental contamination allowed by EPA
Clean-up standards necessary to protect public health and environmental quality
Statistical evaluation of data from the potentially contaminated area
questions.explanation:
Background concentrations typically are of concern only with respect to those 
constituents naturally occurring in soil. Many regulatory officials believe Answers 2 and 3 to 
be true. However, background concentrations of a variety of chemical constituents vary 
widely even in uncontaminated soils. Background concentrations are often used in statistical 
comparisons of levels in areas under investigation to those that are presumably 
uncontaminated.

questions.question: The term for the interaction of two toxins where the combined effect is greater than the sum is:
questions.explanation:
Synergistic effects occur when two substances act together to produce a toxic effect 
greater than the sum of each. For example, asbestos exposure and cigarette smoking produce 
a cancer risk that is much greater than the sum of each risk. Additive effects are the sum of 
each substance on the body. Potentiation is where one substance has no effect unless 
combined with a second substance, and antagonistic effects occur when two substances 
interfere with each others effects, giving an overall lesser effect.

questions.question: Which of the following is the second most plentiful element in the earth's crust:
questions.explanation: The second most plentiful element in the earth's crust is silicon.

questions.question: Failure to adequately clean-up chemical releases can result in:
options: The spill area being considered an unpermitted land disposal unit
Extensive soil and ground water contamination
questions.explanation:
All of the above listed consequences can result from the failure to adequately 
remediate chemical releases. Another impact is a potential decrease in property value.

questions.question: All of the following are natural sources of air pollution EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Fossil fuel is a component of the global carbon cycle that man mines and combusts; 
therefore, it is a man-made pollution source.

questions.question: Diesel engines produce ____ pollutants than do gasoline engines:
options: Less if compression ratios are higher than gasoline engines
questions.explanation:
Diesel engines produce more pollutants than do comparable gasoline engines. 
Compression ratios are necessarily higher in diesel engines.

questions.question: Viable reasons for incineration of air pollutants include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Incineration reduces odors, effectively removes most VOC's, and reduces explosion 
hazards at plants by not allowing build up of flammables.

questions.question: Based on the tonnage of material emitted annually, which of the following sources accounts for the most air pollution in the United States?
questions.explanation:
Transportation, including private automobiles, accounts for approximately 60% of the 
air pollution in the United States.

questions.question: Atomic absorption is distinctly good for what type of analysis?
questions.explanation:
Atomic absorption is an analytical technique which takes advantage of the 
characteristic absorption by metals of certain wavelengths of light.

volume of a cylinder. Its volume is therefore: 
V = [(60 ft)2 / 4] 24 ft 
= 67,858 ft3 

Step 2: The next step is to determine the required capacity of the diked area. The dike must 
contain a complete loss of either tank plus a rainfall overage of 25%. Therefore, the actual 
capacity of the dike is 25% higher than the volume of either tank. 
Total Volume = 1.25 * 67,858 ft3 

= 84,823 ft3 

Step 3: Unfortunately, we cannot use the volume occupied by one of the tanks in the diked 
area. We DO assume that the volume occupied by the ruptured/leaking tank is available, 
though. We do not know the height of the dike, but we DO know the surface area of either 
tank. We will use this number shortly. Calculate the unavailable surface area of either tank. 
Tank Surface Area =  [(60 ft)2 / 4] 
= 2,827 ft2 

Step 4: Based on the dimensions given for the dike surrounding Tank H, we can determine 
the existing surface area of the dike and subtract the additional surface area made unavailable 
by the other tank. 
Existing Surface Area = 190 ft * 140 ft 
= 26,600 ft2 
Net Surface Area = Existing Surface Area - Tank Surface Area 
= 26,600 ft2 - 2,827 ft2 
= 23,773 ft2 

Step 5: Calculate the height of the dike by dividing the Total Volume by the Net Surface 
Area. 
Dike Height = 84,823 ft3 / 23,773 ft2 
= 3.57 ft
