questions.question: The typical "scrubber" used in a factory for acid vapor emissions control is:
questions.explanation:
A wet collector controls emissions through absorption of the air stream with a caustic 
liquid.

questions.question: Secondary standards as regards to drinking water are related to:
questions.explanation:
Secondary standards for drinking water are related to aesthetic values that are more 
socially related.

questions.question: The removal of insoluble matter from water is referred to as:
questions.explanation:
Primary waste treatment removes insoluble matter through screening, removal of grit, 
and primary sedimentation

questions.question: Acronyms are used extensively in the various regulatory programs as a form of shorthand. Which of the following acronyms is not defined by the RCRA program?
questions.explanation:
RQ, standing for Reportable Quantity, is defined under the CERCLA program. 
Please note, however, that hazardous wastes are by definition a subset of hazardous 
substances, and RQs have been assigned to each listed hazardous waste and each 
characteristic of hazardous waste. TCLP, SQG, and LQG are acronyms for RCRA defined 
terms of toxicity characteristic leaching procedure, small quantity generator, and large 
quantity generator, respectively.

questions.question: The toxic chemical which caused the Bhopal disaster had the acronym MIC. This stands for:
questions.explanation: Methyl iso-cyanate was the toxic chemical released during the Bhopal disaster.

questions.question: In situations involving the transfer of industrial property, the buyer should:
options: Determine whether there are any state laws regarding the environmental aspects of real property transfers
Perform business and environmental "due diligence" audits

Determine whether the necessary environmental permits have been obtained, and whether the facility is in compliance with permit terms and conditions. Identify any limitations on permit transfers and the appropriate procedures
questions.explanation:
All of the above activities are prudent in situations involving the transfer of industrial 
properties due to the risks, costs, and liabilities under common law, state environmental 
statutes, and federal environmental statutes, especially CERCLA (Comprehensive 
Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act) or "Superfund".

questions.question: Maximize the useful lifetime of process solutions
options: Maximize the useful lifetime of process solutions
Incorporate preventative maintenance and spill containment measures
questions.explanation:
Good operating practices as waste minimization measures can be implemented to 
achieve any or all of the above listed objectives.

questions.question: One key factor in management success is Crisis Management. Which incident is an example of exemplary crisis management?
options: Union Carbide and Institute, West Virginia
CH2M Hill and the Milwaukee tunnel collapse
questions.explanation:
Johnson & Johnson's handling of the Tylenol scare is considered an excellent example 
of effectively dealing with a major crisis.

questions.question: A flood destroys your company's operations facility. After the emergency management issues are addressed, your company implements several plans to: 1) recover critical files and information that had been stored offsite, 2) set up a temporary facility from which operations can be conducted, and 3) inform customers of the situation and how they will be served. These plans are among examples of a comprehensive loss control activity called:
questions.explanation:
Business continuity planning is a key part of a loss control program. Such plans 
should include recovering corporate information, setting up operations, and financing 
temporary operations until a new facility can be commissioned. Depending upon the risk of a 
natural disaster, some companies purchase business interruption insurance to help finance 
operations.

questions.question: Waste minimization measures are driven by:
questions.explanation:
All of the above listed considerations drive waste minimization/pollution prevention 
efforts. The Pollution Prevention Act of 1990, while not regulatory in nature, is evidence of 
Congressional interest in this area. The Hazardous and Solid Waste Amendments to RCRA 
resulted in waste minimization certifications being placed on manifests, and requirements for 
discussion of waste minimization efforts and achievements being added to biennial reports. 
Many states have their own waste minimization requirements.

questions.question: PRP is an acronym for:
questions.explanation:
PRP has become a common term in the discussion of responsibility for 
environmental contamination. In the United States, the EPA allows the use of the word 
"potentially" in front of the term "responsible party" in the CERCLA context.

questions.question: Joint and several liability defines a scope of liability in the United States. The practical meaning of joint and several liability is best described as:
options: All responsible parties must jointly contribute to clean-up costs, to the extent of their volumetric share of the wastes at the site
Each and every responsible party could be held individually liable for the entire cost of the clean-up
NPL sites where there are multiple responsible parties must act jointly, through generator committees, to severally apportion costs amongst themselves
EPA must allocate costs among responsible parties in a manner that reflects both the volume and toxicity of their wastes, as well as the difficulty of clean-up
questions.explanation:
The liability provisions under Section 107 of CERCLA are strict, joint and several, 
and retroactive in application.

questions.question: Strict liability can refer to the standard of liability in the United States. The practical implications of strict liability in cases of environmental contamination are best described as:
options: The liability applies regardless of fault, and the government does not have to prove intent or negligence on the part of the responsible party
Compliance with laws and regulations in effect at the time of disposal does not matter
The government does not need to prove that a responsible party's waste at the site actually was released or caused harm
questions.explanation:
The liability provisions of CERCLA are found at Section 107, and are strict, joint and 
several, and retroactive.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is the correct definition of the process of adsorption?
options: Adsorption is the process of removing a component of a liquid mixture into a gas stream.
Adsorption is the process of removing a component of a liquid mixture into another liquid.
Adsorption is the process of removing a pure gas or one or more components of a gaseous mixture into a liquid stream.
Adsorption is the process of removing a pure gas or one or more components of a gaseous mixture into a solid bed.
questions.explanation:
Air purifying respirators remove the contaminants in the air by adsorption. Activated charcoal is a 
good example of an adsorbent.

questions.question: Chemical hazardous wastes must be segregated from incompatibles. Chemical wastes should be segregated by general groupings. Which of the following is NOT part of chemical groupings for segregation of hazardous waste?
questions.explanation:
The other groupings are: flammables, non-halogenated organic solvents, halogenated organic 
solvents, organic acids, carcinogens, mercury and mercury compounds, and general "dry" lab chemicals.

questions.question: Hazardous wastes under RCRA are divided into two major categories: characteristic wastes and listed wastes. Which of the following is NOT the property of a characteristic waste?
questions.explanation:
The fourth trait for characteristic hazardous waste is corrosivity. Toxicity is determined by Toxicity 
Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP). Under RCRA, ignitable wastes are defined by their flash points.

questions.question: Air pollutants are classified into "primary" and "secondary pollutants." Which of the following is an example of a secondary air pollutant?
questions.explanation:
Secondary pollutants are formed as a result of reaction between a primary pollutant and moisture and 
other elements in the atmosphere. For example, nitric acid is formed as a result of reaction between nitrogen oxides 
(primary pollutants) and moisture in the atmosphere. Also sulfuric acid which is formed as a result of reaction 
between sulfur oxides and moisture is considered a secondary air pollutant.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a means of control for air pollutants?
questions.explanation:
Combustion is used when the air pollutants are organic gases and vapors. Combustion converts the 
pollutants to carbon dioxide and water. 
Absorption: The harmful gases are removed by a suitable liquid in scrubbers. 
Adsorption: The harmful gases are removed on the surface of a suitable porous solid.

questions.question: All of the following are examples of proper segregation of hazardous wastes EXCEPT:
options: Segregate oxidizers from organics and flammables
questions.explanation:
Oxidizers can release oxygen that can make an ongoing fire in flammables much worse. Acid-base 
reactions are heat generating and the reaction between acids and cyanides can release highly toxic gases.

questions.question: Which of the following steps help reduce storm water pollution from hazardous wastes?
options: Hazardous wastes must be stored in a sealed container which is made of suitable materials of construction and must be properly labeled.
Storage, transportation, and disposal must comply with provisions of federal, state, and local laws and regulations.
Waste containers must be stored in containment facilities
questions.explanation:
The steps outlined in (a), (b), and (c) are designed to minimize storm water pollution from hazardous 
wastes.

questions.question: Ground-level or "bad" ozone is not emitted directly into the air, but is created by chemical reactions. Which of the following chemicals react to produce "bad" ozone?
options: Reaction between oxides of nitrogen (NOx) and volatile organic compounds in the presence of sunlight.
Reaction between oxygen molecule (O2) and oxygen atom (O) in presence of ultra violet light.
Reaction between oxygen and volatile organic compounds catalyzed by lighting
Reaction between sulfur oxide (SOx) and hydrocarbon gases in presence of sunlight
questions.explanation:
Ground-level or "bad" ozone can be generated by the chemical reaction between oxides of nitrogen 
and volatile organic compounds. The reaction is catalyzed by sunlight.

questions.question: Which of the following processes is NOT a source of lead emissions into the air?
questions.explanation:
Other sources of lead emissions into the air include utilities plants and piston-engine air craft 
operating on leaded aviation fuel.

questions.question: The EPA has identified six air pollutants as "criteria" air pollutants. Which of the following is NOT a member of "criteria" air pollutants as identified by the EPA?
questions.explanation:
The other three air pollutants identified as "criteria" pollutants are sulfur oxides, lead, and particulate 
matter.

questions.question: The EPA has identified six air pollutants because it regulates them by developing human health-based and/or environmentally-based criteria for setting permissible levels. These six air pollutants are known as:
questions.explanation:
The six air pollutants are identified by the EPA as "criteria" pollutants. These are carbon monoxide, 
nitrogen oxides, ground-level ozone, sulfur oxides, lead, and particulate matter.

questions.question: Unconfined aquifers are also called:
questions.explanation:
Unconfined aquifers are usually in unconsolidated material and the water table depth varies 
seasonally. The water table tends to rise in the winter when there is more rainfall, and fall in the summer due to less 
rainfall infiltration.

questions.question: The instrument used to measure water table elevation is called a:
questions.explanation: A piezometer is used to measure water table elevation.

questions.question: The ratio of volume of voids to the total volume of rock or soil is called:
questions.explanation:
This ratio is called the total porosity of rock or soil. It is expressed as a percentage or fraction. 
Porosity is a measure of the maximum amount of water a rock or soil can hold when it is saturated with water. For 
example, gravel porosity has a range of 25 to 40 percent.

questions.question: One of the important characteristics of aquifers is "specific yield". Which of the following statements BEST describes this term?
options: It is a measure of how quickly water will pass through the aquifer.
It is the volume of water that is retained on soil or rock after gravity drainage.
It is the volume of water that will drain by gravity from a specific volume of soil or rock.
questions.explanation:
Statement (b) is a description of specific retention. Statement (a) is a description of hydraulic 
conductivity. The porosity of a rock or soil is the sum of specific yield and specific retention.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to calculate the velocity and travel times of pollutants in groundwater?
questions.explanation:
Darcy's Law is useful in quantifying the movement of pollutants through underground waters. It relates 
the discharge (volume per unit time) to the hydraulic conductivity of the aquifer, the area the water moves through 
horizontally, and a dimensionless friction or head pressure loss. 
[Q = 

rac{K \cdot A \cdot (H_1 - H_2)}{L}] 
Where: 
• 
(Q) = discharge, volume per unit time 
• 
(K) = hydraulic conductivity 
• 
(A) = cross sectional area 
• 
(

rac{H_1 - H_2}{L}) = a dimensionless head pressure loss term

questions.question: Which of the following is formed when ground water is pumped from an unconfined aquifer?
questions.explanation: When water is pumped from a confined aquifer, a cone of depression is formed.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered to be the primary source of ground water?
questions.explanation: Rainfall is considered to be the primary source of groundwater.

questions.question: Rainfall has a pH of about 5.7. This means that:
options: Rainfall can dissolve carbonates in the soil or rock.
The ground water has a PH greater than the rainfall.
questions.explanation:
Rainfall generally has a pH less than 7.0 due to dissolved gases from the atmosphere. This makes 
rainfall slightly acidic. Therefore, rainfall can easily dissolve and react with carbonates and other minerals that are 
bases. This process increases the pH of the rainfall as it migrates and joins the underground waters.

questions.question: An underground storage tank containing diesel fuel has been leaking and might have caused groundwater contamination. The monitoring well for sampling must be designed in such a way to provide means for sampling from the _________ of the aquifer.
options: Top, mid-point, and bottom (mix to make a representative sample)
questions.explanation:
Diesel fuel has a specific gravity of less than 1.0 and is insoluble in water. It will float on top of water. 
The sample should be taken from the top of the aquifer.

questions.question: The unsaturated zone is an area directly below the soil surface where the soil particles are surrounded by both water and air. The unsaturated zone is also called the:
questions.explanation:
The unsaturated zone is also called the Vadose zone. The saturated zone is the area beneath the 
unsaturated zone where the soil particles are completely surrounded by water.

questions.question: A measure of the ability of an aquifer to transmit water is:
questions.explanation:
Hydraulic conductivity is a measure of how fast water passes through an aquifer. The fluid properties 
and the properties of the aquifer materials are factored into the value of hydraulic conductivity.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true in regard to soil permeability?
options: It is a measure of how easily water can move through an aquifer.
The permeability value depends on the properties of the aquifer materials only.
Permeability is a value usually obtained in a laboratory.
questions.explanation:
Statements in (a), (b), (c) are true in regard to permeability. Permeability is very similar to hydraulic 
conductivity. Usually, permeability is a value obtained in a laboratory, while hydraulic conductivity is measured in 
field.

questions.question: The boundary between the saturated and unsaturated zones of soil is called the:
questions.explanation:
A potentiometric surface is an area where the hydrostatic pressure exerted by the water table is equal 
to atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: The process that reduces the solubility of hazardous constituents and reduces the exposed area that may allow the migration of the contaminants is called:
questions.explanation:
Most stabilization processes incorporate the waste into a solid matrix using a binding agent or 
polymers.

questions.question: LDR is an acronym for which of the following?
questions.explanation:
LDR is an acronym for Land Disposal Restrictions. LDR restricted wastes are those that fall under the 
land disposal restriction standard under RCRA.

questions.question: Contaminated wastewater and groundwater can be treated biologically to remove hazardous substances. The microorganisms for biological treatment may be classified as heterotrophic and autotrophic. Which of the following statements is true in regard to these classes of microorganisms?
options: Both heterotrophs and autotrophs use organic matter.
questions.explanation:
Heterotrophs use organic matter and autotrophs use inorganic matter as the source of their nutrients 
in contaminated wastewater, groundwater, and soil.

questions.question: Microorganisms may be categorized as aerobic and anaerobic according to their utilization of oxygen. Which of the following statements is true in regard to these classes of microbes?
options: Anaerobic microbes use oxygen that is combined with other elements.
Aerobic microbes use oxygen that is combined with other elements.
Anaerobic microbes can use both free and combined oxygen.
questions.explanation:
Anaerobic microbes use oxygen that is combined with other elements. Examples are nitrates, 
carbonates, or sulfates.

questions.question: Undesirable heavy metals are usually removed from a liquid waste by precipitation. The solubility of heavy metals in a liquid waste can be reduced by varying the ____.
questions.explanation:
The pH is an important factor in removing heavy metals from a liquid waste stream. For example, the 
neutralization of an acidic waste can also cause the precipitation of heavy metals. The hydroxides of heavy metals 
are usually insoluble, so lime is commonly used for precipitating them.

questions.question: Air stripping is commonly used to remove low concentration of hazardous materials from wastewater. Which of the following statements is true in regard to air stripping?
options: Stripping towers may be induced-draft towers.
In stripping towers, the air flows upward and the liquid waste flows downward.
The gas-liquid system eventually reaches equilibrium based on Henry's Law.
questions.explanation:
Statements (a), (b), and (c) are all true in regard to air stripping towers. The air-waste stream usually 
undergoes secondary treatment such as incineration. In steam stripping, live steam is injected into the liquid waste.

questions.question: The removal of low concentrations of hazardous substances from aqueous waste using activated carbon is accomplished by which of the following mechanisms?
questions.explanation:
Adsorption is the process of removing a component of a liquid or gas on a solid. Absorption is the 
process of removing a component into a liquid. Ion exchange is a reversible exchange of ions between liquid and 
solid phases.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true in regard to dust particles?
options: They are formed when particles migrate and condense from the surface of a molten solid into the air.
They consist of mechanically-produced solid particles whose size can range from microscopic to visible.
Dust particles can be inorganic or organic.
The proper evaluation of dust hazards requires information regarding particle size, chemical composition, concentration, and factors that affect dispersion.
questions.explanation: Statements (b), (c), and (d) are true in regard to dust. Statement (a) is a characteristic of fumes.

questions.question: Cyclones are extensively used as an air pollution control device. Which of the following statements is NOT true in regard to cyclones?
options: Cyclones operate to collect relatively large-size particulate matter from a gaseous stream through the use of centrifugal forces.
Dust-laden gas is made to rotate in a decreasing diameter pathway, forcing solids to the outer edge of the gas stream for deposition into the bottom of the cyclone.
Efficiencies of 90% in particle sizes of 10 microns or greater are possible.
One of the disadvantages of cyclones is that operation at elevated temperatures is not possible.
questions.explanation:
Cyclones can operate at elevated temperatures. This is considered to be one of the advantages of 
cyclones.

questions.question: Absorption and wet-scrubbing equipment are used extensively for air pollution control. All of the following statements are true in regard to this type of equipment EXCEPT:
options: The goal is the removal of gases and particulate matter by causing the gaseous contamination to dissolve into the liquid stream and the solids to become entrained in the liquid.
The rate of gas transfer into the liquid is dependent upon the solubility, mass transfer mechanism, and equilibrium concentration of the gas in solution.
One of the advantages of this type of equipment is that high pressure drops are required.
The rate of particulate matter collection at constant pressure drops is inversely proportional to the aerodynamic mean diameter of the particulate matter and scrubber droplets.
questions.explanation: High pressure drops in absorption and wet-scrubbing equipment is a disadvantage.

questions.question: Baghouses are used extensively for air pollution control. Which of the following statements is true in regard to this type of equipment?
options: Baghouses use sieving, impaction, agglomeration, and electrostatic filtration principles to remove solids from a gaseous exhaust stream.
Baghouses maximize the filtration area by configuring the fabric filter media into a series of long, small- diameter fabric tubes, referred to as bags.

They are tightly packed into a housing wherein the dust-laden air moves across the bag fabric, thereby removing it from the gas stream and building up a filter cake which further enhances air cleaning.
questions.explanation: Statements (a), (b), and (c) are true in regard to baghouses.

questions.question: Electrostatic precipitators are used extensively as air pollution control devices. Which of the following statements is true in regard to electrostatic precipitators?
options: They use gaseous ions to charge particles, which are then moved through an electric field to be deposited onto charged collection plates.
Collected particulate material is removed by rapping or washing the plates.
To produce the free ions and electric field, high internal voltages are required.
questions.explanation:
Statements (a), (b), and (c) are true in regard to electrostatic precipitators. Since the collection 
process does not rely on mechanical processes such as sieving or impaction, but rather electrostatic forces, the 
internal gas passages within a precipitator are relatively open with small pressure drops and lower energy costs to 
move the gas stream. Electrostatic precipitators are best suited for removing small particles (less than 1 micron) 
from the air stream. Electrostatic precipitators have very high removal efficiency (99%) for particulate matters.

questions.question: An environmental Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA):
options: Is a tool that can be used to evaluate the potential environmental impacts of a product, material, process, or activity
Helps to promote the responsible design and redesign of products and processes
Allows businesses to make product improvements through environmentally sound process, material, and design choices
questions.explanation: LCA also gives businesses governmental incentives with the goal of obtaining environmental benefits.

questions.question: Vapor-cloud dispersion models used for predictions of migration of hazardous materials into the atmosphere require input of data. All of the following are examples of data input into the dispersion models EXCEPT:
options: Terrain evaluation at the source location
questions.explanation:
Other data that may be required include but are not limited to atmospheric turbulence, cloud cover, 
and solar radiation. The two types of vapor-cloud dispersion models are plume and puff.

questions.question: At the simplest level, treatment of sewage and most wastewaters is carried out through which of the following?
questions.explanation:
At the simplest level, treatment of sewage and most wastewaters is carried out through separation of 
solids from liquids, usually by sedimentation. By progressively converting dissolved material into solids, usually a 
biological floc, which is then settled out, an effluent stream of increasing purity is produced.

questions.question: Wastewater comes in three main types. Which of the following does not belong to the three main types of wastewater?
questions.explanation:
Wastewater comes in three main types namely Blackwater, Graywater and Yellow water. This is 
wastewater that originates from toilet fixtures, dishwashers, and food preparation sinks. It is made up of all the 
things that you can imagine going down the toilets, bath and sink drains.

questions.question: REACH is an acronym for Registration, Evaluation, Authorization and Restriction of Chemicals. Which of the following statements is correct regarding REACH?
options: It is enforced by OSHA under Hazards Communication standard (29CFR1910.1200).
It is a European Union regulation.
It is an EPA regulation enforced under Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA).
It is part of OSHA's voluntary standards.
questions.explanation:
Registration, Evaluation, Authorization and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH) is a European Union 
regulation dating from 18 December 2006. REACH addresses the production and use of chemical substances and 
their potential impacts on both human health and the environment.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Restriction of Hazardous Substances (RoHS)?
options: It is a legislation controlling hazardous substances throughout their whole life cycle.
It is a legislation which focuses on hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment.
It is an EPA regulation enforced under Land Disposal Restrictions (LDR).
It is part of the Globally Harmonized System (GHS) for hazardous substances.
questions.explanation:
REACH is a horizontal legislation controlling the risks associated with chemical substances 
throughout their whole life cycle, while RoHS is a product-specific vertical legislation focuses on hazardous 
substances in electrical and electronic equipment (EEE).

questions.question: 5 workers are exposed to airborne lead at 8-hr TWA's of 27 ag/m3, 42 ag/m3, 54 ag/m3, 24 ag/m3, and 60 ag/m3. What is the mean exposure?
questions.explanation:
In order to get the mean average exposure for the five workers, sum the exposures for 
all workers first. 
(27 + 42 + 54 + 24 + 60) ag/m3 = 207 ag/m3 
Then calculate the mean exposure by dividing the sum by the total number of workers. 
207 ag/m3 / 5 workers = 41.4 a/m3 per worker

questions.explanation:
The mode is the number in a set of numbers that appears most frequently. 27 ppm is 
correct because it appears most frequently in this set of numbers.

questions.question: Which of the following is the LEAST likely property of activated carbon that makes it a good sample collecting medium?
questions.explanation:
Activated carbon is extremely porous and has a non-polar surface. It adsorbs 
molecules to its surface readily. When bathed in a non-polar solvent such as carbon disulfide, 
the adsorbed molecules are easily removed and dissolved into the solvent.

questions.explanation:
All of the answers contain the element silicon. However, only crystalline silicon 
dioxide (SiO2) causes the disease silicosis. Dust from glass, amorphous silica, and aluminum 
silicate are considered nuisance dusts and have minimal long term biological effects.

questions.explanation:
Decibels are units used for measuring noise exposure. Vibration is measured in 
acceleration, frequency, and duration.

questions.explanation:

questions.question: Numerical values that are based on procedures to determine the amount of hazardous materials the human body has absorbed (by measuring the actual materials or their metabolic products in tissue, fluid, or exhaled air) is called a:

BEI's (Biological Exposure Indexes) are numerical values based on procedures to 
determine the amount of a material the human body absorbs by measuring the actual 
materials or their metabolic products in tissue, fluid, or exhaled air.

questions.question: 3.7 x 1010 disintegrations per second equals _______ disintegrations per minute.
questions.explanation:
To calculate the number of disintegrations per minute, simply multiply the number of 
disintegrations per second by 60 sec/min. 
60 sec/min x 3.7 x 1010 dis/sec = 2.22 x 1012 dis/min

questions.question: The term self-accelerating decomposition temperature (SADT), is defined as:
options: The maximum temperature of a liquid at which it gives off vapor sufficient to form an ignitable mixture with air
The minimum temperature of a liquid at which it gives off vapor sufficient to form an ignitable mixture with air
The ambient temperature at which a self-sustaining chemical reaction of stored organic peroxides will occur
The rate of decomposition of certain organic peroxides when stored at very high temperatures
questions.explanation:
The SADT is determined for stored organic peroxides. It is the ambient temperature at 
which a run-away reaction will likely occur.

questions.question: The fall season has arrived at a New England office facility and with it, a rash of HVAC complaints that were not recorded during the summer. Which troubleshooting step should be first?
options: Determine if the dampers are operating properly
Determine if the air distribution is balanced to specifications
Check the make-up air system, or damper
questions.explanation:
During the warm months of the year, large volumes of air of relatively high velocities 
are welcomed by the workers. During the fall or winter months, care must be taken to make 
sure that air blowing over the occupants is kept within acceptable values (comfort conditions) 
suitable for the work situation.

questions.question: The Brief and Scala Model refers to:
questions.explanation:
The Brief and Scala Model refers to unusual work schedules. The model reduces the 
TLV proportionately for increased exposure time and reduced non-exposure time. It is 
generally intended to apply to work schedules longer than 8 hours/day or 40 hours/week.

questions.question: The occupation most likely to encounter metal fume fever is:
questions.explanation:
Metal fume fever is an acute condition of short duration caused by a brief high 
exposure to the freshly generated fumes of metals, such as zinc and magnesium or their 
oxides. Symptoms appear from four to twelve hours following exposure and consist of fever 
and shaking chills.

questions.question: Cumulative trauma disorders (CTD's) are rapidly becoming a major source of workers' compensation losses. The most prevalent form of CTD is:
questions.explanation:
Carpal tunnel syndrome is a common disease of workers performing repeated 
exertions or movements of the fingers/hand and wrist which compress the median nerve in 
the carpal tunnel. It is often associated with tingling, pain or numbness in the thumb and first 
three fingers, frequently resulting in lost time and workers' compensation costs.

questions.question: Disorders that result from repeated exertions or movements of the body are most often described by which of the following terms?
questions.explanation:
Disorders that are caused, precipitated, or aggravated by repeated exertion or 
movements of the body are most frequently called cumulative trauma disorders (CTD's). 
Other terms less commonly used include: repetitive trauma disorders, repetitive strain 
injuries, overuse syndromes, and regional musculoskeletal disorders.

questions.question: What is the WBGT given a wet bulb temperature of 75ºF and a globe temperature of 89ºF (no solar load)?
questions.explanation:
WBGT = 0.7 WB + 0.3 GT = (0.7 * 75ºF) + (0.3 * 89ºF) = 79.2ºF 
where WB = natural wet bulb temperature obtained with wetted sensor exposed to natural air 
movement. GT is the globe temperature take from the center of a 6 in. diameter hollow 
copper sphere painted on the outside with black matte finish (called a globe thermometer).

questions.question: Six workers are exposed to methylene chloride at the following levels (based on an 8-hr TWA): 27 ppm, 31 ppm,12 ppm, 86 ppm, 27 ppm and 40 ppm. What is their statistical median exposure?
questions.explanation:
The median number in a set is the middle number, if the number (n) in the set is an odd 
number. When there are an even number of values in a sequence, the median is found by 
taking the average of the 2 "middle" numbers, in this case: (31 ppm + 27 ppm) / 2 = 29 ppm

questions.question: An employee's exposure to a mixture of solvents is found to be 20 ppm to solvent A, 10 ppm to solvent B, and 14 ppm to solvent C. If the toxic effects of these solvents are additive, and their TLV's are 100 ppm, 50 ppm, and 100 ppm respectively, what is the employee's exposure as a percent of the TLV?
questions.explanation:
To get the total exposure determine the percentage of the TLV of each substance the 
employee is exposed to and add them together or: 
Exposure = (20 ppm/100 ppm)+(10 ppm/50 ppm)+(14 ppm/100 ppm) = 20% + 20% + 14% 
= 54%

questions.question: If a worker is exposed to lead for 4 hr at 24 ag/m3, 3 hr at 48 ag/m3, and 1 hr at 0 ag/m3, what is his exposure as an 8-hr TWA?
questions.explanation:
To get the TWA, you must calculate the exposure rate for each part of the 8-hr day for 
which there is an exposure. 
(24 ag/m3)(4 hr/8 hr) = 12 ag/m3 
(48 ag/m3)(3 hr/8 hr) = 18 ag/m3 
(0 ag/m3)(1 hr/8 hr) = 0 ag/m3 
Then, you need to add together each weighted exposure to get the 8-hr exposure. 
TWA = 12 ag/m3 + 18 ag/m3 + 0 ag/m3 = 30 ag/m3

questions.question: You are evaluating a lifting task in your facility that involves moving tote boxes containing parts from a lower conveyor to an upper conveyor at right angles to each other. The tote boxes have two handles and are easy to grasp. The tote box handles, when on the lower conveyor, are 10 in. from the floor. When the tote box is on the upper conveyor, the handles are 40 in. from the floor. The center of the belt of both conveyors is 10 in. from the feet of the worker. One lift is required every minute during the full 8-hr shift. The tote box weighs 4 lb. How much material can be placed in the tote box?
questions.explanation:
The NIOSH lifting equation is: 

RWL = LC * HM * VM * DM * AM * FM * CM 
where LC = 51 lb 
HM = (10/H) 
VM = [1-0.0075 * absolute value of (V-30)] 
DM = [0.82 + (1.8/D)] 
AM = (1-0.0032 * A) 
(All of the above is part of the lifting equation BEFORE we start applying the numbers from 
the problem.) 
These are the numbers we will use in the RWL equation. 
H = 10 in. . . . this is the horizontal distance from the feet 
V = 10 in. . . . this is the vertical distance from the floor 
D = 30 in. . . . this is how far the item is lifted vertically 
A = 90º . . . this is the asymmetry (body twisting) 
FM = 0.75 ... this is the frequency factor 
CM = 1.00 ... this is the coupling factor 
RWL = 51 lb(10/10)[1 - (0.0075(absolute 10 - 30)](0.82 + (1.8/30)](1 - (0.0032 * 90)] * 0.75 
* 1.00 
= 51 * 1.00 * 0.85 * 0.88 * 0.712 * 0.75 * 1.00 
= 20.37 lb 
Product weight = RWL - tote weight 
= 20.37 lb - 4.0 lb 
= 16.37 lb

questions.question: You are evaluating a lifting task in your facility that involves moving tote boxes containing parts from an upper conveyor to a lower conveyor. The totes are poorly constructed and are difficult to grasp. Most workers simply grasp the bottom of the slippery tote box from the upper conveyor (located 35 in. from the floor) and drop the tote box 1 in. from the lower conveyor (located 9 in. from the floor). The conveyors are at right angles to each other, and the center of the conveyor belts are 24 in. from the feet of the workers. Two lifts are required every minute during a 2-hr shift. The tote box weighs 4 lb. If the weight of parts placed in the tote box is 8 lb, what is the lifting index? Should changes be made?
questions.explanation:
The NIOSH lifting equation is: 
RWL = LC * HM * VM * DM * AM * FM * CM 
where LC = 51 lb 
HM = (10/H) 
VM = [1-0.0075 * absolute value of (V-30)] 
DM = [0.82 + (1.8/D)] 
AM = (1-0.0032 * A) 
(All of the above is part of the lifting equation BEFORE we start applying numbers from the 
problem.) 
These are the numbers we will use in the RWL equation. 
H = 24 in. . . . this is the horizontal distance from the feet 
V = 35 in. . . . this is the vertical distance from the floor 
D = 25 in. . . . this is the lifted distance (the workers drop the tote the last inch - that is why D 
is not 26 in.) 
A = 90º . . . this is the asymmetry (body twisting) 
FM = 0.84 ... this is the frequency factor 
CM = 0.90 ... this is the coupling factor 
RWL = 51 lb(10/24)[1 - (0.0075(absolute 35 -30)] [0.82 + (1.8/25)] [1 -(0.0032 * 90)] * 
0.84 * 0.90 
= 51 lb * 0.417(0.9625) 0.892 * 0.712 * 0.84 * 0.90 = 9.8 lb 
Total load = 4.0 lb + 8.0 lb = 12 lb 
Lifting Index = Load / Recommended Weight Limit 
= 12 lb / 9.8 lb = 1.2 
A lifting index of over 1.00 is too high and indicates that changes to the process and/or to the 
magnitude of the load should be made to reduce the lifting index to 1.00 or less.

questions.question: You are evaluating a lifting task in your facility that involves moving tote boxes containing parts from a lower conveyor to an upper conveyor at right angles to each other. The tote boxes have two handles and are easy to grasp. The tote box handles, when on the lower conveyor, are 10 in. from the floor. When the tote box is on the upper conveyor, the handles are 40 in. from the floor. The center of the belt of both conveyors is 10 in. from the feet of the worker. One lift is required every minute during the 8 hour shift. The tote box weighs 4 lb. If the lower conveyor is raised 10 in., how much more product can be placed in the tote box without exceeding the RWL?
questions.explanation:
The NIOSH lifting equation is: 
RWL = LC * HM * VM * DM * AM * FM * CM 
where 
LC = 51 lb 
HM = (10/H) 
VM = [1-0.0075 * absolute value of (V-30)] 
DM = [0.82 + (1.8/D)] 
AM = (1-0.0032 * A) 
(All of the above is part of the lifting equation BEFORE we start applying the numbers from 
the problem.) 
These are the numbers we will use in the RWL equation. 
H = 10 in. . . . this is the horizontal distance from the feet 
V = 10 in. . . . this is the vertical distance from the floor 
D = 30 in. . . . this is how far the item is lifted vertically 
A = 90º . . . this is the asymmetry (body twisting) 
FM = 0.75 ... this is the frequency factor 
CM = 1.00 ... this is the coupling factor 

RWL1 = 51 lb(10/10) [1 - (0.0075 absolute 10 - 30)](0.82 + (1.8/30)](1- 0.0032 * 90) * 0.75 * 
1.00 = 20.37 lb RWL1 is the initial state. 
When we change things, we must recalculate the new RWL. In this problem, the only things 
that change are the vertical distances. 
V changes to 20 in. from 10 in. 
D changes to 20 in. from 30 in. 
RWL2 = 51 lb (10/10)[1-(0.0075 * absolute 20-30)] [0.82 + (1.8/20)] [1-(0.0032 * 90)] * 0.75 
* 1.00 = 22.92 lb Difference = 22.92 lb - 20.37 lb = 2.55 lb

questions.question: Of the following, which sound measuring instrument is the LEAST commonly used for most noise problems encountered in a manufacturing plant?
questions.explanation:
In a manufacturing plant, with a variety of noise problems, noise measuring equipment 
most commonly used include sound level meters, octave-band analyzers, and noise 
dosimeters. 
SOUND LEVEL METER - This is the basic direct reading instrument used to measure sound 
pressure variations in air. The frequency range is usually 20 to 20,000 Hz. 
OCTAVE-BAND ANALYZER - This instrument is used to determine where the noise 
energy lies in the frequency spectrum. It is an essential piece of equipment for engineering 
control of noise producing machines or equipment. 

NOISE DOSIMETER - This instrument is worn by a worker to accumulate a record of the 
noise energy to which he/she was exposed during the work shift.

questions.question: When might you use the C-weighting on a sound level meter?
options: For estimating adequacy of hearing protective devices
For measuring very high frequency noise
For measuring community noise from aircraft
When trying to most closely imitate the human ear response
questions.explanation:
The C-weighting on a sound level meter can be used to estimate the actual reduction in 
noise level provided by hearing protection. The estimate is performed in three steps: 
Step 1 - Monitor the noise level in the workplace using the C-weighted scale 
Step 2 - Convert the measured noise level to a C-weighted time-weighted average (TWA) 
Step 3 - Subtract the noise reduction rating (NRR) specified by the haring protection 
manufacturer from the C-weighted TWA found in Step 2. 
The value found in Step 3 is based on the C-weighted scale and can be reliably used as a 
conservative estimate of the benefit of wearing hearing protection in high noise 
environments.

questions.question: A charcoal tube sample was taken by drawing 40 liters of air through the tube which was then analyzed for benzene. If 0.5 mg of benzene was found on the tube, what was the concentration of benzene in the air sample assuming STP? (MW of benzene is 78)

questions.question: What does TWA mean?
questions.explanation:
TWA is the acronym for Time Weighted Average. This is expressed in exposure for an 
eight hour day. Therefore, if an exposure was the same and continuous for eight hours, it 
would be the same as the exposure. If the exposure lasted for only four hours, the TWA 
would be divided by 2 to get the 8-hour exposure.

questions.question: Toxicity recognizes several different mechanisms of multiple chemical interaction. What is potentiation?
options: A substance which does not have a toxic effect upon a system or organ, but when in combination with another chemical, makes that chemical much more toxic
Two substances, which when together, interfere with each other's actions
The combined effect of these two chemicals is much greater than the sum effect of each agent acting independently
questions.explanation:
Potentiation is a substance which does not have a toxic effect upon a system or organ, 
but when in combination with another chemical, makes that chemical much more toxic. A 
classic example of this effect is isopropanol and carbon tetrachloride. Isoproponal is not toxic 
to the liver but when it is added to carbon tetrachloride, the toxicity of the CCl4 to the liver is 
greater.

questions.question: Ionizing radiation has the greatest effect on which tissues or organs?
questions.explanation:

by new ones from the bone marrow. However, radiation damage can injure the bone marrow 
so that cell replacement cannot take place. Damage to the body will be permanent in such 
cases. Kidneys and the liver are generally highly resistant to ionizing radiation and will be 
injured only by very high dosages such as those which result from the presence of an internal

questions.question: What do asbestos, silicon dioxide, metal fumes, nitrogen dioxide, and beryllium have in common?
questions.explanation:
Asbestos, silicon dioxide, metal fumes (iron, cadmium, zinc oxides) and beryllium are 
lung damaging agents. In order for a harmful agent to exert its toxic effect, it must come into 
contact with a body cell. To make that contact, entry into the body is made as a result of the 
inhalation of the foregoing in the form of dusts, fibers, or particles which are deposited and 
retained in the lungs, where they (depending on dose response) have the potential to produce 
signs, symptoms, and findings of pulmonary disease. (Asbestos and beryllium are also 
carcinogenic.)

questions.question: What fundamental concept in toxicology is used to determine the safety or hazard of chemical substances?
options: Assessment of the hazard and its impact on the population
Defining safety and health limits of chemical agents
Establishing that a relationship exists between the dose of an agent and the response that it produced in a biologic system
Identifying mechanisms by which noxious substances gain access to the biological system
questions.explanation:
Toxicology is the study of noxious effects of chemical and physical agents. The most 
fundamental concept in toxicology states that a relationship exists between the dose of an 
agent and the response that it produces in a biologic system. The first toxicity data on an 
uncharacterized agent are usually obtained using test animals. A range of doses is found 
where at the upper end all animals die, and at the lower end, they survive.

2.5 = 8/x 
x = 3.2 
Substituting, 3.2 = 2[(L-90)/5] or 3.2 = 2y 
y = 1.59 
Substituting, 
1.59 = (L-90)/5 
L = 98 dB

questions.question: Bone marrow and the eyes are very sensitive to radiation. Damage to the body may be permanent. What other tissue or organ is most sensitive to radiation?
questions.explanation:
White blood cells are the most sensitive to radiation, which reduces their number, 
leaving the body open to infection. Skin is easily damaged; however, the skin has great 
recuperative powers. Radiation will lead to loss of hair. This effect is generally temporary 
after exposure stops; however, the new hair may be of a new color or have other 
characteristics different from the original. To produce sterility in a person would require 
almost a fatal dose. Genetic effects produced by radiation to reproductive cells can only be 
surmised, and would not be known for several generations after exposure.

questions.question: One of the laws governing ideal gas behavior that industrial hygienists must account for when conducting air sampling is Charles' Law. This law describes the relationship of:
options: Pressure with noise level and temperature
questions.explanation:
Charles' Law states that the volume of a gas sample varies directly with absolute 
temperature (e.g., temperature in Kelvin or Rankine). To determine the volume of an ideal 
gas at a new temperature, use Charles' Law. 
New Volume (V2) = Starting Volume (V1)(T2/T1) 
V2 = V1 (T2/T1)

questions.question: Which of the following diseases would be least likely classified as an occupational hazard?
questions.explanation:
Pet shop salesmen, stockmen, and breeders of cats and dogs are occupations that may 
encounter ringworm. Slaughterhouse workers, farmers, and veterinary surgeons are 
occupations having potential to be infected with Q fever, a rickettsial organism. Workers with 
cattle and pigs, beef and pork handlers in slaughterhouses, and farmers can contract 
brucellosis (undulant fever). Yellow fever is caused by a mosquito bite.

questions.question: Which of the following is the least likely occupational disease?
questions.explanation:
Asbestosis and siderosis are a kind of pneumoconiosis involving specific lung changes 
caused by the inhalation of dust or fumes. In the past, asbestos was widely used in 
construction materials (roofing, siding, wallboard, floor tiles, insulation); textiles (fireproof 
clothing, blankets); shipbuilding materials (pipe insulation); and automotive parts (brake 
shoes and clutch pads). Excessive fumes (iron oxide) from welding operations may produce 
siderosis with a pigmentation of the lungs without disability (black in welders lungs and red 
in iron ore miners). Glanders is a bacterial disease that may be contracted by horse trainers, 
veterinary surgeons or anyone having contact with sick horses or mules. Emphysema is most 
commonly associated with cigarette smoking.

questions.question: At 10ºC and 4.0 atm, a sample of gas occupies 1,000 liters. If the gas is reduced in volume to 300 liters and the temperature remains constant, what will the pressure be?
questions.explanation:
Boyle's law states that at constant temperature, pressure and volume are inversely 
related - as the pressure increases the volume decreases. 
P (atm) = 4.0 atm(1,000 liters / 300 liters) 
= 4.0 atm (3.333) 
= 13.33 atm

questions.question: Bonds formed between two different atoms often result in the electrons not being shared equally between them. This unequal sharing is a function of how __________ one atom is, relative to the other.
questions.explanation:
Electronegativity is the property associated with the unequal sharing of electrons 
during bonding. One atom has a greater ability to attract electrons. When the bond is formed, 
the electrons spend more time near one atom. Large differences in electronegativity will 
cause a transfer of electrons (i.e., an ionic bond).

questions.question: Carbon monoxide is formed by:
questions.explanation:
Carbon monoxide is an intermediate oxidation product of carbon. If enough oxygen 
were present the carbon would have been oxidized to carbon dioxide. When there is 
insufficient oxygen to fully oxidize the carbon to carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide is formed.

questions.question: The least likely outcome of exposure to asbestos fibers is:
questions.explanation:
Asbestos is a generic term applied to a number of hydrated mineral silicates, including 
chrysotile, amosite, crocidolite, tremolite, and anthophyllite. Asbestos causes asbestosis, 
cancer of the lungs and digestive tract, and mesothelioma. Asbestosis and asbestos cancer are 
the long term effects of inhaling asbestos fibers (they do not become clinically evident until 
more than 20 years have passed from onset of exposure) whereas, mesotheliomas result from 
a short term exposure and are diffuse and spread rapidly. Death usually results within one 
year of diagnosis. Skin cancer is not a likely outcome of asbestos exposure.

questions.question: Which of the following chemical asphyxiants inhibits cytochrome oxidase and is rapidly fatal?
questions.explanation:
Both hydrogen cyanide and hydrogen sulfide inhibit the enzyme cytochrome oxidase, 
which is essential for tissue respiration. Tissue hypoxia and death may occur rapidly. Carbon 
monoxide interacts with the hemoglobin molecule to produce asphyxia.

questions.question: Which of the following chemicals is NOT a hepatotoxic agent?
questions.explanation:
Arsine is a gas whose primary effect upon inhalation is hemolysis (break down of red 
blood cells). All of the other chemicals are severe hepatotoxic agents. Carbon tetrachloride 
produces severe diffuse central necrosis of the liver, tetrachloroethane produces yellow 
atrophy of the liver, and nitrosoamines and aflatoxins cause severe liver damage.

questions.question: Thalidomide is a classic example of what type of agent?
questions.explanation:
The two potential answers were "mutagenic" and "teratogenic". Thalidomide is a 
classic teratogen. Thalidomide babies were born without limbs because the drug's effect acted 
on the developing fetus. Teratogens have an adverse effect upon the developing fetus. 
Mutagens modify the actual genetic material.

questions.question: Cumulative trauma disorder (CTD) is:
options: An acute injury caused by repetitive motion
A chronic illness caused by exposure to extremes in temperature
A chronic injury caused by an accumulation of micro-injuries
An acute form of carpal tunnel syndrome
questions.explanation:
Cumulative trauma disorder is a type of chronic musculoskeletal injury that is caused 
by an accumulation of many micro-injuries over a period of time. Acute or macro-injuries 
cause immediate pain and damage from sudden or extreme force, while micro-injuries are 
from low-intensity stresses that accumulate over a long period of time.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cumulative trauma disorder?
questions.explanation:
Raynaud's Phenomenon (or Syndrome) is a disorder of the hand and arm sometimes 
resulting from excessive vibration exposure, but not as a result of cumulative trauma. 
Raynaud's Phenonemon can develop from the single use of a vibrating tool, though it 
typically comes from long-term use. In addition, it can be caused by exposure to certain 
chemicals, exposure to cold, and excessive emotional stress. While doctors can diagnose and 
treat the signs and symptoms of Raynaud's Phenonemon, they are still not sure what causes it. 
Thoracic Outlet Syndrome is due to repetitive compression of nerves and blood vessels in the 
neck and shoulder. Tenosynovitis is due to repetitive compression of nerves and blood 
vessels in the wrist. De Quervain's Disease is due to repetitive compression of nerves and 
blood vessels in the thumb.

questions.question: The primary factors that affect development of cumulative trauma disorder (CTD) include all of the following EXCEPT the:

Lack of a proper rest period
questions.explanation:
The age of a worker has little effect on the development of CTD. The accumulation of 
micro-injuries from excessive force is compounded by the frequency of repetition of such 
high risk tasks. (This takes into account the lack of rest between tasks).

questions.question: A sound pressure level of 3 N/m2 corresponds to how many decibels?
questions.explanation:
Lp = 20log (P/Po), where 
Lp = pressure level, P = the measured pressure, and Po is the reference sound pressure of 2 x 
10-5 Pa 
Lp = 20log (3/0.00002) 
= 20log (150,000) 
= 103.5 dB

questions.question: The agent responsible for paralytic shellfish poisoning is:
questions.explanation:
Saxitoxin is actually a complex of toxins produced by the Gonyaulax species 
dinoflagellates (kingdom Protista). Humans develop paralytic shellfish poisoning as a 
consequence of ingesting filter feeding mollusks which have accumulated the dino-
flagellates. Paralytic shellfish poisoning is associated with algal blooms.

questions.question: ___________ is the neurotoxin found in the liver of the pufferfish.
questions.explanation:
In pufferfish poisoning, death is due to skeletal muscle paralysis. Both saxitoxin and 
tetrodotoxin have applications in mechanistic toxicity studies because they selectively block 
the sodium channels along the axons, preventing the inward sodium current while leaving the 
outward potassium current unaffected.

questions.question: Botulinum toxin interferes with the propagation of nerve impulses by preventing the release of ________ from the axon terminal.
questions.explanation:
Botulinum toxin, produced by the bacterium clostridium botulinum, binds irreversibly 
to the axon terminal preventing the development of the end plate potential on the muscle side 
of the synapse. The muscle behaves as if it were denervated. The result is the paralysis 
characteristic of botulism.

and increases in resistance to pulmonary flow. These are mainly a consequence of irritant 
properties. Atmospheric particulates (e.g., particulate sulfates) can enhance the effects of SO2 
on the body.

questions.question: A temperature of 120ºC is equivalent to a temperature of:
questions.explanation:
Kelvin scale is an absolute thermodynamic scale on which the temperature measured is 
based on the average kinetic energy per molecule of a perfect gas. The zero on the Kelvin 
scale is -273.18º Celsius. The size of each Kelvin degree is the same as the Celsius degree. 
Thus, by adding 273.18 to any Celsius temperature, we obtain the corresponding temperature 
on the absolute scale or (120 + 273.18)K = 393.18° K.

questions.question: If a maintenance person moves at a speed of 0.5 times that of sound in a direction away from a noise source producing a sound frequency of f, he would probably hear a sound frequency:
questions.explanation:

away from the source of the sound, successive compressions will reach him at the same rate 
as when he is stationary. Because his rate of speed is less than sound, the compressions don't 

catch up with him until the amplitude is too small to have any effect hence, the frequency he 
hears is less than f.

questions.question: What control measures can be taken for adequate protection against external radiation hazards?
options: Use lead shielding and protective equipment
Follow the principals of the inverse square law
Limit exposure time, work at a safe distance, and use barriers
Use written procedures, employee training, personal protective equipment, and signage
questions.explanation:
Gamma rays, X-rays and neutrons are the most penetrating radiations and usually 
constitute the major external hazards. There are three principal factors that provide the basis 
for radiation protection: time, distance, and shielding. 

TIME - To control personnel exposure, the dose rate from a radiation source may be 
measured and appropriate limits placed on the working time for control of the dose to the 
individual. 

DISTANCE - The intensity of a radiation field decreases as you move further away from the 
radiation source. The relation between radiation exposure rate and distance follows the 
inverse square law. 

SHIELDING - Since ionizing radiation will interact with most materials, in principle any can 
be used for shielding. Some materials, however, like lead, make more efficient shields than 
do others.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most common occupational disease?

Dermatitis, which is classified into primary irritation and sensitization of skin, is the most frequent 
occupational disease. It is caused by contact with acids, alkaline materials such as soaps and detergents, fabric 
softeners, solvents, or other chemicals. The reaction usually looks like a burn.

• 
Cement 
• 
Hair dyes 
• 
Long-term exposure to wet diapers 
• 
Pesticides or weed killers 
• 
Rubber gloves 
•

questions.question: Exposure to petroleum products, greases, and solvents account for the most probable cause of which of the following occupational disease?
questions.explanation:
Many workers simply use hands with no PPE to work with petroleum products, greases, and solvents. 
As a result, dermatitis is the most common occupational disease caused by these products. 
Glanders is an infectious disease that is caused by the bacterium Burkholderia mallei. While people can get the 
disease, glanders is primarily a disease affecting horses. It also affects donkeys and mules and can be naturally 
contracted by other mammals such as goats, dogs, and cats. 
Siderosis is a lung disease caused by inhaling metal fumes. Mortality studies among iron workers (welders, iron 
foundry workers, and steel workers) show that an association exists between working with iron and death from lung 
cancer and other respiratory causes. 
Carpal tunnel syndrome occurs when the median nerve, which runs from the forearm into the palm of the hand, 
becomes pressed or squeezed at the wrist. Symptoms include frequent burning, tingling, or itching numbness in the 
palm of the hand and other fingers. Occupationally speaking, carpal tunnel syndrome is caused by repeated use of 
vibrating hand tools.

questions.question: Which of the following statements BEST describes Cumulative Trauma Disorders (CTD)?
options: Disorders caused as a result of repeated movement of body parts.
Disorders caused as a results of exposure to chemicals over a relative long period of time.
Mental and psychological disorders developed over a period of time as a result of work related stress.
Any disorder, physical or psychological, which is work related and has a cumulative effect over a given period of time.
questions.explanation:
CTD is a term used to describe physical disorders that are caused as a result of repeated movement 
of body parts. CTDs result when repeated stress is placed on tendons, muscles, or nerves causing inflammation or 
damage. Some of the more common CTDs are tendonitis (inflammation of the tendons), tenosynovitis (inflammation 
of the synovial sheath), and carpal tunnel syndrome (compression of the median nerve). Some of the conditions that 
may lead to CTDs are repetition, posture, and lack of rest.

questions.question: In the control of heat stress, an increase in air velocity:
options: Increases heat transfer rates by convection
Decreases heat transfer rates by convection
Heat transfer is only dependent on the temperature of air
Increases heat transfer rate by conduction
questions.explanation:
Increase in air velocity increases heat transfer by convection as well as evaporative rate of heat 
transfer. Heat transfer by convention is directly proportional to the temperature difference and area of heat transfer: 
$$Q = HA(T_1 - T_2)$$ The constant of proportionality H is strongly dependent on the velocity. As velocity 
increases, so does H resulting in an increase in convective rate of heat transfer.

questions.question: Dilution ventilation is best suited for which of the following situations?

questions.explanation:
Dilution ventilation should not be used as a primary control when air contaminants are highly

Molecular Weight of acetone $= (15) \times 2 + 12 + 16 = 58$ $$Q = \frac{(403)(0.79)(8 \times 10^6)(6)}{(58)(1.5 
\times 10^4)}$$ $$Q = 17,565\text{ ft}^3/\text{min.}$$

static pressure is the pressure exerted to the walls of the piping system if the fluid was stationary. Static pressure is 

exerted in all directions. Velocity pressure is the pressure due to kinetic motion of the fluid and is exerted in the 
direction of fluid flow. 
The relationship between total pressure (TP), static pressure (SP), and velocity pressure (VP) is: $$TP = SP + VP$$ 
The relationship between air velocity and velocity pressure is: $$V = 4005 \sqrt{VP}$$ where V is air velocity in feet 
per minute, and VP is velocity pressure in inches of water. 
For the problem at hand: $$VP = \left(\frac{1000}{4005}\right)^2 = 0.06\text{ inches of water}$$ $$TP = -2.0 + 0.06 = 
-1.94$$ Note: Static pressure can have a positive or negative value. Velocity pressure, on the other hand, always 
has a positive value.

questions.question: The cochlea is the main element of the:

waves travel through the cochlea before reaching the hair-like nerve cells for transmission to the brain.

questions.question: Noise Induced Hearing Loss (NIHL) results from over-exposure to high levels of noise. NIHL depends on sound intensity and the exposure time. Which of the following statements is generally true regarding NIHL?
options: High frequency noise is more damaging
Low frequency noise is more damaging
NIHL depends only on the sound intensity and time of exposure
questions.explanation:
Although there are some differences among individuals, exposure to high frequency noise is more 
damaging to the ears than a low frequency noise having the same sound intensity and for the same exposure time. 
NIHL is caused by damage to the microscopic hair cells of the cochlea. A sound level of 85 dB or higher can cause 
permanent damage to hearing, especially if it has a relatively high frequency.

questions.question: Temporary Threshold Shift (TTS) in hearing is caused as a result of damage to which of the following?
questions.explanation:
TTS is caused as a result of over-exposure to loud noise which damages the organ of Corti and its 
hair cells. 
The organ of Corti is located in the inner ear and acts like a microphone for the body. It is situated in one of the 
three parts of the cochlea and contains four rows of hair cells on its surface. There are about 16,000-20,000 hair 
cells in the basilar membrane following the spiral of the cochlea. Small movements of the layers of membrane 
trigger the hair cells, which in turn send a very small voltage to the associated nerve fiber, called an axon. These 
impulses are transferred to the brain for processing.

questions.question: LD50 is:

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is caused by inhalation of metal fumes or dust generated in most welding and grinding operations?
questions.explanation:
Byssinosis is an occupational disease that is caused by overexposure to cotton dust. Brucellosis, also 
called Malta fever, is caused by ingesting unsterilized milk or meat. Presbycusis is loss of hearing as a result of 
aging.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true in regard to threshold limit values (TLVs)?
options: TLV-time weighted average (TWA) is based on the average exposure in an eight hours per day, 40 hours per week schedule.
TLV-short term exposure limit (STEL) is spot exposure for 15 minutes and cannot be repeated more than four times a day.
TLV-ceiling (TLVC) is the exposure limit that cannot be exceeded even momentarily.
questions.explanation:
Statements (a), (b), and (c) are true in regard to TLVs. TLVs, along with biological exposure indices 
(BEIs), are published annually by the American Conference of Governmental Industrial Hygienists (ACGIH).

questions.question: All of the following are areas used in the design of HVAC systems EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) design uses the principles of heat transfer, fluid 
mechanics, and thermodynamics. The design must initially have an estimate of the required heating or cooling, 
which depends on the outside climate as well as the inside desired conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding demand control ventilation to maintain acceptable indoor air quality?
options: Carbon monoxide sensors are used to control the rate of air flow.
Carbon dioxide sensors are used to control the rate of air flow.
Oxygen sensors are used to control the rate of air flow.
questions.explanation:
When the carbon dioxide exhaled by the occupants of a building reaches a certain concentration, the 
carbon dioxide sensors in the building activate the ventilation system.

questions.question: When manually lifting a load, the load must be kept:
options: As far away from the body as possible.
As close to the body as possible.
In such a way that the line through the center of gravity of the load makes an angle of 80 degrees with the hands.
questions.explanation:
The load must be kept as close to the body as possible. This would minimize the moment created by 
the load on the back muscles.

questions.question: The moment generated on the back muscles of a woman as a result of lifting a load compared to the moment generated on the back muscles of a man lifting the same load is generally:
options: Depends on the shape of the load
questions.explanation:
A woman's torso length relative to body weight is generally larger than that for a man. This would 
generally create a larger value of moment on the back muscle of a woman for the same load.

questions.question: In lifting a load:
options: The back should be kept naturally straight
The load must be lifted using legs
The back should make a 90 degree angle with the load
questions.explanation:
It is important to keep the back naturally straight and use the legs in lifting a load. This would not 
generate excessive pressure on the back muscles.

questions.question: The science that applies the knowledge related to human capabilities and limitations to the design of work environments is called:
questions.explanation:
Ergonomics relates human capabilities and limitations to the design of work environment to achieve 
an optimum degree of efficiency and safety. Ergonomics is the science of fitting workplace conditions and job 
demands to the capabilities of the working population. Effective and successful "fits" assure high productivity, 
avoidance of illness and injury risks, and increased satisfaction among the workforce. 
Although the scope of ergonomics is much broader, the term here refers to assessing those work-related factors 
that may pose a risk of musculoskeletal disorders and recommendations to alleviate them. Common examples of 
ergonomic risk factors are found in jobs requiring repetitive, forceful, or prolonged exertions of the hands; frequent 
or heavy lifting, pushing, pulling, or carrying of heavy objects; and prolonged awkward postures. Vibration and cold 
may add risk to these work conditions. 
Jobs or working conditions presenting multiple risk factors will have a higher probability of causing a 
musculoskeletal problem. The level of risk depends on the intensity, frequency, and duration of the exposure to 
these conditions. Environmental work conditions that affect risk include the intensity, frequency, and duration of 
activities.

questions.question: In designing a piece of equipment, the controls and displays must conform to which of the following principles?
options: Controls must be positioned opposite to the displays.
The movement of controls should follow the principle of non-congruity.
If the display moves to the right, the control should move counterclockwise.
Displays should generally move in the same direction as movement of controls.
questions.explanation: Control and display movement must be compatible. (Also see description in the text.)

questions.question: Some industrial tasks may cause tendonitis, bursitis, or carpal tunnel syndrome. Which one of the following is more likely to cause these diseases?
options: One time lifting of a very heavy object
Extensive use of visual display terminals
A static load on hand and shoulder
Frequent twisting in low back area
questions.explanation:
The presence of "static loading" has been found to cause or aggravate disorders such as tendonitis, 
bursitis, or carpal tunnel syndrome.

questions.question: In occupational ergonomics, the abbreviation CTD stands for:
questions.explanation:
In occupational ergonomics, CTD is an abbreviation for Cumulative Trauma Disorders. Cumulative 
trauma disorders (CTDs) are injuries of the musculoskeletal and nervous systems that may be caused by repetitive 
tasks, forceful exertions, vibrations, mechanical compression (pressing against hard surfaces), or sustained or 
awkward positions.

questions.question: To prevent overexertion from manual material handling tasks, a comprehensive and systematic approach is needed involving all elements of a work system. Which one of the following is more likely NOT to be included in such an analysis?
questions.explanation:
Although an object's toxicity is an important factor in safe handling of the object, it is not included as a 
factor for study of overexertion as a result of manual material handling.

questions.question: Approximately what percent of musculoskeletal injuries are caused by pushing or pulling objects?
questions.explanation:
Inappropriate pushing or pulling has been responsible for approximately 20 percent of 
musculoskeletal injuries. Some injuries that are classified as slips or falls can also have contribution from pushing or 
pulling objects.

questions.question: What is the approximate pushing force (in pounds) that a healthy young male can exert on an object, if the floor coefficient of friction is 0.3?
questions.explanation:
A healthy young male, on the average, can exert a pushing force of 44 lb when the coefficient of 
friction between shoes and the floor is 0.3. For coefficients of friction greater than 0.6, the mean push or pull 
strength increases to 66 lb for the same group.

questions.question: The probability of tipping over an object by pushing it increases as the:
options: Grasping point moves above the object's center of gravity
Grasping point moves toward the worker's center of gravity
Grasping point moves below the object's center of gravity
Grasping point becomes more parallel to the object's center of gravity
questions.explanation:
Objects tip over as a result of the moment which is generated by the pushing force. The farther the 
grasping point from object's center of gravity, the higher the probability for the object to tip over.

questions.question: In designing a task requiring pushing objects, it is advantageous to consider which of the following?
options: Use the body weight to lift and then push the object.
Use a mechanical aid as a leverage to lift the load.
Use the body weight to push without any lifting force applied.
Reduce the coefficient of friction to make it easy for the load to slide.
questions.explanation: The safest way to push an object is described in statement (c).

questions.question: Based on anthropometric data, the design features of a work station should accommodate which of the following range of measurements?
questions.explanation:
Based on anthropometric data, (which is the study of dimensions, weights, and strengths of various 
human body members for the design of equipment and work stations), the design features of a work station should 
accommodate from 5th percentile female to 95th percentile male.

questions.question: A piece of equipment is being designed which requires workers to stand and reach vertically to activate its emergency switch. Which one of the following do you recommend for the design of the height of the switch?
questions.explanation: See description in the text.

questions.question: A worker lifts finished products from an assembly line that is 20 inches above the floor and places them in boxes that are located 35 inches above the floor. The weight of each product is 15 lbs. For each lift, the distance of hands away from midpoint between ankles is 12 inches. In order to properly place the load at its destination, the worker needs to turn 45 degrees. The worker places 5 finished products in boxes every minute. The coupling type is classified as "Good." The LI at the origin and destination for 3 hours of continuous work are respectively:
questions.explanation:
For a detailed discussion of NIOSH revised lifting equations, see the section, "Ergonomics and 
Human Factors Engineering." 
The lift must be analyzed at both the origin and destination of the lift:

$10/H = 10/12 = 0.833$

$0.82 + (1.8/15) = 0.940$

FM 0.35 (from Table)

$$\text{RWL (origin)} = 51 \times 0.833 \times 0.925 \times 0.940 \times 1.000 \times 0.35 \times 1.00 = 13\text{ 
lbs.}$$ $$\text{LI} = 15/13 = 1.15\text{ RWL}$$ $$\text{RWL (destination)} = 51 \times 0.833 \times 0.925 \times 
0.940 \times 0.856 \times 0.35 \times 1.00 = 11.06\text{ lbs.}$$ $$\text{LI} = 15/11.06 = 1.355$$ 
Discussion: Since LI exceeds unity (1.0) at both the origin and the destination of the lift, this lifting is considered to 
be hazardous. The lift at the destination, with a Lifting Index of 1.4, is more hazardous than the lift at its origin. The 
lift's destination is therefore the part on the lift that deserves greatest attention. 
NIOSH recommends that ergonomic redesign be used to engineer the hazards out of the lifting situation. However, 
in this case, the lifting could be improved (in order of importance) by these administrative controls: 
• 
Reducing the frequency of lifting. 
• 
Reducing the work duration from 3 hours to less than two hours of continuous lifting by shift rotation. These 
changes can bring the LI down to 0.57. Ergonomic redesign is also important, and much more desirable 
than depending upon administrative controls. By raising the line to 30 inches, and positioning the load 
closer, the LI is reduced to less than half of unity (0.49), significantly increasing the safety of the workers at 
this workstation. Then, if the workers revert to the more hazardous lifting technique of twisting to place the 
load, the LI still remains at just above half of unity (0.57) and their safety has not been compromised.

questions.question: The term "heat stress" deals with which of the following?
options: Too much heat gained by the body
Too much heat loss from the body
Both heat loss from or heat gained by the body
questions.explanation:
Heat stress refers to too much heat gained by the body. In general, the human body is more capable 
of handling the heat loss from the body compared to heat gain. Heat stress is determined by calculating the Wet 
Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) and comparing it to the threshold values published by the ACGIH.

questions.question: Illumination is measured in which of the following units?
questions.explanation:
The "Lux" is the SI unit of illuminance measuring luminous flux per unit area. It is equal to one lumen 
per square meter.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is the correct definition of "dose"?
questions.explanation: Statement (c) is the correct definition of dose.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the science of epidemiology?
options: It deals with prevention of disease in a population.
It deals with frequency of diseases in a population.
It deals with distribution of diseases in a population.
questions.explanation:
Descriptive epidemiological studies focus on the number of cases of a disease in a given time period. 
This type of study provides information on the distribution of the disease as well as the risk factors for an individual 
to contract the disease.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct description of "Presbycusis"?
options: A condition caused as a result of overexposure to metal fumes.
An irreversible hearing loss caused by damage to organ of "corti" and degeneration of neural elements of the auditory nerve.
Loss of sensitivity to high frequency noise as a result of aging
Lack of ability of a person to interpret what is heard.
questions.explanation:
Statement (b) is a description of "Sensorineural Impairment" and statement (d) is a description of 
"Central Impairment".

questions.question: The type of radiation which is capable of dislodging electrons from the atoms is called:
questions.explanation:
Ionizing radiation causes dislodging of electrons. When electrons are removed from an atom which is 
neutral in its normal state, ions are formed, and therefore, the term ionizing radiation.

questions.question: A radioactive material has a half-life of 200 days. If we start with 500 grams of this material, how many grams is left after 450 days?
questions.explanation:
$$N(t) = N_0(1/2)^{t/t_{1/2}}$$ Where: 
• 
$N_0$ is the initial quantity of the substance that will decay (500 grams), 
• 
$N(t)$ is the quantity that still remains and has not yet decayed after a time t (450 days), 
• 
$t_{1/2}$ is the half-life of the decaying quantity (200 days). $$N(t) = 500 \times (1/2)^{450/200} = 500 \times 
(1/2)^{2.25} = 105\text{ grams}$$
