questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding nanoparticles?
options: Are particles between 1 and 100 nanometers (nm) in size with a surrounding interfacial layer.
Through nanotechnology, nanoparticles can help make materials lighter, more durable, and more reactive.
Naturally occurring nanoparticles can be found in volcanic ash, ocean spray, fine sand and dust, and even biological matter (e.g. viruses).
questions.explanation:
Nanoparticles are particles between 1 and 100 nanometers (nm) in size with a surrounding interfacial 
layer. In nanotechnology, a particle is defined as a small object that behaves as a whole unit with respect to its 
transport and properties. Particles are further classified according to diameter. 
Through nanotechnology, nanoparticles can help make materials lighter, more durable, and more reactive. 
Nanoparticles are applicable in a wide variety of industries and uses, including electronics to make computers 
faster, memory chips smaller, and screens clearer and brighter. 
Naturally occurring nanoparticles can be found in volcanic ash, ocean spray, fine sand and dust, and even biological 
matter (e.g. viruses).

questions.question: Employees who abuse alcohol and drugs can pose significant safety and other problems for their employers, managers, and co-workers. Some of the signs of drug and alcohol abuse are diminished job performance, lower productivity, absenteeism, tardiness, mood changes, and problems with relationships. You suspect that one of your employees is abusing drugs. Your company's drug and alcohol testing policy does not include drug testing for reasonable suspicion. All the following are among the actions you should take EXCEPT:
options: Document any complaints, concerns, behavior patterns or witnesses to the behavior.
Observe employee's behaviors with a second management person.
Ask the employee to agree to a drug test to avoid disciplinary action.
questions.explanation:
Many times, the coworkers and /or clients notice an employee being under influence before a 
supervisor notices the same. It is extremely important to document any complaints, concerns, behavior patterns or 
witnesses to the behavior. It is important that a second management person also observes the behavior. Both 
observers must document their observations in detail. Only after everything is documented, you should meet with 
the employee and discuss what has been observed. Always have a second party at the meeting as a witness. Once 
these steps have been taken, you have the option of enforcing whatever is stated in the company's drug and alcohol 
policy.

questions.question: According to the results of a National Institute for Drug Abuse (NIDA) sponsored survey, which of the following statements is true?
options: Drug-using employees are 3.6 times more likely to be involved in a workplace accident.
Drug-using employees are 2.5 times more likely to have absences of eight days or more.
Drug-using employees are three times more likely to be late for work.
questions.explanation:
Also, drug-using employees are 2.2 times more likely to request early dismissal or time off, and five 
times more likely to file a workers' compensation claim.

questions.question: Which of the following are signs that an employee might be abusing drugs?
options: Frequent tardiness and several unexplained absences.
Causing several small incidents which resulted in minor injuries.
questions.explanation:
Other signs of drug abuse include showing very little concern over personal appearance and 
practicing very poor hygiene, unusual physical symptoms or behaviors such as hyperactivity, paranoia or 
overreacting to constructive criticism, and lower levels of productivity in the mornings.

questions.question: Any organization that enters a federal contract for the procurement of property or services valued at $100,000 or more or receives any federal grant must comply with the regulations of which of the following acts?
questions.explanation:
The 1988 Drug-Free Workplace Act requires certification to the federal agency issuing the contract 
that the organization will provide a drug-free workplace. It must be pointed out that although legal in several states, 
marijuana remains a schedule I drug under federal Controlled Substance Act, and therefore, employers must 
include marijuana prohibition in their workplace drug control policy. It must also be pointed out that many 
jurisdictions allow employee drug testing based on probable cause.

questions.question: The steps to successful training program are which of the following ?
options: Site survey, course development, classroom setup, testing
Requirements definition, gap assessment, content development, implementation
Proposal development, pre-testing, content development, post-testing
questions.explanation:
The steps to accomplish a successful training action are: Analysis, 
Design/development, Implementation, Evaluation/improvement. 
Mager, R.F. (1997). Preparing Instructional Objectives, (3rd ed.). CEP Press. 2.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a program sponsored by an Employee Assistance Program?
questions.explanation:
Employee Assistance Programs (EAPs) have gained popularity as a management 
system to retain good employees by assisting them with their personal problems that cause 
occupational problems. For example, in many cases an employee with an alcohol or other 
substance abuse problem can enroll in the appropriate EAP program for treatment without the 
risk of termination provided that the employee meets all of the requirements of the program.

questions.question: As the facility safety professional, you have become acquainted with two line employees that want to learn more about occupational safety in their own work environments beyond what is typically provided to them in their standard training courses. Which of the following is the best way to encourage their continued interest in safety?
options: Work with the employees and their supervisors to develop mutually agreeable written individual development plans outlining new training goals and safety-related responsibilities.
Work with their supervisors to send them to advanced occupational safety training.
Work with the employees and their supervisors to permit them to accompany you for a week.
Work with their supervisors to assign these employees as safety coordinators in their respective operations.
questions.explanation:
Individual development plans (IDPs) are agreements between employees and their 
managers to help increase the employees' satisfaction with their jobs. IDPs should include 
measurable performance goals for attending training, demonstrating new skills, and achieving 
more diverse job responsibilities.

questions.question: In a certain modern high-hazard laboratory, employee identification badges are color- coded. Five different colors are applied in groups of three. Each group of three colors represents one of the possible occupational hazards for which a worker has been properly trained. How many types of occupational safety training can be represented?
questions.explanation:
When the order of selection is significant then it is a permutation. 
Permutations = N! / (N - X)! 
(where N is the total number of colors and X is the number in a single grouping) 
Permutations = 5! / (5-3)! = 120 / 2 = 60 
There are 60 possible types of occupational safety training that can be displayed on an 
employee badge.

questions.question: You passed the CSP Examination with a score of 192. The cumulative statistics for this examination are as follows: The mean score is 180 and the standard deviation is 32. Assuming a standard distribution, how many safety practitioners taking the exam scored higher than you scored?
questions.explanation:
z = (X -x̄ ) / s = (192 - 180) / 32 = 0.375 
With a z of 0.375, refer to the Table of the Normal Distribution and determine the area under 
the curve associated with a z of 0.375. 
To do this, select 0.3 under the "z" column. Go over to the "7" column along the row of z = 
0.3 (representing a z of 0.37). The area for z = 0.37 is 0.1443. The area for z = 0.38 is 0.1480. 
Interpolate these two numbers (take the average). This is the area under the curve for z = 
0.375. 
Area = (0.1443 + 0.1480) / 2 = 0.14615 

Since we are interested in ALL folks who have scored higher than you, we have to add the 
area under the curve less than the mean to the area we just calculated that falls above the 
mean. This means that we have to add 0.50000 to the area we calculated above. 
Total Area = 0.50000 + 0.14615 = 0.64615 
The percentage of folks who scored higher than you scored = 1 - Total Area 
= 1 - 0.64615 
= 0.35385 
= 35.4% scored higher

questions.question: Which of the following is considered to be the least effective method for group teaching?
questions.explanation:
Demonstration is especially effective when a language problem exists. Role playing 
allows participants to try different behaviors without a great deal of risk, providing immediate 
feedback. Discussion allows students to actively participate and lends itself toward greater 
behavioral modification.

questions.question: Training is recognized as a powerful influence and motivator in safety. When developing a safety training program, the first consideration should be to:
options: Determine the scope and content of the training program
questions.explanation:
Objectives should always be spelled out before the content, methods, and staffing can 
be selected. These objectives should be reduced to terms of behavior; in other words, what is 
it that the training participants should be able to accomplish when their training has been 
completed.

questions.question: The best fire extinguisher training course will have what components?
options: Dynamic classroom instruction using extensive graphics and pictures
Classroom instruction with instructor-performed demonstrations of actual fire extinguishers
Classroom instruction with instructor-performed demonstrations and instructor- supervised student use of actual fire extinguishers on controlled fires
Instructor-performed demonstrations along with instructor-supervised student use of actual fire extinguishers on controlled fires
questions.explanation:
The best fire extinguisher training course will couple classroom instruction with actual 
demonstrations leading to student use of fire extinguishers on real fires. Adults learn 
effectively with practical exercises.

questions.question: When confronted with a problem with which you have little practical experience, which of the following problem-solving schemes is likely to produce the best resolution?
options: Establishing a committee of subject matter experts (at least 15) to discuss ways to resolve the problem and come to a consensus
Establishing a small group of subject matter experts (at least 3) to discuss ways to resolve the problem and come to a consensus
Performing your own thorough research and resolving the problem yourself
Delegating the problem to another person with experience and training similar to your own for resolution
questions.explanation:
Though all of these could ultimately lead to the best resolution, the dynamics of a 
small group of subject matter experts typically offer the best foundation for solving problems.

questions.question: After any initial ice-breaking/rapport-building sessions, all training courses should start with:
options: A description of the course's sponsor
questions.explanation:
Though all of these would be appropriate in some training courses, not all training 
courses will have them all. On the other hand, all training courses should have course 
objectives very clearly defined by the instructor at the beginning of the course.

questions.question: Evaluate the following course objectives that are on the instructor's first slide: · To provide the student with the tools necessary to understand and feel comfortable with working in an environment containing hazardous chemicals such as acetone, methanol, methyl ethyl ketone, muriatic acid, lye, and iso-propanol · To provide the student with the confidence to effectively understand the contents of the company's material safety data sheets and the contents of the company's inventory of hazardous chemicals · To provide the student with the knowledge necessary to understand the types of hazards posed by the various chemicals listed above and how the student can protect himself or herself from exposure to these hazards using personal protective equipment · To provide the student with information on OSHA's hazard communication standard and the company's hazard communication program as required by 29 CFR 1910.1200.
options: The objectives are not adequate because they do not adequately define all of the necessary hazard communication training objectives.
The objectives are not adequate because they are too detailed and wordy.
The objectives are not adequate because they are insufficiently detailed for the student.
questions.explanation:
Objectives at the beginning of the course should be as short as possible to help the 
students mentally navigate through the course. Very few details should be given in objectives 
- that's what the rest of the training should provide.

questions.question: Students should be given the opportunity to demonstrate competence in a new skill in the presence of an instructor. Is it a good idea for the instructor to "test" students performing these practical exercises against objective criteria?
options: No, students have sufficient pressure performing the skill without the added stress of being tested.
No, an instructor cannot fairly gauge a student's practical performance against objective criteria.
No, students will be unfairly competing with one another in a testing environment.
questions.explanation:
Without question, an instructor should evaluate a student's practical performance 
against objective criteria for successfully performing the skill.

questions.question: A multiple-choice quiz that requires the student to demonstrate an understanding of the knowledge from a course is an example of what kind of test?
questions.explanation:
Multiple-choice quizzes are typically objective. The difference between an objective 
and a subjective multiple-choice test is how it would be graded by different people with the 
same knowledge as presented by the instructor. A student's score on an objective test will be 
the same no matter who grades it because the facts are absolute and not subject to an 
instructor's interpretation.

questions.question: An essay test that requires the students to demonstrate an understanding of the two objectives from a course is an example of what kind of test?
questions.explanation:
Even though this is an essay test, it is still objective because the essay question is 
limited to an explanation of the objectives from the course. These objectives are based on the 
facts that the instructor presented and do not require much in the way of subjective 
interpretation. There could be some subjectiveness in the grading, however, this test would be 
mostly objective.

questions.question: An essay test that requires the students to interpret the meaning of a philosophy discussed during the class is an example of what kind of test?
questions.explanation:
This is an example of a subjective test. The interpretation of a philosophy is subjective 
to both the student and the instructor. There will likely be very broad differences in grading 
based on the specific experiences of the graders.

questions.question: Modern technology exists for presenting visual images to students. A popular example of more modern visual imaging devices is the:
questions.explanation:
Computer video projectors have gained popularity due to their light weight, affordable 
prices, and their ability to present colorful images without the need to physically print or 
produce an image from film or on transparencies.

questions.question: With the proliferation and advancement of computer technology, instructors have access to sophisticated software tools for generating visual and audio aids (multimedia presentation software). Two commercial examples of this software include:
questions.explanation:
Microsoft PowerPoint and Corel Presentations are two of the most popular 
multimedia presentation software packages. When connected to a computer video projector, 
these software packages assist instructors with their presentations by providing colorful 
graphics and pictures along with video and audio clips and animations.

questions.question: When conducting presentations, there is usually confusion whether it should be done primarily using auditory or visual signals. Which one of the following is NOT true:
options: When the message is simple - use auditory signals
When the message is short - use auditory signals
When the message will be referred to later - use visual signals
When the message deals with events in time - use visual signals
questions.explanation:
When the message deals with events in time, one should primarily use auditory 
signals. When the message deals with events in space, visual signals should primarily be 
used.

questions.question: Besides expertise with the instructional material, an effective instructor must consider:
options: The time of day in which the class will be held
The layout of the room in which the class will be held
The names of the students in the class
The background and informational needs of the students
questions.explanation:
Though all of the above can help, an effective instructor must consider the 
background and the informational needs of the students to effectively present the material. 

Background includes educational background, experience, language skills (for speakers of 
languages not native to the instructor), and positions within the company. Informational 
needs are also critical. A class full of high-level managers will need far less detail on specific 
operational issues but may need much more detail on legal and regulatory issues and other 
business management information.

questions.question: In most cases, safety-related training courses for managers will be _____________ than a similar course for line/operations employees.
questions.explanation:
In most cases, the mana ger's awareness component of a safety-related class will be 
shorter. In these components, managers are interested in the course's objectives and what they 
need to do (as managers) to ensure that the course's objectives are implemented by their 
employees.

questions.question: What is the best technique to explain a process flow or other sequential operation to employees with a low level of formal education?
questions.explanation:
Where possible, visual cues and explanations should be provided to employees who 
have a low level of formal education (i.e., employees who are functionally illiterate). These 
can be explained; however, the visual explanation should be sufficient.

questions.question: CBT is:
options: A system for assessing employee aptitude by computer
A system for delivering computer-based training to employees
A method for characterizing employee behavior traits
A strategy for calculating the employee's basic technical skills
questions.explanation:
Computer-based training is now an accepted method for delivering training to 
employees. Site-specific information can easily be adapted into more generic training 
programs, and employees' understanding of the material can be evaluated easily.

questions.question: In a training course, you give a quiz at the end of the course to assess the students' understanding of the course content. Several of your students score 68% while the rest scored between 95% and 100%. What should you do next?
options: Require them to retake the course and retake the quiz.
Require them to retake the sections of the course containing the material that they missed and require them to retake the relevant section of the quiz.
Research the questions they missed and discuss the quiz questions and course content with the students before determining any additional activities.
questions.explanation:
In many cases, course quizzes have questions that can be misinterpreted by some 
students. Also note that a 70% is not necessarily an adequate raw score. Some quizzes may 
require a 100% raw score to pass while others may require a 60% raw score. Quizzes should 
be considered holistically with respect to the objectives of the course.

questions.question: Safety professionals frequently require feedback to understand the effectiveness of various safety-related management systems. Which of the following is a typical method for obtaining feedback on management systems?
questions.explanation:
There are several methods for obtaining feedback. Sometimes, the feedback is 
obtained formally, sometimes it's obtained informally.

questions.question: On a quiz you developed and delivered to assess the students' understanding of the course material, you noticed that 15 out of your 30 students missed the same question. Your first action should be to:
options: Rewrite this question as it is obviously poorly written.
Abandon this question from this quiz and rescore the students' quizzes.
Discuss this question with a sample of students from the class (including those who missed it and those who did not).
questions.explanation:
Though you could perform a formal statistical treatment on this quiz question to 
officially determine that it is anomalous, your gut tells you that when half the class misses the 
same question, there is likely a system error in either the test or the instruction. Before you 
rewrite the quiz question, you have to know more about the problem. Is it the wording in the 
question? Did you cover the material in class? The answers to these questions will likely 
come from a discussion with a sample of students from the class.

questions.question: What type of formal statistical treatment would you apply to an item on a training quiz to determine whether the item was statistically missed more frequently than would be statistically expected?
questions.explanation:
A 
-test would be used to determine the statistical significance of a test problem that 
was observed as missed more than was expected.

questions.question: Of the following, which would be considered the minimum number of exam items from which a viable statistical sampling could be obtained?
questions.explanation:
Most statisticians would agree that a sample of between 15 and 20 items is the 
minimum number of points from which viable statistical sampling can be performed.

questions.question: Your test instructions are as follows: "This test has 25 multiple-choice questions. Each question has exactly one correct answer selection and four incorrect answer selections. Choose the correct answer to each question from the five answer selections. You will receive 2 points if you select the correct answer for the question. You will receive 0 points if you select no answer (i.e., leave the question blank), and you will have 1 point deducted for each wrong answer you select." One of your students correctly answered 22 questions and incorrectly answered 2 while leaving one blank. What is this student's percentage score?
questions.explanation:
The total points that are available are 50 points (25 questions * 2 points per question). 
This student earned 44 points from correct answers (22 questions * 2 points per questions) 
but lost 2 points from incorrect answers (2 wrong questions * 1 point per wrong question). 
Therefore, his raw score was 42 points (44 points - 2 points = 42 points). The percentage 
score is therefore 84% (42 points/50 points = 0.84 = 84%)
questions.exclusion_reason: Formula, advanced calculation, or typesetting-dependent mathematical content

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is NOT true concerning conducting presentations?
options: A moving person should use auditory signals
A stationary person should use visual signals
If the message calls for immediate action, auditory signals should be used
When the receiving location is noisy, auditory signals should be used.
questions.explanation: When the receiving location is noisy, anything BUT auditory signals should be used.

questions.question: Which of the following technologies supports duplex voice communication?
questions.explanation:
Duplex communication is supported when all parties can hear all other parties and 
speak to all other parties at the same time. A telephone is an example of a device that 
supports duplex communication. Conventional and trunked radio systems are typically 
simplex (i.e., only one person can talk at a time).

questions.question: Software "suites" have become popular both at home and at workplaces to help automate record keeping chores. What main types of software are typically found in a standard business software suite marketed to homes and businesses?
options: Modem software, operating system, human resources software
questions.explanation:
Frequently, more than just word processing, spreadsheet, and database software are 
included in software suites. Multimedia presentation software, e-mail, Internet, and other 
software are frequently included as well.

questions.question: By what mechanisms can existing data be input into a computerized data logging system?
options: Electronically, via a scanner and optical character recognition software
Electronically, via an interface with another computer on which the data resides
questions.explanation:
There are hundreds of ways to obtain data and make it reside on a specific computer. 
Using local and wide area network technology, as well as the Internet, computers on the other 
side of the world can provide data to a specific computer. Raw data can be processed by a 
computer through sensors and sent to a central computer for storage and distribution. Images 
and sound can even be captured, categorized, and stored.

questions.question: A colleague e-mails you the following line of text: http://www.osha-slc.gov/OshStd_toc/OSHA_Std_toc_19 10.html This is an example of a(n):
options: Internet address via file transfer protocol
Internet address via hypertext transfer protocol
questions.explanation:
A hypertext transfer protocol string such as this one is commonly called a "web 
address" or "website." There are several protocols for transferring information through the 
Internet. Each has advantages and disadvantages. In this particular case, the Internet address 
points to the table of contents of OSHA's General Industry Safety and Health Standards 
(those standards associated with 29 CFR 1910 ).

questions.question: On your computer, you have a digital image of a hazardous condition you noticed last week. You want to immediately send this image to your peer at another facility. Both of you have e-mail. You attach the computer file containing the image to the body of your e-mail. In which of the following image formats would you likely send the image?
questions.explanation:
There are other ways to attach the image. For example, you could insert the image into 
a word processor document and send the word processor document instead of just the image. 
You could also send the image in several proprietary formats if you knew that your peer's 
computer had the capability to read these formats. JPEG and GIF formats are nearly 
universal, and these formats should be used for images if you are unsure of the capabilities of 
the receiver's computer.

questions.question: When teaching a class, body language is important. Regarding attire, which of the following is most appropriate?
options: Dress the same way as the majority of the students so that you "fit-in" with the students. If your students are dressed very casually, then you should be dressed very casually.

Dress "one notch better" than your students. If your students are dressed very causally, then you should dress business casual - if your students are dressed business casual, then you should wear a tie (man) or a suit (woman), etc.
Dress is completely irrelevant when leading a training class.
questions.explanation:
Most experts will say that the instructor should be dressed better than the majority of 
his or her students, but not to the point where the instructor looks out of place. Dressing 
slightly better than your students may influence your students to consciously and 
unconsciously respect you as an expert and also allow you to stand out so that you are easily 
identified during breaks.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding communication?
options: Both the sender's and the receiver's body language is very important in one-on-one communication.
Visual communication is inappropriate in groups of ten or more.
Visual communication is inappropriate in groups of twenty or more.
Body language is only important in one-on-one communication.
questions.explanation:
Some experts say that body language is as important as the actual content of the verbal 
communication during communication - regardless of whether the communication is one-on-
one or to an audience. Visual communication is appropriate for any number of people as is 
verbal communication.

questions.question: Didactic model is the teaching model that:
options: presents a straight forward direction of learning, instructing the participants on what to do and how to do it.
provides for the accomplishment of quantitative testing results.
presents open ended discussion topics based on the instructor's experiences, allowing a free flow of thought by the participants.
questions.explanation:
Didactic instruction refers to the teaching of information, often morally or 
philosophically based. 
Biech, E. (2005). Training for Dummies, (1st ed.). Wiley Publishing, Inc.. 25.

questions.question: Increasing participation of the participants is an ongoing objective of good trainers. What do all trainers always have control of to help increase participation?
questions.explanation:
A trainer only has control over their own actions: communication skills, interpretive 
skills, personal traits, interpersonal style, learning techniques, attending skills and process 
factors. 
Biech, E. (2005). Training for Dummies, (1st ed.). Wiley Publishing, Inc.. 151.

questions.question: During the lecture part of a course, the trainer works to balance eye contact with all the participants and to move around the room in a manner that encourages participation by the whole class. This would be an example of which of the following trainer controlled actions or traits to increase participation?
questions.explanation:
Attending skills of training include: providing consistent eye contact, balanced eye 
contact, demonstrate attentive moves, providing affirmative non-verbals and staying engaged. 
Biech, E. (2005). Training for Dummies, (1st ed.). Wiley Publishing, Inc.. 153.

questions.question: In an effort to build participation, a trainer starts by asking simple questions for a show of hands, building to simple short answer questions and then to discussion questions. The trainer also works to encourage participation from quiet participants. This would be an example of which of the following trainer controlled actions or traits to increase participation?
questions.explanation:
Process factors employed by trainers include: balancing participation of the 
participants, maintaining flow of interactions, building participation, and creating an 
inclusive environment. 
Biech, E. (2005). Training for Dummies, (1st ed.). Wiley Publishing, Inc.. 154.

questions.question: Cognitive psychology research has identified three factors influencing how well and how much we learn. Which one do we as individuals have the least capability of changing?
questions.explanation:
Three factors that have been identified through cognitive psychology research that 
influence how well and how much we learn are ability, prior knowledge and motivation. Of 
these, learning ability is the one which is most dependent on genetic makeup. 
Stolovitch, H.D., & Keeps, E.J. (2011). Telling Ain't Training, (2nd ed.). ASTD Press. 40.

questions.question: The determination of whether there is a problem worth solving and if training or instruction is the proper solution is part of which phase of the instructional preparation?
questions.explanation:
During the analysis phase of instructional preparation, the first step is to determine if 
there is a problem that needs to be addressed, then to make sure that training is part of the 
way to correct the problem. Part of analysis should also assess what type of training should 
be used. 
Mager, R.F. (1997). Preparing Instructional Objectives, (3rd ed.). CEP Press. 2.

questions.question: The first step to developing training or instruction is to:
questions.explanation:
The first step of developing training is to complete the analysis to determine what 
problem exists, if training is part of the solution and what kind of instruction is appropriate. 
Once the analysis is complete, training objectives can be developed that can be used to guide 
the development of the training. 
Mager, R.F. (1997). Preparing Instructional Objectives, (3rd ed.). CEP Press. 2.

questions.question: John has been hired by an automotive detail business to perform a job task analysis 2 weeks after the employees have been trained in the corporation's new processes for completing auto detailing. Which training evaluation level is John involved in?
questions.explanation:
Behavior - measures whether the skills and knowledge learned are being 
implemented. 
Don Kirkpatrick's four levels of training evaluation are reaction, learning, behavior, and 
results: 
Reaction - measures participant satisfaction with the training. 
Learning - measure the extent to which learning has occurred. 
Behavior - measures whether the skills and knowledge learned are being implemented. 
Results - measures the business impact of the implemented skills and knowledge. 
Biech, E. (2005). Training for Dummies, (1st ed.). Wiley Publishing, Inc.. 255.

questions.question: A manager knows training is necessary when:
options: the employees need to know something that they don't already know.
a survey has been conducted indicating the employees are not completing tasks properly.
at the conclusion of an audit, the auditor has indicated training is the proper corrective action.
questions.explanation:
Basically, training is only effective when "something" is not known by people who 
have a need to know that "something". If there is no need to know the information or the 
skill, the training is not adding benefit. 
Mager, Dr. R.F. (1999). What Every Manager Should Know about Training, (2nd ed.). CEP 
Press. 12.

questions.question: Which instruction type would be best suited to teach a new set of employees the steps to accomplish the task associated with their new position, position A8, on the assembly line?
questions.explanation:
Training - the purpose of training is to create a change that is consistent and 
reproducible. 
Instruction - the purpose is to provide the learner the ability to apply what is learned in more 
general terms, to adapt the learning to different situations. 
Education - education builds general models and value systems, occurring over a longer term, 
assembling a variety of experiences, learning and events. 
Stolovitch, H.D., & Keeps, E.J. (2011). Telling Ain't Training, (2nd ed.). ASTD Press. 9.

questions.question: A new group of laborers have been hired for the day shift at the chemical plant. They are required to learn the safety rules and responsibilities related to working at the plant. Which term best describes the type or level of learning necessary?
questions.explanation:
Training - the purpose of training is to create a change that is consistent and 
reproducible. 
Instruction - the purpose is to provide the learner the ability to apply what is learned in more 
general terms, to adapt the learning to different situations. 
Education - education builds general models and value systems, occurring over a longer term, 
assembling a variety of experiences, learning and events. 
Stolovitch, H.D., & Keeps, E.J. (2011). Telling Ain't Training, (2nd ed.). ASTD Press. 10.

questions.question: Numerous organizations exist creating standards and guides for everything in industry. One such organization coordinates and publishes the American Nation Standards. This organization is:
questions.explanation:
The American National Standards Institute, Inc. provides oversight and verification of 
the process for the development of consensus standards published as American National 
Standards. 
American Society of Safety Engineers (2009). Criteria for Acceptable Practices in Safety, 
Health and Environmental Training, ANSI/ASSE Z490.1, (1st ed.). American National 
Standards Institute. 2.

questions.question: The ASSE serves as secretariat to the ANSI accredited committee that developed the American National Standard: Criteria for Accepted Practices in Safety, Health, and Environmental Training. The number of this standard is:
questions.explanation:
ANSI Z490.1, Criteria for Accepted Practices in Safety, Health, and Environmental 
Training. 
American Society of Safety Engineers (2009). Criteria for Acceptable Practices in Safety, 
Health and Environmental Training, ANSI/ASSE Z490.1, (1st ed.). American National 
Standards Institute. 3.

questions.question: Numerous standards setting bodies exist. Some are based in individual countries and some are multinational. Which of the following is a multinational standard setting organization?
questions.explanation:
ISO, the International Organization for Standardization is specifically directed at 
developing and publishing standards for international application. 
ASSE, the American Association of Safety Engineers is a United States based organization 
that promotes the safety and health profession. 
ANSI, the American National Standards Institute is a United States based standards 
development organization. 
BSI, British Standards Institution is the United Kingdom's national standards body.

questions.question: In ANSI Z490.1, Criteria for Accepted Practices in Safety, Health, and Environmental Training, when 'should' is used in the standard it indicates a statement that is:
questions.explanation:
"Should" indicates a recommendation that is not required. 
American Society of Safety Engineers (2009). Criteria for Acceptable Practices in Safety, 
Health and Environmental Training, ANSI/ASSE Z490.1, (1st ed.). American National 
Standards Institute. 10.

questions.question: In ANSI Z490.1, Criteria for Accepted Practices in Safety, Health, and Environmental Training, when 'shall' is used in the standard it indicates a statement that is:
options: a requirement that is strongly suggested.
questions.explanation:
"Shall" indicates a mandatory requirement. 
American Society of Safety Engineers (2009). Criteria for Acceptable Practices in Safety, 
Health and Environmental Training, ANSI/ASSE Z490.1, (1st ed.). American National 
Standards Institute. 11.

questions.question: Under the ANSI Z490.1 standard, the Annexes of the standard are provided for:
options: further clarification of the meaning of the standard and clear direction on how to comply with the standard.
useful information that may be of use to particular audiences with varying levels of usefulness.
use by all persons and organizations that will implement the standard in developing their training programs.
implementation by the Committee members when determined appropriate.
questions.explanation:
Under the ANSI Z490.1 standard, the Annexes of the standard are provided for useful 
information that may be of use to particular audiences with varying levels of usefulness. 
American Society of Safety Engineers (2009). Criteria for Acceptable Practices in Safety, 
Health and Environmental Training, ANSI/ASSE Z490.1, (1st ed.). American National 
Standards Institute. 29.

questions.question: The ANSI/ASSE Z490.1 - 2009, Criteria for Acceptable Practices in Safety, Health and Environmental Training uses a two column format. In this format:
options: The left column establishes the requirements of the standard and the right column provides explanatory information.
The left column provides the requirement headings and the right column explains the specific actions necessary to meet the standard.
The left column establishes the requirements approved by the committee and the right column provides the opinions of the dissenting members.
There is no two column format in the ANSI standards system.
questions.explanation:
The ANSI/ASSE Z490.1 - 2009, Criteria for Acceptable Practices in Safety, Health 
and Environmental Training uses a two column format. The left column establishes the 
requirements of the standard and the right column provides explanatory information. 
American Society of Safety Engineers (2009). Criteria for Acceptable Practices in Safety, 
Health and Environmental Training, ANSI/ASSE Z490.1, (1st ed.). American National 
Standards Institute. 7.

questions.question: Training that lacks in ___________ will result in slower improvement, confusion or deviation from expectations.
questions.explanation:
Consistency is critical to training to provide for clear understanding and maximizing 
performance in line with expectations. 
Baldwin, D.A. (1992). Safety and Environmental Training: Using Compliance to Improve 
Your Company, (1st ed.). Van Nostrand Reinhold. 16.

questions.question: An objective for the course states that, "Students will be able to apply systems engineering concepts to solve the challenges of project management. " Which objective types does this objective best illustrate?
questions.explanation:
Problem-centered objectives address problem solving skills requiring the application 
of complex intellectual skills often involving the use of pre-existing knowledge and skills. 
Galbraith, M.W. (2004). Adult Learning Methods: A Guide for Effective Instruction, (3rd 
ed.). Krieger Publishing Company. 106.

questions.question: Which of the following is an activity where individuals generate ideas related to a topic or task; done in groups or individually with no restriction on quality of ideas?
Which of the following is an outcome statement?
options: Provide instruction to the proper management of hazardous waste.
Conduct practical exercises in spill response.
Be able to properly don a respirator.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer describes an outcome, something that the student is able to 
achieve and continue to achieve after the instructional process is complete. The other three 
options describe the process of teaching, training or instruction. 
Mager, R.F. (1997). Preparing Instructional Objectives, (3rd ed.). CEP Press. 23.

questions.question: Which step of the training cycle is testing the training participants prior to the beginning of class?
questions.explanation:
Analysis includes the validation of training needs and objectives, the assessment of 
needs, or even if training is needed. 
Design and development incorporates the identifying and assembling the methodology and 
materials needed to accomplish the training. Design should be based on the findings of the 
analysis. 
Implementation involves the actual performance of the training activity whether it is 
classroom instruction, self-paced, on-the job or other form of training. 
Evaluation is any process that determines if the objectives were accomplished and the desired 
outcomes were achieved. Evaluation occurs after (and sometimes during) training and can 
feed into the beginning of the next training cycle, testing participants at the end of training. 
Biech, E. (2005). Training for Dummies, (1st ed.). Wiley Publishing, Inc.. 42.

questions.question: Which step of the training cycle is testing participants at the end of training?
questions.explanation:
Analysis includes the validation of training needs and objectives, the assessment of 
needs, or even if training is needed. 
Design and development incorporates the identifying and assembling the methodology and 
materials needed to accomplish the training. Design should be based on the findings of the 
analysis. 
Implementation involves the actual performance of the training activity whether it is 
classroom instruction, self-paced, on-the job or other form of training. 
Evaluation is any process that determines if the objectives were accomplished and the desired 
outcomes were achieved. Evaluation occurs after (and sometimes during) training and can 
feed into the beginning of the next training cycle, testing participants at the end of training. 
Biech, E. (2005). Training for Dummies, (1st ed.). Wiley Publishing, Inc.. 43.

questions.question: Of which of the learning categories does a video and practice fall in to?
questions.explanation:
The three learning categories are knowledge, skills and attitude. Examples of ways to 
gain knowledge are: audiotapes, lectures, articles, and diagrams. Examples of ways to impart 
new skills are: demonstrations, role playing, videos and practice, exercises and worksheets. 
Examples of tools to change values are: debates, structured games, self-analysis and 
exercises. 
Biech, E. (2005). Training for Dummies, (1st ed.). Wiley Publishing, Inc.. 30.

questions.question: The classic college final examination is an example of which level of learning evaluation?
questions.explanation:
Learning - measure the extent to which learning has occurred. 
Don Kirkpatrick's four levels of training evaluation are reaction, learning, behavior, and 
results. 
Reaction - measures participant satisfaction with the training. 
Learning - measure the extent to which learning has occurred. 
Behavior - measures whether the skills and knowledge learned are being implemented. 
Results - measures the business impact of the implemented skills and knowledge. 
Biech, E. (2005). Training for Dummies, (1st ed.). Wiley Publishing, Inc.. 254.

questions.question: What type of evaluation method is typically accomplished through the use of true/false questions, matching lists or fill-in-the-blank questions?
questions.explanation:
The following is a selection of evaluation methods: 
Objective tests - specific questions directed at measuring the trainees learning of the 
information specified in the course objectives. Usually quantitative in nature. 
Attitude surveys - used to identify changes in attitudes usually related to work habits, 
motivation, values, beliefs and working relationships. Qualitative in nature. 
Simulation and observation - an instructor observes the trainee in a job simulation to 
determine if the desired skills or behaviors have been learned. 
Productivity or performance reports - real time production data is used to assess performance 
improvement after training. 
Post-training surveys - are used to assess the retention and implementation of knowledge or 
skills learned at training. Subjective and qualitative in nature. 
Needs/objectives/content comparison - used to determine if a program was relevant to the 
needs. This is effectively a cross walk of the needs to the objectives and the objectives to that 
actual training content. 
Evaluation forms - used to collect participant input on their 'satisfaction' with a program. 
Interviews - useful for assessing skills and knowledge understanding and implementation 
when observation is not viable. 
Instructor evaluation - used to measure an instructors effectiveness, competence and 
instructional skills. 
Biech, E. (2005). Training for Dummies, (1st ed.). Wiley Publishing, Inc.. 263.

questions.question: When broken down to the basics, learning is:
options: nothing more than the transfer of information from the source to the learner.
an activity that takes place in a classroom type environment.
a transformation where the leaner's mind is different.
questions.explanation:
The best answer is that learning is a transformation where the leaner's mind is 
different. The purpose of training is to bring about change. 
Stolovitch, H.D., & Keeps, E.J. (2011). Telling Ain't Training, (2nd ed.). ASTD Press. 13.

questions.question: With regard to learner evaluation, which of the following is most accurate?
options: To be effective, learner evaluations should be accomplished as soon as possible after the training has been completed. This allows the students to reinforce what they have learned in class.
Effective learner evaluation can occur before, during and immediately following the training or even some time after the training has been completed.
Effective post training evaluation has to be supported by an appropriate pre-training exam, thus allowing a true measure of what the learner has accomplished through the course.
Mid-training evaluation is limited in effectiveness and usefulness. Typically, mid- training evaluation is performed to provide a transition from one subject to another.
questions.explanation:
Learner evaluations can be performed before, during and after the training activity. 
Post training evaluation may be accomplished immediately after the training or sometime 
later. The time period in which evaluations are accomplished depends on the purpose of the 
evaluation. 
Galbraith, M.W. (2004). Adult Learning Methods: A Guide for Effective Instruction, (3rd 
ed.). Krieger Publishing Company. 111.

questions.question: The first step in development of a safety training program must be to:
options: Identify employees who may need training
Prepare workbooks that are easy to understand
Find instructors who are qualified in the subject of training
Define objectives of the training program
questions.explanation:
The most important step in development of a safety and health program is to clearly define the goals 
and objectives of the program.

questions.question: In defining a safety training program, "validity" refers to:
options: Ensuring that the elements of the training program cover all relevant legal requirements of the tasks.
Ensuring that the program is feasible and covers the areas which reduce risk and liability.
Identification of hazards of each task and the required knowledge and skills for safe performance.
Identification and analysis of each component of the training program to ensure that all covered areas are technically and legally correct.
questions.explanation:
In defining an effective safety training program, validity refers to identification of the hazards 
associated with each task and the required knowledge and skills to perform those tasks in a safe manner.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding a learning curve?
options: The level of proficiency gained is inversely proportional with the amount of time devoted to learning.
The level of proficiency gained is directly proportional with the amount of time devoted to learning.
The level of proficiency gained varies exponentially with the amount of time devoted to learning.
The level of proficiency gained is directly proportional with the amount of time devoted to learning but eventually tends to reach a limit.
questions.explanation:
The learning curve suggests that the level of proficiency gained increases with the time devoted to 
learning but eventually tends to reach a limit.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the characteristics of role-playing training technique?
options: It can be used effectively to find innovative approaches to solving problems.
Brain storming is used to find solutions to specific problems.
It is an effective tool for identifying, evaluating, and changing personnel issues.
questions.explanation:
Statements (b), (c), and (d) are all true in regard to role-playing training technique. This approach is 
not necessarily used to find innovative approaches to problem solving. 
This is an excellent technique for management as well as other employees within an organization to achieve a 
number of benefits. For example, salespersons within an organization can be trained by having two people act in a 
sales scenario—one acts as the salesperson and the other as the customer. The trainer and/or trainees have the 
opportunity to observe the role play and make their comments afterwards.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding the meeting or conference method of training?
options: This technique is effective because it allows each member to bring his/her knowledge to the meeting.
The number of people in each meeting must be limited in such a way to allow effective discussions and exchange of ideas.
The ideas and opinions of each member must be recorded and a summary report must be prepared and presented to each group member.
The main reason for success of the meeting method of training is the fact that the group leader can have control of the topics that are being discussed.
questions.explanation:
Statements (a), (b), and (c) are true in regard to the conference method of training. Statement (d) is 
not considered to be one of the reasons for the success of this type of training technique. 
This method of training takes a problem-solving approach. A group takes on a problem or issue and work together 
to come up with solutions. Among the disadvantages of this method of training are the difficulties in controlling a 
group or the group coming up with solutions that might be different from management's, resulting in conflict.

questions.question: Certain personal motives can have a direct positive impact on people's behavior. This in turn can have a positive impact on the outcome of training. Which of the following is considered to be the highest motivation factor?
questions.explanation:
Achievement is considered to be the largest driving force behind motivating individuals to change 
behavior to enhance training.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding a cost-benefit analysis for training programs?
options: The benefits of a training program must exceed its costs.
The cost of a training program can usually be estimated with considerable accuracy.
Improved operating conditions can be a benefit of a training program.
Lowering the indirect average cost of an accident is usually considered a benefit of a training program.
questions.explanation:
Training programs are usually designed to reduce or eliminate the number of preventable accidents, 
improve housekeeping and operating conditions, etc. Lowering the average indirect cost of accidents is not 
considered to be a goal of a successful training program.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding a performance-based training program?
options: The focus of the training program is to solve a specific on-the-job problem.
This type of training, in general, can not be measured by analysis of worker's performance.
Feedback from workers during the evaluation of program has minimal effect on the final training.
Feedback from supervisors, in general, does not affect the final training program.
questions.explanation:
Performance-based training focuses on solving a specific on-the-job problem. Safety training 
programs in general are more cost-effective when the training focuses on specific performance outcomes, rather 
than training on a wide range of knowledge and skills that trainees may not be sure how to apply to their jobs.

questions.question: In many training programs, case studies are used for training purposes. Which of the following is the BEST description of case study?
options: Case study is a method of training in which group participation is not addressed.
Case study is a description of how people or organizations have dealt with a certain situation.
Case studies usually are an ineffective way of dealing with the development of problem-solving techniques.
Case studies are usually about generalizations and do not address specific conclusions.
questions.explanation:
A case study is a description of how people or organizations have dealt with a certain situation. One 
of the disadvantages of the case study method of training is that it may not relate to the actual work situation. 
The case study method of training encourages trainees not only to apply known concepts to workplace situations 
but also to develop new concepts and ideologies. The main objective of this method of training is problem 
identification; the solution to the problem is secondary.

questions.question: In computer-based safety training, LANs can be used to deliver training to many workstations. LAN is an acronym for:
questions.explanation: In computer terminology LAN is an acronym for Local Area Network.

questions.question: Which the following is NOT one of the three domains of learning?
questions.explanation:
"Interactive" is not considered to be one of the three domains of learning. The cognitive domain deals 
with mental skills (knowledge). The affective domain provides enhancement in emotional areas that can affect, for 
example, attitude. The psychomotor domain of learning deals with the enhancement of physical skills. Therefore, 
any training program should focus on improving the learners' knowledge, skills, and/or attitudes.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true in regard to safety training?
options: Safety training can be effective when the trainees are motivated.
Effective safety training, in general, does not affect employee morale.
The cost of safety training may be easier to hide than the cost of new equipment or facilities.
Safety training has a critical role in an occupational safety program.
questions.explanation:
Effective safety training can have a very positive effect on employee morale. Studies by the National 
Institute of Health have concluded that worker participation in the training program has a marked impact on the 
outcome of the program. These studies concluded that training involving behavioral modeling, a substantial amount 
of practice, and dialog is generally more effective than other methods of safety and health training. The present 
findings challenge the current emphasis on more passive computer-based and distance training methods within the 
public health workforce.

questions.question: One of the elements of developing an effective safety training program is to develop learning activities. All of the following are steps involved in developing learning activities EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Identifying training needs is not one the steps involved in developing learning activities.

questions.question: All of the following are considered to be red flags for the need or consideration of a safety training program EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Lack of instructional materials does not indicate that there is a need for a safety training program. 
The first step in the training process is a basic one; to determine whether a problem can be solved by training. 
Problems that can be addressed effectively by training include those that arise from lack of knowledge of a work 
process, unfamiliarity with equipment, or incorrect execution of a task. Training is less effective (but still can be 
used) for problems arising from an employee's lack of motivation or lack of attention to the job. Whatever its 
purpose, training is most effective when designed in relation to the goals of the employer's total safety and health 
program. 
If the problem is one that can be solved, in whole or in part by training, then the next step is to determine what 
training is needed. For this, it is necessary to identify what the employee is expected to do and in what ways, if any, 
the employee's performance is deficient. This information can be obtained by conducting a job analysis that 
pinpoints what an employee needs to know in order to perform a job. 
Once the kind of training that is needed has been determined, it is equally important to determine what kind of 
training is not needed. Employees should be made aware of all the steps involved in a task or procedure, but 
training should focus on those steps on which improved performance is needed. This avoids unnecessary training 
and tailors the training to meet the needs of the employees.

questions.question: Effective safety training programs require clearly stated goals and objectives that are measurable. All of the following are considered to be components of objectives EXCEPT:
options: Standard of quality for performance that is described
questions.explanation:
The "performance" is a statement of what the trainee will do. In order to have an effective safety 
training program, the condition of the work must be taken into account. Each objective must have a standard of 
quality for the performance that is described. Developing learning activities is not considered to be one of the 
components in identifying goals and objectives.

questions.question: In developing safety training programs, "performance" is a statement of what the trainee will do. It must include an action verb that describes a behavior that is observable and measurable. Which of the following is considered to be an action verb that is measurable?
questions.explanation:
Verbs such as "appreciate", "understand", and "know" are examples of action verbs that are not 
measurable and should not be used for describing performance in safety training. On the other hand, verbs such as 
"select", "manipulate", "discriminate", and "identify" are action verbs that clearly denote specific actions.

questions.question: In developing a "performance" statement for safety training purposes, it is important to ensure that what the trainee is expected to do is observable and measurable. All of the following are examples of measurable performances EXCEPT:
options: Understand how to respond to a hazardous chemical spill
List the steps that need to be followed in an emergency evacuation
Select the proper tools necessary for heat exchanger maintenance
Fill out a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest for shipment of hazardous waste
questions.explanation:
The verb "understand" does not describe a behavior that is measurable. Examples in statements (b), 
(c), and (d) all describe behaviors that are clearly measurable and/or observable.

questions.question: Safety training objectives must be based on which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Job Hazard Analysis will identify the safety hazards that workers may encounter on the job. 
Appropriate engineering and administrative controls as well training can be provided to either eliminate or reduce 
the risk of exposure to hazardous conditions. 
Supervisors can use the findings of a job hazard analysis to eliminate and prevent hazards in their workplaces. This 
is likely to result in fewer worker injuries and illnesses; safer, more effective work methods; reduced workers' 
compensation costs; and increased worker productivity. The analysis also can be a valuable tool for training new 
employees in the steps required to perform their jobs safely. 
A job hazard analysis can be conducted on many jobs in the workplace. Priority should go to the following types of 
jobs: 

• 
Jobs with the highest injury or illness rates 
• 
Jobs with the potential to cause severe or disabling injuries or illness, even if there is no history of previous 
accidents 
• 
Jobs in which one simple human error could lead to a severe accident or injury 
• 
Jobs that are new to your operation or have undergone changes in processes and procedures 
• 
Jobs complex enough to require written instructions

questions.question: There are three steps to ensuring that learning activities succeed in enabling the trainees to master the behaviors listed in the training objectives. Which of the following is the correct order of these steps?
options: Identify the learning characteristics of the trainees, structure the materials and activities into the training program, and develop or select instructional materials and activities.
Structure the materials and activities into the training program, develop or select instructional materials and activities, and identify the learning characteristics of the trainees.
Identify the learning characteristics of the trainees, develop or select instructional materials and activities, and structure the materials and activities into the training program.
Develop or select instructional materials and activities, identify the learning characteristics of the trainees, and structure the materials and activities into the training program.
questions.explanation:
The correct order of the steps to be followed is statement (c). 
Once you have stated precisely what the objectives for the training program are, then learning activities can be 
identified and described. Learning activities enable employees to demonstrate that they have acquired the desired 
skills and knowledge. 
To ensure that employees transfer the skills or knowledge from the learning activity to the job, the learning situation 
should simulate the actual job as closely as possible. Thus, employers may want to arrange the objectives and 
activities in a sequence that corresponds to the order in which the tasks are to be performed on the job, if a specific 
process is to be learned. 
For instance, if an employee must learn the beginning processes of using a machine, the sequence might be: (1) to 
check that the power source is connected; (2) to ensure that the safety devices are in place and are operative; (3) to 
know when and how to throw the switch; and so on.

questions.question: All of the following are considered to be characteristics of the trainee population that may affect learning EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
According to Mager and Beach, the characteristics of the target population that may affect learning 
are physical characteristics, education, motivation, and interests.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true in regard to conducting a safety training program?
options: It is important to keep the trainees mentally active.
The presentation must be tailored to the values and learning styles of the trainees.
Unreasonable fears of occupational hazards must be avoided.
If the content of the course were tailored to the trainees learning needs and learning styles, starting with a pilot program would be considered an inefficient way of conducting training.
questions.explanation:
Actually, in this situation, the pilot program will hold the trainees' interests. Once a training program 
has been developed, it is always a good idea to conduct the training in a pilot program.

questions.question: All of the following are considered to be guidelines that an experienced instructor would follow when presenting a safety training program EXCEPT:
options: Do not stay physically close to your listeners.
Remember that trainees tend to remember narrative chunks more than sophisticated information.
Appear to have fun, even be theatrical, if necessary.
questions.explanation:
It is a good idea to stay physically close to the trainees while making a presentation. Also, it is helpful 
to place the information being presented in a larger, and interesting context. It is important to deliver only the 
quantity of material that the trainees need to know.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true in regard to presenting safety training materials?
options: The trainees will be much more open to learning if the instructor is successful in giving them a sense of disequilibrium.
Many educational psychologists believe that disequilibrium (the state of being out of balance) is not essential to learning.
The effectiveness of a safety training presentation depends both on the trainees and the instructor.
It is essential for the instructor to provide motivation to learn.
questions.explanation:
Statements (a), (c), and (d) are all true in regard to safety training presentation. Many educational 
psychologists believe that bringing a state of "out of balance" to trainees is essential to learning. 
It is also important for the instructor to rehearse the presentation. Being positive and showing enthusiasm, speaking 
loud enough so everyone can hear, and making eye contact with trainees are among other factors that contribute to 
effective presentations.

questions.question: The first step in developing a safety training program is to conduct a needs assessment. "Needs assessment" refers to the process of determining if a safety training program is needed. Several techniques can be used to conduct a needs assessment. These include observation of employees performing the job, use of questionnaires, studying technical records and manuals, and interviewing subject matter experts. There are both advantages and disadvantages associated with different methods of needs assessment. All of the following are considered to be advantages of the "use of questionnaires" method of needs assessment EXCEPT:
options: Can collect data from a large number of persons
The data collected can be easily summarized
questions.explanation:
Possible low return rates or inappropriate responses is one of the disadvantages of using 
questionnaires to conduct a needs assessment for safety training. This method is also time consuming and, in 
general, lacks detail.

questions.question: One of the methods used in conducting a needs assessment for safety training programs is to interview experts in the subject matter. All of the following are considered to be disadvantages of using this method to conduct a needs assessment EXCEPT:
options: It can uncover details of training needs
questions.explanation:
One of the advantages of the interview method of conducting needs assessment for a safety training 
program is that it is good at uncovering the detailed of training needs, as well as causes and solutions of problems.

questions.question: One of the methods used in conducting a needs assessment for a safety training program is to read technical records and manuals. All of the following are considered to be advantages of using this method of needs assessment EXCEPT:
options: Good source of information on procedure
Good source of task information for new jobs
questions.explanation:
Another disadvantage of using this method of conducting needs assessment for a safety training 
program is that one may be unable to understand the technical language.

questions.question: The needs assessment process for determining whether a safety training program is needed is comprised of three factors; organizational analysis, person analysis, and task analysis. All of the following are factors that needs to be considered in organizational analysis EXCEPT:
options: Managers' and peers' support for training activities
questions.explanation:
Observation, use of questionnaires, studying technical manuals and records, and interviewing subject 
matter experts are different techniques used for the needs assessment process. Statements (b), (c), and (d) are 
factors that need to be considered in organizational analysis.

questions.question: Research has shown that cognitive ability has a considerable amount of influence on learning and on job performance. Cognitive ability includes three dimensions. All of the following are considered to be a dimension of cognitive ability EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Attitudes and motivations are not considered to be one of the three dimensions of cognitive ability. 
Cognitive ability can be measured by certain tests. Cognitive ability tests assess abilities involved in thinking (for 
example, reasoning, perception, memory, verbal and mathematical ability, and problem solving). Such tests pose 
questions designed to estimate applicants' potential to use mental processes to solve work-related problems or to 
acquire new job knowledge.

questions.question: Learning can be viewed as a relatively permanent change in an individual's capabilities that is not related to the growth process. These capabilities can be related to specific learning outcomes. All of the following are examples of types of learning outcomes EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Other examples of learning outcomes are intellectual skills and cognitive strategies. Trainee learning 
outcomes must be measurable, specific, practical, meaningful, and consistent.

questions.question: Learning is a relatively permanent change in an individual's capabilities that is not related to the growth process. These capabilities are related to specific learning outcomes. Examples of learning outcomes are verbal information, intellectual skills, motor skills, attitude, and cognitive strategies. Which of the following capabilities is related to the cognitive strategies learning outcome?
options: Manage one's own thinking and learning process
Choose a personal course of action
State, tell, or describe previously stored information
Execute a physical action with precision and timing
questions.explanation:
Statement (b) is related to the attitudes learning outcome, statement (c) is related to the verbal 
information learning outcome, and statement (d) is related to the motor skills learning outcome.

questions.question: Several learning theories have been proposed that relate to how we learn. All of the following are examples of learning theories EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Other proposed learning theories are the need theory, the expectancy theory, the adult learning 
theory, and the information processing theory. 
The goal setting theory emphasizes setting goals that are specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, and time-
targeted (SMART). This theory states that individuals in a group that has a common goal must clearly understand 
what is expected from them. 
The adult learning theory focuses on the following: 
• 
Adults in general want to have a reason why they should learn. 
• 
Adults use their own experiences to assist in their learning process. 
• 
New social rules determine the readiness of adults to learn. 
• 
Adults generally have a desire to apply what they have learned to problem solving. 
The expectancy theory states that individuals can be motivated to learn if they have certain expectations. 
The information processing theory is a cognitive processing theory. It focuses on how the mind functions. Learning 
elements such as rehearsal are associated with this theory, but emphasis is placed on how information is 
processed. 
The need theory explains the amount of value that a person places on certain outcomes. 
Reinforcement theory states that learners choose or avoid certain actions or behavior based on the consequences 
that are expected. Choices that led to positive consequences in the past have a tendency to be repeated, while 
those actions that resulted in a negative consequence in the past are avoided. 
The social learning theory, developed by Albert Bandura, focuses on observing the attitudes, behaviors, and 
emotional reactions of others. This learning theory emphasizes learning by observation, and considers that "we 
learn from each other."

questions.question: Reinforcement theory is one of the several proposed learning theories. Which of the following statements BEST describes the "reinforcement theory"?
options: Emphasizes that people learn by observing other individuals who, in their opinion, are knowledgeable and credible.
Assumes that an individual's behavior is the outcome of the person's conscious goals and intentions.
Emphasizes that the past outcomes of certain behaviors can motivate people to perform or avoid certain behaviors.
Explains the amount of value that a person places on certain outcomes.
questions.explanation:
Statement (a) is a description of social learning theory, statement (b) is a description of the goal 
setting theory, and statement (d) is a description of need theories.

questions.question: Which of the following statements BEST describes the information processing theory of learning?
options: Suggests that an individual's behavior is based on expectancy, instrumentality, and valence
Suggests that the orientation to learning must be problem-centered instead of subject-centered
Suggests that the instruction must be based on the learner's interests and competencies
Emphasizes the internal processes that occur when training content is learned and retained
questions.explanation:
Statement (a) is a description of the expectancy theory of learning. Statements (b) and (c) are both 
descriptions of the adult learning theory.

questions.question: According to the social learning theory, a person's learning is influenced by his or her self-efficacy. Which of the following statements BEST describes the concept of self-efficacy?
options: Learners must remember the behavior or skills that they observe.
Behavior modification is a training method that is based on reinforcement.
An individual's judgment about whether he/she can successfully learn knowledge and skills.
A need that motivates a person to behave in a manner to satisfy a deficiency.
questions.explanation:
Self-efficacy is best described by statement (c). Another way to describe self-efficacy is that it is an 
individual's belief in his or her ability to succeed in a particular situation.

questions.question: The expectancy theory of learning suggests that three factors are the basis for an individual's behavior. These factors are expectancy, instrumentality and valence. Which of the following statements best describes valence?
options: The value an individual places on an outcome
Adults have a need to know why they are learning something
Even the best designed training program cannot be successful if employees feel that their job security is threatened
Changes in the intensity or frequency of the stimulus that affect attention
questions.explanation:
Valence that is one of the factors that can influence an individual's behavior according to the 
expectancy theory of learning is best described by statement (a).

questions.question: The learning processes can be divided into eight different categories. These are: Expectancy, Perception, Working storage, Semantic encoding, Long-term storage, Retrieval, Generalizing, Gratifying. Which of the following BEST describes semantic encoding?
options: Refers to the mental state that the learner brings to the instructional process
Refers to the ability to organize the message from the environment so that it can be processed and acted upon
Refers to identifying learned material in long-term memory and using it to influence performance
questions.explanation:
Statement (a) is a description of expectancy, statement (b) is a description of perception, and 
statement (c) is a description of retrieval.

questions.question: Knowing the objectives of a training program greatly helps employees to learn best. A training objective has three components. Which of the following is NOT considered to be a component of a training objective?
options: A statement to elaborate the amount to be learned
A statement of what the employee's performance is expected to be
A statement of the quality of performance that is acceptable
A statement of the conditions under which the employee is expected to perform the outcome of the learning
questions.explanation:
Statements in (b), (c), and (d) are components of a training objective. Other examples of training 
program objectives include, but are not limited to, increasing productivity, better product quality, a better work 
environment, and improving health and safety.

questions.question: Seating arrangement at the training site must be based on the type of trainee interaction desired and the desired trainee-trainer interaction. All of the following are types of seating arrangements EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
